q: 谁负责组合后的数据保证？
q_en: Who owns the guarantees of the composed data system?
scenario: 一个资料页同时需要主库、缓存、搜索索引和异步邮件；对外只暴露一个资料 API。
scenario_en: A profile service uses a primary DB, cache, search index, and async email, but exposes one profile API.
options: 每个中间件各自保证端到端的一致语义
应用服务负责把组件拼成一个一致接口
客户端分别理解每个后端组件
options_en: Each middleware component guarantees the consistent end-to-end semantics by itself.
The application service composes components into one consistent interface.
Clients understand and call every backend component separately.
tradeoff: 组件专用能力 vs 组合后语义

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用程序接口：服务对调用方承诺的请求和响应边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the request and response contract a service exposes to callers.

diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> API[Profile API]
API --> DB[(Primary DB)]
API --> Cache[(Cache)]
API --> Search[(Search index)]
API --> Queue[[Queue]]
why: 把多个通用组件拼成一个服务后，对外语义由组合层负责。代价是应用代码要处理失效、重试和派生数据同步。
why_en: Once several tools are composed behind one API, the application layer owns the visible guarantees and their failure modes.
whenOtherWins: 若服务只使用单一数据库且无缓存/索引副本，组件自身的保证通常已经足够。
optionExplanations: 每个中间件只保证自己内部的行为，不了解其他组件的状态，没法单靠它们拼出跨组件一致的对外语义。
多个通用组件拼成一个服务后，对外的一致语义只能由应用层统一兜住——缓存、索引各自独立，只有它能补上失效和同步。
把内部拓扑暴露给客户端，等于让每个调用方都要自己搞懂缓存、索引怎么失效同步，维护和出错面都会爆炸。
optionExplanations_en: Each middleware layer only guarantees its own local behavior, so relying on it alone to stitch together cross-component semantics does not work.
Once several tools sit behind one API, the application layer is the only place that can own consistent guarantees across cache, index, and DB.
Exposing internal topology to clients means every caller has to understand cache and index invalidation itself, which explodes the maintenance surface.

q: 派生数据最大的设计风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main design risk with derived data?
scenario: 订单服务写主库后，还要更新缓存和搜索索引；任何一步都可能失败。
scenario_en: An order service writes the primary database, then updates a cache and a search index; any step may fail.
options: 派生副本的存储和维护成本一定高于主数据
副本可能与主数据短暂或永久分叉
主库不能再做强一致写入
options_en: Derived replicas always cost more to store and maintain than the primary.
The copies can temporarily or permanently diverge from the source.
The primary database can no longer support strong writes.
tradeoff: 读路径加速 vs 派生一致性

termDefinitions.meaning: 变更日志：按顺序记录数据修改，供下游重放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A change log records data modifications in order so downstream views can replay them.

why: 缓存和索引都是主数据的派生视图，失败会让读路径看到旧值或漏值。常见收尾是变更日志、重放和可观测的修复任务。
why_en: Derived views can drift from the source, so designs need a replayable change path and visible repair process.
optionExplanations: 成本高低是采购问题，不是这里的设计风险——它不会让读路径突然看到错误数据。
订单已经提交成功，缓存里却还是旧价、索引里搜不到这单；两边一旦分叉，只能靠重放补回来。
派生数据本身不限制主库的写入能力，主库该怎么强一致写还是怎么写，问题出在派生副本追不上。
optionExplanations_en: Cost is a procurement concern, not the risk that makes stale data show up in the read path.
The order commits, yet the cache still shows the old price and the index cannot find it; once they diverge only a replay closes the gap.
Having derived copies does not limit the primary's write consistency; the risk is that the copies fall behind, not that primary writes get weaker.

q: 这里该怎么区分 fault 和 failure？
q_en: How should you distinguish a fault from a failure here?
scenario: 一个节点磁盘坏了，但副本接管后用户请求仍成功。
scenario_en: One node loses a disk, but a replica takes over and user requests still succeed.
options: 磁盘坏是 failure，副本接管是 fault
磁盘坏是 fault，用户服务中断才是 failure
两者之间没有任何区别，只是同一现象换了个不同的叫法
options_en: The disk loss is a failure, and replica takeover is a fault.
The disk loss is a fault; user-visible service outage is the failure.
There is no difference at all; it's the same phenomenon under a different name.
tradeoff: 局部异常 vs 用户可见服务
why: fault 是局部组件偏离预期，failure 是系统没有向用户提供所需服务。容错设计的目标是让 fault 不升级成 failure。
why_en: A fault is local misbehavior, while a failure is user-visible service loss; fault tolerance keeps the former from becoming the latter.
optionExplanations: 这里说反了——磁盘坏是局部组件的偏离，副本接管让服务照常运行，用户完全没受影响。
磁盘坏是局部组件偏离预期，也就是 fault；只有当用户请求真的失败时，才算 failure，这次副本接管挡住了它。
两者不是同一件事——分清 fault 和 failure，才能说清容错设计到底防住了什么。
optionExplanations_en: This has it backwards: the disk loss is the local deviation, and replica takeover kept the service working with no visible impact.
The disk loss is a component deviating from spec, which is a fault; only a user-visible failure would count as a failure, and takeover prevented that here.
They are not interchangeable — separating fault from failure is exactly what lets you say fault tolerance worked in this incident.

q: 为什么要故意注入故障？
q_en: Why deliberately inject faults?
scenario: 支付外围的推荐服务已经有重试和降级；团队担心异常路径从没被真实触发。
scenario_en: A recommendation service around payments has retries and fallback, but the team worries those paths are never exercised.
options: 在生产环境证明任何故障都不会再发生
持续演练恢复路径，暴露错误处理缺陷
替代单元测试和代码审查
options_en: It proves in production that no fault can ever happen again.
To exercise recovery paths and expose error-handling bugs.
To replace unit tests and code review.
tradeoff: 演练信心 vs 注入风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 降级路径：主路径失败时提供较弱但可用的结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fallback is a weaker but usable path when the primary path fails.

why: 容错代码很容易只在纸面上存在，故障注入让它在低风险窗口反复跑起来。代价是必须有隔离、停止开关和清晰告警。
why_en: Fault injection is useful because recovery code must be exercised before a real incident depends on it.
whenOtherWins: 若还没有隔离、告警和回滚，先补这些基础保护，再做故障注入。
optionExplanations: 故障总会发生，注入故障证明不了「永不故障」，那不是它的目的。
恢复路径写在代码里不代表真的能跑，故障注入在低风险窗口反复触发它，把纸面上的容错变成验证过的能力。
单元测试和代码审查查的是代码逻辑本身，故障注入查的是系统在真实故障下的行为，两者不能互相替代。
optionExplanations_en: Faults will still happen; injecting them cannot prove they never will, so that is not the point.
Recovery code sitting untested is just paper — fault injection exercises it repeatedly in a low-risk window and turns it into a verified capability.
Unit tests and code review check the logic itself, while fault injection checks real system behavior under failure; neither substitutes for the other.

q: 这里优先选哪类可靠性策略？
q_en: Which reliability strategy should come first here?
scenario: 服务处理用户隐私数据；一旦被未授权下载，事后恢复数据库也无法撤回泄露。
scenario_en: A service stores private user data; once it is downloaded without authorization, restoring the database cannot undo the leak.
options: 主要依赖事后重试
优先预防和最小权限
定期故障注入下载路径
options_en: Rely mainly on after-the-fact retries.
Prioritize prevention and least privilege.
Regularly inject faults into the download path.
tradeoff: 故障恢复 vs 不可逆损害预防
why: 有些事件不能被治愈，隐私泄露就是这样。这里先减小发生概率和爆炸半径，再谈恢复。
why_en: For irreversible harm like data exposure, prevention and blast-radius reduction matter more than recovery after the fact.
whenOtherWins: 若损害可重试且可撤销，例如临时网络错误，恢复机制通常更经济。
optionExplanations: 事后重试能补救可以重来的错误，但隐私一旦泄露就无法撤回，重试对这种伤害没有意义。
隐私泄露这类不可逆伤害，最优先的是降低发生概率和爆炸半径，也就是预防和最小权限，而不是等出事再补救。
故障注入是为了验证恢复路径，但泄露没有恢复路径可言——这里要防的是根本不让它发生。
optionExplanations_en: After-the-fact retries can fix recoverable mistakes, but a privacy leak cannot be undone, so retrying does not help.
For irreversible harm like a leak, the priority is cutting the odds and blast radius up front — prevention and least privilege — not fixing it later.
Fault injection is for validating recovery paths, but a leak has no recovery path; the goal here is stopping it from happening at all.

q: 哪个判断更适合排障？
q_en: Which diagnosis is more useful?
scenario: 一个集群里，单块磁盘损坏只影响一台机器；同一个输入触发所有应用实例崩溃。
scenario_en: In a cluster, one disk failure affects one machine, while one bad input crashes every app instance.
options: 两者都通常独立随机
软件 bug 往往相关，硬件故障更常独立
硬件故障通常也会同时击穿所有节点机器
options_en: Both are usually independent and random.
Software bugs are often correlated, while hardware faults are more often independent.
Hardware faults usually knock out every node machine at once.
tradeoff: 随机局部故障 vs 系统性故障
why: 软件错误会在相同代码和相同假设里同时爆发，所以更容易造成全局失败。硬件故障也可能相关，但通常先按局部冗余处理。
why_en: Software faults are dangerous because the same bug and assumption can fail across many nodes at once.
optionExplanations: 实际情况并不对称——同一份代码里的软件 bug 更容易被同一个输入同时触发，硬件坏盘通常只影响那一块盘。
软件 bug 藏在所有实例共享的同一份代码和假设里，一个触发条件就能让全部实例同时倒下；硬件故障更常只坏一台。
这次事故正好相反：坏盘只影响一台机器，是同一个输入让所有实例同时崩溃暴露了软件层面的相关性。
optionExplanations_en: They are not symmetric in practice — a software bug in shared code is more likely to be triggered by the same input across every instance at once.
A software bug lives in the code and assumptions every instance shares, so one triggering input can take them all down together; hardware faults are usually more isolated.
This incident shows the opposite: the bad disk hit only one machine, while the same input crashed every app instance — that's software-level correlation.

q: 这个量级最直接推出什么设计？
q_en: What design follows most directly from this scale?
scenario: 一个存储集群有 10,000 块磁盘；即使单盘平均寿命按多年估算，集群每天也会遇到硬件损坏。
scenario_en: A storage cluster has 10,000 disks; even if each disk lasts years on average, the fleet sees hardware failures regularly.
options: 把磁盘故障当罕见手工事件
默认有副本、替换和重建流程
只购买更贵的单块磁盘
options_en: Treat disk failure as a rare manual event.
Assume replicas, replacement, and rebuild workflows.
Only buy more expensive individual disks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均失效时间：单个组件失效前的平均运行时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mean Time To Failure is the average operating time before one component fails.

why: 单件设备很可靠，乘上大规模数量后就会变成日常事件。这个数字的用途是决定运维流程和数据冗余，而不是背磁盘寿命。
why_en: At fleet size, rare per-device failures become routine, so the design needs redundancy and rebuild operations.
optionExplanations: 单块磁盘确实少见坏，但把它当成手工小概率事件，规划不出应对每天必然发生的故障流程。
单件设备可靠，乘上一万块盘之后，坏盘就从偶发变成了每天都会遇到的常态，设计上要默认有副本、替换和重建。
买更贵的单块磁盘只降低单件故障率，降不到零，规模效应下集群照样天天遇到坏盘。
optionExplanations_en: A single disk rarely fails, but treating it as a rare manual event won't give you a process for failures that happen daily at fleet scale.
One device is reliable, but across ten thousand disks, failure becomes routine — so the design should default to replicas, replacement, and rebuild workflows.
Buying pricier individual disks only lowers the per-disk failure rate, never to zero, so the fleet still hits failures every day regardless.

q: 可靠性方案应偏向什么？
q_en: Which reliability approach fits best?
scenario: 云平台可能无预警回收虚拟机；服务还要在打补丁时不中断。
scenario_en: A cloud platform may reclaim VMs without warning, and the service must patch hosts without downtime.
options: 只给单机加双电源和 RAID
让软件能容忍整台机器消失
把所有状态放在本机内存
options_en: Only add dual power supplies and RAID to one host.
Make the software tolerate losing a whole machine.
Keep all state in local memory.
tradeoff: 单机可靠性 vs 软件级容错

termDefinitions.meaning: 磁盘冗余阵列：用多块磁盘提高可用性或吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAID uses multiple disks to improve availability or throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 虚拟机：云平台上运行操作系统实例的隔离计算单元。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A VM is an isolated compute instance that runs an operating system on a cloud platform.

why: 云环境里机器本身不是稳定边界，服务要能迁移、重试或从副本接管。代价是分布式状态和部署流程更复杂。
why_en: In cloud environments, machine loss is normal enough that the service should survive it through replication and handoff.
whenOtherWins: 若固定单机运行且短暂停机可接受，硬件冗余和备份可以先满足需求。
optionExplanations: 双电源和 RAID 只保护单台机器不宕，云平台随时可能直接回收整台虚拟机，这道防线挡不住。
云上机器本身不是稳定边界，软件要能在整台机器消失时迁移、重试或让副本接管，才扛得住无预警回收。
状态全放本机内存，机器一被回收数据就没了，这跟容忍整机消失的目标正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: Dual power and RAID only protect a single host from crashing; they do nothing when the cloud platform reclaims the whole VM without warning.
A cloud machine is not a stable boundary, so the software must tolerate the whole machine vanishing via migration, retries, or replica handoff.
Keeping all state in local memory means it's gone the moment the machine is reclaimed — the opposite of tolerating a lost machine.

q: 哪些手段能降低系统性软件故障风险？
q_en: Which practices reduce systematic software-fault risk?
scenario: 一个服务偶发全实例崩溃，原因可能是隐藏假设被特殊输入触发。
scenario_en: A service sometimes crashes all instances because a rare input violates a hidden assumption.
options: 监控运行时不变量并告警
用进程隔离和自动重启限制影响
只增加同版本实例数量
用测试覆盖罕见边界条件
options_en: Monitor runtime invariants and alert on violations.
Use process isolation and automatic restart to limit impact.
Only add more instances of the same version.
Test rare edge cases.
why: 系统性 bug 会随同一代码复制，单纯加实例不解决。更好的做法是暴露假设、限制传播，并让异常路径可恢复。
why_en: Systematic bugs replicate with the code, so mitigation needs observability, isolation, and edge-case testing rather than just more nodes.
optionExplanations: 运行时不变量被破坏往往是系统性 bug 最早的信号，监控加告警能在崩溃前甚至崩溃时就发现它。
进程隔离和自动重启把一个实例的崩溃圈在局部，不让同一个触发条件顺着共享状态波及其他实例。
同版本实例共享同一份代码和假设，加得越多，被同一个输入同时打垮的实例也越多，反而放大故障。
针对性测试罕见边界条件能在上线前就触发那个隐藏假设，比等它在生产里被用户发现更便宜。
optionExplanations_en: A broken runtime invariant is often the earliest signal of a systematic bug, so monitoring and alerting can catch it before or as it crashes.
Process isolation and automatic restart contain one instance's crash locally instead of letting the same trigger cascade through shared state.
Same-version instances share the same code and assumptions, so adding more of them just gives the same input more copies to crash at once.
Testing rare edge cases on purpose can trip the hidden assumption before release, which is cheaper than a user finding it in production.

q: 哪些设计能降低人为错误造成的故障？
q_en: Which designs reduce failures caused by human error?
scenario: 运维经常要改配置、发版本、修数据；最大风险不是恶意，而是正常人会犯错。
scenario_en: Operators regularly change config, deploy code, and repair data; the main risk is ordinary human error, not malice.
options: 危险操作提供预览和确认
生产实验直接用真实用户流量
灰度发布并快速回滚
把修复脚本做成可重放任务
options_en: Provide preview and confirmation for dangerous actions.
Run production experiments directly on real user traffic.
Roll out gradually with fast rollback.
Make repair jobs replayable.
why: 人为错误挡不住，只能减少机会、缩小影响面，并让恢复更快。灰度和可重放修复把一次错误从全站事故降成可控事件。
why_en: Human error is inevitable, so good systems reduce chances, shrink blast radius, and make recovery fast.
optionExplanations: 危险操作先给预览和二次确认，能在人真下手之前拦住「手滑」式的错误。
直接拿真实用户流量做实验，出问题时波及的就是真实业务而不是安全环境，反而放大了人为错误的代价。
灰度发布把改动先放到一小部分流量验证，出问题能快速回滚，把全站事故降级成小范围可控事件。
把修复脚本做成可重放任务，出错后能安全地重跑一次，而不是靠人再手工修一遍、再犯一次错。
optionExplanations_en: Previewing and confirming dangerous actions catches a slip before the person actually commits it.
Running experiments directly on real user traffic means a mistake hits real business impact instead of a safe environment, which amplifies human error.
Gradual rollout validates a change on a small slice of traffic first and rolls back fast, turning a potential outage into a small, controllable event.
Making repair jobs replayable lets you safely rerun a fix instead of relying on a person to redo the manual steps and risk another mistake.

q: 最该先补哪道保护？
q_en: Which guardrail should you add first?
scenario: 新同事要学习批量改价工具；错误改价会直接影响真实订单。
scenario_en: A new teammate must learn a bulk price-change tool; mistakes would affect real orders.
options: 只写更长更详细的操作手册文档
提供接近真实数据的非生产沙箱
禁止新同事接触工具
options_en: Just write a longer, more detailed operations manual.
Provide a non-production sandbox with realistic data.
Ban new teammates from using the tool.
tradeoff: 学习速度 vs 生产爆炸半径
why: 沙箱把学习和破坏生产解耦，能让人犯错但不伤用户。文档有帮助，但不能替代安全练习环境。
why_en: A realistic sandbox lets people make mistakes without turning learning into a production incident.
whenOtherWins: 若操作只读且影响很低，清晰文档可能够用；高危写操作才需要沙箱。
optionExplanations: 更长的文档只是多读几段字，挡不住手快出错的操作，改价工具的风险还在。
接近真实数据的非生产沙箱，能让新人真的练手、犯错，但不会碰到真实订单，学习和破坏生产被解耦了。
禁止新同事碰工具只是把风险往后拖，等真正上手时还是没练过，风险原封不动地留到那一刻。
optionExplanations_en: A longer runbook just adds more reading; it does not stop someone's hand from slipping on the real pricing tool.
A sandbox with realistic data lets a newcomer actually practice and make mistakes without ever touching real orders, decoupling learning from production risk.
Banning newcomers from the tool only delays the risk — the first time they do touch it for real, they still have zero practice.

q: 发布策略的关键是什么？
q_en: What matters most in the release strategy?
scenario: 推荐排序新版本可能影响收入；离线测试通过，但线上分布仍不确定。
scenario_en: A new ranking version may affect revenue; offline tests pass, but online behavior is uncertain.
options: 一次性全量发布以获得最快反馈
灰度放量并能快速回滚
只在事故后增加监控
options_en: Ship to everyone at once for the fastest feedback.
Ramp gradually and keep rollback fast.
Add monitoring only after an incident.
tradeoff: 反馈速度 vs 影响面
why: 灰度把未知 bug 限制在小流量里，回滚把恢复时间压短。代价是发布系统和指标门禁要先做好。
why_en: Gradual rollout limits unknown bugs to small traffic slices, and fast rollback reduces recovery time.
optionExplanations: 一次性全量发布确实反馈最快，但任何未知 bug 也会同时打到所有用户，没有缓冲空间。
灰度放量把未知问题限制在一小片流量里，配合快速回滚，能把发现问题到恢复的时间压到最短。
只在事故后补监控，等于承认要先出一次事故才肯投入，监控本该在发布前就到位。
optionExplanations_en: Shipping to everyone at once does give the fastest feedback, but it also means any unknown bug hits every user with no buffer.
Ramping gradually limits an unknown bug to a small slice of traffic, and fast rollback keeps the time from detection to recovery short.
Adding monitoring only after an incident means you accept eating one outage first — it should already be in place before the release ships.

q: 监控应该补什么？
q_en: What should monitoring add?
scenario: 一个队列承诺消息不丢；事故时只看到消费者变慢，不知道入队和出队是否守恒。
scenario_en: A queue promises not to lose messages; during an incident, the team sees slow consumers but not whether inputs equal outputs.
options: 只看机器 CPU 使用率
持续检查业务不变量和错误率
只记录成功请求日志
options_en: Watch only machine CPU usage.
Continuously check business invariants and error rates.
Log only successful requests.
tradeoff: 资源健康 vs 语义健康

termDefinitions.meaning: 中央处理器：执行程序指令的计算资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CPU is the processor resource that executes program instructions.

why: 可靠性监控要看系统承诺是否还成立，而不只是资源图。消息守恒这类不变量能更早暴露数据正确性问题。
why_en: Reliability monitoring should check whether service promises still hold, not only whether machines look busy.
whenOtherWins: 若还没定义业务承诺，先写清不变量，再决定该监控哪些信号。
optionExplanations: CPU 使用率正常不代表业务承诺还成立，这次事故看的正是消息有没有丢，而不是机器忙不忙。
持续检查入队出队是否守恒这类业务不变量，能比资源图更早暴露「消息丢了」这种正确性问题。
只记录成功请求，等于把失败和丢失的消息从日志里抹掉了，正好是这次最想知道的部分。
optionExplanations_en: Normal CPU usage doesn't mean the service promise still holds — this incident is about whether messages got lost, not whether machines are busy.
Continuously checking an invariant like enqueue/dequeue balance can surface a correctness problem like lost messages earlier than resource graphs would.
Logging only successful requests erases exactly the failed or lost messages that this incident needs to see.

q: 可靠性投入该怎么取舍？
q_en: How should reliability investment be traded off?
scenario: 团队在验证一个无人使用的新产品概念；预算很小，目标是下周找到市场信号。
scenario_en: A team is validating a new product idea with no users yet; budget is tiny and the goal is market signal next week.
options: 按银行核心系统标准设计
接受有限可靠性并明确风险
完全不做备份和恢复
options_en: Design it like a core banking system.
Accept limited reliability and make the risk explicit.
Skip backup and recovery entirely.
tradeoff: 可靠性成本 vs 学习速度
why: 可靠性不是免费的，早期原型可以有意识地少做一些。边界要写清楚，避免把临时取舍变成长期隐患。
why_en: For an early prototype, limited reliability can be a conscious tradeoff as long as the risk is explicit and revisited.
whenOtherWins: 若已有真实用户、资金或合规责任，可靠性投入要提前加大。
optionExplanations: 按银行核心系统标准设计，会把本该花在找市场信号上的时间和预算都投进可靠性里，早期原型付不起。
接受有限可靠性但把边界写清楚，让团队知道自己在承担什么风险，这才配得上小预算、快验证的目标。
完全不做备份和恢复，一旦出问题连「有意识地少做」都算不上，只是彻底没人管这个风险。
optionExplanations_en: Designing it like a core banking system pours the budget and time meant for finding market signal into reliability the prototype can't afford.
Accepting limited reliability while writing the risk down explicitly matches a small-budget, fast-validation goal — the team knows what it's trading away.
Skipping backup and recovery entirely isn't even a conscious tradeoff anymore; it just means nobody is tracking the risk at all.

q: 可扩展性问题应如何表述？
q_en: How should a scalability question be phrased?
text: 不要只说系统“可扩展”；更好的问法是：当 {{某个负载参数}} 增长时，我们有哪些 {{资源或架构}} 选择来维持性能？
text_en: Do not just say a system is scalable; ask: when a {{specific load parameter}} grows, what {{resource or architecture}} choices keep performance acceptable?
why: 可扩展性是相对某种增长方式的讨论，不是系统的永久标签。先命名负载，后谈扩容。
why_en: Scalability is not a permanent label; name the growing load parameter before discussing how to cope.

q: 哪个负载参数最该先量化？
q_en: Which load parameter should be quantified first?
scenario: 聊天室读写都不大，但每个房间同时在线人数差异很大；热门房间会拖垮广播路径。
scenario_en: A chat app has modest total reads and writes, but room concurrency varies widely; hot rooms stress broadcast paths.
options: 代码仓库里的源文件总数量
每个房间同时在线人数分布
数据库表名长度
options_en: The total number of source files in the code repository.
Distribution of concurrently active users per room.
Length of database table names.
tradeoff: 平均总量 vs 热点分布

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数：服务每秒处理的请求或查询数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queries Per Second is the number of requests or queries a service handles each second.

why: 负载参数要抓住会改变瓶颈的量。这里总 QPS 不够，房间并发分布决定一次消息要扇出多少连接。
why_en: The right load parameter is the one that changes the bottleneck; here room concurrency drives fan-out work.
whenOtherWins: 若瓶颈来自全局请求率而非房间热点，总 QPS 会比房间分布更优先。
optionExplanations: 代码仓库文件数量跟聊天室的实时负载没有关系，改变不了广播路径的瓶颈。
每个房间同时在线人数的分布，直接决定一条消息要往多少个连接扇出，是这里真正会拖垮系统的量。
表名长度是纯粹的元数据细节，不会随负载变化，量化它对定位瓶颈毫无帮助。
optionExplanations_en: The number of files in the code repository has nothing to do with the chat room's live load and won't move the fan-out bottleneck.
The distribution of concurrently active users per room directly decides how many connections one message must fan out to — that's the real bottleneck driver.
Table name length is a static metadata detail that never changes with load, so quantifying it does nothing to locate the bottleneck.

q: 默认把工作放在哪条路径？
q_en: Where should the work go by default?
scenario: 社交 Feed 读请求远多于发帖；普通用户粉丝不多，读首页必须很快。
scenario_en: A social feed has far more reads than posts; ordinary users have modest follower counts, and home timeline reads must be fast.
options: 读首页时再查关注列表并合并
发帖时预写入粉丝收件箱
每次请求全表扫描最新帖子
options_en: At read time, fetch follows and merge posts.
At write time, pre-fill follower inboxes.
Full-scan all recent posts on every request.
tradeoff: 读路径延迟 vs 写路径放大
diagram:
flowchart LR
Post[Post tweet] --> Fanout[Fan out to followers]
Fanout --> I1[Inbox A]
Fanout --> I2[Inbox B]
Read[Home read] --> I1
why: 读多写少时，预计算首页能把高频读变成便宜读取。代价是发帖会被粉丝数放大，明星账号要特殊处理。
why_en: When reads dominate writes, precomputing timelines makes reads cheap, but posting cost grows with follower fan-out.
whenOtherWins: 若写入远多于读取，或粉丝数极端巨大，读时合并可能更划算。
optionExplanations: 读首页时才查关注列表合并，等于把合并工作堆在高频的读路径上，跟「读多写少要让读便宜」的目标反着来。
发帖时就预写入粉丝收件箱，把工作挪到低频的写路径，换来首页读取只是一次简单查询，很快。
全表扫描最新帖子在数据量变大后会越来越慢，读多写少场景下完全撑不住高频首页请求。
optionExplanations_en: Merging follows at read time piles the merge work onto the high-frequency read path, which fights the goal of keeping frequent reads cheap.
Pre-filling follower inboxes at post time moves the work to the low-frequency write path, so a home feed read becomes one cheap lookup.
Full-scanning recent posts gets slower as data grows and cannot keep up with a high-frequency home-feed read path.

q: 核心取舍轴是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff?
scenario: 同一个 Feed 系统要在读时合并和写时扇出之间选择；两者都能生成首页。
scenario_en: The same feed system can assemble timelines either by read-time merge or write-time fan-out; both can produce a home feed.
options: 读时合并省写入但读更重
写时扇出省所有存储
两者只差编程语言
options_en: Read-time merge saves writes but makes reads heavier.
Write-time fan-out saves all storage.
They differ only by programming language.
tradeoff: 读时计算 vs 写时预计算
why: 读时合并把成本推到每次首页读取，写时扇出把成本推到发帖和收件箱存储。选哪个取决于读写比例和粉丝分布。
why_en: Read-time merge pays on every feed read; write-time fan-out pays on posting and inbox storage, so the workload shape decides.
optionExplanations: 读时合并确实省下了预写入粉丝收件箱的存储和写入成本，但代价是每次打开首页都要现算，读会更重。
写时扇出能让首页读取只是一次简单查询，但要为每个粉丝都写一份收件箱记录，存储和写入成本更高，不是「省所有存储」。
两种方案的差异是把成本放在读路径还是写路径，跟用什么编程语言实现完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Read-time merge does avoid pre-filling follower inboxes, but the cost is that every home-feed open now has to compute the merge live, so reads get heavier.
Write-time fan-out makes reads a cheap lookup, but it means writing one inbox entry per follower, which costs more storage and writes, not less.
The real difference is which path — read or write — absorbs the cost; it has nothing to do with the implementation language.

q: 明星账号该怎么处理？
q_en: How should celebrity accounts be handled?
scenario: Feed 系统已经写时扇出普通用户；少数明星账号有千万粉丝，单条动态会产生巨大写峰值。
scenario_en: A feed system fans out ordinary users on write; a few celebrity accounts have tens of millions of followers and create huge write spikes.
options: 所有账号都统一改成读时合并
明星跳过写时扇出，读时再合并
禁止明星发帖
options_en: Switch every account to merge-on-read uniformly.
Skip write fan-out for celebrities and merge them at read time.
Prevent celebrities from posting.
tradeoff: 统一架构 vs 热点特例
why: 混合方案把普通用户的快读保住，同时避免明星发帖造成爆炸写入。代价是读路径要额外合并少量特殊来源。
why_en: The hybrid keeps cheap reads for normal users while avoiding massive celebrity write fan-out.
whenOtherWins: 若明星账号很少被读，异步分批写时扇出也可能够用。
optionExplanations: 把所有账号都改成读时合并，会让普通用户的首页也变慢，丢掉了写时扇出本来带来的快读优势。
明星账号跳过写时扇出、读时再合并，既避免了千万粉丝造成的写入峰值，又保住了普通用户的快速首页读取。
禁止明星发帖直接牺牲了产品功能，而不是解决「扇出成本随粉丝数暴涨」这个工程问题。
optionExplanations_en: Moving every account to read-time merge slows down the home feed for normal users too, throwing away the fast reads write fan-out was giving them.
Skipping write fan-out for celebrities and merging them at read time avoids the massive write spike while keeping fast home-feed reads for everyone else.
Banning celebrities from posting just removes a product feature instead of solving the actual problem of fan-out cost scaling with follower count.

q: 该分别看哪个指标？
q_en: Which metrics fit these workloads?
scenario: 夜间报表处理关心多久跑完整批数据；网页请求关心用户等多久。
scenario_en: A nightly report cares how long the whole dataset takes; a web request cares how long the user waits.
options: 批处理看吞吐/总时长，在线服务看响应时间
两者都只看平均 CPU
批处理看 p99，在线服务只看总行数
options_en: Batch jobs use throughput or total runtime, while online services use response time.
Both should only watch average CPU.
Batch jobs use p99, while online services only count rows.
tradeoff: 总处理效率 vs 单请求等待

termDefinitions.meaning: 中央处理器：执行程序指令的计算资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CPU is the processor resource that executes program instructions.

why: 批处理目标是单位时间处理多少数据或总耗时，在线请求目标是用户等待分布。指标先跟交互模式对齐。
why_en: Batch workloads care about throughput or job duration, while online workloads care about user-visible response-time distribution.
optionExplanations: 批处理关心跑完一整批数据要多久，在线服务关心用户等待的分布，两者的目标指标本来就不同。
平均 CPU 反映的是资源占用，跟「数据多久处理完」或「用户等多久」都对不上，两类系统都不该只看它。
批处理该看整体吞吐或耗时，p99 是在线服务盯尾延迟用的；总行数也不是在线请求关心的指标。
optionExplanations_en: Batch jobs care about how long the whole run takes; online services care about the distribution of user wait time — the target metrics are different by design.
Average CPU reflects resource usage, not how long a batch takes or how long a user waits, so neither workload should rely on it alone.
Batch jobs should track overall throughput or duration; p99 is for online tail latency, and raw row count isn't what an online request cares about.

q: response time 包含什么？
q_en: What does response time include?
scenario: 一次请求在服务器排队 80ms、执行 20ms、网络往返 40ms；用户看到的是完整等待。
scenario_en: A request waits in a queue for 80 ms, runs for 20 ms, and spends 40 ms on the network; the user sees the full wait.
options: 只包含服务执行时间
包含排队、执行和网络等用户可见等待
只包含建立连接的 TCP 握手时间
options_en: Only service execution time.
Queueing, service time, network time, and other user-visible waiting.
Only the TCP handshake time to set up the connection.
tradeoff: 服务时间 vs 端到端等待

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输控制协议：提供可靠字节流连接的网络协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a network protocol that provides a reliable byte stream connection.

why: 响应时间是客户端看到的端到端等待；latency 常指请求等待被处理的时间。排队会让服务本身很快也表现很慢。
why_en: Response time is the end-to-end wait seen by the client, so queueing can make a fast handler feel slow.

rows: 只包含服务执行时间场景
只包含服务执行时间成本
包含排队、执行和网络等用户可见等待
包含排队、执行和网…场景
包含排队、执行和网络等…成本
只包含 TCP 握手时间
只包含 TCP 握…场景
只包含 TCP 握手时间成本

optionExplanations: 只算执行时间会漏掉排队和网络往返，用户实际感受到的是从发出请求到收到响应的全部等待。
排队、执行、网络往返加在一起才是用户真正等到的时间，服务本身很快也可能因为排队显得很慢。
TCP 握手只是网络往返里的一小段，不能代表用户看到的完整响应时间。
optionExplanations_en: Counting only execution time misses queueing and network round-trip — the user feels the full wait from request sent to response received.
Queueing, execution, and network round-trip together make up what the user actually waits for; a fast handler can still feel slow if it's stuck queueing.
A TCP handshake is just one small slice of the round trip, not the full response time the user experiences.

q: SLO 更应该盯什么？
q_en: What should the SLO focus on?
scenario: 电商页面会并行调用 20 个后端；平均响应正常，但少数慢调用会拖慢整页。
scenario_en: An ecommerce page calls 20 backends in parallel; average latency looks fine, but a few slow calls delay the whole page.
options: 只盯请求的平均值，忽略长尾
盯 p95/p99 尾延迟
只盯最快那批请求
options_en: Watch only the request average and ignore the long tail.
Tail latency at p95 and p99.
Only the fastest requests.
tradeoff: 典型体验 vs 尾部体验

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队承诺或追踪的性能/可用性目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Objective is a target for service performance or availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位：99% 请求快于这个阈值，1% 请求更慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The 99th percentile is the threshold below which 99% of requests complete.

why: 并行 fan-out 下，整页要等最慢的关键调用。高百分位能暴露少数用户和多调用页面真正感受到的慢。
why_en: With parallel fan-out, the page waits for the slowest important call, so high percentiles show the pain averages hide.
whenOtherWins: 若只是看单次典型体验且没有多后端 fan-out，中位数可以先作为粗指标。
optionExplanations: 平均值会被大多数正常请求盖住，看不出那一小撮拖慢整页的慢调用。
20 个后端并行调用时，整页要等最慢的那个，p95/p99 这类高百分位才能暴露出真正拖慢用户的少数请求。
只看最快请求等于完全忽略了拖慢整页的那部分调用，跟这里想解决的问题正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: The average gets smoothed over by the many normal requests, hiding the small slice of slow calls that actually drag down the page.
With 20 parallel backend calls, the whole page waits for the slowest one, so high percentiles like p95/p99 are what expose the calls really hurting users.
Watching only the fastest requests ignores exactly the slow calls dragging the page down — the opposite of what this problem needs.

q: 这会造成什么现象？
q_en: What phenomenon does this cause?
scenario: 服务器一次只能并行处理少量请求；几个慢请求占住 worker 后，后面的快请求也在队列里等。
scenario_en: A server can process only a few requests in parallel; a few slow requests occupy workers, so later fast requests wait in the queue.
options: 队头阻塞抬高尾延迟
请求排队反而抬高缓存命中率
排队会让平均请求体积变小
options_en: Head-of-line blocking raises tail latency.
Queueing somehow raises the cache hit rate.
Queueing makes the average request body smaller.
tradeoff: 并发限制 vs 队列等待

termDefinitions.meaning: 队头阻塞：前面的慢任务挡住后面的任务继续执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Head-of-line blocking means a slow item at the front delays items behind it.

why: 慢请求挡在队头时，后面的轻请求也会被记成慢响应。客户端侧测量才能看见这段排队等待。
why_en: Head-of-line blocking makes later fast requests wait behind slow ones, so client-side timing captures the real delay.
optionExplanations: 慢请求占住 worker 后，排在它后面的快请求也要跟着等，整体尾延迟被拖高，这正是 head-of-line blocking。
排队变长跟缓存命中率没有因果关系，命中率不会因为请求在等待就自动提高。
排队会让请求等更久，但不会改变请求体本身的大小，这两者互不影响。
optionExplanations_en: Once slow requests occupy the workers, the fast requests waiting behind them get delayed too, raising overall tail latency — that's head-of-line blocking.
A longer queue has no causal link to cache hit rate; hit rate doesn't rise just because requests are waiting.
Queueing makes requests wait longer, but it does not change the size of the request body itself — the two are unrelated.

q: 这种压测会低估什么？
q_en: What will this load test underestimate?
scenario: 压测客户端等上一个请求返回后才发下一个；真实用户不会这样排队等待。
scenario_en: A load-test client waits for each response before sending the next request; real users do not coordinate that way.
options: 服务器队列和尾延迟
代码行数
磁盘可用容量的上限
options_en: Server queueing and tail latency.
Lines of code.
The upper bound of available disk capacity.
tradeoff: 闭环客户端便利 vs 真实到达过程
why: 闭环压测会在服务变慢时自动少发请求，队列被人为压短。开环负载更接近外部请求持续到来的现实。
why_en: Closed-loop load tests send less load when the service slows, so they can hide queueing and tail latency.
whenOtherWins: 若只做单请求微基准，闭环测试可用；容量压测要保持外部到达率。
optionExplanations: 客户端等上一个请求返回才发下一个，服务变慢时发出的请求也会跟着变少，队列和尾延迟因此被人为压低、看不出来。
代码行数跟压测客户端怎么发请求毫无关系，不是这种测试方式会低估的东西。
磁盘容量是静态资源指标，压测的请求节奏快慢不会让它被低估。
optionExplanations_en: A closed-loop client waits for the previous response before sending the next request, so when the service slows down it sends less load, artificially hiding queueing and tail latency.
Lines of code have nothing to do with how the load-test client paces requests, so it's not something this test style would underestimate.
Disk capacity is a static resource metric; the pacing of a load test doesn't cause it to be underestimated.

q: 正确聚合方式是什么？
q_en: What is the correct way to aggregate percentiles?
scenario: 多台服务各自上报 p99；平台想得到全站 p99。
scenario_en: Several service instances report their own p99; the platform wants the fleet-wide p99.
options: 直接平均各实例 p99
合并原始直方图后重新计算
取实例名称排序后的中位数
options_en: Average the instance p99 values.
Merge the raw histograms and recompute.
Take the median by instance name order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位：99% 请求快于这个阈值，1% 请求更慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The 99th percentile is the threshold below which 99% of requests complete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队承诺或追踪的性能/可用性目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Objective is a target for service performance or availability.

why: 百分位不是可加指标，平均 p99 没有清晰含义。要先合并延迟分布，再从合并后的分布求百分位。
why_en: Percentiles are properties of a distribution, so merge histograms first and then recompute the percentile.
optionExplanations: 百分位不是可加指标，直接平均各实例的 p99 得不出有意义的全站数字。
先把各实例的原始延迟直方图合并成一份，再从合并后的分布里求百分位，这样算出的才是真实的全站 p99。
按实例名称排序取中位数跟延迟分布毫无关系，只是巧合地凑出一个数字。
optionExplanations_en: Percentiles are not additive, so averaging each instance's p99 does not produce a meaningful fleet-wide number.
Merge the raw latency histograms from every instance first, then compute the percentile from that merged distribution — that gives the real fleet-wide p99.
Sorting by instance name and taking the median has nothing to do with the latency distribution; it's just a coincidental number.

q: scale up 和 scale out 怎么取舍？
q_en: How do scale up and scale out trade off?
scenario: 单机数据库接近容量上限；团队可买更强机器，也可把负载分到多台。
scenario_en: A single-node database is near capacity; the team can buy a bigger machine or split load across machines.
options: scale up 省复杂度，scale out 省单机成本
scale out 一定更简单，也完全不增加任何协调成本
scale up 自动带来跨机容灾和弹性扩容
options_en: Scaling up buys simplicity; scaling out buys cheaper capacity.
Scaling out is always simpler and adds no coordination cost whatsoever.
Scaling up automatically gives cross-machine failover and elasticity.
tradeoff: 单机简单性 vs 分布式容量
why: 垂直扩容保留单机语义，通常更容易运维；水平扩容能突破单机上限，但会引入分片、复制和故障处理。
why_en: Vertical scaling preserves single-node simplicity, while horizontal scaling buys headroom at the cost of distributed-systems complexity.
optionExplanations: 垂直扩容不引入分布式复杂度，代价是更贵的机器和单机容量上限；水平扩容突破了上限，但要处理分片、复制和故障。
水平扩容一样要付协调成本——分片路由、副本一致性都要自己处理，并不会自动变简单。
垂直扩容只是换了台更强的机器，本身不会带来跨机器容灾或弹性伸缩的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Scaling up avoids distributed complexity at the cost of pricier hardware and a hard capacity ceiling; scaling out breaks that ceiling but adds sharding, replication, and failure handling.
Scaling out still pays a coordination cost — shard routing and replica consistency don't get simpler on their own.
Scaling up is just a stronger single machine; it doesn't automatically grant cross-machine disaster tolerance or elasticity.

q: 弹性扩容什么时候值得？
q_en: When is elastic scaling worth it?
scenario: 活动流量不可预测，可能在几分钟内暴涨；平时流量很低。
scenario_en: Campaign traffic is unpredictable and may spike within minutes, while normal traffic is low.
options: 负载高度不可预测时
负载稳定且人工容量评审足够时
任何有数据库的系统都必须自动扩
options_en: When load is highly unpredictable.
When load is stable and manual capacity review is enough.
Every system with a database must autoscale.
tradeoff: 自动响应速度 vs 运维可预测性
why: 弹性扩容用自动化换取对突发负载的响应速度。稳定负载下，人工扩容更简单，也更少出现自动化误判。
why_en: Elastic scaling trades operational complexity for fast response to unpredictable load spikes.
whenOtherWins: 若流量稳定且容量评审成熟，手动扩容更简单、也更可预测。
optionExplanations: 负载高度不可预测、可能几分钟内暴涨时，自动弹性扩容能比人工审批更快跟上，值这个自动化成本。
负载稳定时，人工容量评审就够用，自动化反而多了误判和复杂度的风险，不划算。
不是所有带数据库的系统都要自动扩，很多稳定负载的系统用人工容量规划就足够。
optionExplanations_en: When load is highly unpredictable and can spike within minutes, elastic autoscaling keeps up faster than manual approval, which is worth the automation cost.
When load is stable, manual capacity review is already enough, and adding automation just adds risk of misjudged scale-ups without real benefit.
Not every system with a database needs autoscaling; many stable-load systems are fine with manual capacity planning.

q: 为什么 stateful 扩展更难？
q_en: Why is stateful scaling harder?
scenario: Web 层无状态，复制十份后都能处理请求；数据库保存用户状态，不能简单复制十份当作同一份数据。
scenario_en: The web tier is stateless and can be copied ten times; the database holds user state and cannot be copied blindly as one dataset.
options: 状态需要一致性、放置和恢复规则
有状态服务根本不能使用网络通信
无状态服务一定不需要监控
options_en: State needs consistency, placement, and recovery rules.
Stateful services simply cannot use the network at all.
Stateless services never need monitoring.
tradeoff: 无状态复制便利 vs 状态一致性成本
why: 无状态实例可以被负载均衡随意替换，状态数据要回答哪份是最新、放在哪里、坏了怎么补。分布式数据系统复杂度主要来自这些问题。
why_en: Stateless replicas are easy to replace, but state needs rules for freshness, placement, and recovery.
optionExplanations: 状态数据要回答哪份最新、放在哪、坏了怎么补，这些一致性、放置和恢复规则正是无状态服务不用操心的部分。
有状态服务照样要用网络做复制和协调，这不是它跟无状态服务的区别所在。
无状态服务同样需要监控，只是它的状态更简单，不代表可以完全不监控。
optionExplanations_en: State has to answer which copy is freshest, where it lives, and how to repair it — those consistency, placement, and recovery rules are exactly what stateless services skip.
Stateful services still use the network for replication and coordination; that's not what separates them from stateless ones.
Stateless services still need monitoring too; simpler state doesn't mean no monitoring at all.

q: 为什么架构不能只按总吞吐选？
q_en: Why is total throughput not enough to choose the architecture?
scenario: 两个系统吞吐相同：一个每秒十万次 1KB 请求，另一个每分钟三次 2GB 上传。
scenario_en: Two systems have similar byte throughput: one has 100k tiny requests per second, the other has three 2 GB uploads per minute.
options: 请求形状决定连接、排队和存储路径
只要 MB/s 相同架构就相同
大文件系统不需要容量规划
options_en: Request shape determines connections, queueing, and storage path.
The same MB/s always means the same architecture.
Large-file systems do not need capacity planning.
tradeoff: 总吞吐量 vs 请求形状
why: 总字节率相同也可能有完全不同瓶颈：同样约 100 MB/s，可以是 10万×1KB，也可以是 3×2GB/分钟。前者压并发和调度，后者压分片上传和持久化。
why_en: The same roughly 100 MB/s can be 100k x 1KB requests or 3 x 2GB uploads a minute — one stresses concurrency, the other stresses multipart upload and durability.
whenOtherWins: 若请求大小和并发形状也相同，总吞吐才可能作为主要容量指标。
optionExplanations: 十万次 1KB 小请求考验的是并发连接和调度，三次 2GB 大文件考验的是分片上传和持久化，请求形状不同，路径也完全不同。
总字节率一样不代表瓶颈一样，小请求和大文件在连接数、排队方式、存储路径上差异巨大。
越是大对象越需要提前规划分片上传和存储容量，这里说反了——大对象反而更需要容量规划。
optionExplanations_en: A hundred thousand 1KB requests stress concurrency and scheduling, while three 2GB uploads stress chunked upload and durable storage — the request shape decides the path, not just the byte rate.
Equal MB/s does not mean equal bottlenecks; small requests and huge objects differ hugely in connection count, queueing, and storage path.
Large-object systems need chunked-upload and capacity planning even more, not less — this option has it backwards.

q: 哪些能力属于良好 operability？
q_en: Which capabilities are part of good operability?
scenario: 一个数据系统交给值班团队长期运行；目标是让例行操作少出错、可诊断。
scenario_en: A data system will be operated by an on-call team for years; routine work should be low-risk and diagnosable.
options: 清晰监控和运行时可见性
能滚动维护单台机器
只有作者知道的隐式操作模型
默认安全但允许受控覆盖
options_en: Clear monitoring and runtime visibility.
The ability to maintain one machine at a time.
An implicit model known only by the original author.
Safe defaults with controlled override.
why: 可运维性让团队把精力花在高价值判断上，而不是猜系统内部状态。可见性、自动化接口和可预测行为是基础。
why_en: Operability means the team can see, predict, and safely manage the system during routine work and incidents.
optionExplanations: 清晰的监控和运行时可见性，让值班团队能看懂系统在做什么，而不是靠猜。
能滚动维护单台机器而不停服务，是例行操作不出全站事故的基本能力。
只有作者自己懂的隐式操作模型，等于把系统的可维护性绑死在一个人身上，风险很高。
默认安全、但允许受控覆盖，既防住误操作，又不妨碍真正需要越权处理的场景。
optionExplanations_en: Clear monitoring and runtime visibility let the on-call team see what the system is actually doing instead of guessing.
Being able to maintain one machine at a time without taking the whole service down is the baseline for routine operations that don't turn into outages.
An implicit operating model known only to its author ties the system's maintainability to one person, which is a serious risk.
Safe defaults with controlled override block accidental misuse while still allowing the rare case that genuinely needs elevated access.

q: simplicity 真正在减少什么？
q_en: What does simplicity actually reduce?
text: 系统设计里的 simplicity 不是减少功能，而是减少 {{accidental complexity}}：实现方式带来的、用户问题本身不要求的复杂度。
text_en: In system design, simplicity does not mean fewer features; it reduces {{accidental complexity}}, complexity from implementation rather than the user problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 偶然复杂度：问题本身不需要、由实现选择引入的复杂度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Accidental complexity is complexity introduced by implementation choices rather than by the problem itself.

why: 好的抽象隐藏机器细节、存储细节或恢复细节，让工程师能在更高层做判断。抽象也会失败，所以要看它是否真的减轻推理负担。
why_en: Good abstractions hide implementation details so engineers can reason at the right level, but the abstraction must actually reduce cognitive load.

q: 好的抽象应该隐藏什么？
q_en: What should a good abstraction hide?
scenario: 团队把缓存、主库和搜索索引封装成一个写接口；调用方只关心写入后能按关键字查到。
scenario_en: A team wraps cache, primary DB, and search index behind one write API; callers only care that data becomes searchable.
options: 所有失败和延迟事实
内部同步细节，但保留可观察的语义和限制
让调用方手动更新每一个内部的组件状态
options_en: All facts about failure and latency.
Internal synchronization details while keeping visible semantics and limits.
It makes callers manually update every internal component's state.
tradeoff: 隐藏实现细节 vs 暴露语义边界

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用程序接口：服务对调用方承诺的请求和响应边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the request and response contract a service exposes to callers.

why: 抽象不是假装复杂度不存在，而是把调用方不该管理的步骤藏起来，并清楚说明可见保证。代价是抽象层要承担监控和修复。
why_en: A good abstraction hides internal steps without hiding the observable contract and its limits.
whenOtherWins: 若限制本身影响调用方判断，就应该暴露在接口合同里，而不是藏起来。
optionExplanations: 隐藏所有失败和延迟事实，调用方连「写入还没同步完」都不知道，等于假装复杂度不存在。
抽象该藏的是内部怎么同步缓存、主库和索引，但要保留调用方能观察到的语义和限制，比如写后能不能立刻查到。
要求调用方手动更新每个组件，等于完全没有抽象，跟封装成一个写接口的目标正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Hiding every fact about failure and latency means the caller doesn't even know a write hasn't synced yet — that's pretending the complexity doesn't exist.
A good abstraction hides internal sync steps between cache, primary, and index, but keeps the caller-visible semantics and limits, like when a write becomes readable.
Requiring the caller to manually update each component is not an abstraction at all — it's the opposite of wrapping them behind one write interface.

q: 什么设计会让这种演进更容易？
q_en: What design makes this evolution easier?
scenario: Feed 系统初版读时合并，后来读流量暴涨，需要迁移到预计算收件箱。
scenario_en: A feed system starts with read-time merge, but read traffic grows and it must move toward precomputed inboxes.
options: 把读模型封装在稳定接口后面
让所有客户端直接写 SQL join
把缓存格式当公开合同
options_en: Put the read model behind a stable interface.
Let every client issue SQL joins directly.
Treat the cache format as a public contract.
tradeoff: 内部可替换性 vs 公开接口约束
why: 可演化性来自低耦合和好抽象：内部从读时合并换成写时扇出，客户端仍调用同一个读接口。代价是接口要提前选好稳定语义。
why_en: Evolvability improves when internal architecture can change behind a stable interface.
whenOtherWins: 若系统很小且不会替换内部实现，直接查询内部表可以短期更快。
optionExplanations: 把读模型封装在稳定接口后面，内部从读时合并换成写时扇出时，客户端完全不用改代码。
让所有客户端直接写 SQL join，等于把内部实现细节焊死在每个调用方身上，以后想换实现就要改遍所有客户端。
把缓存格式当公开合同，会让缓存的内部结构变得不能随便调整，也锁死了未来的演进空间。
optionExplanations_en: Putting the read model behind a stable interface means switching the internals from read-time merge to write-time fan-out needs no client changes at all.
Letting every client issue SQL joins directly welds the internal implementation into every caller, so changing it later means touching every client.
Treating the cache format as a public contract locks its internal structure in place and removes the room to evolve it later.

q: 按依赖关系排列 Feed 架构演进判断。
q_en: Order the reasoning steps for feed architecture evolution.
scenario: 一个社交 Feed 从小规模增长到读多写少，并出现明星热点。
scenario_en: A social feed grows from small scale to read-heavy traffic with celebrity hot spots.
steps: 对明星账号例外处理，避免单条动态产生巨大写峰值。
先量化读写比例和粉丝分布，而不是只看总请求数。
普通用户采用写时扇出，换取便宜的首页读取。
为迁移保留稳定读接口，让内部模型可替换。
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Measure read/write and follower distribution] --> B[Fan out normal users on write]
B --> C[Handle celebrities at read time]
C --> D[Keep stable read API]
why: 先描述负载形状，再把主要成本移到更少发生的路径，最后给长尾热点和演进留出口。这样回答比背某个固定架构更像系统设计。
why_en: The reasoning starts with workload shape, then moves cost to the rarer path, then handles hot spots and future migration.

q: 哪些属于非功能需求？
q_en: Which are non-functional requirements?
scenario: 在评审一个数据产品时，团队同时讨论功能、可靠性、合规、可维护性和安全。
scenario_en: When reviewing a data product, the team discusses features, reliability, compliance, maintainability, and security.
options: 支持用户按关键词搜索
99.9% 可用性目标
满足数据保留合规
新增一个导出按钮
options_en: Support keyword search.
A 99.9% availability target.
Meet data-retention compliance.
Add an export button.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议：对外或合同化的服务质量承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Agreement is an external or contractual service-quality commitment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队承诺或追踪的性能/可用性目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Objective is a target for service performance or availability.

why: 功能需求说系统做什么，非功能需求约束它以什么质量和边界运行。可靠性、合规和可维护性会直接改变架构选择。
why_en: Functional requirements say what the system does; non-functional requirements constrain the quality and operating boundaries.
optionExplanations: 支持关键词搜索说的是系统「做什么」，属于功能需求，不是这里要挑的非功能需求。
99.9% 可用性目标约束系统运行的质量，不描述具体功能，是典型的非功能需求。
数据保留合规同样是运行边界和约束，不是某个具体功能，也算非功能需求。
新增一个导出按钮同样描述的是系统新增了什么功能，属于功能需求，不是这道题要挑的那类需求。
optionExplanations_en: Supporting keyword search describes what the system does, so it's a functional requirement, not the non-functional one being picked here.
A 99.9% availability target constrains the quality the system runs at rather than describing a feature, which makes it a classic non-functional requirement.
Data-retention compliance is also an operating boundary rather than a specific feature, so it counts as non-functional too.
Adding an export button likewise describes a new feature the system gains, a functional requirement, not the kind this question is picking out.

q: 数据模型为什么会影响系统设计？
q_en: Why do data models shape system design?
text: 应用通常把现实对象映射成 {{应用数据结构}}，再映射成 {{通用数据模型}}，最后由数据库映射成 {{字节存储格式}}。
text_en: Applications usually map real-world objects to {{application structures}}, then to a {{general data model}}, and finally the database maps that to {{bytes on storage}}.
why: 每一层模型都会放大某些操作、压低另一些操作。选错模型后，上层代码会被迫补洞。
why_en: Each model makes some operations natural and others awkward, so a poor fit pushes complexity into application code.

q: 选数据模型时先问什么？
q_en: What should you ask first when choosing a data model?
scenario: 新系统要记录用户资料、关注关系、推荐关系和组织实体；关系会持续增加。
scenario_en: A new system stores profiles, follows, recommendations, and organization entities; relationships will keep growing.
options: 哪个数据库宣传更流行
数据关系和查询会怎样变化
哪种文件扩展名最短
options_en: Which database is more hyped.
How relationships and queries are likely to change.
Which file extension is shortest.
tradeoff: 工具偏好 vs 数据形状
why: 数据模型内含使用假设：树状、表格、多对多图，适合的查询不同。先看关系形状，才能判断复杂度会落在哪一层。
why_en: A data model encodes assumptions about relationships and queries, so start with the shape of the data.
whenOtherWins: 若关系形状已经稳定且单一，团队经验和运维成本可以成为更强约束。
optionExplanations: 数据库流行度是采购口碑，不会告诉你关系会怎么长出来，选错了照样返工。
关系会持续增加时，先看数据之间的关系形状和查询会怎么变，才能判断复杂度落在哪一层，再挑模型。
文件扩展名长短跟数据关系毫无关系，纯属无关变量。
optionExplanations_en: Database popularity is just word of mouth about tooling; it says nothing about how your relationships will grow, so it can still steer you wrong.
When relationships keep growing, start from how the data relates and how queries will change — that tells you where the complexity will land.
File extension length has nothing to do with data relationships; it is an irrelevant variable.

q: 哪些是常见 NoSQL 采用动因？
q_en: Which are common reasons teams adopt NoSQL stores?
scenario: 团队评估是否在关系型数据库旁边引入非关系型存储。
scenario_en: A team is deciding whether to add a non-relational store alongside a relational database.
options: 需要更高写扩展或更大数据集
关系模型不支持所有专门查询
希望所有数据都自动强一致
想要更灵活的数据形状
options_en: Need higher write scaling or larger datasets.
The relational model does not fit every specialized query.
Want all data to become automatically strongly consistent.
Want a more flexible data shape.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库总称，强调不只使用 SQL/关系模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL, often expanded as Not Only SQL, is a broad label for non-relational data stores.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化查询语言：关系数据库常用的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the declarative query language commonly used with relational databases.

why: NoSQL 不是单一技术，而是一组对关系模型限制的不同回应。它通常换来专门能力，也会带来查询、事务或运维取舍。
why_en: NoSQL is not one technology; it is a family of tradeoffs around scale, query shape, and schema flexibility.
optionExplanations: 关系模型在写扩展和超大数据集上会先顶到瓶颈，这正是团队引入 NoSQL 常见的动因之一。
关系模型的固定表结构不适合所有专门查询形状，比如深层嵌套或图状路径查询，这也是常见动因。
NoSQL 并不会让所有数据自动变强一致，很多 NoSQL 系统反而放宽一致性去换可用性和扩展性。
想要更灵活、随时能变化的数据形状，而不是先固定 schema，也是团队考虑 NoSQL 的常见原因。
optionExplanations_en: The relational model tends to hit limits on write scaling and very large datasets first, which is a common reason teams reach for NoSQL.
A fixed table structure does not fit every specialized query shape, like deep nesting or graph-style paths, which is another common driver.
NoSQL does not make data automatically strongly consistent; many NoSQL systems actually relax consistency to gain availability and scale.
Wanting a flexible, evolving data shape instead of a schema fixed up front is also a common reason teams consider NoSQL.

q: 这更像哪种持久化策略？
q_en: Which persistence strategy fits this mix?
scenario: 交易数据需要事务和报表，消息正文要全文搜索，用户关系还要做路径查询。
scenario_en: Transactions need relational queries, message bodies need full-text search, and user relationships need path queries.
options: 只用一个工具解决所有访问模式
按访问模式组合多个数据系统
把所有查询都搬到客户端循环
options_en: Use one tool for every access pattern.
Combine several data systems by access pattern.
Move every query into client-side loops.
tradeoff: 单系统简单性 vs 多模型适配度

termDefinitions.meaning: 创建、读取、更新、删除：常见数据操作集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CRUD stands for Create, Read, Update, and Delete, the basic data operations.

why: polyglot persistence 承认不同访问模式可能需要不同存储。代价是跨系统同步、运维和一致性边界要由架构显式处理。
why_en: Polyglot persistence fits when different access patterns need different storage engines, but synchronization becomes part of the design.
whenOtherWins: 若一种数据库自然覆盖所有访问模式，单系统会减少同步和运维成本。
optionExplanations: 只用一个工具覆盖事务、全文搜索和路径查询，等于逼一个引擎同时擅长三件互相冲突的事，通常做不到。
事务走 OLTP 库、正文走倒排索引、关系走图存储，三种访问模式各自吃到对应的索引结构。
把所有查询搬到客户端循环，等于放弃了每个存储引擎本该做的索引和优化工作，效率会大幅下降。
optionExplanations_en: Using one tool for transactions, full-text search, and path queries forces a single engine to be great at three conflicting jobs at once, which rarely works.
Transactions go to the OLTP store, body text to an inverted index, relationships to a graph store — each pattern gets the index it needs.
Moving every query into client-side loops throws away the indexing and optimization each storage engine is built to do, and performance suffers badly.

q: ORM 主要缓解什么问题？
q_en: What problem does an ORM mainly reduce?
scenario: 应用代码里用户资料是一个对象，但关系库里职位、教育经历和联系方式被拆成多张表。
scenario_en: In application code a user profile is one object, but in the relational database jobs, education, and contacts live in separate tables.
options: 对象和表之间的样板转换
网络分区下的一致性
磁盘页的物理布局
options_en: Boilerplate translation between objects and tables.
Consistency during network partitions.
Physical layout of disk pages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象关系映射：在应用对象和关系表之间转换的框架或模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object-Relational Mapping converts between application objects and relational tables.

why: ORM 能少写映射代码，但不能消除对象图和关系表之间的语义差异。复杂关联、查询形状和事务边界仍要设计。
why_en: An ORM reduces mapping boilerplate, but it does not remove the semantic gap between object graphs and relational tables.
optionExplanations: 应用里资料是一整个对象，关系库里却拆成多张表，ORM 主要就是省掉这段来回转换的样板代码。
网络分区下的一致性是分布式系统层面的问题，跟对象和表之间的映射没关系，ORM 也解决不了它。
磁盘页物理布局是存储引擎内部的事，ORM 工作在应用和数据库接口之间，够不到这一层。
optionExplanations_en: The app sees one object while the relational tables split it across many rows, and an ORM mainly removes that repetitive translation code.
Consistency during network partitions is a distributed-systems problem that has nothing to do with mapping objects to tables, so an ORM can't fix it.
Physical disk-page layout is the storage engine's internal concern; an ORM works above the database interface and never reaches that layer.

q: 哪种模型更自然？
q_en: Which model is more natural?
scenario: 用户简历页面通常一次读取整份资料；职位和教育经历只属于该用户，嵌套层级不深。
scenario_en: A resume page usually reads the whole profile; jobs and education belong only to that user and nesting is shallow.
options: 把资料作为一个文档存储
把每个字段拆成独立服务
用图遍历每个标量字段
options_en: Store the profile as one document.
Split every field into a separate service.
Use graph traversal for every scalar field.
tradeoff: 读取局部性 vs 关联灵活性

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种常用的文本数据表示格式，适合嵌套对象和数组。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON is a common text format for nested objects and arrays.

why: 树状的一对多数据适合文档模型，因为读取整棵树只要一次定位。代价是跨文档引用和局部大更新会更麻烦。
why_en: A document model fits shallow one-to-many trees that are usually read as a whole.
whenOtherWins: 若职位、学校、推荐人都要独立演进，关系或图模型会比文档更合适。
optionExplanations: 整份资料一次性读取、嵌套层级又浅，正好是文档模型的强项——一次定位就能取回整棵树。
把每个字段拆成独立服务，会让本来一次读就够的简历页变成多次跨服务调用，白白增加延迟和复杂度。
用图遍历处理每个标量字段是杀鸡用牛刀，图擅长的是多跳关系，不是给单个字段做定位。
optionExplanations_en: Reading the whole profile at once with shallow nesting is exactly what a document model is good at — one lookup fetches the whole tree.
Splitting every field into its own service turns a single-read page into many cross-service calls, adding latency and complexity for no benefit.
Using graph traversal for a scalar field is overkill; graphs are for multi-hop relationships, not for locating a single field.

q: 地区字段应更偏向怎么存？
q_en: How should the region field be stored?
scenario: 资料里地区名要支持改名、多语言展示和按层级搜索；很多用户会引用同一地区。
scenario_en: Profile regions need renaming, localization, and hierarchy-aware search; many users refer to the same region.
options: 每份资料都直接复制并存一份显示文本
保存稳定 ID，显示名放在地区实体
把地区名存在代码常量里
options_en: Each profile just copies and stores its own display text.
Store a stable ID and keep display names in a region entity.
Store region names as code constants.
tradeoff: 复制读取便利 vs 更新一致性
why: 有共享含义且会改名的值适合规范化成实体 ID。这样更新和翻译发生在一处，但读取时需要解析引用。
why_en: Shared values that may change should be normalized behind stable IDs, trading read joins for update consistency.
whenOtherWins: 若值是真正自由文本且不会共享或改名，直接存文本更简单。
optionExplanations: 每份资料复制显示文本，地区一改名就要同步改遍所有引用它的资料，维护成本很高。
地区会改名、又被很多资料共享，保存稳定 ID、把显示名放在地区实体里，改名只需要改一处，读取时再解析引用。
把地区名硬编码进代码常量，改名要发版才能生效，也没法做多语言展示。
optionExplanations_en: Copying display text into every profile means a single rename requires updating every profile that referenced it, which is expensive to maintain.
Since the region can be renamed and is shared, storing a stable ID with the display name on a region entity means a rename touches one place, at the cost of resolving the reference on read.
Hard-coding region names as code constants means a rename needs a deploy and rules out per-language display names.

q: 复制字段带来的主要成本是什么？
q_en: What is the main cost of copied fields?
scenario: 推荐卡片里复制了作者姓名和头像；作者换头像后，旧推荐也要显示新头像。
scenario_en: Recommendation cards copy author names and photos; when an author changes photo, old recommendations should show the new one.
options: 每一次读取都必然变得更慢
所有副本需要更新或接受不一致
数据库不能再建立索引
options_en: Every single read necessarily becomes slower.
All copies must be updated or tolerate inconsistency.
The database can no longer create indexes.
tradeoff: 读路径便利 vs 写入传播成本
why: 反规范化用写入和修复成本换读取便利。只要复制的是会变化的信息，就要有传播、重算或接受旧值的策略。
why_en: Denormalization trades read convenience for update propagation or stale copies when the duplicated value changes.
optionExplanations: 读变慢不是复制字段的直接后果，复制本身其实是为了让读更快，代价出现在写入侧。
作者换头像后，所有复制了头像的旧推荐卡片要么被更新，要么就一直显示旧值，这正是反规范化的核心成本。
复制字段和能不能建索引没有关系，索引仍然可以正常建在这些复制出来的字段上。
optionExplanations_en: Slower reads are not the direct cost of duplicating a field; duplication exists precisely to make reads faster, and the cost lands on the write side instead.
Once the author changes avatars, every old recommendation card that copied the avatar must either be updated or keep showing a stale value — that's the real cost of denormalization.
Duplicating a field has nothing to do with whether it can be indexed; indexes still work fine on the copied fields.

q: 文档模型会遇到什么压力？
q_en: What pressure will the document model face?
scenario: 简历系统后来把公司、学校、推荐人都做成独立实体，并要展示它们的最新信息。
scenario_en: A resume system later turns companies, schools, and recommenders into separate entities and must show their latest information.
options: 多对多引用要在应用层 join
一对多嵌套在文档里会完全消失
所有字段都必须退化成字符串
options_en: Many-to-many references force joins in application code.
One-to-many nesting disappears entirely in documents.
Every field has to degrade into a string.
tradeoff: 树状局部性 vs 多对多关联
why: 文档模型擅长拥有关系，不擅长大量共享实体互相引用。关系变多后，复杂度会从数据库 join 移到应用代码或同步流程。
why_en: Documents fit ownership trees, but many shared entities push joins or duplication into the application.
whenOtherWins: 若资料永远只按整文档读取且少有共享实体，文档模型仍然很顺。
optionExplanations: 公司、学校、推荐人这些被大量简历共享的实体，数据库端没有 join，只能靠应用代码自己拼，或者干脆复制一份。
一对多的嵌套关系不会因为加了共享实体就消失，两种关系形状是并存的，只是多对多部分需要额外处理。
字段该是数字还是字符串，跟实体之间是不是多对多毫无关系，这个说法没有依据。
optionExplanations_en: Entities like company, school, and referrer that many resumes share have no server-side join, so the app has to stitch them together itself, or duplicate the data.
One-to-many nesting doesn't disappear just because shared entities were added; the two relationship shapes coexist, and only the many-to-many part needs extra handling.
Whether a field is a number or a string has nothing to do with entities being many-to-many; this claim has no basis.

q: 这种 access path 暴露会带来什么后果？
q_en: What consequence comes from exposing access paths?
scenario: 一个旧式数据模型要求应用沿预定义指针路径找记录；新增查询路径要改很多手写遍历代码。
scenario_en: An old data model requires applications to follow predefined pointer paths; a new query path forces many traversal-code changes.
options: 查询代码和物理路径紧耦合
查询优化器获得更多自由
数据模型更容易演进
options_en: Query code becomes tightly coupled to physical paths.
The optimizer gains more freedom.
The data model becomes easier to evolve.
tradeoff: 手工路径效率 vs 查询演进灵活性
why: 手写访问路径把“怎么找”写进应用，一改关系形状就要改代码。关系模型的胜利之一就是把这部分交给优化器。
why_en: Manual access paths bake how-to-find-it logic into the app, making model evolution painful.
optionExplanations: 沿预定义指针路径找记录，等于把“怎么找”硬编码进应用代码，关系形状一变，所有手写遍历都要跟着改。
这种模型恰恰相反——固定访问路径限制了优化器的空间，它没有自由去改用别的路径。
访问路径写死在应用里，新增查询要改很多遍历代码，模型演进反而更难，不是更容易。
optionExplanations_en: Following predefined pointer paths bakes the how-to-find-it logic straight into the application, so any change to the relationship shape forces a rewrite of the hand-written traversal.
It's the opposite here — a fixed access path limits the optimizer's freedom rather than giving it more room to choose a different path.
With access paths hard-coded into the app, adding a new query means rewriting a lot of traversal code, so evolving the model gets harder, not easier.

q: 关系模型哪个特性最有帮助？
q_en: Which relational feature helps most?
scenario: 产品新增筛选维度；你希望加索引后旧查询自动受益，而不是改每个调用方。
scenario_en: A product adds a new filter dimension; after adding an index, old queries should benefit without changing every caller.
options: 应用手写遍历顺序
查询优化器选择访问路径
每条记录只能有一个父节点
options_en: The app hand-writes traversal order.
The query optimizer chooses access paths.
Each record can have only one parent.
tradeoff: 应用控制路径 vs 优化器自由

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接：按关联条件把多个表或集合的记录组合起来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines records from multiple tables or collections using a relationship condition.

why: 声明式查询说想要什么，优化器决定用哪个索引和 join 顺序。这样加索引是数据库内部优化，而不是应用协议变化。
why_en: Declarative queries let the optimizer change access paths without changing application queries.
whenOtherWins: 若查询路径极少且要手工压榨硬件，定制访问路径可能短期更快。
optionExplanations: 手写遍历顺序把“怎么找”焊死在应用代码里，新增索引不会自动被旧查询用上。
加索引后想让旧查询自动受益，靠的正是查询优化器自己挑访问路径，这是声明式查询的核心好处。
每条记录只能有一个父节点是层级模型的限制，跟“加索引后旧查询自动受益”这件事没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Hand-writing the traversal order welds how-to-find-it into the app, so a new index does not automatically help existing queries.
Letting existing queries benefit automatically from a new index is exactly what the query optimizer choosing access paths gives you.
Each record having only one parent is a hierarchical-model constraint; it has nothing to do with old queries benefiting from a new index.

q: 文档和关系模型最关键的差别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between document and relational models here?
scenario: 一个系统既有用户资料树，也有公司、学校、推荐关系等共享实体。
scenario_en: A system has profile-shaped trees plus shared entities such as companies, schools, and recommendations.
options: 文档偏局部树，关系偏共享引用
关系模型完全不能存储嵌套数据
文档模型能自动解决多对多关系
options_en: Documents favor local trees; relational favors shared references.
Relational models cannot store nested data at all.
Document models solve many-to-many automatically.
tradeoff: 局部读取 vs 共享关系

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种常用的文本数据表示格式，适合嵌套对象和数组。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON is a common text format for nested objects and arrays.

why: 文档模型把一份对象读得顺，关系模型把共享实体和多对多关系处理得顺。真实系统常需要在这两种压力之间折中。
why_en: Documents are convenient for local object trees, while relational models are stronger for shared references and joins.
optionExplanations: 文档模型把一份对象的局部树读得很顺，关系模型把共享实体和 join 处理得更好，这正是两者的分野。
关系模型完全能存嵌套数据，只是要拆成多张表用外键表示，这个说法不成立。
文档模型不会自动解决多对多，遇到共享实体照样要引用或反规范化，跟关系模型一样要处理。
optionExplanations_en: Documents read a local object tree smoothly, while relational models handle shared entities and joins better — that's exactly the dividing line.
Relational models can absolutely store nested data, just split across tables with foreign keys, so this claim doesn't hold.
Document models do not auto-solve many-to-many; shared entities still need references or denormalization, same as in relational models.

q: schema-on-read 和 schema-on-write 怎么选？
q_en: How should you choose schema-on-read versus schema-on-write?
scenario: 事件数据来自多个外部合作方，字段经常变化；核心订单表则必须每行结构一致。
scenario_en: Event data comes from multiple partners and changes often; the core orders table must have a consistent structure.
options: 外部事件 schema-on-read，核心订单 schema-on-write
所有数据都统一用 schema-on-read，把所有的错误都统一留到读取时
所有数据都用 schema-on-write，旧记录必须先全量迁移
options_en: Schema-on-read for external events, schema-on-write for core orders.
Use schema-on-read for everything, deferring every error to read time.
Make everything schema-on-write and migrate every old record first.
tradeoff: 灵活接入 vs 结构保障
why: schema-on-read 把解释推迟到读取，适合异构和外部变化；schema-on-write 在写入时强制结构，适合核心一致数据。
why_en: Schema-on-read fits heterogeneous changing data, while schema-on-write fits core records that need enforced structure.
optionExplanations: 外部事件字段常变、来源又多，适合读时再解释；核心订单必须每行结构一致，适合写入时就强制校验，两边分开处理正合适。
所有数据都无 schema、错误留到读时，核心订单这种必须行行一致的数据反而会被这种做法放进去脏数据。
要求全量迁移完才能读旧记录，等于把渐进式迁移变成一次高风险的大停机，没必要这么极端。
optionExplanations_en: External event fields change often and come from many sources, so interpreting them at read time fits; core orders need every row consistent, so enforcing structure at write time fits — splitting the two is the right call.
Making everything schemaless and deferring errors to read time would let bad data slip into core order records that must be consistent row by row.
Requiring a full migration before any old record can be read turns a gradual migration into one risky long outage, which is unnecessarily extreme.

q: 更稳的迁移方式是什么？
q_en: What is a safer migration approach?
scenario: 用户表要把 full_name 拆成 first_name；表很大，不能长时间重写每一行。
scenario_en: A users table must split full_name into first_name; the table is huge and cannot be rewritten for a long time.
options: 一次性 UPDATE 全表并停机等待
加新字段，读路径兼容旧记录，后台逐步回填
删除旧字段后让错误暴露
options_en: Run one full-table UPDATE and wait in downtime.
Add the new field, keep reads compatible with old records, and backfill gradually.
Delete the old field and let errors surface.
tradeoff: 一次性简洁 vs 在线兼容
why: 大表格式变化常用兼容读加渐进回填，避免把迁移变成一个长事务和长停机。代价是代码要在一段时间内支持两种形状。
why_en: For large tables, compatible reads plus gradual backfill avoid a long blocking rewrite.
whenOtherWins: 若表很小或有明确维护窗，一次性迁移更简单。
optionExplanations: 一次性 UPDATE 全表要锁住整张大表、停机等待，行数一多耗时会长到业务无法接受。
加新字段、读路径兼容旧记录、后台逐步回填，能避免长事务和长停机，代价是代码要在过渡期同时支持新旧两种形状。
直接删掉旧字段让错误暴露，等于把迁移风险转嫁给线上用户，出错才发现，代价太高。
optionExplanations_en: Running one full-table UPDATE locks the whole large table and forces downtime that grows unacceptably long as row count increases.
Adding the new field, keeping reads compatible with old records, and backfilling gradually avoids a long transaction or outage, at the cost of the code supporting both shapes for a while.
Deleting the old field and letting errors surface pushes the migration risk onto live users, who find out only when something breaks.

q: 哪种 schema 策略更自然？
q_en: Which schema strategy is more natural?
scenario: 日志集合里混有几十种外部设备上报的记录；设备厂商会随时加字段。
scenario_en: A log collection mixes dozens of external device record shapes; vendors may add fields at any time.
options: 强制每种设备先建独立关系表再写入
使用 schema-on-read 并在消费端解释
拒绝所有未知字段，要求厂商先同步 schema
options_en: Force each device type into its own relational table before writing.
Use schema-on-read and interpret records in consumers.
Reject unknown fields and require vendors to sync the schema first.
tradeoff: 接入灵活性 vs 读取端复杂度
why: 外部异构数据很难让写入端先满足统一结构。schema-on-read 接受变化，但消费代码要处理缺字段和版本差异。
why_en: Schema-on-read is natural for externally shaped, heterogeneous records, while consumers must handle missing fields and versions.
whenOtherWins: 若记录结构统一且写错代价高，schema-on-write 更能保护数据质量。
optionExplanations: 要求每种设备先建独立关系表才能写入，等于要求外部厂商先配合你的 schema，现实里很难做到。
新型号今天多报一个字段、明天少报一个，写入端不用改表；解析代码给缺失字段兜个默认值就行。
拒绝所有未知字段、要求厂商先同步 schema，实际上会挡住大量正常上报的数据，不现实。
optionExplanations_en: Requiring every device type to have its own relational table before it can write means external vendors must conform to your schema first, which rarely happens in practice.
A new device model adds a field today and drops one tomorrow; nothing is migrated, the parser just defaults whatever is missing.
Rejecting every unknown field and requiring vendors to sync the schema first would block a large share of normal incoming reports.

q: 文档局部性带来的收益是什么？
q_en: What benefit does document locality provide?
scenario: 页面渲染每次都要读取用户资料的大部分字段；这些字段通常一起更新很少。
scenario_en: Rendering a page reads most profile fields every time; these fields are rarely updated together.
options: 一次定位能取回相关字段
数据库自动避免所有写放大
可以跳过持久化
options_en: One lookup can fetch related fields together.
The database automatically avoids all write amplification.
Persistence can be skipped.
tradeoff: 整块读取效率 vs 局部更新成本
why: 相关字段连续存储时，整页读取少做多表查找和额外 seek。收益只在经常读大块文档时明显。
why_en: Document locality helps when the workload frequently reads most of the document together.
whenOtherWins: 若只读少数字段或频繁增长子数组，拆表或引用会更合适。
optionExplanations: 相关字段连续存储在一起，渲染页面时一次定位就能取回大部分字段，少走多表查找。
局部性不会自动消除写放大，大文档局部更新反而可能触发整文档重写，两者是两回事。
局部性说的是读取效率，不代表可以跳过持久化，数据照样要落盘。
optionExplanations_en: With related fields stored together, one lookup during page render can fetch most fields at once, avoiding extra multi-table lookups.
Locality does not eliminate write amplification; a small update to a large document can still trigger a full document rewrite — those are separate issues.
Locality is about read efficiency; it does not mean persistence can be skipped, the data still has to be written to disk.

q: 这种建模的写入风险是什么？
q_en: What write risk does this model create?
scenario: 一个文档已经很大；每次给数组追加元素都会让编码大小变化。
scenario_en: A document is already large; every append to an array changes the encoded size.
options: 可能重写整个文档并放大写成本
join 会自动更快
读取时不需要任何 I/O
options_en: It may rewrite the whole document and amplify write cost.
Joins automatically become faster.
Reads require no I/O.
tradeoff: 读取局部性 vs 写入放大
why: 文档局部性不是免费午餐。大文档局部更新可能变成整文档重写，所以文档要小，增长型子集合要谨慎嵌套。
why_en: Document locality is not free; large growing documents can turn small logical updates into large rewrites.
optionExplanations: 文档已经很大时，给数组追加一个元素也可能触发整份文档重新编码写入，写入成本被放大了。
局部更新变成整文档重写，跟 join 变快没有任何关系，这个说法答非所问。
写入需要把变化后的内容落盘，不可能跳过 I/O，这个说法直接不成立。
optionExplanations_en: When a document is already large, appending one array element can still force the whole document to be re-encoded and rewritten, amplifying write cost.
A local update turning into a full rewrite has nothing to do with joins getting faster; this answer doesn't address the question.
A write still has to persist the changed content to disk, so skipping I/O entirely is simply not true.

q: 数据库能力演进的合理方向是什么？
q_en: What database capability direction fits this need?
scenario: 应用既需要 JSON 风格的嵌套字段，也需要 SQL join 和索引查询。
scenario_en: An application needs JSON-style nested fields plus SQL joins and indexed queries.
options: 关系和文档能力混合
只保留最早的层级模型
禁止嵌套数据进入数据库
options_en: A hybrid of relational and document capabilities.
Keep only the earliest hierarchical model.
Ban nested data from the database.
tradeoff: 模型纯粹性 vs 组合能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种常用的文本数据表示格式，适合嵌套对象和数组。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JSON is a common text format for nested objects and arrays.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化查询语言：关系数据库常用的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the declarative query language commonly used with relational databases.

why: 关系和文档模型互补，现代系统常把 JSON 支持、索引和 join 放在同一产品里。选型时看组合能力，而不是口号阵营。
why_en: Relational and document features complement each other, so hybrid support can fit mixed workloads better than a slogan-driven choice.
whenOtherWins: 若访问模式非常单一，专用纯文档库或纯关系库可能更简单。
optionExplanations: 既要 JSON 风格嵌套字段，又要 SQL join 和索引，混合关系与文档能力正好覆盖两种压力，不用二选一。
只保留最早的层级模型退回到了指针式访问路径，连关系模型带来的优化器自由都丢了，是倒退不是方向。
禁止嵌套数据进数据库，等于放弃了 JSON 风格字段这个明确需求，不符合场景。
optionExplanations_en: Needing both JSON-style nested fields and SQL joins with indexes is exactly what a relational-document hybrid covers, without forcing a binary choice.
Keeping only the earliest hierarchical model reverts to pointer-style access paths and loses even the optimizer freedom relational models gained — that's a step backward, not a direction.
Banning nested data from the database throws away the explicit need for JSON-style fields, so it doesn't fit the scenario.

q: 为什么声明式查询合适？
q_en: Why is a declarative query suitable?
scenario: 数据库查询只需要“找出满足条件的订单并按月份聚合”，不想固定扫描顺序和 join 顺序。
scenario_en: A database query only needs orders matching conditions aggregated by month; it should not hard-code scan and join order.
options: 它描述结果形状，让优化器决定执行方式
它要求程序员手写出每一步循环过程
它禁止数据库使用索引
options_en: It describes the result shape and lets the optimizer choose execution.
It forces the programmer to hand-write every loop step.
It prevents the database from using indexes.
tradeoff: 表达结果 vs 固定算法

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化查询语言：关系数据库常用的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the declarative query language commonly used with relational databases.

why: 声明式语言说要什么，不说怎么做。数据库因此可以换索引、换 join 算法或并行执行，而不改查询语义。
why_en: Declarative queries state the desired result, giving the database room to optimize execution without changing semantics.
whenOtherWins: 若必须控制每一步副作用和顺序，命令式 API 才更合适。
optionExplanations: 只描述“满足条件的订单按月份聚合”这个结果形状，具体怎么扫描、怎么 join 交给优化器决定，这正是声明式的意义。
要求程序员写每一步循环，就是命令式而不是声明式，跟这里想要的“不固定扫描顺序”正好相反。
声明式查询不会禁止使用索引，恰恰相反，它给了优化器选择索引的自由。
optionExplanations_en: Describing only the result shape — matching orders aggregated by month — and letting the optimizer decide the scan and join order is exactly what declarative means.
Requiring the programmer to write every loop step is imperative, not declarative, which is the opposite of not fixing the scan order here.
A declarative query doesn't ban indexes — quite the opposite, it gives the optimizer freedom to pick which index to use.

q: 声明式查询为什么更安全？
q_en: Why is a declarative query safer here?
scenario: 存储引擎想在后台移动记录、回收空间；查询没有声明排序要求。
scenario_en: The storage engine wants to move records in the background to reclaim space; the query did not request any ordering.
options: 未声明顺序时，数据库可改变物理顺序
应用循环会自动忽略顺序
移动记录物理位置一定会破坏 SQL 结果
options_en: If no order is declared, the database may change physical order.
Application loops automatically ignore order.
Moving a record physically will always break the SQL result.
tradeoff: 物理布局自由 vs 应用顺序依赖
why: 声明式查询只承诺声明过的结果属性，未要求顺序就不绑定物理布局。命令式遍历更容易把偶然顺序变成隐藏依赖。
why_en: Declarative queries avoid depending on physical order unless the query explicitly asks for an order.
optionExplanations: 查询没有声明排序要求时，数据库可以在后台随意移动记录、回收空间，因为它只承诺声明过的结果属性。
应用循环不会自动忽略顺序，命令式遍历反而更容易把偶然出现的顺序当成隐藏依赖。
移动记录不会破坏 SQL 语义，只要查询没有依赖未声明的物理顺序，结果照样正确。
optionExplanations_en: When no order is declared, the database is free to move records around and reclaim space in the background, because it only promises the properties actually declared.
Application loops do not automatically ignore order — imperative traversal is more likely to accidentally depend on whatever order happens to show up.
Moving records does not break SQL semantics as long as the query never relied on an undeclared physical order.

q: 为什么声明式形式更利于并行？
q_en: Why does the declarative form help parallelism?
scenario: 查询只描述过滤、分组和聚合结果；机器有多核和多节点可用。
scenario_en: A query describes filters, grouping, and aggregation; the system has many cores and nodes available.
options: 系统可选择并行执行计划
程序员写的循环天然可并行
并行只取决于表名
options_en: The system can choose a parallel execution plan.
Programmer-written loops are naturally parallel.
Parallelism depends only on table names.
tradeoff: 执行自由度 vs 顺序控制
why: 声明式查询没有固定每一步执行顺序，优化器可以把扫描、过滤和聚合拆给多个执行单元。命令式代码常把顺序依赖写死。
why_en: Because declarative queries do not fix every step, the engine has room to choose parallel execution plans.
optionExplanations: 声明式查询没有固定每一步的执行顺序，系统可以把扫描、过滤、聚合拆给多核或多节点并行跑。
程序员手写的循环通常有明确的先后依赖，天然就是串行的，不会自动变成并行。
能不能并行取决于查询有没有把执行步骤写死，跟表名本身没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Declarative queries don't fix the order of each step, so the engine can split scanning, filtering, and aggregation across multiple cores or nodes.
Hand-written loops usually have explicit step-by-step dependencies, which makes them inherently sequential, not automatically parallel.
Whether something can run in parallel depends on whether execution steps are hard-coded, not on what the table happens to be named.

q: 这个例子对应数据库里的什么思想？
q_en: What database idea does this example mirror?
scenario: 浏览器样式规则只写“选中项的标题变蓝”，而不是手写遍历 DOM 并设置每个节点。
scenario_en: A browser style rule says selected titles are blue instead of hand-walking the DOM and setting each node.
options: 声明式规则让运行时负责匹配和优化
所有 UI 都必须存进关系库
命令式遍历更容易自动修复
options_en: Declarative rules let the runtime match and optimize.
All UI must be stored in a relational database.
Imperative traversal is easier to auto-repair.
tradeoff: 声明模式 vs 手写遍历

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档对象模型：浏览器把页面表示成可操作的节点树。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Document Object Model represents a web page as a manipulable tree of nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化查询语言：关系数据库常用的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the declarative query language commonly used with relational databases.

why: CSS 像 SQL 一样描述匹配模式，浏览器或数据库负责怎么找和何时更新。好处是实现能优化，规则语义不变。
why_en: CSS mirrors SQL in that it declares a pattern while the runtime decides how to match and optimize it.
whenOtherWins: 若页面逻辑必须执行复杂副作用，命令式 DOM 代码可能不可避免。
optionExplanations: CSS 规则只写“选中项标题变蓝”，具体怎么匹配 DOM、什么时候重绘由浏览器决定，这跟数据库声明式查询是同一个思想。
这个例子讲的是声明式规则，不是在说所有 UI 数据都必须存进关系库，两者没关系。
命令式遍历需要手写每一步，出错时更难定位和修复，跟“更容易自动修复”正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: CSS rules only state the outcome — the selected item's title turns blue — while the browser decides how to match the DOM and when to repaint, the same idea as a declarative database query.
This example is about declarative rules, not about requiring all UI data to live in a relational database — the two are unrelated.
Imperative traversal requires hand-writing every step, which makes it harder, not easier, to locate and fix problems automatically.

q: 为什么要求函数尽量纯？
q_en: Why should the functions be pure?
scenario: 一个分布式查询框架会在多台机器上重试 map 和 reduce 函数。
scenario_en: A distributed query framework may retry map and reduce functions on many machines.
options: 重试和乱序执行不会产生外部副作用
纯函数能访问任意外部数据库
纯函数一定比 SQL 更声明式
options_en: Retries and out-of-order execution will not create external side effects.
Pure functions can access any external database.
Pure functions are always more declarative than SQL.
tradeoff: 分布式重试安全 vs 函数表达自由

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种分布式批处理模型，把输入映射成键值对再按键归约。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MapReduce is a distributed batch model that maps inputs to key-value pairs and reduces by key.

why: MapReduce 会并行、重试、换机器执行代码；纯函数只依赖输入，失败重跑才安全。代价是查询要拆成受限的 map/reduce 逻辑。
why_en: MapReduce needs pure functions so retries and distributed execution do not cause accidental side effects.
optionExplanations: map 和 reduce 函数只依赖输入、不产生外部副作用，框架才能放心地在任意机器上重试或乱序重跑它们。
纯函数恰恰不能随意访问外部数据库，一旦依赖外部状态，重试就可能产生不一致的副作用。
纯不纯是函数的性质，跟声明式与否是两个维度，不能说纯函数一定比 SQL 更声明式。
optionExplanations_en: Because map and reduce depend only on their input and produce no external side effects, the framework can safely retry or reorder them on any machine.
Pure functions specifically must not freely touch external databases — depending on external state is exactly what makes retries risk inconsistent side effects.
Purity and declarativeness are different dimensions, so a pure function isn't automatically more declarative than SQL.

q: 比 MapReduce 更友好的接口是什么？
q_en: What interface is friendlier than MapReduce here?
scenario: 文档库要做过滤、分组、求和；团队不想维护两段互相配合的 JavaScript 函数。
scenario_en: A document database must filter, group, and sum; the team does not want to maintain two coordinated JavaScript functions.
options: 声明式 aggregation pipeline
每条记录单独发 HTTP 请求
把整段报表聚合逻辑都写进客户端 for 循环里
options_en: A declarative aggregation pipeline.
Send one HTTP request per record.
Push the whole report aggregation into a client-side for loop.
tradeoff: 查询可读性 vs 自定义代码自由

termDefinitions.meaning: 超文本传输协议：Web 客户端和服务端常用的请求响应协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the request-response protocol commonly used between web clients and servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种分布式批处理模型，把输入映射成键值对再按键归约。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MapReduce is a distributed batch model that maps inputs to key-value pairs and reduces by key.

why: 聚合管道把常见过滤和分组表达成数据操作步骤，优化空间也更大。MapReduce 仍适合更自定义的批处理逻辑。
why_en: An aggregation pipeline is easier for common filter-group-sum queries and leaves more room for optimization than hand-written MapReduce functions.
whenOtherWins: 若查询逻辑高度自定义且难用管道表达，MapReduce 或用户函数可能更合适。
optionExplanations: 聚合管道把过滤、分组、求和表达成一串声明式的数据操作步骤，省掉了手写两段互相配合的 JavaScript 函数。
每条记录单独发一次 HTTP 请求，网络开销会随记录数线性增长，比批量聚合慢得多，也更复杂。
把报表逻辑搬进客户端 for 循环，等于放弃了数据库本该做的过滤和聚合优化，效率明显更差。
optionExplanations_en: An aggregation pipeline expresses filter, group, and sum as a chain of declarative steps, replacing the need to hand-write two coordinating JavaScript functions.
Sending one HTTP request per record makes network overhead grow linearly with record count, far slower and more complex than batched aggregation.
Moving reporting logic into a client-side for loop throws away the filtering and aggregation optimizations the database is built to do.

q: 哪类数据模型更自然？
q_en: Which data model is more natural?
scenario: 应用主要问题是人、地点、事件、组织之间不断新增关系，并且查询常要沿关系走多跳。
scenario_en: An application is mostly about people, places, events, and organizations with evolving relationships and multi-hop traversal queries.
options: 图模型
只含一个根的文档树
固定宽度 CSV 文件
options_en: A graph model.
A single-root document tree.
A fixed-width CSV file.
tradeoff: 关系遍历能力 vs 树状局部性
why: 多对多关系很多且路径查询常见时，图模型把边作为一等对象。文档树会把这些关系变成引用和应用层遍历。
why_en: A graph model fits dense many-to-many relationships and multi-hop traversal because edges are first-class data.
whenOtherWins: 若数据主要是单个对象树且整块读取，文档模型更简单。
optionExplanations: 人、地点、事件、组织之间关系持续新增、查询又常沿关系走多跳，图模型把边当一等对象，正好贴合这种压力。
只含一个根的文档树擅长局部对象，遇到大量互相引用的实体和多跳查询会很吃力，需要靠应用层拼接。
固定宽度 CSV 完全没有表达关系的能力，连基本的多对多都存不了，跟这里的需求完全不搭。
