optionExplanations_en: With relationships among people, places, events, and organizations constantly growing and queries often hopping multiple edges, a graph model fits because it treats edges as first-class data.
A single-root document tree is good for local objects, but it struggles once many shared entities reference each other and queries need multiple hops.
A fixed-width CSV file has no way to express relationships at all, not even basic many-to-many links, so it doesn't fit this need.

q: 图模型的两个基本对象是什么？
q_en: What are the two basic objects in a graph model?
text: 图由 {{vertices/nodes}} 和 {{edges/relationships}} 组成；前者表示实体，后者表示实体之间的连接。
text_en: A graph consists of {{vertices/nodes}} and {{edges/relationships}}; vertices represent entities, and edges represent connections.
why: 把边显式建模后，关系本身可以带标签和属性，查询也能围绕路径展开。
why_en: Once edges are explicit, relationships can carry labels and properties, and queries can be expressed as paths.

q: property graph 通常把哪些内容作为一等结构？
q_en: What are first-class structures in a property graph?
scenario: 团队准备用 property graph 存人、城市、婚姻、出生地和居住地。
scenario_en: A team wants to store people, cities, marriages, birthplaces, and residences in a property graph.
options: vertex 的属性
edge 的起点和终点
edge 的标签和属性
唯一的全局根节点
options_en: Properties on vertices.
The start and end vertices of an edge.
Labels and properties on edges.
One global root node.
why: property graph 同时描述实体和关系；边不只是外键，还能表达关系类型和关系属性。它不要求所有数据挂在同一个根下面。
why_en: A property graph models both entities and relationships directly; edges can have labels and properties.
optionExplanations: vertex 上挂的属性，比如姓名、出生日期，在图模型里是一等的实体数据。
每条 edge 都明确记录它连接的起点和终点 vertex，这是图能被遍历的基础。
edge 不只是一条连线，还能带标签（比如 marriedTo）和自己的属性（比如结婚日期），这也是一等结构。
任何一个 vertex 都能当查询起点，不必像 XML 那样从唯一的根往下钻。
optionExplanations_en: Properties attached to a vertex, like a person's name or birth date, are first-class entity data in a property graph.
Every edge explicitly records the start and end vertices it connects, which is what makes the graph traversable at all.
An edge is more than a line — it can carry a label (like marriedTo) and its own properties (like a marriage date), also first-class structure.
Any vertex can be a query entry point; you never have to drill down from one root the way XML forces you to.

q: 边表上最该有什么索引？
q_en: Which indexes matter most on the edge table?
scenario: 查询经常从某个人出发找所有关系，也会从某个城市反查出生或居住的人。
scenario_en: Queries often start from a person and follow relationships, and also start from a city to find people born or living there.
options: 只按 edge_id 排序，靠边的编号去定位相连的两个端点顶点
按 tail_vertex 和 head_vertex 各建索引
只给 label 建全文索引，再按关系名过滤两端
options_en: Sort only by edge_id and locate the two connected endpoint vertices via edge numbers.
Index tail_vertex and head_vertex separately.
Index only label with full text, then filter both ends by relationship name.
tradeoff: 边身份查询 vs 邻接遍历
why: 图遍历需要快速找到出边和入边。只按边 ID 查不到某个点相连的边，遍历会退化成扫描。
why_en: Graph traversal needs fast lookup of outgoing and incoming edges, so indexes on both endpoints matter.
whenOtherWins: 若只按 edge_id 审计单条边，端点索引就不是主路径。
optionExplanations: 只按 edge_id 排序，给定一个点想找它相连的边，还是得扫描全部边表，起不到索引的作用。
查询既要从某个人找所有关系，也要从某个城市反查相关的人，分别给 tail_vertex 和 head_vertex 建索引才能两个方向都快速定位。
只给 label 建全文索引，能按关系名过滤，但定位不到某个具体点相连的边，解决不了遍历的核心需求。
optionExplanations_en: Sorting only by edge_id means finding the edges touching a given vertex still requires scanning the whole edge table — the index doesn't help.
Since queries go both from a person outward and from a city back to people, indexing tail_vertex and head_vertex separately lets both directions resolve quickly.
A full-text index on label only lets you filter by relationship name; it can't locate the edges attached to a specific vertex, which is the real traversal need.

q: 图模型为什么利于演进？
q_en: Why does a graph model help evolution?
scenario: 社交产品后来要给用户加食物过敏、活动签到、地点层级等新关系。
scenario_en: A social product later adds food allergies, event check-ins, and location hierarchies as new relationships.
options: 能加新 vertex/edge 类型而不重写旧关系
所有关系查询都会自动变成 O(1)
它会彻底地禁止不同的实体类型共存于同一张图里面
options_en: New vertex and edge types can be added without rewriting old relationships.
Every relationship query automatically becomes O(1).
It flatly forbids different entity types from coexisting in one graph.
tradeoff: 模型灵活性 vs 查询治理成本
why: 图模型对异构关系很宽容，新事实可以作为新边或新点加入。代价是查询治理和索引策略要跟着关系增长演进。
why_en: Graphs evolve well because new facts can often be added as new vertices or edges without remapping the whole model.
optionExplanations: 食物过敏、活动签到这些新关系，可以直接作为新的 vertex 或 edge 类型加进图里，不用重写已有的关系数据。
图模型不会让所有查询自动变成 O(1)，多跳遍历的成本仍然取决于路径长度和索引情况。
图模型反而鼓励不同实体类型共存，人、地点、活动可以在同一张图里用不同标签区分，这个说法说反了。
optionExplanations_en: New relationships like food allergies or event check-ins can be added directly as new vertex or edge types without rewriting the existing relationship data.
A graph model does not make every query automatically O(1); multi-hop traversal cost still depends on path length and available indexes.
A graph model actually encourages different entity types to coexist, distinguished by labels — this option has it backwards.

q: Cypher 的优势是什么？
q_en: What is Cypher good at here?
scenario: 要找“出生在美国某地、现在住在欧洲某地”的人；路径中可能隔着州、国家、洲等多层地点。
scenario_en: Find people born somewhere within the US and now living somewhere within Europe; paths may pass through city, state, country, and continent levels.
options: 用路径模式声明要匹配的关系
要求应用手写每一层循环
只能查询固定两跳路径
options_en: Declare the relationship pattern to match.
Require the app to hand-code every traversal loop.
Only query fixed two-hop paths.
tradeoff: 路径声明 vs 手写遍历

termDefinitions.meaning: Neo4j 推广的声明式属性图查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cypher is a declarative property-graph query language popularized by Neo4j.

why: Cypher 把点和边的模式写成接近图形的语法，优化器再决定从哪个点开始找。它适合表达路径，不是强迫你写遍历过程。
why_en: Cypher is useful because it declares graph patterns while the engine chooses how to execute the traversal.
whenOtherWins: 若只是固定表连接且没有路径语义，SQL join 会更自然。
optionExplanations: 你只写 (p)-[:BORN_IN]->()-[:WITHIN*0..]->(us) 这种模式，跳几层由 *0.. 决定。
要求应用手写每一层循环，正是 Cypher 想避免的事，跟它的声明式优势正相反。
Cypher 并不限制只能查两跳，它可以用可变长度路径表达任意多跳的关系。
optionExplanations_en: You only write the pattern (p)-[:BORN_IN]->()-[:WITHIN*0..]->(us), and *0.. decides how many hops to take.
Requiring the app to hand-code every traversal loop is exactly what Cypher avoids, the opposite of its declarative advantage.
Cypher isn't limited to two-hop paths at all — it can express arbitrarily many hops with variable-length path syntax.

q: 查询语言需要支持什么？
q_en: What should the query language support?
scenario: 地点层级深度不固定：居住地可能直接是国家，也可能是城市、州、省再到国家。
scenario_en: Location hierarchy depth is not fixed: a residence may point to a country directly or pass through city, state, and province nodes.
options: 固定数量 join
可变长度路径遍历
只能按字符串前缀匹配
options_en: A fixed number of joins.
Variable-length path traversal.
Only string-prefix matching.
tradeoff: 固定 join 数 vs 可变路径
why: 层级深度不固定时，固定 join 数会漏结果或写出多份查询。可变长度路径把“沿 within 走到目标”作为一个模式表达。
why_en: Variable-length traversal fits hierarchies where the number of hops is not known in advance.
whenOtherWins: 若层级深度固定且很浅，固定 join 数更简单。
optionExplanations: 层级深度不固定时，固定数量的 join 只能覆盖某个具体深度，深一层或浅一层的记录就会被漏掉。
居住地可能直接是国家，也可能要经过城市、州、省好几层，可变长度路径遍历能把不确定跳数的关系当一个模式表达出来。
只按字符串前缀匹配跟地点的层级关系毫无关系，解决不了跳数不固定的问题。
optionExplanations_en: When hierarchy depth isn't fixed, a fixed number of joins only covers one specific depth, so records that are shallower or deeper get missed.
Since a residence can be a country directly or nested through city, state, and province, variable-length path traversal expresses that unknown hop count as one pattern.
Matching by string prefix has nothing to do with location hierarchy and doesn't solve the unknown-hop-count problem.

q: 主要差别是什么？
q_en: What is the main difference?
scenario: 同一个多跳地点查询可以用 SQL recursive CTE 写，也可以用图查询语言写。
scenario_en: The same multi-hop location query can be written with SQL recursive CTEs or with a graph query language.
options: SQL 递归 CTE 能写但啰嗦，图语言更贴路径
SQL 完全不能表达递归路径或者任意多跳关系
图语言用不了索引，只能全图扫描起步
options_en: Recursive CTEs in SQL work but read verbosely; graph languages fit paths directly.
SQL cannot express recursive paths or any multi-hop relationships at all.
Graph languages cannot use indexes and must start from a full scan.
tradeoff: 通用关系能力 vs 路径表达力

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化查询语言：关系数据库常用的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the declarative query language commonly used with relational databases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 公共表表达式：SQL 中给子查询命名并可递归引用的结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Common Table Expression names a subquery and can be recursive in SQL.

why: 关系库能表达图遍历，但语法和心智模型不一定顺手。数据模型合适时，查询会短很多，也更不容易写错。
why_en: Relational SQL can express recursive traversal, but graph languages usually make path-shaped queries clearer.
optionExplanations: SQL 的 recursive CTE 确实能表达同样的多跳查询，但语法更啰嗦；图查询语言把路径写得更贴近“沿关系走”的心智模型。
SQL 完全能表达递归路径查询，recursive CTE 就是为这个设计的，这个说法不成立。
图语言照样能用索引定位起点，不需要每次全图扫描，这个说法把图数据库的能力说反了。
optionExplanations_en: SQL's recursive CTE can express the same multi-hop query, but it's more verbose; a graph query language writes it closer to the mental model of following relationships.
SQL absolutely can express recursive path queries — the recursive CTE exists exactly for this, so this claim doesn't hold.
Graph languages can still use indexes to locate starting points; they don't need a full scan every time, so this claim has it backwards.

q: 最好的回答是什么？
q_en: What is the best answer?
scenario: 有人说图数据库只是旧 network model 回潮；你要解释关键区别。
scenario_en: Someone says graph databases are just the old network model returning; you need to explain the key difference.
options: 图数据库通常支持任意边和声明式查询，不强迫唯一访问路径
两者完全一样
CODASYL 比图数据库更加无 schema 约束
options_en: Graph databases usually allow arbitrary edges and declarative queries instead of forcing one access path.
They are exactly the same.
CODASYL is even more schema-free than a graph database.
tradeoff: 预定义路径 vs 灵活遍历

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种早期网络数据库模型标准，应用沿访问路径遍历记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CODASYL was an early network database model where applications traversed records through access paths.

why: 相似点是都能沿连接走，差别是图数据库不把应用绑死在预定义访问路径上。它还能按 ID 或属性索引找起点。
why_en: Graph databases resemble network traversal, but they avoid hard-wiring applications to predefined access paths.
optionExplanations: 图数据库通常允许任意边、用声明式查询表达路径，不像旧 network model 那样强迫应用只能走预定义的一条访问路径。
两者的关键区别正是访问路径是否被强制固定，说“完全一样”忽略了这个核心差异。
CODASYL 恰恰是要求预定义访问路径的模型，比图数据库更不灵活，这个说法说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Graph databases usually allow arbitrary edges and declarative queries, unlike the old network model that forced the application onto one predefined access path.
The key difference is exactly whether the access path is hard-wired; saying they are the same ignores that core distinction.
CODASYL is the one that requires predefined access paths, making it less flexible than graph databases — this option has it backwards.

q: triple-store 的基本记录是什么？
q_en: What is the basic record in a triple-store?
scenario: 团队要用三元组表示知识库事实，例如“Lucy marriedTo Alain”。
scenario_en: A team wants to represent knowledge-base facts as triples such as Lucy marriedTo Alain.
options: subject, predicate, object
table, row, page
cache, queue, worker 三段结构
options_en: Subject, predicate, object.
Table, row, page.
cache, queue, worker (three parts)
why: 三元组把属性和关系都写成同一种三段事实。object 可以是普通值，也可以是另一个实体。
why_en: A triple-store represents both properties and relationships as subject-predicate-object facts.
optionExplanations: subject、predicate、object 三段构成一条事实，比如「Lucy marriedTo Alain」，这是 triple-store 的基本记录单位。
table、row、page 是关系数据库和存储引擎的术语，不是 triple-store 用来描述事实的记录形式。
cache、queue、worker 是完全不相关的系统组件术语，跟三元组事实模型没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Subject, predicate, and object together form one fact, like Lucy marriedTo Alain — that's the basic record unit in a triple-store.
Table, row, and page are relational-database and storage-engine terms, not how a triple-store expresses a fact.
Cache, queue, and worker are unrelated system-component terms with nothing to do with the triple fact model.

q: RDF 为什么常用 URI 命名谓词？
q_en: Why does RDF often name predicates with URIs?
scenario: 两个组织都发布 within 关系，但一个指地理包含，一个指公司组织层级。
scenario_en: Two organizations publish a within relationship, but one means geographic containment and the other means org hierarchy.
options: 避免不同发布者的同名词冲突
让每个查询都访问公网 URL
强制所有数据使用 XML
options_en: To avoid collisions between names from different publishers.
So every query must fetch public URLs.
To force all data to use XML.
tradeoff: 全局合并能力 vs 名字冗长

termDefinitions.meaning: 资源描述框架：用三元组发布和交换图状数据的 W3C 模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resource Description Framework is a W3C model for publishing graph-shaped data as triples.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一资源标识符：用于全局命名资源或谓词的字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Uniform Resource Identifier is a string used to globally name a resource or predicate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可扩展标记语言：一种树状文本数据编码格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XML is a tree-shaped text data encoding format.

why: URI 给谓词加命名空间，合并互联网范围数据时不容易把同名关系误当同义。它是名字，不一定要求 URL 可访问。
why_en: URIs namespace predicates so independently published data can be merged without accidental name collisions.
optionExplanations: 两个组织都发布叫 within 的谓词，一个指地理包含、一个指公司层级，URI 命名空间能把它们区分开，避免误当成同一种关系合并。
用 URI 命名谓词是为了避免命名冲突，不是要求每次查询都真去访问那个公网地址，它更像一个带命名空间的标识符。
URI 命名空间跟数据要不要用 XML 编码没有关系，RDF 也能用其他格式序列化。
optionExplanations_en: When two organizations both publish a within predicate — one meaning geographic containment, one meaning org hierarchy — URI namespacing keeps them from being merged as the same relationship.
Naming predicates with URIs is about avoiding name collisions, not requiring every query to actually fetch that public address; it works more like a namespaced identifier.
URI namespacing has nothing to do with whether the data must use XML — RDF can be serialized in other formats too.

q: 哪种查询能力最贴合？
q_en: Which query capability fits best?
scenario: 知识图谱用 RDF 三元组存地点层级；查询要沿 within 任意多跳找到国家。
scenario_en: A knowledge graph stores location hierarchy as RDF triples; queries must follow within for any number of hops to reach a country.
options: SPARQL property path
用固定深度的两表 join 逐层展开关系
全文搜索分词后做模糊匹配
options_en: A SPARQL property path.
Expand relationships level by level with fixed-depth two-table joins.
Full-text tokenization with fuzzy matching.
tradeoff: 图路径表达 vs 固定关系查询

termDefinitions.meaning: SPARQL 协议和 RDF 查询语言：用于 RDF 三元组的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language is a declarative query language for RDF triples.
termDefinitions.fullName: SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language

termDefinitions.meaning: 资源描述框架：用三元组发布和交换图状数据的 W3C 模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resource Description Framework is a W3C model for publishing graph-shaped data as triples.

why: SPARQL 面向 RDF 三元组，property path 能把多跳关系写成路径模式。固定 join 数无法覆盖未知深度。
why_en: SPARQL property paths fit RDF graphs when traversal depth is not known ahead of time.
whenOtherWins: 若数据不是 RDF 三元组，Cypher 或 SQL 递归可能更贴合现有模型。
optionExplanations: 知识图谱用 RDF 三元组存地点层级，查询要沿 within 任意多跳找国家，SPARQL property path 正是为这种不确定跳数设计的。
固定两表 join 只能覆盖一个固定深度，地点层级跳数不确定时会漏掉更深或更浅的记录。
全文搜索分词是给文本内容匹配用的，跟沿着 within 关系多跳查找完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: With RDF triples storing location hierarchy and queries needing to hop through within relationships to reach a country, SPARQL property paths are built exactly for that unknown hop count.
A fixed two-table join only covers one specific depth, so it misses records at other levels when the hierarchy depth varies.
Full-text tokenization matches text content; it has nothing to do with hopping along within relationships.

q: 两者应怎么理解？
q_en: How should you understand the two models?
scenario: 同一组人物和地点关系既可建成 property graph，也可写成 triple-store。
scenario_en: The same people-location relationships can be modeled as a property graph or as a triple-store.
options: 概念接近，术语和生态不同
triple-store 不能表示边
property graph 不能给边加标签
options_en: They are conceptually close but differ in terminology and ecosystem.
Triple-stores cannot represent edges.
Property graphs cannot label edges.
tradeoff: 标准互通 vs 属性图工具

termDefinitions.meaning: SPARQL 协议和 RDF 查询语言：用于 RDF 三元组的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language is a declarative query language for RDF triples.
termDefinitions.fullName: SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language

why: 三元组和属性图都能表达点、边和属性；差别更多在表示方式、标准和查询生态。选型要看工具链和查询语言。
why_en: Triple-stores and property graphs can express similar graphs; tooling, standards, and query languages often drive the choice.
optionExplanations: 同一组人物和地点关系既能建成 property graph，也能写成 triple-store，两者概念相近，主要差在术语、标准和生态系统。
triple-store 完全可以表示边——一条 subject-predicate-object 三元组本身就是一条带方向的边。
property graph 恰恰支持给边加标签和属性，这正是它相对纯三元组的优势之一，这个说法说反了。
optionExplanations_en: The same people-and-places relationships can be modeled as a property graph or written as triples — the concepts are close, differing mainly in terminology, standards, and ecosystem.
A triple-store absolutely can represent an edge — a subject-predicate-object triple is itself a directed edge.
A property graph specifically supports labeling and adding properties to edges, which is one of its advantages over plain triples — this option has it backwards.

q: Datalog 什么时候更有吸引力？
q_en: When is Datalog more attractive?
scenario: 复杂图查询里，“地点属于某国家”会被很多查询复用，并且需要递归推导。
scenario_en: In complex graph queries, location-within-country is reused by many queries and needs recursive derivation.
options: 需要可复用规则和递归推导时
只做一次简单点查时
完全不需要声明式查询时
options_en: When reusable rules and recursive derivation matter.
For a one-off simple point lookup.
When declarative querying is not needed at all.
tradeoff: 规则复用 vs 简单查询便利

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种声明式逻辑查询语言，用事实和规则推导结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Datalog is a declarative logic query language that derives results from facts and rules.

why: Datalog 把派生谓词写成规则，复杂查询可以分层组合。它不一定适合一次性简单查询，但适合规则会被复用的模型。
why_en: Datalog shines when reusable recursive rules make complex graph logic easier to compose.
whenOtherWins: 若只是一次性简单查询，Cypher/SPARQL 这类直接模式更省心。
optionExplanations: 「地点属于某国家」这种规则会被很多查询反复用到，还需要递归推导，Datalog 把它写成可复用规则，正好省去重复表达。
只做一次简单点查时，Datalog 的规则分层反而是多余的开销，不是它最有吸引力的场景。
Datalog 本身就是声明式查询的一种，说完全不需要声明式查询时它才有吸引力，逻辑不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Since a rule like a place belongs to a country gets reused across many queries and needs recursive derivation, Datalog lets you write it once as a reusable rule.
For a one-off simple point lookup, Datalog's layered rules are unnecessary overhead, not where it shines.
Datalog is itself a declarative query style, so claiming it's attractive precisely when declarative querying isn't needed doesn't make sense.

q: 按 Datalog 递归推导顺序排列。
q_en: Order the Datalog recursive-derivation steps.
scenario: 地点图里 Idaho within USA，USA within North America；查询要推导 Idaho 属于 North America。
scenario_en: In a location graph, Idaho is within the USA and the USA is within North America; the query derives that Idaho is within North America.
steps: 用递归规则把 Idaho 通过 USA 继续推到 North America。
先用基础事实得到 USA 属于 North America。
查询使用派生出的 within_recursive 结果。
定义规则：直接命名匹配和沿 within 继续递归。
diagram:
flowchart LR
Rules[Rules] --> USA[USA within North America]
USA --> Idaho[Idaho within North America]
Idaho --> Query[Query derived facts]
why: Datalog 的关键是先声明规则，再让系统反复应用规则直到推出可查询的派生事实。代价是思维方式比直接 MATCH 更间接。
why_en: Datalog works by declaring rules and repeatedly applying them until derived facts can answer the query.

q: 怎么匹配更合理？
q_en: Which matching is most reasonable?
scenario: 团队在属性图、RDF 数据和可复用逻辑规则之间选查询语言。
scenario_en: A team is choosing query languages for a property graph, RDF data, and reusable logic rules.
options: Cypher-属性图，SPARQL-RDF，Datalog-规则推导
Cypher-CSV，SPARQL-磁盘页，Datalog-HTTP 路由
三者只差关键字拼写
options_en: Cypher for property graphs, SPARQL for RDF, Datalog for rule derivation.
Cypher for CSV, SPARQL for disk pages, Datalog for HTTP routes.
They differ only in keyword spelling.
tradeoff: 统一声明式思想 vs 模型专用表达

termDefinitions.meaning: 资源描述框架：用三元组发布和交换图状数据的 W3C 模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resource Description Framework is a W3C model for publishing graph-shaped data as triples.

termDefinitions.meaning: SPARQL 协议和 RDF 查询语言：用于 RDF 三元组的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language is a declarative query language for RDF triples.
termDefinitions.fullName: SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language

why: 三种语言都偏声明式，但各自围绕不同数据模型和表达习惯。不要只比较语法，要看数据表示和查询复用方式。
why_en: Cypher, SPARQL, and Datalog are all declarative-ish, but they fit different data models and reasoning styles.
optionExplanations: Cypher 面向属性图、SPARQL 面向 RDF 三元组、Datalog 面向可复用逻辑规则，三者分别匹配团队要选的三种数据形态。
Cypher、SPARQL、Datalog 分别对应的是属性图、RDF 和规则推导，不是 CSV、磁盘页或 HTTP 路由这些不相关的东西。
三者的差别不只是关键字拼写，而是围绕完全不同的数据模型和查询表达方式设计的。
optionExplanations_en: Cypher targets property graphs, SPARQL targets RDF triples, and Datalog targets reusable logical rules — each matches one of the three data shapes the team is choosing between.
Cypher, SPARQL, and Datalog map to property graphs, RDF, and rule derivation respectively, not to unrelated things like CSV, disk pages, or HTTP routes.
The differences go far beyond keyword spelling; each language is built around a distinct data model and way of expressing queries.

q: 哪个配对最合理？
q_en: Which pairing is most reasonable?
scenario: 一个产品要在用户资料树、订单表和社交关系网络之间选主要存储模型。
scenario_en: A product is choosing primary storage models for profile trees, order tables, and a social relationship network.
options: 资料树用文档，订单用关系，人脉用图
所有场景都强制用文档模型
所有场景都改成手写指针式访问路径
options_en: Documents for profile trees, relational for orders, graph for social networks.
Force the document model on every scenario.
Every scenario switches to hand-coded pointer access paths.
tradeoff: 单模型统一性 vs 关系形状适配
why: 文档、关系、图分别擅长局部树、共享表和多跳关系。真实架构可以组合模型，但每个边界都要说明同步和一致性。
why_en: Documents, relational tables, and graphs each fit a different relationship shape, and real systems may combine them deliberately.
whenOtherWins: 若团队必须只运维一个数据库，选一个混合能力强的系统会更实际。
optionExplanations: 资料树用文档存局部对象，订单这类共享实体用关系表和 join，社交关系网络用图表达多跳连接——三种模型各管各擅长的部分。
强制所有场景都用文档，会让订单的共享实体和社交网络的多跳关系都很难表达，白白丢掉关系模型和图模型的优势。
所有场景都手写指针访问路径，等于放弃优化器和声明式查询带来的所有好处，回到最原始的模型。
optionExplanations_en: Using documents for profile trees, relational tables and joins for shared order entities, and a graph for the relationship network lets each model handle what it's best at.
Forcing every scenario into documents makes shared order entities and multi-hop social relationships hard to express, throwing away what relational and graph models are good at.
Hand-writing pointer access paths everywhere gives up all the benefits of the optimizer and declarative queries, reverting to the most primitive model.

q: 应用层 join 的直接后果是什么？
q_en: What is the direct consequence of application-side joins?
scenario: 文档数据库不支持服务端 join；页面需要把订单里的 customer_id、product_id 都解析成最新详情。
scenario_en: A document database lacks server-side joins; a page must resolve customer_id and product_id to latest details.
options: 多次数据库请求和更多应用复杂度
所有引用自动强一致
查询优化器获得更多全局信息
options_en: More database round trips and more application complexity.
All references become automatically strongly consistent.
The optimizer gets more global information.
tradeoff: 数据库 join 能力 vs 应用复杂度
why: 把 join 搬到应用层通常会增加网络往返，并让应用处理缓存、批量查询和缺失引用。数据库内部 join 往往能更好地优化。
why_en: Moving joins into application code usually adds round trips and forces the app to handle batching and missing references.
optionExplanations: 文档数据库没有服务端 join，页面要把 customer_id、product_id 解析成详情，只能靠应用发多次请求，代码也要多处理缓存和批量查询逻辑。
引用不会因为搬到应用层就自动变强一致，反而更容易出现读到过期详情的情况。
应用层 join 拿不到数据库内部的统计信息和索引结构，优化器的全局信息其实变少了，不是变多了。
optionExplanations_en: With no server-side join, resolving customer_id and product_id into details means the app fires multiple round trips and has to manage caching and batching itself.
References do not become automatically strongly consistent just because the join moved to the app — it actually becomes easier to read stale details.
An application-side join loses access to the database's internal statistics and index structures, so the optimizer actually has less global information, not more.

q: 哪种 schema 更合适？
q_en: Which schema approach fits best?
scenario: 支付订单每行都必须有金额、币种、状态和创建时间；缺字段应在写入时失败。
scenario_en: Every payment order must have amount, currency, status, and creation time; missing fields should fail at write time.
options: schema-on-write
完全无校验 schema-on-read
把结构写在注释里
options_en: Schema-on-write.
Pure schema-on-read with no validation.
Put the structure only in comments.
tradeoff: 写入约束 vs 格式灵活
why: 核心记录结构稳定且必须正确时，写入时校验能把错误挡在数据入口。灵活性下降，但数据质量和文档性更强。
why_en: Schema-on-write fits stable core records because bad data is rejected at the boundary.
whenOtherWins: 若字段来自外部且经常变化，schema-on-read 能降低接入摩擦。
optionExplanations: 金额、币种、状态、创建时间必须每行都有，缺字段应在写入时就失败，schema-on-write 能把错误挡在数据入口，正好符合这个要求。
完全无校验的 schema-on-read 会让缺字段的支付记录先写进去，等读取甚至对账时才发现问题，风险太晚才暴露。
结构写在注释里没有任何强制力，数据库不会替你校验，缺字段照样能写进去。
optionExplanations_en: With amount, currency, status, and creation time required on every row and missing fields expected to fail on write, schema-on-write rejects bad data right at the entry point.
Pure schema-on-read with no validation would let payment rows with missing fields get written first, only surfacing the problem later at read or reconciliation time.
Putting the structure only in comments has no enforcement power — the database won't validate anything, and rows with missing fields can still be written.

q: 哪个思路说明局部性不只属于文档库？
q_en: Which idea shows locality is not only for document stores?
scenario: 关系数据里订单和订单行总是一起读；团队想保留 SQL，又想减少跨表读取成本。
scenario_en: Orders and order lines are usually read together; the team wants to keep SQL while reducing cross-table read cost.
options: 在关系模型里支持父子行物理邻近
完全放弃 join
把订单行序列化进日志文件且不可查询
options_en: Support physical locality for parent-child rows in a relational model.
Give up joins entirely.
Serialize order lines into an unqueryable log file.
tradeoff: 关系查询能力 vs 物理局部性
why: 局部性是存储布局思想，不等于文档模型专利。关系系统也可以用 interleaving 或类似布局让常一起读的数据靠近。
why_en: Locality is a storage-layout idea, not a document-only feature; relational systems can also colocate parent-child data.
whenOtherWins: 若读写模式不需要局部性，普通规范化关系表更简单。
optionExplanations: 局部性说的是把常一起读的数据物理上放近，关系模型也能靠 interleaving 之类的机制让父子行邻近存储，不必放弃 SQL。
完全放弃 join 会丢掉关系模型本身的能力，跟“既想保留 SQL”的前提直接冲突。
把订单行序列化进不可查询的日志文件，读取时反而要额外解析，也没法用 SQL 直接查询，跟目标背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Locality just means placing frequently-co-read data physically close together; a relational model can do this too via interleaving, without giving up SQL.
Giving up joins entirely throws away what makes it relational in the first place, which conflicts with wanting to keep SQL.
Serializing order lines into an unqueryable log file adds extra parsing on read and loses direct SQL querying — the opposite of the goal here.

q: 这说明数据模型的什么风险？
q_en: What data-model risk does this show?
scenario: 初版用户资料只有嵌套职位；后来职位要链接公司页、校友、推荐人和共同联系人。
scenario_en: The first profile model has nested jobs; later jobs link to company pages, alumni, recommenders, and mutual contacts.
options: 数据会随功能变得更互联
所有需求都会保持树状
越早反规范化越不会变
options_en: Data tends to become more interconnected as features grow.
All requirements stay tree-shaped.
Early denormalization prevents future change.
tradeoff: 初版简单性 vs 未来关联增长
why: 很多产品从树状资料开始，但功能会把共享实体和关系拉进来。早期建模要给引用和迁移留余地。
why_en: Many products start with tree-shaped data, but features often introduce shared entities and relationships over time.
optionExplanations: 职位后来要链接公司页、校友、推荐人和共同联系人，说明功能一增加，原本树状的数据会自然被拉向更互联的形状。
这个例子恰恰说明需求不会一直停留在树状，后续功能引入了共享实体和横向关系。
越早反规范化，改动共享实体时要同步的副本反而越多，不会让模型更不容易变。
optionExplanations_en: Once positions need to link to company pages, alumni, referrers, and mutual contacts, the once tree-shaped data naturally pulls toward a more interconnected shape as features grow.
This example shows the opposite — requirements did not stay tree-shaped; later features introduced shared entities and cross-links.
Denormalizing earlier just means more copies to keep in sync whenever a shared entity changes, not a model that's harder to disturb.

q: 语言限制带来的收益是什么？
q_en: What benefit comes from this language limitation?
scenario: SQL 不允许查询依赖未声明的物理顺序；数据库因此可以改变执行计划。
scenario_en: SQL does not let a query depend on undeclared physical order; the database can change execution plans.
options: 实现可以优化而不破坏语义
应用能控制每个磁盘 seek
查询一定比任何代码都快
options_en: The implementation can optimize without breaking semantics.
The application can control every disk seek.
The query is always faster than any code.
tradeoff: 表达限制 vs 优化自由
why: 声明式语言少给程序员一些控制，换来数据库更多重排和并行空间。限制不是缺陷，而是优化合同的一部分。
why_en: Declarative limits are useful because they give the engine freedom to optimize while preserving query meaning.
optionExplanations: SQL 不让查询依赖未声明的物理顺序，这个限制换来的是数据库能自由重排执行计划，而不破坏查询原本的语义承诺。
应用不能控制每个磁盘 seek，这正是声明式语言把控制权交给数据库引擎的地方，不是语言限制带来的收益。
查询不会因为是声明式的就一定比任何手写代码都快，性能取决于优化器和索引，不是语言形式本身的必然结果。
optionExplanations_en: SQL forbidding queries from depending on undeclared physical order is exactly what lets the database freely reorder its execution plan without breaking the query's stated semantics.
The app not controlling every disk seek is precisely where a declarative language hands control to the engine — it's not itself the benefit of the language limit.
A declarative query isn't automatically faster than any hand-written code; performance depends on the optimizer and indexes, not the language form alone.

q: 图模型为什么能容纳这类异构数据？
q_en: Why can graph models hold this heterogeneous data?
scenario: 一个社交图同时包含人、地点、活动、评论、签到和组织。
scenario_en: A social graph contains people, places, events, comments, check-ins, and organizations.
options: 不同类型实体都可作为 vertex
不同关系可用不同 edge label
所有实体必须共用完全相同字段
新关系可作为新边加入
options_en: Different entity types can be vertices.
Different relationships can use different edge labels.
All entities must share exactly the same fields.
New relationships can be added as new edges.
why: 图模型不要求所有点长一样，也不要求只有一种关系。它用标签和属性保持语义边界。
why_en: A graph can mix entity and relationship types because labels and properties carry the meaning.
optionExplanations: 人、地点、活动、评论等不同类型的实体都能作为 vertex 存进同一张图，不需要各自建独立的表结构。
人和地点之间、人和活动之间可以用不同的 edge label 区分关系种类，同一张图里能容纳多种语义不同的边。
图模型不要求所有实体共用完全相同的字段，不同类型的 vertex 可以有各自的属性集合，这个说法不成立。
食物过敏、签到这类新出现的关系，可以直接作为新的边加进已有的图里，不用改动老数据的结构。
optionExplanations_en: People, places, activities, and comments — different entity types — can all be vertices in the same graph without needing separate table structures for each.
Relationships between people and places, or people and activities, can use different edge labels, so one graph can hold many semantically distinct kinds of edges.
A graph model does not require every entity to share exactly the same fields; different vertex types can carry their own property sets, so this claim doesn't hold.
New relationships like food allergies or check-ins can be added directly as new edges to the existing graph, without restructuring the old data.

q: 这种嵌套项引用有什么问题？
q_en: What is the problem with referencing nested items this way?
scenario: 文档中 positions 是数组；外部评论想指向“用户 251 的第二段工作经历”。
scenario_en: In a document, positions is an array; an external comment wants to point to the second job of user 251.
options: 引用依赖文档内部位置，重排会变脆
文档里的数组项天然拥有全局唯一身份
关系库不能表达数组
options_en: The reference depends on internal position and becomes fragile if reordered.
Array items inside a document have a natural global identity.
Relational databases cannot represent arrays.
tradeoff: 嵌套便利 vs 稳定身份
why: 文档内部子项常没有稳定全局身份，引用只能靠路径或位置。只要外部实体要指向它，就该考虑提升成独立实体。
why_en: Nested items often lack stable global identity, so external references to positions or paths are fragile.
optionExplanations: 引用「第二段工作经历」依赖的是数组里的内部位置，一旦这个数组被重排或增删，指向的内容就可能变成别的记录。
数组项并不天然拥有全局唯一身份，它只有在文档内部按位置才有意义，外部想稳定引用它就很脆弱。
关系库完全能用一张单独的表来表达数组式的一对多数据，这个说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Referencing the second work-experience entry depends on its position inside the array, so if the array gets reordered or edited, the reference can silently point at something else.
Array items don't have stable global identity by default — they only make sense by position inside the document, which makes external references to them fragile.
Relational databases can absolutely represent array-like one-to-many data using a separate table, so this claim doesn't hold.

q: 数据模型怎样改变思考方式？
q_en: How do data models change how you think?
text: 关系模型让你自然想到 {{表、键和 join}}；文档模型让你自然想到 {{局部对象树}}；图模型让你自然想到 {{点、边和路径}}。
text_en: The relational model makes you think in {{tables, keys, and joins}}; the document model in {{local object trees}}; the graph model in {{vertices, edges, and paths}}.
why: 这不是术语偏好，而是会改变需求拆分、查询表达和未来演进成本的设计选择。
why_en: This is not just terminology; the model changes how requirements, queries, and evolution costs are shaped.

q: 哪个片段最像 Cypher 路径？
q_en: Which snippet looks like a Cypher path?
scenario: 查询要表达“person 的出生地沿 within 任意多跳到 United States”。学习目标是识别图路径语法，而不是背完整查询。
scenario_en: The query needs to say a person's birthplace follows within for any number of hops to the United States; the goal is recognizing graph path syntax.
options: (person)-[:BORN_IN]->()-[:WITHIN*0..]->(us)
SELECT * FROM people ORDER BY name LIMIT 10
for row in rows: follow(row.parent_id)
options_en: (person)-[:BORN_IN]->()-[:WITHIN*0..]->(us)
SELECT * FROM people ORDER BY name LIMIT 10
for row in rows: follow(row.parent_id)
tradeoff: 图路径声明 vs 命令式遍历

termDefinitions.meaning: Neo4j 推广的声明式属性图查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cypher is a declarative property-graph query language popularized by Neo4j.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结构化查询语言：关系数据库常用的声明式查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the declarative query language commonly used with relational databases.

why: Cypher 用括号表示点、箭头表示边，*0.. 表示可变长度路径。这个形式把多跳遍历写成模式，而不是手写循环。
why_en: Cypher uses node-and-edge patterns, and *0.. marks a variable-length traversal instead of a hand-written loop.
whenOtherWins: 若目标是表格聚合而非图路径，SQL 片段会更合适。
optionExplanations: 读法是：从 person 走一条 BORN_IN 边，再沿 WITHIN 向上跳 0 到多次，最后落在 us 上。
这是标准 SQL 的 SELECT 语句，按 name 排序取全部人，跟图路径遍历完全是两种查询形式。
这是手写的命令式循环，逐行 follow 父节点，跟 Cypher 那种声明式路径模式语法正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Read it as: leave person by a BORN_IN edge, hop up WITHIN zero or more times, and land on us.
This is a standard SQL SELECT statement ordering everyone by name, a completely different query style from graph path traversal.
This is a hand-written imperative loop that follows the parent row by row, the opposite of Cypher's declarative path-pattern syntax.

q: 为什么追加日志写入很快？
q_en: Why are append-only log writes fast?
scenario: 一个 key-value 写入路径只需要把新值追加到文件末尾；读性能暂时不是瓶颈。
scenario_en: A key-value write path only needs to append new values to the end of a file; read performance is not the bottleneck yet.
options: 顺序写避免随机覆盖
每次写都重排整个文件
写入前必须扫描所有历史值
options_en: Sequential writes avoid random overwrites.
Every write re-sorts the whole file.
Each write must scan all historical values first.
tradeoff: 写入简单性 vs 读取查找成本
why: 追加写是存储系统里最便宜的操作之一，尤其比随机覆盖简单。代价是读路径要靠索引或扫描找到最新值。
why_en: Appending is cheap because it avoids random in-place updates, but reads need an index or scan to find the latest value.
whenOtherWins: 若读取延迟已经是瓶颈，需要先设计索引，而不是只优化写入。
optionExplanations: 顺序写只往文件末尾追加，不用像随机覆盖那样先定位再改写磁盘上分散的位置，磁头或 SSD 都跑得更顺。
每次写都重排整个文件的成本会随文件变大线性增长，跟“追加写很快”的前提正好相反。
写入前扫描所有历史值，等于把每次写都变成一次全量读，追加写的意义就是不需要这一步。
optionExplanations_en: A sequential write only appends to the end of the file instead of seeking around to overwrite scattered locations, which keeps disk heads or SSDs moving smoothly.
Re-sorting the whole file on every write would make cost grow with file size, the opposite of why append-only writes are cheap.
Scanning all historical values before writing would turn every write into a full read, defeating the point of appending in the first place.

q: 索引的基本取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the basic index tradeoff?
scenario: 数据库可以给每个查询字段都建索引，但写入量也很高。
scenario_en: A database could index every query field, but the write volume is high.
options: 索引加速读，但每次写要维护索引
索引让读写都免费
索引只影响磁盘容量，不影响写入
options_en: Indexes speed up reads, but each write must maintain them.
Indexes make both reads and writes free.
Indexes only affect disk capacity, not writes.
tradeoff: 读取延迟 vs 写入维护
why: 索引是从主数据派生的辅助结构，能减少读扫描，也会增加写入维护成本。索引选择应该由真实查询模式驱动。
why_en: An index is derived metadata that speeds reads while adding write-maintenance cost.

rows: 索引加速读，但每次写要维护索引
索引加速读，但每次…场景
索引加速读，但每次写要…成本
索引让读写都免费场景
索引让读写都免费成本
索引只影响磁盘容量，不影响写入
索引只影响磁盘容量…场景
索引只影响磁盘容量，不…成本

optionExplanations: 索引加速了按条件查找的读取，但每次写入都要同步更新每个相关索引，写入侧的维护成本是真实存在的。
索引不会让读写都变免费，它把成本从读路径转移了一部分到写路径，本身是一种取舍而不是白拿。
索引不仅占磁盘容量，每次写入都要更新索引结构，直接影响写入延迟和吞吐。
optionExplanations_en: An index speeds up conditional reads, but every write must update each relevant index too, so the write-side maintenance cost is real.
Indexes don't make both reads and writes free — they shift some cost from the read path onto the write path, which is a tradeoff, not a free lunch.
Indexes cost more than just disk space; every write has to update the index structure, which directly affects write latency and throughput.

q: 哪种简单索引很合适？
q_en: Which simple index fits well?
scenario: 键数量能放进内存，值很大但每次按 key 精确读取；没有范围查询需求。
scenario_en: The number of keys fits in memory, values are large, and reads are exact lookups by key; no range queries are needed.
options: 内存 hash map 指向日志偏移
按 key 排序的多维 R-tree
只保留全文件 grep
options_en: An in-memory hash map pointing to log offsets.
A multidimensional R-tree sorted by key.
Keep only full-file grep.
tradeoff: 点查速度 vs 范围查询能力
why: hash 索引用内存保存 key 到文件偏移，精确点查只需一次定位。前提是 key 集合能放进内存，且不需要范围扫描。
why_en: A hash index fits exact key lookups when the key set fits in memory and range scans are not needed.
whenOtherWins: 若 key 数量放不进内存或要范围扫描，SSTable/B-tree 更合适。
optionExplanations: key 集合能放进内存、按 key 精确读取又没有范围查询需求时，内存 hash map 指向日志偏移能一次定位取到值，简单又快。
多维 R-tree 是给空间范围查询设计的，这里既没有多维数据也没有范围查询需求，用不上。
只留全文件 grep 意味着每次查询都要扫一遍整个文件，key 数量一大就完全撑不住。
optionExplanations_en: With the key set fitting in memory and only exact key lookups needed, an in-memory hash map pointing to log offsets resolves a read in one jump.
A multidimensional R-tree is built for spatial range queries; there's neither multidimensional data nor a range-query need here.
Relying on full-file grep means scanning the whole file on every lookup, which falls apart as the key count grows.

q: 这种负载适合哪类存储形状？
q_en: Which storage shape fits this workload?
scenario: 播放计数服务有大量更新，但不同视频 key 的数量可控；value 可以从磁盘读取。
scenario_en: A play-count service has many updates, but the number of distinct video keys is controlled; values can be read from disk.
options: key 索引常驻内存的追加日志
只能用列式数据仓库做全表扫描和聚合
必须用图数据库做多跳邻居关系遍历
options_en: An append-only log with the key index kept in RAM.
Only a columnar warehouse doing full scans and aggregation.
A graph database doing multi-hop neighbor traversal.
tradeoff: 内存 key 目录 vs 高写吞吐

termDefinitions.meaning: 随机访问内存：断电易失但访问很快的主存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random Access Memory is fast volatile main memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: Riak 使用过的日志型 key-value 存储引擎，内存保存 key 到文件偏移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bitcask is a log-structured key-value engine that keeps key-to-offset metadata in memory.

why: 大量每 key 更新适合追加日志加内存 key 索引，因为写入顺序化，读取按偏移取值。限制是 key 数量要受 RAM 约束。
why_en: A log-structured hash index works well for many updates per key as long as the key directory fits in RAM.
whenOtherWins: 若 key 空间巨大且很少重复更新，内存 hash 目录会成为瓶颈。
optionExplanations: 写只是在文件末尾追加一条；读时用内存里 key→字节偏移的映射，一次 seek 就拿到 value。
列式数据仓库是为大规模分析扫描设计的，跟这里高频按 key 更新的负载完全不匹配。
图数据库遍历是为多跳关系查询设计的，这里没有关系遍历需求，用不上。
optionExplanations_en: A write just appends to the end of the file; a read uses the in-memory key-to-offset map and one seek gets the value.
A columnar data warehouse is built for large-scale analytic scans, which doesn't match this high-frequency per-key update workload at all.
Graph database traversal is for multi-hop relationship queries; there's no relationship traversal need here.

q: 按 compaction 和 tombstone 生命周期排序。
q_en: Order the compaction and tombstone lifecycle.
scenario: 一个追加日志 key-value 存储要回收旧版本，并正确处理删除。
scenario_en: An append-only key-value store must reclaim old versions and handle deletes correctly.
steps: 后台合并相邻段，只保留每个 key 的最新记录。
删除 key 时追加 tombstone，而不是原地擦掉旧值。
切换读路径到新段后，旧段才能删除。
写入先追加到当前段，段满后冻结成不可变文件。

termDefinitions.meaning: 删除标记：追加到日志里的特殊记录，表示某个 key 已删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone is a delete marker appended to a log so compaction can remove older values.

diagram:
flowchart LR
W[Append writes] --> F[Freeze segment]
D[Append tombstone] --> M[Merge segments]
M --> N[New compacted segment]
N --> R[Route reads to new segment]
R --> X[Delete old segments]
why: 追加日志先产生多个不可变段，删除也变成一条记录；合并时 tombstone 才能清掉旧值。代价是磁盘空间要等后台回收。
why_en: Compaction reclaims old log entries by merging immutable segments, with tombstones carrying deletes until old values can be discarded.

q: 读取某个 key 时通常先查哪一段？
q_en: Which segment should a read check first?
scenario: 日志被切成多个不可变段，每段都有自己的内存 hash 表。
scenario_en: The log is split into immutable segments, and each segment has its own in-memory hash table.
options: 最新段，再向旧段回退
最旧段，再向新段回退
随机选择一个段
options_en: The newest segment, then older segments.
The oldest segment, then newer segments.
A random segment.
why: 较新的段覆盖较旧段的同 key 值，所以读路径从最新段开始。后台合并要控制段数量，避免一次读检查太多表。
why_en: Reads check newer segments first because newer values override older ones for the same key.
optionExplanations: 较新的段会覆盖较旧段里同一个 key 的值，所以读取要先查最新段，找不到再往旧段回退。
先查最旧段找到的值可能早就被更新的段覆盖了，这样读到的会是过期值，顺序反了。
随机选段完全放弃了“新值覆盖旧值”这个规则，读到的结果没有正确性保证。
optionExplanations_en: A newer segment can override an older segment's value for the same key, so reads must check the newest segment first and fall back to older ones only if needed.
Starting from the oldest segment risks returning a value that's already been overridden by a newer segment — the order is backwards.
Picking a random segment abandons the newer-overrides-older rule entirely, so the result has no correctness guarantee.

q: 为什么要保存 hash 表快照？
q_en: Why store hash-table snapshots?
scenario: 数据库重启后，内存 hash 表丢失；段文件还在磁盘上。
scenario_en: After restart, the in-memory hash tables are gone, while segment files remain on disk.
options: 避免每次启动全量扫描段来重建索引
强制让所有的值都只存在内存里
替代磁盘上的数据段
options_en: To avoid scanning all segments on every startup to rebuild indexes.
Force all values to live only in memory.
To replace the data segments on disk.
tradeoff: 恢复速度 vs 快照维护成本
why: hash 索引本身是内存派生结构，崩溃后可从段重建，但大段会让启动很慢。快照把恢复时间从全量扫描压短。
why_en: Hash-index snapshots reduce restart time by avoiding a full segment scan to rebuild in-memory metadata.
optionExplanations: 内存 hash 表丢失后，如果没有快照，每次启动都要把所有段完整扫一遍才能重建索引，段一多启动就会很慢，快照正是为了避免这个。
快照保存的是索引本身，不会让所有值都只存在内存，实际数据仍然在磁盘段文件里。
快照是为了加快索引重建，不是用来替代磁盘上的数据段，段文件依然是数据的真实来源。
optionExplanations_en: Without a snapshot, every restart would need a full scan of every segment to rebuild the index, which gets slow as segments pile up — that's exactly what the snapshot avoids.
A snapshot saves the index itself; it doesn't put all values only in memory — the actual data still lives in the on-disk segment files.
A snapshot speeds up index rebuilding; it doesn't replace the on-disk data segments, which remain the source of truth.

q: checksum 的作用是什么？
q_en: What does a checksum do here?
scenario: 数据库可能在追加一条记录写到一半时崩溃；重启后文件尾部有残缺字节。
scenario_en: The database may crash halfway through appending a record; after restart the file tail has partial bytes.
options: 识别并忽略残缺记录
把旧值自动合并成新值
让范围查询变快
options_en: Detect and ignore a partial record.
Automatically merge old values into new ones.
Make range queries faster.
tradeoff: 写入简单性 vs 崩溃检测
why: 追加日志也会遇到半写入，checksum 让恢复过程知道哪里开始不可信。通常丢弃尾部坏记录，再从最后完整记录继续。
why_en: A checksum lets recovery detect a partially written log record and continue from the last valid one.
optionExplanations: 半写入的记录字节是残缺的，checksum 校验不通过就能识别出它，恢复时直接跳过或丢弃，不会把坏数据当成有效值读出来。
checksum 只是校验数据完整性的手段，它不会替你决定该保留哪个版本，更不会自动合并新旧值。
checksum 跟范围查询的执行速度没有关系，它解决的是崩溃恢复时的数据完整性问题。
optionExplanations_en: A partially written record has corrupted bytes, so it fails the checksum check, letting recovery detect and skip it instead of reading garbage as a valid value.
A checksum only verifies data integrity; it doesn't decide which version to keep or automatically merge old and new values.
A checksum has nothing to do with how fast range queries run; it addresses data integrity during crash recovery.

q: 追加型设计有哪些工程收益？
q_en: What engineering benefits does append-only design provide?
scenario: 团队质疑为什么不直接原地覆盖旧值，而要不断追加新值。
scenario_en: A team asks why not overwrite old values in place instead of appending new values.
options: 顺序写通常更快
崩溃恢复更容易推理
不可变段可并发读取
无需任何磁盘空间回收
options_en: Sequential writes are usually faster.
Crash recovery is easier to reason about.
Immutable segments can be read concurrently.
No disk-space reclamation is ever needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入/输出：程序和磁盘、网络等外部设备交换数据的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Input/Output is data movement between a program and external devices such as disks or networks.

why: 追加和不可变段让写入、并发读、崩溃边界都更简单。空间不会自动回来，所以需要 compaction。
why_en: Append-only immutable segments simplify writes, reads, and recovery, but they need compaction to reclaim space.
optionExplanations: 顺序写不用像随机覆盖那样反复寻址，通常比原地更新更快，这也是追加设计的直接收益之一。
不可变的追加段让崩溃恢复更容易推理——半写的只是最后一条记录，前面的段都是完整且不变的。
段一旦写完就不再改动，多个读线程可以同时安全地读同一个段，不用担心读到写入过程中的中间状态。
追加不等于空间无限，旧值和已删除的数据仍然占着磁盘，需要靠 compaction 才能把空间收回来。
optionExplanations_en: Sequential writes skip the repeated seeking that random overwrites need, which is a direct speed benefit of the append design.
Immutable append-only segments make crash recovery easier to reason about — only the very last record can be partially written, and everything before it is complete and unchanged.
Once a segment is fully written it never changes again, so multiple readers can safely read it concurrently without seeing a write in progress.
Appending doesn't reclaim space by itself — stale and deleted values still sit on disk until compaction runs to recover it.

q: hash 索引的限制有哪些？
q_en: What are the limitations of hash indexes?
scenario: 一个 key-value 存储用内存 hash 表索引追加日志；产品开始要求按 key 前缀范围扫描。
scenario_en: A key-value store uses an in-memory hash table over an append-only log; the product now needs prefix range scans by key.
options: key 目录需要放进内存
范围查询不高效
精确 key 查询完全不能做
磁盘 hash map 扩容和冲突处理复杂
options_en: The key directory must fit in memory.
Range queries are inefficient.
Exact key lookups are impossible.
On-disk hash maps are hard to grow and handle collisions in.
tradeoff: 点查索引 vs 有序范围扫描

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序字符串表：按 key 有序的不可变段文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Sorted String Table is an immutable segment file sorted by key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种按 key 有序的页式树索引，广泛用于数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a page-oriented sorted tree index widely used in databases.

why: hash 索引很擅长点查，但不保序。需要范围扫描时，排序结构如 SSTable 或 B-tree 更自然。
why_en: Hash indexes are good for point lookups, but sorted structures fit range scans better.

rows: key 目录需要放进内存
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
key 目录需要放进内存成本
范围查询和稳定读延迟更重要时
精确 key 查询完全不能做
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
精确 key 查询完全…成本
磁盘 hash map 扩容和冲突…

optionExplanations: 内存 hash map 要保存每个 key 到文件偏移的映射，key 一多，这份目录本身就要占用相应的内存空间。
hash 索引按哈希值分布 key，没有天然的顺序，想按前缀做范围扫描时找不到连续区间，效率很差。
这里说反了——hash 索引恰恰最擅长精确 key 查询，一次哈希定位就能取到偏移，它弱的是范围扫描不是点查。
磁盘上的 hash map 要处理扩容重新分布和哈希冲突，实现复杂度比内存版本高不少。
optionExplanations_en: An in-memory hash map has to store every key's offset, so the directory itself grows with the number of keys and needs enough RAM.
A hash index distributes keys by hash value with no natural order, so there's no contiguous range to scan for a prefix query, which makes it inefficient.
This has it backwards — a hash index is exactly what's good at exact key lookups, one hash gets you the offset; its weakness is range scans, not point queries.
An on-disk hash map has to handle resizing and hash collisions, which adds real implementation complexity compared to the in-memory version.

q: 排序段带来的核心收益是什么？
q_en: What is the core benefit of sorted segments?
scenario: 多个段文件都按 key 排序；后台要合并它们并保留每个 key 的最新值。
scenario_en: Several segment files are sorted by key; the background job must merge them and keep the newest value per key.
options: 能像 merge sort 一样顺序合并
必须把全部数据都放进内存才能查
每次读都要随机访问所有 segment
options_en: Segments can be merged sequentially like merge sort.
All data must fit in memory before it can be queried.
Every read randomly accesses every segment.
tradeoff: 有序维护成本 vs 合并效率

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序字符串表：按 key 有序的不可变段文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Sorted String Table is an immutable segment file sorted by key.

why: SSTable 的有序性让合并可以顺序推进，遇到重复 key 保留更新段的值。即使文件大于内存，也能流式合并。
why_en: Sorted SSTables can be merged sequentially, keeping the newest value for duplicate keys without loading everything into memory.
whenOtherWins: 若写入必须立即按页原地更新，B-tree 思路会更直接。
optionExplanations: 每个段本身已经按 key 排好序，合并多个段就像归并排序一样按序推进，遇到重复 key 时保留更新段的值即可。
排序段的合并是流式进行的，不需要把全部数据一次性放进内存，这正是它比 hash 索引更适合大数据量的原因。
合并按 key 顺序推进，靠的是顺序读取相邻块，不是每次读都随机访问所有块。
optionExplanations_en: Each segment is already sorted by key, so merging several of them proceeds like a merge sort, keeping the value from the newer segment whenever keys repeat.
Merging sorted segments happens as a stream, so it never needs to load everything into memory at once, which is why it scales past hash indexes for large data.
The merge advances by reading adjacent blocks in order, not by randomly accessing every block on each read.

q: 为什么 sparse index 够用？
q_en: Why is a sparse index enough?
scenario: SSTable 文件按 key 排序，key 和 value 变长；内存不够保存每个 key 的精确偏移。
scenario_en: An SSTable file is sorted by key, keys and values are variable length, and memory cannot hold every exact key offset.
options: 保存部分边界 key，跳到附近后顺序扫描
完全不需要内存索引
把每个 value 都完整复制到内存索引里
options_en: Store some boundary keys, jump nearby, then scan sequentially.
No in-memory index is needed at all.
Copy every value fully into an in-memory index.
tradeoff: 索引内存 vs 局部扫描

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序字符串表：按 key 有序的不可变段文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Sorted String Table is an immutable segment file sorted by key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 随机访问内存：断电易失但访问很快的主存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random Access Memory is fast volatile main memory.

why: 有序文件允许先定位到目标 key 附近，再扫描一小段。稀疏索引用少量内存换可控的局部扫描。
why_en: A sparse index works because sorted files let you jump near the target key and scan a small range.
whenOtherWins: 若记录定长且文件支持二分定位，稀疏索引的必要性会下降。
optionExplanations: 文件已经按 key 排好序，稀疏索引只保存一部分边界 key，查询时先跳到附近位置，再顺序扫一小段就能找到目标，不用记住每个 key 的精确偏移。
完全不用内存索引意味着每次查询都要从文件开头顺序扫，key 一多延迟就会难以接受。
把每个 value 复制进内存，等于放弃了“内存不够”这个前提，跟场景约束直接矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Since the file is already sorted, a sparse index storing only some boundary keys lets a lookup jump near the target and scan a short stretch, without remembering every key's exact offset.
Skipping an in-memory index entirely means every query scans from the start of the file, which becomes unacceptably slow as the key count grows.
Copying every value into memory directly contradicts the given constraint that memory can't hold precise offsets for every key.

q: 为什么按块压缩有帮助？
q_en: Why does block compression help?
scenario: 读 SSTable 时通常会扫描一小段相邻 key-value；磁盘带宽比 CPU 更紧。
scenario_en: Reading an SSTable usually scans a small neighboring block of key-value pairs; disk bandwidth is tighter than CPU.
options: 减少磁盘读写字节，用少量 CPU 解压
让 key 不再需要排序
彻底消除后台所有的 compaction 工作
options_en: It reduces bytes read and written, spending some CPU to decompress.
It removes the need for sorted keys.
Eliminate all background compaction work entirely.
tradeoff: CPU 解压成本 vs 磁盘带宽

termDefinitions.meaning: 中央处理器：执行程序指令的计算资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CPU is the processor resource that executes program instructions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入/输出：程序和磁盘、网络等外部设备交换数据的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Input/Output is data movement between a program and external devices such as disks or networks.

why: 相邻记录一起读，就可以把它们成块压缩。磁盘带宽常比 CPU 更贵，所以压缩能让整体查询更快。
why_en: Block compression helps because the engine trades a little CPU for fewer disk bytes on nearby records.
optionExplanations: 相邻 key-value 常被一起读到，按块压缩能减少实际读写的磁盘字节数，只花一点 CPU 去解压，磁盘带宽比 CPU 更紧张时这笔账划算。
按块压缩跟 key 是否排序无关，SSTable 本身依然要求 key 有序，这个说法不成立。
压缩不会消除后台合并，SSTable 之间该做的 compaction 照样要做，只是压缩发生在块内部。
optionExplanations_en: Since nearby key-value pairs are usually read together, block compression cuts the actual disk bytes read and written at the cost of a little CPU to decompress — worth it when disk bandwidth is tighter than CPU.
Block compression has nothing to do with whether keys are sorted; SSTables still require sorted keys regardless, so this claim doesn't hold.
Compression doesn't remove the need for background compaction between SSTables — that still has to happen, just on compressed blocks.

q: 按 LSM 写入路径排序。
q_en: Order the LSM write path.
scenario: 一个 LSM 型存储引擎接收乱序写入，但磁盘段必须按 key 有序。
scenario_en: An LSM-style engine receives writes in arbitrary order, but on-disk segments must be sorted by key.
steps: 后台把多个 SSTable 归并压缩，丢弃旧值。
写入先进内存有序结构 memtable。
memtable 达阈值后刷成新的 SSTable。
读取先查 memtable，再查新到旧的 SSTable。

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志结构合并树：把写入缓存在内存并批量刷成有序不可变文件的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Log-Structured Merge-tree buffers writes in memory and flushes immutable sorted files that are merged later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序字符串表：按 key 有序的不可变段文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Sorted String Table is an immutable segment file sorted by key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存中的有序写缓冲，达到阈值后刷成 SSTable。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is an in-memory sorted write buffer that later flushes to an SSTable.

diagram:
flowchart LR
Write[Write] --> Mem[memtable]
Mem --> Flush[flush]
Flush --> SST[SSTable]
SST --> Compact[compaction]
Read[Read] --> Mem
Read --> SST
why: LSM 用内存有序结构吸收乱序写，再批量刷成有序不可变文件。代价是读路径可能查多层，后台 compaction 要持续追上。
why_en: An LSM tree buffers random writes in a sorted memtable and flushes immutable SSTables, paying with multi-level reads and compaction work.

q: 按崩溃恢复链路排序。
q_en: Order the crash-recovery chain.
scenario: LSM 引擎的最新写入先在 memtable；机器可能在 flush 前崩溃。
scenario_en: In an LSM engine, the newest writes are in the memtable; the machine may crash before flush.
steps: 重启时重放 commit log，重建 memtable。
每次写入先追加到磁盘 commit log。
memtable 成功刷成 SSTable 后，对应 log 可丢弃。
写入同时更新内存 memtable。

termDefinitions.meaning: 提交日志：写入内存结构前后追加的持久记录，用于崩溃恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A commit log is a durable append-only record used to recover recent writes after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序字符串表：按 key 有序的不可变段文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Sorted String Table is an immutable segment file sorted by key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存中的有序写缓冲，达到阈值后刷成 SSTable。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is an in-memory sorted write buffer that later flushes to an SSTable.

why: commit log 只为恢复内存写缓冲存在；正常读写靠 memtable 和 SSTable。代价是每次写多一次顺序日志写入。
why_en: The commit log protects unflushed memtable writes by replaying them after a crash.

q: 哪种结构能减少无效磁盘读？
q_en: Which structure reduces unnecessary disk reads?
scenario: LSM 读一个不存在的 key 时，可能要从 memtable 查到最老 SSTable 才能确认不存在。
scenario_en: When an LSM reads a missing key, it may need to check the memtable and every SSTable before proving absence.
options: Bloom filter
随机 sleep
把所有 SSTable 改名
options_en: A Bloom filter.
Random sleep.
Rename all SSTables.
tradeoff: 少量内存/误报 vs 无效磁盘读取

termDefinitions.meaning: 布隆过滤器：内存高效的近似集合结构，可判断元素肯定不存在或可能存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a memory-efficient approximate set that says an item is definitely absent or possibly present.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志结构合并树：把写入缓存在内存并批量刷成有序不可变文件的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Log-Structured Merge-tree buffers writes in memory and flushes immutable sorted files that are merged later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序字符串表：按 key 有序的不可变段文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Sorted String Table is an immutable segment file sorted by key.

why: Bloom filter 能快速判断某个段肯定没有这个 key，从而跳过磁盘读取。它可能有误报，但不会把存在的 key 错判为肯定不存在。
why_en: A Bloom filter can rule out SSTables that definitely do not contain a key, reducing disk reads for misses.
whenOtherWins: 若几乎没有 miss 或过滤器内存太紧，Bloom filter 收益会变小。
optionExplanations: 查询先问 filter：答 no 就直接跳过这个段，答 maybe 才真去读盘，误报只多花一次读。
随机 sleep 只会让查询变慢，不会减少任何一次不必要的磁盘读取。
改 SSTable 的文件名不会改变它包不包含目标 key，跟减少无效读取没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Ask the filter first: a no skips the segment outright, a maybe costs one real disk read, and a false positive costs only that.
Randomly sleeping only slows the query down; it doesn't cut a single unnecessary disk read.
Renaming SSTables doesn't change whether they contain the target key, so it has nothing to do with reducing wasted reads.

q: 相比 hash 索引，LSM/SSTable 的优势是什么？
q_en: What advantage do LSM/SSTables have over hash indexes?
scenario: 产品要按 key 前缀扫描一段连续范围，数据远大于内存。
scenario_en: The product needs to scan a continuous key-prefix range, and the data is much larger than memory.
options: 磁盘段按 key 排序，范围扫描顺序进行
每个 key 都必须完整放在内存索引里
只能做单点精确查询
options_en: On-disk segments are sorted by key, so range scans are sequential.
Every key must live entirely in the in-memory index.
Only exact point lookups are possible.
tradeoff: 有序扫描 vs hash 点查

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志结构合并树：把写入缓存在内存并批量刷成有序不可变文件的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Log-Structured Merge-tree buffers writes in memory and flushes immutable sorted files that are merged later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序字符串表：按 key 有序的不可变段文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Sorted String Table is an immutable segment file sorted by key.

why: 排序是范围查询的关键。SSTable 可以从范围起点附近开始顺序扫，而 hash 索引没有自然顺序。
why_en: Sorted SSTables support efficient range scans because nearby keys are stored near each other.
whenOtherWins: 若只做点查且 key 目录可放内存，hash 索引可能更简单更快。
optionExplanations: 磁盘上的段本身按 key 排好序，扫一段连续范围只要从起点附近开始顺序读下去，不需要跳来跳去。
数据远大于内存时，要求每个 key 全在内存里根本做不到，这也是 hash 索引不适合这种规模的原因之一。
排序段照样能做单点精确查询，说它只能做点查是低估了它，也没答到范围扫描这个真正的差别上。
optionExplanations_en: On-disk segments are already sorted by key, so scanning a contiguous range just means reading sequentially from near the start point, no jumping around needed.
With data much larger than memory, requiring every key to be entirely in memory is simply impossible, which is one reason a hash index doesn't fit this scale.
Sorted segments can still do exact point lookups too, so claiming they're limited to that undersells them and misses the real range-scan advantage being asked about.

q: 这描述的是哪类索引？
q_en: Which index does this describe?
scenario: 一个索引把数据分成固定大小页面；根页指向子页，子页负责连续 key 范围。
scenario_en: An index splits data into fixed-size pages; the root page points to child pages, and each child owns a continuous key range.
options: B-tree
append-only hash log
bitmap cube
options_en: B-tree.
Append-only hash log.
Bitmap cube.
why: B-tree 用固定页和范围边界组织有序 key，查找时从根页一路走到叶页。它广泛用于关系数据库索引。
why_en: A B-tree organizes sorted keys into fixed pages and follows page references from root to leaf.
optionExplanations: 根页指向子页、子页负责连续 key 范围、数据切成固定大小页面，这正是 B-tree 组织有序数据的经典结构。
append-only hash log 是靠追加写文件加内存 hash 表定位的，没有根页指向子页这种分层结构。
bitmap cube 是分析场景里按维度预聚合的结构，跟固定页面加根子页指针的描述对不上。
optionExplanations_en: A root page pointing to child pages that each own a contiguous key range, all organized into fixed-size pages, is exactly the classic B-tree structure.
An append-only hash log locates data via an append log plus an in-memory hash table; it has no root-to-child page hierarchy.
A bitmap cube is a pre-aggregated structure for analytics by dimension, which doesn't match a description of fixed pages with root-to-child pointers.

q: 按 B-tree 插入分裂顺序排列。
q_en: Order the B-tree insert split steps.
scenario: B-tree 叶页已满，插入的新 key 落在这个页的范围内。
scenario_en: A B-tree leaf page is full, and a new key belongs in that page's range.
steps: 把满页拆成两个半满页。
从根页按 key 范围找到目标叶页。
在父页写入新的范围边界和页面引用。
把新 key 放入对应的新叶页。
diagram:
flowchart LR
Find[Find leaf] --> Split[Split full page]
Split --> Insert[Insert key]
Insert --> Parent[Update parent boundary]
why: B-tree 通过页分裂保持平衡，查找高度维持在对数级。风险是分裂要改多个页，崩溃恢复必须保护中间状态。
why_en: B-tree page splits keep the tree balanced, but they touch multiple pages and need crash protection.

q: 为什么需要 WAL？
q_en: Why does it need a WAL?
scenario: B-tree 插入导致叶页和父页都要覆盖写；机器可能只写完一部分就崩溃。
scenario_en: A B-tree insert overwrites both leaf and parent pages; the machine may crash after writing only some of them.
options: 崩溃后用日志把树恢复到一致状态
让 B-tree 变成列式存储
避免任何页面写入
options_en: To restore the tree to a consistent state after a crash.
To turn the B-tree into columnar storage.
To avoid all page writes.
tradeoff: 原地更新效率 vs 恢复日志成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 预写日志：修改数据页前先持久记录修改，用于崩溃恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Write-Ahead Log records changes durably before data pages are modified, enabling crash recovery.

why: B-tree 原地覆盖多个页，中途崩溃会留下不一致引用。WAL 先记录修改意图，重启后可 redo 到一致状态。
why_en: A WAL protects multi-page in-place updates by replaying logged changes after a crash.
optionExplanations: 顺序是先 fsync 日志再改页面；重启时重做日志尾部，半写完的页分裂就能被补齐。
WAL 跟把 B-tree 改造成列式存储完全是两回事，它解决的是崩溃恢复问题，不是存储布局问题。
WAL 不是为了避免页面写入，它本身也要写日志，只是让崩溃后的恢复有据可依。
optionExplanations_en: The order is fsync the log first, then touch the pages; on restart the tail is redone so a half-finished page split gets completed.
A WAL has nothing to do with turning a B-tree into columnar storage; it solves crash recovery, not storage layout.
A WAL isn't meant to avoid page writes at all — it writes its own log — it just gives recovery something reliable to replay after a crash.

q: 哪种 B-tree 变体思路合适？
q_en: Which B-tree variant idea fits?
scenario: 数据库希望避免原地覆盖页面，并让读事务能继续看到旧版本树。
scenario_en: A database wants to avoid overwriting pages in place and let read transactions keep seeing the old tree version.
options: copy-on-write 页面
删除所有父指针
把每个页的大小都改成 1 字节
options_en: Copy-on-write pages.
Delete all parent pointers.
Change every page size down to one byte.
tradeoff: 快照友好 vs 额外写入/回收
why: copy-on-write 把修改页写到新位置，再更新父链指向新页。旧页可供旧快照读取，但会增加写入和空间回收工作。
why_en: Copy-on-write writes modified pages elsewhere and links parents to the new version, which helps snapshots at the cost of extra writes.
whenOtherWins: 若写放大和空间回收比快照读更重要，传统 WAL 覆盖页可能更合适。
optionExplanations: 父链一路改到根，最后一次原子写换掉根指针；换根前开始的读事务仍指着旧根。
删除所有父指针会让树完全无法从根导航到叶子，跟“避免原地覆盖”这个目标毫无关系。
把页大小改成 1 字节只会让页数量暴增、管理开销爆炸，不解决原地覆盖或旧版本可见性的问题。
optionExplanations_en: The parent chain is rewritten up to the root and swapped in one atomic write; readers that started earlier still point at the old root.
Deleting all parent pointers would make the tree impossible to navigate from root to leaf at all, which has nothing to do with avoiding in-place overwrites.
Shrinking the page size to one byte would just explode the page count and management overhead, without addressing in-place overwrites or old-version visibility.

q: 哪些是常见 B-tree 优化思路？
q_en: Which are common B-tree optimization ideas?
scenario: 一个成熟 B-tree 实现要减少树高、优化范围扫描，并降低恢复复杂度。
scenario_en: A mature B-tree implementation wants to reduce tree height, improve range scans, and reduce recovery complexity.
options: 内部页只存足够区分范围的短 key
叶页加左右兄弟指针
尽量让相邻叶页物理接近
每次读都全表扫描
options_en: Store abbreviated separator keys in internal pages.
Add sibling pointers between leaf pages.
Try to place neighboring leaves physically nearby.
Full-scan the table for every read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入/输出：程序和磁盘、网络等外部设备交换数据的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Input/Output is data movement between a program and external devices such as disks or networks.

why: 这些优化都围绕减少树层数或让有序扫描更顺。全表扫描不是 B-tree 优化，而是索引没发挥作用。
why_en: B-tree optimizations aim to reduce tree height or make ordered scans smoother, not to fall back to full scans.
optionExplanations: 内部页只存足够区分子树范围的短 key，能让每一页容纳更多分支，从而降低整棵树的高度。
叶页之间加左右兄弟指针，做范围扫描时不用每次都回到父页再往下找，可以直接沿叶子链滑过去。
让相邻叶页在磁盘上物理靠近，范围扫描时更容易变成顺序 I/O，减少随机寻道。
每次读都全表扫描等于完全放弃了索引的作用，这是索引失效的表现，不是一种优化手段。
optionExplanations_en: Storing only abbreviated separator keys in internal pages lets each page hold more branches, which reduces the overall height of the tree.
Adding sibling pointers between leaf pages lets a range scan slide across the leaf chain directly, instead of climbing back up to the parent each time.
Placing neighboring leaves physically close on disk turns range scans closer to sequential I/O, cutting down on random seeks.
Full-scanning on every read means the index isn't being used at all — that's a sign the index failed, not an optimization technique.

q: 优先评估哪类索引？
q_en: Which index family should you evaluate first?
scenario: 工作负载有高吞吐随机写，读取可以容忍偶尔查多层并依赖后台 compaction。
scenario_en: The workload has high-throughput random writes, and reads can tolerate checking multiple levels with background compaction.
options: LSM-tree
只读数据立方体
无索引堆文件
options_en: An LSM-tree.
A read-only data cube.
An unindexed heap file.
tradeoff: 随机写吞吐 vs 读放大/compaction

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志结构合并树：把写入缓存在内存并批量刷成有序不可变文件的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Log-Structured Merge-tree buffers writes in memory and flushes immutable sorted files that are merged later.

why: LSM 把随机写变成内存缓冲和顺序刷盘，通常更适合高写吞吐。代价是 compaction、读放大和尾延迟需要监控。
why_en: An LSM-tree often fits high random-write throughput because it turns writes into buffered sequential flushes.
whenOtherWins: 若读延迟可预测性和事务范围锁更重要，B-tree 往往更稳。
optionExplanations: 写先进 memtable，满了整段顺序 flush 成 SSTable，磁盘上几乎没有随机写。
只读数据立方体是分析场景的预聚合结构，处理不了持续的高吞吐随机写入。
无索引堆文件没有任何加速读取的结构，写入虽然简单，但完全没利用到排序或索引带来的读取优势。
optionExplanations_en: Writes land in a memtable and flush as whole sorted segments, so the disk sees almost no random writes.
A read-only data cube is a pre-aggregated analytics structure; it can't absorb sustained high-throughput random writes at all.
An unindexed heap file has no structure to speed up reads at all — writes are simple, but there's no benefit from sorting or indexing.

q: 这说明 LSM 的什么代价？
q_en: What cost of LSM does this show?
scenario: LSM 存储平均延迟正常，但 p99 偶尔很高；排查发现后台 compaction 正在抢磁盘。
scenario_en: An LSM store has normal average latency, but p99 spikes; investigation finds background compaction competing for disk.
options: compaction 可能影响尾延迟
LSM 结构根本无法处理高写入负载
排序段不能做范围查询
options_en: Compaction can hurt tail latency.
An LSM structure simply cannot handle heavy write load.
Sorted segments cannot do range scans.
tradeoff: 高写吞吐 vs 尾延迟可预测性

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志结构合并树：把写入缓存在内存并批量刷成有序不可变文件的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Log-Structured Merge-tree buffers writes in memory and flushes immutable sorted files that are merged later.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位：99% 请求快于这个阈值，1% 请求更慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The 99th percentile is the threshold below which 99% of requests complete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入/输出：程序和磁盘、网络等外部设备交换数据的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Input/Output is data movement between a program and external devices such as disks or networks.

why: LSM 的后台合并通常不太影响平均值，但会和前台请求争 I/O，拉高高百分位。容量和 compaction 速度要跟写入速率匹配。
why_en: LSM compaction may barely move averages but still compete for I/O and raise high-percentile latency.
optionExplanations: 后台 compaction 要跟前台请求抢磁盘 I/O，平均延迟可能没受什么影响，但会把少数请求的等待时间拉得很高，正是这里看到的 p99 尖峰。
LSM 完全能处理写入，甚至是它的强项，这个说法跟场景描述矛盾。
排序段本身很适合范围查询，这个说法答非所问，跟这里 p99 变高的原因无关。
optionExplanations_en: Background compaction competes with foreground requests for disk I/O, so the average may barely move while a small fraction of requests wait much longer — exactly the p99 spike seen here.
LSM handling writes well is actually its strength, so this claim contradicts the scenario.
Sorted segments being good for range queries doesn't answer the question and has nothing to do with why p99 spiked here.

q: 哪类索引更有利？
q_en: Which index family is more favorable?
scenario: 数据库要在 key 范围上加锁来实现事务隔离；每个 key 在索引里只有一个明确位置更方便。
scenario_en: A database needs key-range locks for transaction isolation; it helps if each key has one clear place in the index.
options: B-tree
多层未压缩 LSM 段
无序日志加 hash
options_en: B-tree.
Many uncompacted LSM levels.
An unordered log with a hash index.
tradeoff: 事务范围锁便利 vs 写入优化
why: B-tree 中每个 key 在树里有明确位置，范围锁可以挂在树范围上。LSM 可能有多个版本分布在多层，事务实现要处理更多细节。
why_en: B-trees are convenient for key-range locking because each key has a clear place in the index.
whenOtherWins: 若主要目标是高写吞吐且事务隔离较弱，LSM 会更有吸引力。
optionExplanations: B-tree 里每个 key 在树中都有明确唯一的位置，范围锁可以直接挂在树的某段范围上，事务隔离实现起来更直接。
未压缩的多层 LSM 段里，同一个 key 的不同版本可能分布在好几层，事务要跟踪的位置和版本更多，实现更复杂。
无序日志加 hash 索引连 key 的顺序都没有，更谈不上在一段范围上方便地加锁。
optionExplanations_en: In a B-tree, every key has one clear location in the tree, so a range lock can attach directly to a span of the tree, which makes transaction isolation more straightforward to implement.
In uncompacted multi-level LSM segments, different versions of the same key can be spread across several levels, giving a transaction more positions and versions to track.
An unordered log with a hash index doesn't even preserve key order, so there's no natural range to lock against in the first place.

q: secondary index 与主键索引的关键差别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between a secondary index and a primary-key index?
scenario: 订单表主键唯一，但按 customer_id 查订单时，一个 customer_id 会对应很多订单。
scenario_en: An orders table has a unique primary key, but a lookup by customer_id maps one customer to many orders.
options: secondary index 的 key 可重复
secondary index 不能用 B-tree
secondary index 只能存在内存
options_en: Secondary-index keys may repeat.
A secondary index cannot use a B-tree.
A secondary index must live only in memory.
why: 二级索引常把非唯一字段映射到一组行 ID，或把行 ID 拼进 key 让组合 key 唯一。它对 join 和过滤很关键。
why_en: A secondary index often maps a non-unique value to many row IDs, making joins and filters efficient.
optionExplanations: 多个订单可以共享同一个 customer_id，所以二级索引的 key 允许重复，这正是它和主键索引最直接的区别。
实现上仍是 B-tree，只是叶子挂的是一串行 ID 列表（postings），而不是单条记录。
二级索引和主键索引一样可以持久化到磁盘，并不要求只能存在内存里。
optionExplanations_en: Many orders can share the same customer_id, so secondary-index keys are allowed to repeat — that's exactly the direct difference from a primary-key index.
It is still a B-tree; the leaf just holds a postings list of row IDs instead of a single record.
A secondary index can be persisted to disk just like a primary index; it isn't required to live only in memory.

q: heap file 和 clustered index 的取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the heap file versus clustered index tradeoff?
scenario: 表有多个二级索引；读路径常从索引找到行，再去取完整记录。
scenario_en: A table has several secondary indexes; reads often use an index to find a row and then fetch the full record.
options: heap 不复制行，clustered 把行放进主索引
clustered index 不存行数据，只保存行指针
heap file 会自动按主键排序支持范围扫描
options_en: A heap avoids copying rows; a clustered index keeps rows in the primary index.
A clustered index stores no row data and only keeps row pointers.
A heap file is automatically sorted by primary key for range scans.
tradeoff: 减少数据复制 vs 减少读跳转
why: heap 把行存一处，多个索引只存引用；clustered index 把行数据和主索引放一起，点读更少跳。代价是复制和更新路径不同。
why_en: A heap stores rows once and indexes point to them, while a clustered index stores row data in the primary index for faster primary-key reads.
optionExplanations: 多个二级索引只存指向同一行的指针；clustered 少一次随机 I/O，但行变长时会页分裂。
恰恰相反，clustered 索引把完整行数据存进主索引本身，而不是只存指针。
heap file 本身没有天然顺序，不会自动按主键排序，想按范围扫描还是要靠额外的索引。
optionExplanations_en: Several secondary indexes just store pointers to the same row; a clustered index saves one random I/O but splits pages when a row grows.
A clustered index is precisely the one that stores the full row data inside the primary index itself, not just pointers — this option has it backwards.
A heap file has no inherent order and isn't automatically sorted by primary key; range scans still need a separate index.

q: 为什么 covering index 有用？
q_en: Why is a covering index useful?
scenario: 查询只需要 order_id、status、updated_at；这些列已经包含在一个索引里。
scenario_en: A query needs only order_id, status, and updated_at; those columns are already included in one index.
options: 查询可只读索引，不回表取完整行
它会删除主表
它让写入操作完全没有任何成本
options_en: The query can read only the index without fetching the full row.
It deletes the base table.
It makes writes completely free of cost.
tradeoff: 读路径少跳转 vs 写入/存储开销

termDefinitions.meaning: 输入/输出：程序和磁盘、网络等外部设备交换数据的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Input/Output is data movement between a program and external devices such as disks or networks.

why: covering index 把查询需要的列放进索引，命中后不用再跳到 heap 或 clustered 行。代价是索引更大，写入要维护更多副本。
why_en: A covering index answers a query from the index alone, trading faster reads for larger indexes and write maintenance.
whenOtherWins: 若查询总要读完整行且写很多，普通索引加回表可能更省。
optionExplanations: 执行计划里会显示 index only scan，完全不碰主表；代价是这几列在索引里又存了一份。
它只是把几列数据多存了一份，跟删除主表毫无关系，主表照样存在。
写入这些被索引覆盖的列时，索引也要跟着更新，写入并不是无成本的。
optionExplanations_en: The plan shows an index-only scan that never touches the table; the price is a second copy of those columns.
A covering index just stores a few extra columns; it has nothing to do with deleting the base table, which still exists.
Writing to the columns the index covers still has to update the index too, so writes are not free.

q: 为什么这个索引帮不上太多？
q_en: Why does this index help little?
scenario: 有索引 (last_name, first_name)。查询只按 first_name 过滤，last_name 不给条件。
scenario_en: There is an index on (last_name, first_name). A query filters only by first_name and gives no last_name condition.
options: 组合索引按最左前缀排序
B-tree 不能存字符串
索引只能用于排序不能过滤
options_en: A concatenated index is ordered by the leftmost prefix.
B-trees cannot store strings.
Indexes can only sort, not filter.
tradeoff: 组合键顺序 vs 查询谓词顺序
why: (last_name, first_name) 先按姓分组，再在同姓内按名排序。没有姓条件时，所有姓里同名的人分散在各处。
why_en: A concatenated index is useful by its leading fields; without last_name, first_name values are scattered across the index.
optionExplanations: 查 first_name='John' 时只能全扫：John 分散在 Smith、Lee、Wang 各个区间，没有连续范围可 seek。
B-tree 本身完全能存字符串 key，这个说法跟索引帮不上忙的原因没有关系。
索引不仅能排序，也能用来过滤，只是这里过滤条件没用上索引的最左前缀，这个说法把索引的能力说错了。
optionExplanations_en: Searching first_name='John' can only scan: the Johns sit inside the Smith, Lee, and Wang ranges, so there is no contiguous range to seek.
A B-tree can absolutely store string keys; that's unrelated to why this particular index doesn't help here.
Indexes can filter as well as sort — the real issue is that the filter here skips the leftmost prefix, so this option mischaracterizes what indexes can do.

q: 哪类索引更自然？
q_en: Which index is more natural?
scenario: 餐馆搜索要找地图矩形内的点，同时约束 latitude 和 longitude 两个范围。
scenario_en: Restaurant search must find points inside a map rectangle, constraining both latitude and longitude ranges.
options: R-tree 或空间索引
只按 latitude 的单列 B-tree
只按名称全文搜索
options_en: An R-tree or spatial index.
A single-column B-tree on latitude only.
Full-text search on names only.
tradeoff: 单维有序扫描 vs 多维剪枝

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种空间索引结构，用边界框组织多维对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An R-tree is a spatial index that organizes multidimensional objects by bounding boxes.

why: 二维范围不能靠一个单列有序索引同时裁掉南北和东西范围。空间索引能按多维区域缩小候选。
why_en: A spatial index fits two-dimensional range search because one single-column order cannot prune both dimensions well.
whenOtherWins: 若只按单一维度过滤，普通 B-tree/LSM 单列索引通常足够。
optionExplanations: 矩形范围要同时约束纬度和经度两个维度，R-tree 这类空间索引能按多维区域裁剪候选，一次查询同时满足两个方向的范围。
只按 latitude 建的单列 B-tree 只能裁剪南北方向，经度范围还是要逐条过滤，起不到多维裁剪的作用。
只按名称做全文搜索完全没用到坐标信息，找不到地图矩形范围内的点。
optionExplanations_en: A map rectangle constrains latitude and longitude at the same time, and an R-tree or spatial index can prune candidates across both dimensions in one query.
A single-column B-tree on latitude only prunes the north-south direction; longitude still has to be filtered row by row, so it doesn't give real multidimensional pruning.
Full-text search on names alone ignores coordinates entirely and can't find points inside a map rectangle.

q: 哪类索引思路更合适？
q_en: Which indexing idea fits better?
scenario: 搜索框要容忍用户把单词拼错一个字符；普通有序索引只能做精确或范围匹配。
scenario_en: A search box should tolerate a one-character typo; a normal sorted index supports exact or range matches.
options: 基于编辑距离的 fuzzy index
只用主键 B-tree
把所有的词都转成同一个 key 存储
options_en: A fuzzy index based on edit distance.
Only a primary-key B-tree.
Turn every term into one and the same key.
tradeoff: 精确匹配速度 vs 相似匹配能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用全文搜索索引库，Elasticsearch 和 Solr 使用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lucene is a full-text search indexing library used by Elasticsearch and Solr.

why: 模糊搜索需要按相似度找词，而不是只按排序相邻找词。像 Lucene 这类搜索引擎会用专门结构处理编辑距离。
why_en: Fuzzy search needs similarity-aware lookup, not just exact or sorted key lookup.
whenOtherWins: 若只需要精确 key 查找或范围扫描，普通有序索引更简单。
optionExplanations: 容忍拼错一个字符需要按相似度找词，基于编辑距离的 fuzzy index 正是为这种近似匹配设计的结构。
只用主键 B-tree 只能做精确或范围匹配，拼错一个字符就找不到目标词，完全不满足模糊匹配的需求。
把所有词转成同一个 key 会让不同的词互相混淆，反而丢失了区分能力，不是模糊匹配该有的做法。
optionExplanations_en: Tolerating a single misspelled character needs similarity-aware lookup, which is exactly what an edit-distance-based fuzzy index is built for.
A primary-key B-tree only supports exact or range matching, so a single typo would miss the target word entirely, failing the fuzzy-match requirement.
Mapping every word to the same key would collapse distinct words together, losing the ability to distinguish them at all — the opposite of fuzzy matching.

q: 持久化该怎么做？
q_en: How can durability be provided?
scenario: 服务希望读写都从内存数据结构完成，但重启后不能丢掉已确认写入。
scenario_en: A service wants reads and writes to use in-memory structures, but acknowledged writes must survive restart.
options: 写变更日志或快照，重启时加载
只相信进程内变量，不落盘
禁止任何备份和快照
options_en: Write a change log or snapshots and reload them on restart.
Trust only in-process variables and never persist.
Forbid all backups and snapshots.
tradeoff: 内存访问速度 vs 恢复持久性

termDefinitions.meaning: 随机访问内存：断电易失但访问很快的主存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random Access Memory is fast volatile main memory.

why: 内存数据库仍可把磁盘当恢复介质：正常读走内存，写入追加日志或定期快照。代价是恢复时间和持久化策略要设计。
why_en: An in-memory database can still be durable by logging or snapshotting changes and rebuilding memory on restart.
whenOtherWins: 若数据只是可丢缓存，重启丢失可以接受，持久化可弱化。
optionExplanations: 正常读写照样从内存结构完成，同时把变更写进日志或定期打快照，重启时用它们重建内存状态，就不会丢掉已确认的写入。
只信任进程内变量意味着进程一重启数据就全没了，跟“重启后不能丢数据”的要求直接冲突。
禁止任何备份等于放弃了持久化能力，跟这里明确要求的“不能丢已确认写入”背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Normal reads and writes still go through the in-memory structure, while a change log or periodic snapshots record enough to rebuild that state on restart without losing confirmed writes.
Trusting only process-local variables means the data vanishes the moment the process restarts, directly conflicting with the requirement not to lose data after a restart.
Forbidding all backups gives up any durability at all, which goes directly against the stated requirement not to lose confirmed writes.

q: 性能差距更可能来自哪里？
q_en: Where is the performance gap more likely to come from?
scenario: 某数据库数据集完全被操作系统 page cache 命中，但内存数据库仍可能更快。
scenario_en: A database's dataset is fully served from the OS page cache, yet an in-memory database may still be faster.
options: 避免把内存结构编码成磁盘页格式
内存数据库永远不写磁盘
page cache 会故意变慢
options_en: Avoiding the overhead of encoding in-memory structures into disk-page formats.
In-memory databases never write to disk.
The page cache intentionally slows down.
tradeoff: 磁盘布局兼容性 vs 内存结构效率
why: 如果磁盘读已被缓存，优势不只是少读磁盘，而是少了围绕磁盘布局设计的数据结构开销。内存模型也能提供更丰富的数据结构。
why_en: When disk reads are already cached, in-memory databases can still win by avoiding disk-layout overheads.

rows: 避免把内存结构编码成磁盘页格式
避免把内存结构编码…场景
避免把内存结构编码成磁…成本
内存数据库永远不写磁盘
内存数据库永远不写…场景
内存数据库永远不写磁盘成本

optionExplanations: 磁盘数据虽然已经被 page cache 命中，但磁盘型数据库仍要按磁盘页格式编码数据结构，内存数据库省掉了这层编码解码开销，还能用更丰富的数据结构。
内存数据库通常仍然会写磁盘做持久化，只是正常读写路径不依赖它，这个说法过于绝对。
page cache 命中本身不会主动变慢，它只是没有消除数据结构本身围绕磁盘布局设计带来的开销。
optionExplanations_en: Even with disk reads already hitting the page cache, a disk-oriented database still has to encode its structures into a disk-page format; an in-memory database skips that encoding overhead and can use richer structures.
An in-memory database usually still writes to disk for durability, just not on the normal read/write path — so this claim is too absolute.
A page-cache hit doesn't get slower on its own; it just doesn't remove the overhead baked into structures designed around disk layout.

q: 这种思路叫什么更合适？
q_en: What idea fits this approach?
scenario: 内存数据库的数据偶尔超过 RAM；冷记录可以落盘，热点记录仍在内存里服务。
scenario_en: An in-memory database sometimes exceeds RAM; cold records can move to disk while hot records remain in memory.
options: anti-caching
把所有二级索引删除掉
全表随机排序
options_en: Anti-caching.
Drop every secondary index.
Randomly sorting the table.
tradeoff: 内存模型速度 vs 超内存容量

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存数据库把冷记录主动换出到磁盘，需要时再取回的技术。
