The specific values of n, w, and r affect read freshness and conflict probability, but they don't make conflict handling disappear entirely — this claim is too absolute.

q: 哪些情况会削弱 quorum 读到最新值的直觉？
q_en: Which cases weaken the intuition that quorums always read the latest value?
why: quorum 交集是有用直觉，不是完整线性一致证明；并发、部分失败和 sloppy 写都会让读语义变复杂。
why_en: Quorum overlap is useful intuition, not a full linearizability proof; concurrency, partial failure, and sloppy writes complicate reads.
scenario: leaderless 数据库配置满足 w+r>n，团队以为这等于线性一致读。
scenario_en: A leaderless database has w+r>n, and the team assumes this means linearizable reads.
options: sloppy quorum 写到非 home 节点
并发写没有自然先后
写失败但部分副本已落盘
所有副本都在同一机架
options_en: A sloppy quorum writes to non-home nodes
Concurrent writes have no natural order
A failed write may land on some replicas
All replicas are in one rack
tradeoff: 可调可用性 vs 强一致保证

termDefinitions.meaning: Quorum 是读或写必须得到响应的最小副本数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas that must respond to a read or write.

optionExplanations: sloppy quorum 允许写落到不属于这个 key 正常归属组的节点上，读 quorum 交集的前提被打破了，读到的不一定是最新写。
并发写之间没有天然的先后顺序，读 quorum 交集只能保证读到某次成功写，不能保证读到“最新”这个说法本身有意义的那一次。
一次写只成功了一部分副本、之后失败，这些部分落盘的数据仍然可能影响读 quorum 看到的结果，跟“简单线性一致”的直觉不符。
所有副本在同一机架只是物理部署位置，不会削弱 quorum 交集这条逻辑保证本身，它跟这里讨论的问题无关。
optionExplanations_en: A sloppy quorum lets writes land on nodes outside the key's normal home set, breaking the assumption that the read quorum overlaps with the actual successful-write set, so a read isn't guaranteed to see the latest write.
Concurrent writes have no natural order between them, so read-quorum overlap can only guarantee seeing some successful write, not necessarily the one meaningfully called latest.
A write that only partially succeeded before failing can still leave data on some replicas that affects what a read quorum sees, which doesn't match the simple linearizability intuition.
All replicas being in one rack is just a physical placement detail; it doesn't weaken the logical guarantee of quorum overlap and is unrelated to the issue being discussed here.

q: leader-based 复制为什么更容易监控 lag？
q_en: Why is leader-based replication easier to monitor for lag?
why: 单主复制有统一日志顺序，leader 位置减 follower 位置就是落后量；leaderless 没有这么简单的全局顺序。
why_en: Single-leader replication has a shared log order, so subtracting follower position from leader position estimates lag.
scenario: 运维要报警：某个 follower 落后 leader 超过阈值就通知。
scenario_en: Operations wants an alert when a follower lags behind the leader beyond a threshold.
options: 同一复制日志位置
每个写都没有顺序编号
只能靠用户投诉抽样
必须读完所有业务对象
options_en: A shared replication-log position
Every write has no ordering number
Only sample user complaints
Read every business object
whenOtherWins: leaderless 系统需要按版本分布或采样估计 staleness，不能只看一个日志差值。
tradeoff: 统一顺序可观测 vs 无主灵活性
optionExplanations: 单主复制下所有写都经过同一条日志、有统一的顺序编号，leader 的日志位置减去 follower 的日志位置就直接是它落后了多少。
每个写恰恰是带顺序编号的，这也是能算出落后量的前提，这个说法说反了。
靠用户投诉抽样是被动、粗糙的做法，单主复制其实有更直接的办法，不需要靠这种间接信号。
监控 lag 只需要比较日志位置这类元数据，不需要真的把所有业务对象内容读一遍。
optionExplanations_en: With single-leader replication, every write goes through the same ordered log, so subtracting the follower's log position from the leader's directly gives how far behind it is.
Writes are precisely given ordering numbers, which is exactly what makes computing the lag possible — this option has it backwards.
Relying on sampled user complaints is a passive, imprecise signal; single-leader replication actually has a much more direct way to measure lag.
Monitoring lag only requires comparing lightweight metadata like log positions, not actually reading through every business object's content.

q: leaderless 只靠 read repair 的可观测风险是什么？
q_en: What observability risk appears when leaderless systems rely only on read repair?
why: read repair 由读取触发，冷 key 不读就不修；没有 anti-entropy 时，staleness 很难给出上限。
why_en: Read repair is triggered by reads, so cold keys may stay stale and staleness can be hard to bound without anti-entropy.
scenario: 某些历史订单 key 几乎不会被读取，但其中一个副本曾经宕机漏掉更新。
scenario_en: Some historical order keys are rarely read, and one replica missed an update during an outage.
options: 旧副本可能长期没人发现
每次后台都会立即扫描修复
quorum 公式会删除旧值
客户端会自动知道最大落后时间
options_en: A stale replica may remain undiscovered for a long time
A background scan repairs it immediately every time
The quorum formula deletes old values
Clients automatically know the maximum staleness
tradeoff: 读时修复省后台成本 vs 冷数据陈旧

termDefinitions.meaning: Read repair 是读多个副本时发现旧值，并顺手把新值写回旧副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read repair fixes stale replicas when a multi-replica read discovers a newer value.

termDefinitions.meaning: Anti-entropy 是后台比较副本差异并补齐缺失数据的同步过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Anti-entropy is a background process that compares replicas and copies missing data.

optionExplanations: read repair 只在有人读这个 key 时才触发，几乎没人读的历史订单副本一旦漏掉了一次更新，可能长期没人发现，也没有其它机制主动去修它。
read repair 是被动触发的，不是每次后台自动扫描修复，冷 key 没人读就不会被立刻发现和修复。
quorum 公式只是判断读写集合有没有交集，它不会主动删除任何旧值，这个说法不成立。
客户端不知道某个副本落后了多久；缺少后台比对修复机制时，staleness 上限给不出保证。
optionExplanations_en: Read repair only fires when someone reads that key, so a historical order replica that almost never gets read can miss an update and stay stale for a long time with nothing else to catch it.
Read repair is reactive, not a proactive background scan on its own; a cold key that no one reads won't get caught or fixed automatically.
The quorum formula only checks whether the read and write sets overlap; it doesn't actively delete any old value, so this claim doesn't hold.
The client has no idea how far behind a given replica is, and without anti-entropy as a backstop, there's no real bound you can put on staleness.

q: 网络分区时 sloppy quorum 提高了什么？
q_en: What does sloppy quorum improve during a network partition?
why: sloppy quorum 牺牲传统 quorum 的 home 节点交集，换取分区期间仍能把写保存到若干可达节点。
why_en: Sloppy quorum trades home-replica overlap for the ability to durably accept writes on reachable nodes.
scenario: 客户端够不到某个 key 的 home 副本组，但还能连到集群里其它节点，业务更在乎继续接写。
scenario_en: A client cannot reach the home replicas for a key but can reach other cluster nodes, and write availability matters most.
options: 把写临时放到可达非 home 节点
强制等待 home 节点恢复后再写
把读写都路由到 leader
删除该 key 的副本限制
options_en: Temporarily write to reachable non-home nodes
Force writes to wait until the home node recovers.
Route reads and writes to a leader
Remove replica placement rules
whenOtherWins: 如果必须让 quorum 读立刻看到最新写，严格 home quorum 更合适。
tradeoff: 写可用性 vs 读到最新的保证

termDefinitions.meaning: Quorum 是读或写必须得到响应的最小副本数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas that must respond to a read or write.

termDefinitions.meaning: Hinted handoff 是临时节点代收写入，目标节点恢复后再交还。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hinted handoff stores a write temporarily on another node and later hands it to the home replica.

optionExplanations: 够不到 home 副本组时，写被临时放到还连得上的其它节点，先把写保住而不是直接失败。
强制等 home 节点恢复正是这个机制想避免的，那样分区期间就完全没法接写了。
它讨论的是无主架构里写去哪存，跟把读写路由到某个 leader 不是一回事。
它只是临时放宽写落在哪个节点，并没有改动副本数量或分布这些规则本身。
optionExplanations_en: When the home replica group is unreachable, sloppy quorum lets the write land temporarily on whatever cluster nodes are still reachable, so the write gets saved instead of failing just because the usual few nodes can't be reached.
Forcing a wait for home replicas to recover is exactly what sloppy quorum is trying to avoid — that would mean no writes at all during the partition.
Sloppy quorum is about where a write can land in a leaderless architecture, not about routing reads and writes to a leader, which doesn't exist here.
Sloppy quorum only temporarily relaxes which node a write can land on; it doesn't remove the replica placement rules themselves.

q: hinted handoff 的恢复链是什么？
q_en: What recovery chain does hinted handoff use?
why: hinted handoff 是 sloppy quorum 的收尾动作：先代收，网络恢复后再把写搬回负责该 key 的副本。
why_en: Hinted handoff completes sloppy quorum by moving temporary writes back to the home replicas after recovery.
scenario: 节点 A 暂时代替 home 节点 H 接收了某个 key 的写入，之后 H 恢复联通。
scenario_en: Node A temporarily accepts a write for home node H, and H later becomes reachable.
options: A 把暂存写交还给 H
A 永久成为该 key 的 home
H 删除所有旧版本
客户端必须重新提交写
options_en: A hands the temporary write back to H
A permanently becomes the key's home
H deletes all old versions
The client must resubmit the write
tradeoff: 临时代收可用性 vs 回放延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: Hinted handoff 是临时节点代收写入，目标节点恢复后再交还。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hinted handoff stores a write temporarily on another node and later hands it to the home replica.

termDefinitions.meaning: Quorum 是读或写必须得到响应的最小副本数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas that must respond to a read or write.

optionExplanations: A 只是临时代收，一旦 H 恢复联通，A 就会把这些暂存的写交还给 H，让数据最终回到真正负责这个 key 的副本组里。
A 只是临时顶替，网络恢复后写会被交还给 H，A 不会因为代收过就永久变成这个 key 的 home 节点。
H 恢复联通后要接收 A 交还的写并把它们并入自己的数据，而不是删掉自己已有的旧版本。
客户端在写入时就已经得到了成功响应，H 恢复后的补齐工作是 A 和 H 之间的事，不需要客户端重新提交。
optionExplanations_en: A is only holding the writes temporarily, and once H is reachable again, A hands those stashed writes back to H, so the data eventually lands where it's supposed to live.
A is just a stand-in; once the network recovers, the writes get handed back to H, and A doesn't permanently become that key's home just for having covered temporarily.
Once H is reachable again, it needs to receive and incorporate the writes A held onto, not delete its own existing older versions.
The client already got a success response at write time; reconciling once H recovers is a matter between A and H, not something the client needs to resubmit.

q: leaderless 多数据中心通常怎样隐藏跨洲延迟？
q_en: How does leaderless multi-datacenter replication usually hide cross-region latency?
why: 本地 quorum 把用户延迟限制在本地网络内，跨洲链路的慢和抖动由异步复制吸收。
why_en: A local quorum keeps user latency within the local network, while async replication absorbs cross-region delay.
scenario: Cassandra 风格集群跨两个数据中心，客户端希望本地写尽快返回，同时异地副本最终跟上。
scenario_en: A Cassandra-style cluster spans two datacenters, and clients want local writes to return quickly while remote replicas catch up.
options: 等待本地 quorum，远端异步复制
每次写都要等待全球所有副本都确认
只在夜间复制
把 n 限制为一个数据中心
options_en: Wait for a local quorum and replicate remote copies asynchronously
Each write waits for every replica worldwide to ack.
Replicate only at night
Limit n to one datacenter
whenOtherWins: 全球强一致业务要等待跨数据中心共识或集中写入，不能只靠本地 quorum。
tradeoff: 本地低延迟 vs 全球新鲜度

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 是面向高可用和分区扩展的分布式宽列数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a distributed wide-column database built for availability and partitioned scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: Quorum 是读或写必须得到响应的最小副本数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum number of replicas that must respond to a read or write.

optionExplanations: 客户端的写只需要等本地数据中心内凑够 quorum 就能返回，延迟被限制在本地网络里，跨洲那份副本靠异步复制慢慢跟上，用户完全感觉不到那段延迟。
每次写都等全球所有副本确认，会让每次写都要承受跨洲往返延迟，正是想要隐藏掉的那种延迟。
只在夜间复制会让白天写入的数据长时间只有本地一份，跨数据中心的一致性和可用性都得不到保障。
把 n 限制成一个数据中心，等于放弃了跨数据中心复制本身，不再是多数据中心场景。
optionExplanations_en: A client's write only has to wait for a quorum within the local datacenter to return, so latency stays inside the local network, while the remote copy catches up via async replication with the user never feeling that delay.
Waiting for every global replica on every write forces each write to pay the cross-continent round trip — exactly the latency this design is trying to hide.
Replicating only at night leaves daytime writes with just one local copy for hours, giving up consistency and availability across datacenters.
Limiting n to one datacenter effectively gives up cross-datacenter replication altogether, no longer a multi-datacenter setup at all.

q: leaderless 中并发写为什么没有自然先后？
q_en: Why do concurrent leaderless writes have no natural order?
why: 并发的定义是没有 happens-before 关系，不是墙钟时间完全相同；不同副本的到达顺序不能当全局事实。
why_en: Concurrency means no happens-before relationship, not necessarily identical wall-clock time.
scenario: 客户端 A 和 B 同时写同一个 key，彼此都没读到对方的写；不同副本收到顺序不同。
scenario_en: Clients A and B write the same key concurrently, neither saw the other write, and replicas receive them in different orders.
options: 两次写互相不知道对方
时间戳一定代表因果
先到某副本的写就是全局先发生
读 quorum 会自动合并业务语义
options_en: Neither write knew about the other
Timestamps always represent causality
The write that reaches one replica first happened first globally
Read quorums automatically merge business meaning
tradeoff: 无主并发接写 vs 全局顺序
optionExplanations: A 写的时候完全没看到 B 的写，B 写的时候也没看到 A 的写，两次写互相不知道对方的存在，这正是并发的定义——没有谁在因果上先于谁。
时间戳只是墙钟读数，不同机器的时钟本身可能有偏差，不能直接当成谁先谁后的因果证据。
某个副本先收到哪次写只取决于网络路径和延迟，跟这次写在全局意义上是不是真的先发生没有必然联系。
读 quorum 只是收集多个副本的响应，它不理解写的具体业务含义，不会替你自动合并两次并发写代表的业务意图。
optionExplanations_en: A's write happened with no knowledge of B's write, and B's write happened with no knowledge of A's — neither knew about the other, which is exactly what concurrency means: no causal ordering between them.
A timestamp is just a wall-clock reading, and clocks on different machines can be skewed, so it can't be taken directly as proof of which write causally came first.
Which write a given replica happens to receive first depends purely on network path and delay, with no necessary connection to which one truly happened first globally.
A read quorum just collects responses from multiple replicas; it has no understanding of the business meaning behind a write and won't automatically merge the intent of two concurrent writes.

q: happens-before 如何定义并发？
q_en: How does happens-before define concurrency?
why: 这个定义看因果信息，不看两个操作在墙钟上是否重叠。
why_en: This definition is about causal knowledge, not whether wall-clock times overlap.
text: 如果操作 B 知道或依赖操作 A，则 A {{happens-before}} B；如果 A 和 B 谁也不知道谁，它们就是{{并发}}。
text_en: If operation B knows about or depends on A, then A {{happens-before}} B; if neither knows about the other, they are {{concurrent}}.

q: 单副本版本号如何区分覆盖和并发？
q_en: How does a single-replica version number distinguish overwrite from concurrency?
why: 写入携带的旧版本告诉服务器这次修改基于哪些状态；没见过的更高版本不能被安全覆盖。
why_en: The prior version says what state the write is based on; unseen higher versions must remain as concurrent siblings.
scenario: 两个客户端编辑购物车，服务器要求写入携带上次读取到的版本号。
scenario_en: Two clients edit a shopping cart, and the server requires writes to include the version read earlier.
steps: 读返回当前未被覆盖的值和最新版本
客户端合并读到的值后提交新值和旧版本
服务器覆盖不高于旧版本的值
服务器保留更高版本的并发 sibling

termDefinitions.meaning: Version vector 是每个副本一个版本号的集合，用来判断覆盖关系和并发写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version vector tracks per-replica versions to distinguish overwrites from concurrent writes.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  R[read values + version] --> M[client merges]
  M --> W[write value + prior version]
  W --> S[server overwrites seen versions]
  S --> K[keeps unseen siblings]

q: 合并购物车 siblings 时为什么删除需要 tombstone？
q_en: Why do cart-sibling merges need tombstones for deletes?
why: 没有 tombstone，另一个 sibling 里的旧商品会在并集时复活；删除标记让合并逻辑知道移除也发生过。
why_en: Without a tombstone, an old item in another sibling can be resurrected by a union merge.
scenario: 购物车允许添加和删除商品；两个并发 sibling 做集合并集时，被一个客户端删除的商品可能又出现。
scenario_en: A cart supports adds and removes; unioning two concurrent siblings may resurrect an item removed by one client.
options: 删除也要作为带版本的事实参与合并
删除可以直接物理移除不留痕
LWW 一定保留所有删除
read repair 会理解购物车语义
options_en: A delete must be a versioned fact in the merge
Deletes can be physically removed with no trace
LWW always preserves every delete
Read repair understands cart semantics
tradeoff: 正确删除语义 vs 墓碑存储/清理成本

termDefinitions.meaning: Tombstone 是删除标记，用来在合并并发版本时保留删除事实。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone records a deletion so merges do not accidentally resurrect data.

termDefinitions.meaning: Last Write Wins（LWW）：按时间戳或类似顺序只保留一个胜出写入的冲突处理策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LWW keeps one winning write by timestamp or another ordering rule.

termDefinitions.meaning: Read repair 是读多个副本时发现旧值，并顺手把新值写回旧副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read repair fixes stale replicas when a multi-replica read discovers a newer value.

optionExplanations: 删除也必须留下一个带版本的记号参与合并，不然合并逻辑根本不知道这件商品曾经被删过，只会把它当成另一个副本里还存在的正常商品。
物理删除不留痕的话，并集合并时另一份副本里那件旧商品会重新出现，跟删除意图相反。
LWW 只按时间戳留一个赢家，遇到并集合并这种场景时并不天然保证删除操作被保留下来。
read repair 只是把落后副本补齐到最新状态，它不理解购物车加减商品这种业务语义，不会替你判断该不该保留某次删除。
optionExplanations_en: A delete also has to leave a versioned marker that participates in the merge, otherwise the merge logic has no idea that item was ever removed and just treats it like a normal item still present in the other sibling.
Physically removing it with no trace means the other sibling's still-present old record resurrects the item during a union merge, the opposite of what the delete intended.
LWW just keeps one winner by timestamp; it doesn't inherently guarantee a delete survives a union-style merge scenario.
Read repair just brings a lagging replica up to date; it has no understanding of cart add/remove semantics and won't decide on its own whether a delete should be honored.

q: 多副本 leaderless 为什么需要 version vector？
q_en: Why does multi-replica leaderless replication need version vectors?
why: version vector 记录每个副本的进度，服务器才能判断新写覆盖了哪些历史、哪些值仍是并发 siblings。
why_en: A version vector tracks progress per replica so the server can tell overwrites from concurrent siblings.
scenario: 多个副本都能接写；只用单个版本号无法说明某次写看见了哪些副本上的历史。
scenario_en: Multiple replicas accept writes, and one scalar version cannot say which replica histories a write has seen.
options: 每个副本一个计数器来表达因果进度
用一个全局墙钟时间戳来排序写入
让客户端永远只读一个副本
把所有并发写交给 LWW
options_en: Use one counter per replica to express causal progress
Order writes by one global wall-clock timestamp.
Make clients always read one replica
Send every concurrent write to LWW
whenOtherWins: 单 leader 严格排序时，一个日志位置通常就足够表达进度。
tradeoff: 因果精度 vs 元数据大小

termDefinitions.meaning: Version vector 是每个副本一个版本号的集合，用来判断覆盖关系和并发写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version vector tracks per-replica versions to distinguish overwrites from concurrent writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Vector clock 是用多个计数器表达分布式事件因果关系的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vector clock uses multiple counters to represent causal relationships between distributed events.

termDefinitions.meaning: Last Write Wins（LWW）：按时间戳或类似顺序只保留一个胜出写入的冲突处理策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LWW keeps one winning write by timestamp or another ordering rule.

optionExplanations: 每个副本各自维护一个计数器，合起来就能表达“这次写看到了哪些副本上的哪些历史”，服务器靠比较这些计数器判断谁覆盖了谁、谁是并发的 siblings。
全局墙钟时间戳本身可能有偏差，也没法表达“这次写是否见过另一次写”这种因果关系，只能给出一个不可靠的顺序。
让客户端永远只读一个副本回避了问题，不是解决因果追踪的机制，而且会牺牲多副本带来的可用性好处。
把所有并发写交给 LWW 是丢弃信息来强排顺序，跟保留因果、区分覆盖与并发的目标正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Each replica maintains its own counter, and together they express which replicas' histories a given write has seen, letting the server tell overwrites apart from concurrent siblings.
A single global wall-clock timestamp can itself be skewed and can't express whether one write saw another — it only gives an unreliable ordering.
Making clients always read one replica sidesteps the problem rather than solving causal tracking, and it gives up the availability benefit of having multiple replicas.

Sending every concurrent write to LWW discards information to force an arbitrary order, the opposite of what a version vector is trying to preserve — the distinction between overwrites and concurrency.

q: 三种复制模型的面试总括怎么说？
q_en: How would you summarize the three replication models in an interview?
why: 复制模型先问写入口和排序权在哪里；写入口越分散，可用性越好，但冲突和因果元数据越重要。
why_en: Ask where writes enter and who orders them; more distributed write entry improves availability but increases conflict and causality work.
scenario: 面试官让你为全球用户资料服务比较 single-leader、multi-leader 和 leaderless。
scenario_en: An interviewer asks you to compare single-leader, multi-leader, and leaderless replication for a global profile service.
options: 按写入口和排序权比较
三者只差字段编码方式
无主一定提供强一致读
多主完全不需要解冲突
options_en: Compare by write entry and ordering authority
They only differ in field encoding
Leaderless always gives strongly consistent reads
Multi-leader never needs conflict handling
tradeoff: 集中排序 vs 分散可用
optionExplanations: 先问写入口在哪、谁有排序权：单主集中在一个节点，多主分散到几个节点各自本地排序，无主则没有固定排序权、靠 quorum 和版本信息协调，写入口越分散可用性越好但冲突处理越重要。
三种模型的核心差别在于写入口和一致性/冲突处理方式，不只是字段怎么编码这种表面差异。
无主架构靠 quorum 交集给出的是弱一致性保证，不是强一致读，这个说法不成立。
多主架构本地各自接写，天然会产生并发冲突，说它完全不需要解冲突正好说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Start by asking where writes enter and who has ordering authority: single-leader centralizes it on one node, multi-leader spreads it across several nodes each ordering locally, and leaderless has no fixed ordering authority at all, relying on quorums and version metadata — the more distributed the write entry, the better the availability, but the more conflict handling matters.
The core difference between the three models is where writes enter and how consistency and conflicts get handled, not a surface-level difference like field encoding.
Leaderless architectures give a weaker guarantee via quorum overlap, not strongly consistent reads, so this claim doesn't hold.
Multi-leader accepts writes locally at each site, which naturally produces concurrent conflicts, so claiming it never needs conflict handling has it exactly backwards.

q: 购物车可离线编辑且不能丢添加项时怎么选冲突策略？
q_en: How should a cart handle offline edits without losing added items?
why: 购物车的业务意图是合并多端操作，不是选一个赢家。合并单位 = 每个商品条目，不是整个购物车对象；删除用 tombstone 表达。
why_en: A cart wants both sides merged rather than one winner, so the merge unit is each line item, not the whole cart object, and deletes need a tombstone.
scenario: 用户手机离线添加商品，电脑也添加商品；同步后业务希望保留两边添加，删除也不能复活。
scenario_en: A user adds items offline on a phone and also on a laptop; after sync, additions should survive and deletes must not resurrect.
options: 保留 siblings/CRDT 合并
直接用 LWW 的时间戳来覆盖较旧的写
按设备 ID 大小选赢家
同步失败就清空购物车
options_en: Keep siblings or use CRDT merge
Just use LWW timestamps to overwrite older writes.
Let the larger device ID win
Clear the cart on sync failure
whenOtherWins: 缓存值或可重算派生数据可以接受 LWW，因为丢一个写不会丢业务事实。
tradeoff: 业务语义保留 vs 合并复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: Conflict-free Replicated Data Type（CRDT）：能在并发更新后自动合并并收敛的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CRDT is a data type that can merge concurrent updates and converge automatically.

termDefinitions.meaning: Last Write Wins（LWW）：按时间戳或类似顺序只保留一个胜出写入的冲突处理策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LWW keeps one winning write by timestamp or another ordering rule.

termDefinitions.meaning: Tombstone 是删除标记，用来在合并并发版本时保留删除事实。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone records a deletion so merges do not accidentally resurrect data.

optionExplanations: 购物车要保留手机和电脑两边各自添加的商品，不是选一个赢家覆盖另一个，siblings 或 CRDT 合并正好能做到这一点，删除再配合 tombstone 就不会被复活。
直接用 LWW 覆盖旧写，会让后添加的那一边的商品覆盖掉先添加的那一边，先添加的商品就这样丢了，跟“两边添加都要保留”矛盾。
按设备 ID 大小选赢家本质上还是选一个赢家覆盖另一个，一样会丢掉输的那一边添加的商品。
同步失败就清空购物车是最坏的处理方式，会把两边的修改全部丢掉，跟“不能丢添加项”的要求完全相反。
optionExplanations_en: The cart needs to keep items added on both the phone and the laptop rather than picking one winner to overwrite the other, and siblings or CRDT merging does exactly that, with tombstones keeping a delete from being resurrected.
Using LWW to overwrite older writes would let whichever side added items later overwrite the other, silently losing the earlier side's additions — contradicting the requirement to keep both.
Picking a winner by device ID is still just picking one side to overwrite the other, losing whatever the losing side added.
Clearing the cart on sync failure is the worst option — it throws away both sides' changes entirely, the exact opposite of never losing an added item.

q: 分区和复制在架构上是什么关系？
q_en: How do partitioning and replication relate architecturally?
why: 分区解决容量和吞吐分摊，复制解决容错和读扩展；两者通常组合，但选择维度不同。
why_en: Partitioning spreads capacity and throughput, while replication adds fault tolerance and read scale.
scenario: 一个集群把数据拆成多个 partition，每个 partition 又有多个副本。
scenario_en: A cluster splits data into partitions, and each partition has multiple replicas.
options: 记录归一分区，分区可复制
复制会自动选择分区键
一个节点只能存一分区
分区后不能再做复制
options_en: A record belongs to one partition, and partitions can be replicated
Replication automatically chooses the partition key
One node can store only one partition
Partitioned data cannot be replicated
tradeoff: 横向拆分 vs 冗余副本
optionExplanations: 一条记录固定属于某一个分区，而这个分区本身又可以有多个副本，两件事叠在一起才是完整的架构。
复制协议不会替你决定分区键该怎么选，分区键是单独的设计决定。
一个节点完全可以同时存多个分区，这也是分区数常常远大于节点数的原因。
分区之后照样可以对每个分区做复制，这两件事是正交叠加的，不是互斥的。
optionExplanations_en: A record belongs to exactly one partition, and that partition itself can have multiple replicas — the two ideas stack together to form the full architecture.
The replication protocol doesn't choose the partition key for you; that's a separate design decision.
One node can easily hold multiple partitions at once, which is why the partition count is often much larger than the node count.
Partitioning and replication compose — you can still replicate each partition afterward, they aren't mutually exclusive.

q: 分区最想避免什么？
q_en: What does partitioning mainly try to avoid?
why: hot spot 会让集群容量被单个忙节点限制，其它节点再空也帮不上。
why_en: A hot spot makes one busy node the bottleneck even if the rest of the cluster is idle.
text: 分区的目标是让数据和查询负载均匀分到节点；某个 partition 承担过多请求就是{{hot spot}}。
text_en: Partitioning tries to spread data and query load evenly; a partition with disproportionate load is a {{hot spot}}.

q: 随机放置记录为什么不是好分区方案？
q_en: Why is random record placement a poor partitioning scheme?
why: 分区方案不只要均匀，还要可路由；随机放置缺少 key 到节点的确定映射。
why_en: A partitioning scheme needs routing as well as balance; random placement lacks a deterministic key-to-node mapping.
scenario: 数据库把每条记录随机丢到一个节点，写入分布很均匀，但查询通常按主键找单条记录。
scenario_en: A database randomly places each record on a node; writes are balanced, but reads usually fetch one record by primary key.
options: 读时不知道去哪，只能查很多节点
写入一定会集中到同一个热点节点
无法存储任何大数据
复制日志会消失
options_en: Reads do not know where to go and must query many nodes
Writes will always concentrate on one hot node.
Large data cannot be stored
Replication logs disappear
tradeoff: 均匀性 vs 可定位读取
optionExplanations: 随机放置没有 key 到节点的确定映射，按主键查一条记录时不知道该去问哪个节点，只能把所有节点都问一遍。
随机放置恰恰是均匀分布写入的，问题不在写入集中，而在读取没法路由。
随机放置本身不限制能存的数据总量，能不能存大数据跟这个问题无关。
复制日志是另一套机制，跟记录被随机放到哪个节点没有关系，不会因此消失。
optionExplanations_en: Random placement has no deterministic key-to-node mapping, so a primary-key lookup has no idea which node to ask and ends up querying all of them.
Random placement actually distributes writes evenly; the problem isn't write concentration, it's that reads can't be routed.
Random placement by itself doesn't cap how much data can be stored; that's unrelated to this question.
Replication logs are a separate mechanism from where a record happens to land, so they don't disappear because of random placement.

q: 什么时候 key range 分区很合适？
q_en: When is key-range partitioning a good fit?
why: range 分区保留排序，一小时的连续查询 ≈ 落到 1-2 个相邻分区；代价是相邻热门 key 可能形成 hot spot。
why_en: Range partitioning keeps the sort order, so a one-hour scan touches roughly one or two adjacent partitions, at the risk of a hot spot on neighbouring popular keys.
scenario: 传感器查询常按设备和时间范围扫描，应用需要取某设备最近一小时的连续记录。
scenario_en: Sensor queries often scan by device and time range, such as one device's last hour of readings.
options: 按有序 key range 分区并在分区内排序
对完整 key 做随机 hash 分区以打散热点
每条记录随机放到任意节点
只依赖全局二级索引查时间
options_en: Partition by sorted key range and keep each partition sorted.
Hash-partition on the full key randomly to spread hot spots.
Place each record on a random node.
Rely only on a global secondary index for time.
whenOtherWins: 如果访问主要是随机主键点查且写入分布偏斜，hash 分区通常更稳。
tradeoff: 范围扫描效率 vs 热点风险

termDefinitions.meaning: Sorted String Table（SSTable）：按 key 排序、不可变的磁盘表文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is an immutable on-disk table sorted by key.

optionExplanations: 按有序 key range 分区、分区内部又保持排序，某设备连续一小时的记录会落在少数几个相邻分区里，一次扫描就能顺序取出。
对完整 key 做随机 hash 会打乱设备和时间的顺序关系，一次范围扫描要打到很多分区才能凑齐结果。
每条记录随机放节点连查询该去哪个节点都不知道，更谈不上按时间范围高效扫描。
只用全局二级索引能帮助按条件过滤，但不会解决数据本身该按什么方式分区存放的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning by ordered key ranges and keeping keys sorted inside each partition means one device's continuous hour of readings lands in a small set of adjacent partitions, so one sequential scan retrieves them.
Hashing the whole key scrambles the relationship between device and time, so one range scan would have to hit many scattered partitions to assemble the result.
Placing each record randomly means a query doesn't even know which node to ask, let alone scan a time range efficiently.
Using only a global secondary index helps filter by a condition, but it doesn't address how the underlying data should be partitioned for storage.

q: 为什么只按时间戳 range 分区会写热点？
q_en: Why does range partitioning only by timestamp create a write hot spot?
why: 时间递增 key 把写入集中在排序末端；range 分区的优势变成了写入集中点。
why_en: Monotonically increasing time keys concentrate writes at the end of the ordered range.
scenario: 所有传感器读数都按当前时间写入，partition 边界按日期划分。
scenario_en: All sensor readings are written with the current timestamp, and partitions are split by date.
options: 新写都会打到今天这个分区
历史分区会同时接收所有写
range 查询会完全不可用
hash 函数会失效
options_en: All new writes hit today's partition
Historical partitions receive all writes
Range queries become impossible
The hash function fails
tradeoff: 时间范围查询简单 vs 当前时间写热点
optionExplanations: 分区边界按日期划分、key 又按当前时间递增，所有传感器的新读数全都落进今天这个分区，写入压力全压在一个分区上。
越旧的历史分区写入量反而越少甚至没有，新数据只会往最新那个分区堆，不会分散到历史分区。
range 查询本身不受影响，问题出在写入集中而不是查询能力，这个说法答非所问。
分区边界怎么划跟 hash 函数完全无关，这里用的是 range 分区不是 hash 分区。
optionExplanations_en: With partition boundaries drawn by date and keys monotonically increasing with time, every sensor's new reading lands in today's partition, piling all the write pressure onto one place.
Older historical partitions actually get less or no new traffic; new data only piles onto the latest partition, it doesn't spread across historical ones.
Range queries themselves are unaffected — the issue is write concentration, not query capability, so this option doesn't address the question.
How partition boundaries are drawn has nothing to do with a hash function; this scenario uses range partitioning, not hashing.

q: 传感器数据如何兼顾写分散和时间范围查？
q_en: How can sensor data balance write spread and time-range scans?
why: sensor_id 先分散并发写，timestamp 在单个传感器内保留排序；跨多个传感器查询要分别扫再合并。
why_en: The sensor ID spreads concurrent writes, while the timestamp preserves per-sensor order.
scenario: 有许多传感器同时上报，查询常按某个传感器取时间范围。
scenario_en: Many sensors report at once, and queries usually fetch a time range for one sensor.
options: key=(sensor_id,time)
key 只用单调递增的 timestamp
key 只用随机数后缀
所有传感器写同一 key
options_en: key=(sensor_id,time)
Use only a monotonically increasing timestamp as the key.
Use only a random suffix
Write every sensor to one key
whenOtherWins: 如果查询总是全站按时间聚合，纯 sensor 前缀会增加 fan-out。
tradeoff: 写入分散 vs 跨传感器查询 fan-out
optionExplanations: key=(sensor_id, time) 让 sensor_id 先把并发写分散到不同分区，time 又在同一个传感器内部保留顺序，跨传感器时间范围查询要各自扫描再合并。
key 只用 timestamp 会重现按时间集中写热点的老问题，多个传感器的并发写还是会挤在同一段时间范围内。
key 只用随机数后缀虽然能打散写入，但完全丢掉了按传感器取时间范围这个查询模式所需要的顺序信息。
所有传感器写同一个 key 会让写入压力全部集中在一处，连基本的并发写分散都做不到。
optionExplanations_en: key=(sensor_id, time) lets sensor_id spread concurrent writes across partitions first, while time preserves order within a single sensor, and a cross-sensor time-range query would scan each one and merge.
Using only timestamp as the key recreates the same time-concentrated write hotspot, since many sensors' concurrent writes still cluster around the same time window.
Using only a random suffix does spread writes, but it completely loses the ordering information needed for the per-sensor time-range query pattern.
Writing every sensor to one key concentrates all write pressure in one place, failing even the basic goal of spreading concurrent writes.

q: 随机主键点查为什么常用 hash 分区？
q_en: Why do random primary-key lookups often use hash partitioning?
why: 好的 hash 能把偏斜 key 空间打散，点查仍可由 hash 直接路由；代价是主键范围顺序丢失。
why_en: A good hash spreads skewed key space while preserving direct routing for point lookups.
scenario: 用户资料按 user_id 点查和更新，user_id 分布可能不均，范围查询很少。
scenario_en: User profiles are looked up and updated by user_id, with few range queries and possibly uneven IDs.
options: hash key 后按 hash 范围分区
按 user_id 字典序 range 分区
每次查询 scatter/gather
把所有用户放一个 leader
options_en: Hash the key and partition hash ranges
Partition by user_id lexicographic ranges
Scatter/gather every query
Put all users on one leader
whenOtherWins: 如果主需求是连续范围扫描，key range 分区比 hash 更合适。
tradeoff: 均匀点查负载 vs 范围查询能力

termDefinitions.meaning: Message-Digest Algorithm 5（MD5）：一种哈希函数，分区时只需要其分布性而非安全性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MD5 is a hash function; partitioning cares about distribution, not cryptographic safety.

optionExplanations: 先对 key 做 hash 再按 hash 值范围分区，能把本来分布不均的 user_id 打散开，点查时还是能靠同一个 hash 函数直接算出该去哪个分区。
按 user_id 字典序做 range 分区，遇到 user_id 分布不均时会让某些分区数据量远大于其它分区，跟目标相反。
每次查询都 scatter/gather 意味着一次点查要问遍所有分区，完全没利用上按 key 能直接路由这个优势。
把所有用户放一个 leader 会让这台机器承担全部读写压力，跟“分区”想要的横向扩展背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Hashing the key and partitioning by hash range spreads out an otherwise skewed user_id distribution, while a point lookup can still compute the right partition directly from the same hash function.
Range-partitioning by user_id's lexicographic order would let some partitions balloon far larger than others when user_id distribution is skewed, the opposite of the goal.
Doing scatter/gather on every query means one point lookup has to ask every partition, completely failing to use the direct-routing advantage a key affords.
Putting all users on one leader dumps all the read and write load onto a single machine, working against the whole point of partitioning for horizontal scale.

q: key range 和 hash 分区的核心对比是什么？
q_en: What is the core contrast between key-range and hash partitioning?
why: 分区键选择先看访问模式：要相邻 key 一起读就保序，要抵抗 key 分布偏斜就 hash。
why_en: Choose by access pattern: preserve order when adjacent keys are read together, hash when skewed keys must be spread.
scenario: 订单库既有按订单号点查，也有按时间范围导出；团队要选主分区方式。
scenario_en: An order store needs both order-id lookups and time-range exports, and the team must choose the primary partitioning approach.
options: range 保序利于范围查，hash 打散利于均匀负载
range 永远更均匀，hash 永远支持高效范围查
两者只差副本数
hash 不需要路由元数据
options_en: Range preserves order for scans; hash spreads load
Range is always more even and hash always supports efficient range queries.
They differ only in replica count
Hash needs no routing metadata
tradeoff: 范围局部性 vs 负载均匀性
optionExplanations: range 分区保留了 key 的顺序，按时间范围导出这类查询能落到相邻的几个分区；hash 分区把 key 打散，牺牲顺序换来按订单号点查时负载更均匀。
两种分区方式各有偏斜和保序的取舍，不能说 range 永远更均匀，也不能说 hash 永远支持范围查询，这个说法过于绝对。
两者的核心差别在数据怎么落到分区、能不能保序，不是副本数量这种复制层面的参数。
hash 分区照样需要知道 key 到分区的路由规则，说它不需要路由元数据是不成立的。
optionExplanations_en: Range partitioning preserves key order, so a time-range export lands on a handful of adjacent partitions; hash partitioning scrambles the key, trading away order for more even load when point-querying by order number.
Each scheme trades order for balance differently — it isn't true that range is always more balanced or that hash always supports ranges; this claim is too absolute.
The core difference is how data lands on partitions and whether order is preserved, not a replication-layer parameter like replica count.
Hash partitioning still needs to know the key-to-partition routing rule, so claiming it needs no routing metadata doesn't hold.

q: 为什么不要把 consistent hashing 当成一致性保证？
q_en: Why shouldn't consistent hashing be treated as a consistency guarantee?
why: 这里的 consistent 指 key 映射在节点变化时少移动；它不承诺读到最新值或事务一致性。
why_en: Here, consistent means key mapping changes minimally as nodes change; it does not promise fresh reads or transactions.
scenario: 团队听到 consistent hashing，以为它能保证副本读写强一致。
scenario_en: A team hears 'consistent hashing' and assumes it gives strong consistency for replicas.
options: 它是负载/重平衡技术，不是读写一致性语义
它等价于 ACID consistency
它能解决所有 split brain
它要求所有查询走 leader
options_en: It is a load/rebalancing technique, not read-write consistency
It is the same as ACID consistency
It solves every split brain
It requires all queries to go through a leader
tradeoff: 术语相似 vs 语义完全不同
optionExplanations: consistent hashing 这个词里的 consistent 指的是节点增减时 key 到节点的映射变动很小，是一种负载和重平衡技术，跟读写要不要一致、能不能读到最新值是两回事。
它跟 ACID 里的 consistency 是完全不同层面的概念，不能划等号。
split brain 是复制和选主层面的问题，这个哈希方案只管 key 怎么映射到节点。
它跟集群里有没有 leader 无关，也不要求查询都经过某个固定节点。
optionExplanations_en: The consistent in consistent hashing refers to key-to-node mapping changing minimally as nodes come and go — it's a load and rebalancing technique, a completely different thing from read-write consistency or getting the freshest value.
It's an entirely different concept from ACID consistency and shouldn't be equated with it.
Split brain is a replication and leader-election problem; consistent hashing only decides how keys map to nodes and doesn't solve that.
Consistent hashing doesn't require every query to route through a leader — it's unrelated to whether a leader exists at all.

q: Cassandra 复合主键的折中点是什么？
q_en: What compromise does Cassandra's compound key make?
why: 第一列决定数据落在哪个 partition，后续列保留分区内排序：单分区 ≈ 一个用户的全部动态按时间有序。
why_en: The first column picks the partition and the rest keep the order inside it, so one partition holds roughly one user's whole timeline in time order.
scenario: 社交应用要按 user_id 分散用户动态，又要按时间顺序读取某个用户的动态。
scenario_en: A social app wants to spread posts by user_id but read one user's posts in timestamp order.
options: hash 第一列分区，后续列在分区内排序
hash 所有的列并彻底丢掉排序顺序信息
只按时间 range 分区
每条动态复制到所有分区
options_en: Hash the first column for partitioning and sort later columns inside it
Hash all columns and drop all ordering info.
Range-partition only by time
Copy every post to all partitions
whenOtherWins: 如果查询经常跨所有用户按时间扫，这个模型会产生大量分区 fan-out。
tradeoff: 按实体局部性 vs 全局范围查询

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 是面向高可用和分区扩展的分布式宽列数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a distributed wide-column database built for availability and partitioned scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: Sorted String Table（SSTable）：按 key 排序、不可变的磁盘表文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is an immutable on-disk table sorted by key.

optionExplanations: 第一列 hash 决定动态落在哪个分区，把不同用户的写分散开；后续列在分区内部保持排序，让同一用户的动态能按时间顺序高效读出。
hash 所有列会连同用户内部的时间顺序也一起打散，读某个用户按时间顺序的动态时就没法直接顺序扫了。
只按时间 range 分区会重现所有用户写入集中在最新时间段的老问题，没有解决按用户分散写入的需求。
每条动态复制到所有分区会让存储成本随分区数线性膨胀，完全不是折中方案，是浪费。
optionExplanations_en: Hashing the first column decides which partition a post lands in, spreading different users' writes apart, while later columns stay sorted within that partition, letting one user's posts be read back in time order efficiently.
Hashing every column would scramble the in-user time order too, so reading one user's posts in chronological order would no longer be a simple sequential scan.
Range-partitioning only by time recreates the old problem of every user's writes concentrating in the latest time window, failing to spread writes by user.
Copying every post to every partition makes storage cost grow linearly with partition count, which isn't a tradeoff at all, just waste.

q: 单个热 key 压垮分区时怎么办？
q_en: What can you do when one hot key overloads a partition?
why: 相同 key 的 hash 永远相同，换 hash 不会分散单 key。拆分单位 = 热 key × N 个后缀，读时要 fan-out N 次再合并。
why_en: The same key always hashes the same way, so only splitting it into N suffixed sub-keys spreads the writes — and reads then fan out to all N and merge.
scenario: 明星用户发布动态后，所有评论都写到同一个 activity_id，hash 后仍然落同一分区。
scenario_en: After a celebrity posts, all comments write to one activity_id, and hashing still sends them to one partition.
options: 给热 key 加少量随机 shard 后缀
换一个更强的加密 hash 函数重新计算
直接按当前节点数取模分配
把这个分区的 follower 删掉
options_en: Add a small random shard suffix to the hot key.
Switch to a stronger cryptographic hash and recompute.
Just take the key modulo the current node count.
Delete the followers of that partition.
whenOtherWins: 普通低流量 key 不要拆，否则每次读都要多查多合并。
tradeoff: 写入分散 vs 读取合并成本

termDefinitions.meaning: Message-Digest Algorithm 5（MD5）：一种哈希函数，分区时只需要其分布性而非安全性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MD5 is a hash function; partitioning cares about distribution, not cryptographic safety.

optionExplanations: 同一个 key 不管用什么 hash 函数都会落到同一个位置，人为在热 key 后面加上少量随机 shard 后缀，等于把它拆成多个子 key，写入才能真正分散到不同分区。
换一个加密强度更高的 hash 函数，同一个输入照样只会产生同一个输出，热 key 还是会落在同一个分区，问题没解决。
按节点数取模只是另一种映射方式，同一个 key 依然映射到固定的一个位置，不会分散这一个 key 的写入。
删除 follower 是在削弱容错能力，跟一个热 key 压垮它所在分区这个问题完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: The same key always hashes to the same place no matter what hash function is used, so adding a small random shard suffix to the hot key effectively splits it into multiple subkeys, actually spreading the writes across partitions.
Switching to a stronger cryptographic hash still produces one fixed output for the same input, so the hot key still lands on the same partition — the problem isn't solved.
Taking modulo by node count is just another mapping scheme; the same key still maps to one fixed spot, so it doesn't spread that one key's writes.
Removing followers weakens fault tolerance and has nothing to do with one hot key overwhelming its partition.

q: 热 key 加随机后缀的读代价是什么？
q_en: What read cost comes from adding random suffixes to a hot key?
why: 拆 key 是把写压力换成读放大和额外 bookkeeping；只应对少数已识别热 key 使用。
why_en: Key splitting trades write pressure for read amplification and bookkeeping, so use it only for identified hot keys.
scenario: 评论写入被拆到 100 个子 key，产品页要展示该活动的完整评论列表。
scenario_en: Comment writes are split across 100 subkeys, and the product page must show the full comment list.
options: 读要查所有子 key 并合并排序
读会自动只查询其中一个子 key
写入会重新集中
二级索引不再需要维护
options_en: Reads must fetch all subkeys and merge/sort them
Reads will automatically hit just one sub-key.
Writes concentrate again
Secondary indexes need no maintenance
tradeoff: 写扩展 vs 读放大
optionExplanations: 评论被拆到 100 个子 key 后分散存在不同分区，想展示完整评论列表就得把这 100 个子 key 全部查一遍，再把结果合并排序。
读并不会自动只查一个子 key，恰恰相反，完整列表要求把所有拆出来的子 key 都查到，否则会漏掉一部分评论。
拆 key 是长期分散写入的策略，不会因为读取而让写入重新集中回一个 key。
拆 key 只影响数据落在哪个分区，二级索引该维护的还是要维护，这个说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: With comments split across 100 subkeys living in different partitions, showing the full comment list means querying all 100 subkeys and merging and sorting the results.
Reads don't automatically fetch just one subkey — quite the opposite, a complete list requires querying every split-out subkey, or some comments get missed.
Splitting a key is a lasting strategy for spreading writes; reading from it doesn't cause writes to reconcentrate onto one key.
Splitting a key only changes where data lands; any secondary index still needs its usual maintenance, so this claim doesn't hold.

q: 分区数据库的二级索引为什么麻烦？
q_en: Why are secondary indexes hard in a partitioned database?
why: 主键分区让点查好路由，二级条件却可能命中所有分区；索引本身也必须选择分区方式。
why_en: Primary-key partitioning routes point lookups well, but secondary terms may match records across many partitions.
scenario: 二手车库按 listing_id 分区，但用户要按 color 和 make 搜索。
scenario_en: A used-car database is partitioned by listing_id, but users search by color and make.
options: 搜索字段不一定指向唯一主分区
二级索引只能建立在主键之上
所有索引都必须放单机
写入不需要更新索引
options_en: The search term does not necessarily map to one primary partition
Secondary indexes can only be built on the primary key.
All indexes must live on one machine
Writes do not update indexes
tradeoff: 主键路由简单 vs 多维搜索复杂

搜索字段不一定指向…场景
搜索字段不一定指向唯一…成本

二级索引只能用于主键场景
二级索引只能用于主键成本
所有索引都必须放单机
所有索引都必须放单机场景
所有索引都必须放单机成本
写入不需要更新索引场景
写入不需要更新索引成本

optionExplanations: 按 listing_id 分区能让主键查询直接路由到一个分区，但按 color 或 make 搜索时，符合条件的车可能分散在所有分区里，搜索词并不指向唯一一个主分区。
二级索引恰恰是为了支持按非主键字段查询而存在的，说它只能用于主键正好说反了它的用途。
索引本身也需要选择分区方式（local 还是 global），不是必须挤在单机上，这个说法把选项说死了。
写入一条记录如果改变了被索引的字段，相关的二级索引也要跟着更新，不更新的说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning by listing_id routes primary-key lookups directly to one partition, but searching by color or make can match cars scattered across every partition, since the search term doesn't map to one primary partition.
A secondary index exists precisely to support queries on non-primary-key fields, so claiming it can only query primary keys has it exactly backwards.
An index itself still has to choose a partitioning scheme (local or global); it doesn't have to live on one machine, so this option forecloses an option that actually exists.
Writing a record that changes an indexed field still needs the relevant secondary index updated, so claiming writes skip index updates doesn't hold.

q: 写入频繁的分区表何时偏向 local secondary index？
q_en: When should a write-heavy partitioned table favor local secondary indexes?
why: local index 让写路径只触碰文档所在分区；代价是按索引读要查多个分区再合并。
why_en: A local index keeps writes on the document's partition, at the cost of querying many partitions for index reads.
scenario: 商品文档按 product_id 分区，写入和更新很多；搜索延迟可以接受 scatter/gather。
scenario_en: Product documents are partitioned by product_id with many writes and updates; search can tolerate scatter/gather.
options: 索引和文档同分区，写只改一个分区
全局按 term 分区的二级索引
把所有索引放单节点
不维护任何索引
options_en: Keep the index local to the document partition
A global term-partitioned secondary index.
Put every index on one node
Maintain no indexes
whenOtherWins: 如果二级索引读是主路径且必须低延迟，全局 term index 更合适。
tradeoff: 写入局部性 vs 查询 fan-out
optionExplanations: 索引条目和它描述的文档放在同一个分区，写一条商品只需要改这一个分区里的文档加索引，代价是按索引搜索时要去查多个分区再合并（scatter/gather），这里场景明确能接受这个代价。
全局按 term 分区索引会让写一条商品可能要更新多个索引分区，跟“写入和更新很多”这个场景想要减轻写路径负担的方向相反。
把所有索引放单节点会让这台机器成为写入和查询的瓶颈，跟分区想要的横向扩展背道而驰。
不维护任何索引意味着放弃按颜色、品牌搜索这类功能，跟场景描述的“需要搜索”矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the index entry local to the document's own partition means writing a product only touches that one partition's document and index, at the cost of scatter/gather across partitions when searching by index — a cost this scenario explicitly says it can tolerate.
Partitioning a global index by term would make writing one product potentially touch several index partitions, working against a write-heavy scenario that wants to keep the write path light.
Putting every index on one node turns that machine into a bottleneck for writes and queries, working against the whole point of partitioning for scale.
Maintaining no indexes at all means giving up search by color or brand entirely, which contradicts the scenario's stated need for search.

q: scatter/gather 查询为什么放大尾延迟？
q_en: Why does scatter/gather amplify tail latency?
why: 并行能降低平均等待，但请求要等足够多分区返回；分区越多，碰到慢节点的概率越高。
why_en: Parallelism helps average latency, but the request often waits for the slowest needed partition.
scenario: 搜索红色汽车时需要并行问 50 个分区，然后等结果合并返回。
scenario_en: Searching for red cars queries 50 partitions in parallel and merges the results.
options: 整体延迟常被最慢分区拖住
每个分区都会因此变得更快
只要并行就没有失败
写入会减少一半
options_en: Overall latency is often held by the slowest partition
Every partition therefore gets faster.
Parallelism removes all failures
Writes are cut in half
tradeoff: 查询覆盖面 vs 尾延迟
optionExplanations: 要凑齐 50 个分区的搜索结果才能返回，只要其中一个分区变慢，整体请求就要等它，分区越多碰到慢分区的概率也越高，尾延迟被拖住了。
并行查询不会让单个分区本身变得更快，它只是同时问了很多分区，每个分区各自的处理速度没变。
并行只是同时发出请求，不会消除任何一个分区可能失败或变慢的风险，这个说法不成立。
scatter/gather 是查询模式，跟写入量会不会减半完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Assembling results from 50 partitions means the whole request has to wait for the slowest one to respond, and the more partitions involved, the higher the odds of hitting a slow one, dragging up tail latency.
Running queries in parallel doesn't make any individual partition faster — it just asks many of them at once, but each partition's own processing speed is unchanged.
Parallelism just means requests go out simultaneously; it doesn't remove the risk that any given partition fails or slows down.
Scatter/gather is a query pattern, completely unrelated to whether write volume gets cut in half.

q: 读多的二级索引为什么考虑 term-partitioned global index？
q_en: Why consider a term-partitioned global index for read-heavy secondary-index queries?
why: global index 把同一搜索 term 的引用聚在一起，读路径少 fan-out；写一个文档时可能要更新多个索引分区。
why_en: A global index colocates one search term's references, reducing read fan-out while making writes touch multiple index partitions.
scenario: 用户搜索 color=red 的请求很多，产品希望不用每次扫所有商品分区。
scenario_en: Users frequently search for color=red, and the product wants to avoid scanning every product partition each time.
options: 全局索引按 term 分区
每个文档分区维护本地索引
删除二级索引后全表扫
随机挑一个分区查询
options_en: Partition the global index by term
Keep local indexes per document partition
Remove the secondary index and scan
Query one random partition
whenOtherWins: 写入频繁且可接受 scatter/gather 时，local index 更简单。
tradeoff: 读 fan-out vs 写 fan-out

termDefinitions.meaning: Application Programming Interface（API）：服务暴露给调用方的操作和数据契约。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the operation and data contract exposed to callers.

optionExplanations: 把全局索引按搜索词分区，所有引用 color=red 的记录聚在同一个索引分区，一次搜索少走几个分区就能拿到结果，不用每次都扫全部商品分区。
每个文档分区各自维护本地索引，搜索一个词还是要去问所有商品分区，没有解决“不用每次扫所有分区”这个诉求。
删除二级索引后全表扫会让每次搜索的代价随数据量线性增长，跟提升读效率的目标完全相反。
随机挑一个分区查询会漏掉分布在其它分区的匹配结果，得不到正确的搜索结果。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning the global index by search term collects every reference to color=red into the same index partition, so one search hits far fewer partitions instead of scanning every product partition each time.
Keeping local indexes per document partition still requires querying every product partition for one search term, failing to address the goal of not scanning everything each time.
Removing the secondary index and scanning would make every search's cost grow linearly with data size, the opposite of improving read efficiency.
Querying one random partition would miss matching results scattered across the others, giving an incorrect search result.

q: global index 按 term 值还是 term hash 分区怎么选？
q_en: How do you choose term-value versus term-hash partitioning for a global index?
why: 索引分区也在保序和均匀之间取舍；price 这类范围条件更喜欢保序，热门 term 更怕热点。
why_en: Index partitioning has the same order-versus-balance tradeoff: ranges like price benefit from order, while hot terms need spreading.
scenario: 车库搜索既有 price 范围过滤，也有 color 精确过滤；索引本身也要分区。
scenario_en: A car search supports price ranges and exact color filters, and the index itself must be partitioned.
options: 按 term 值利于范围查，按 hash 更均匀
按 term hash 分区仍能保留范围顺序
按 term 值分区一定不会有热点
两种分法对写路径完全一样
options_en: Partitioning by term value helps range queries; hashing spreads load more evenly.
Hash-partitioning by term still preserves range order.
Partitioning by term value never creates a hot spot.
Both choices behave identically on the write path.

q: hash(key) mod N 为什么不适合扩容？
q_en: Why is hash(key) mod N bad for scaling out?
why: 取模把节点数写进每个 key 的位置计算；扩容改了公式，导致大规模搬迁。
why_en: Modulo bakes the node count into placement, so changing node count changes placement for many keys.
scenario: 集群从 10 个节点扩到 11 个节点，如果分区规则直接用 hash(key) mod 节点数。

实际情况正相反，只有极少数 key 是因为 N 变化恰好还留在原节点，绝大多数都要搬家，这个说法夸大了不受影响的比例。
分区规则怎么定跟范围查询快不快没有直接关系，这个说法答非所问。

q: hash 分区扩容时固定分区数有什么好处？

why: key 到 partition 的映射不变，扩容只搬少量整个 partition；请求在迁移完成前还能按旧归属服务。

重新计算每个 key 的节点正是 hash mod N 那种方案的做法，恰恰是固定 partition 数想要避免的大规模搬迁。

Requests can keep being served against the old partition ownership during migration; writes don't need to halt until the migration finishes.

q: key range 数据为什么常用动态 partition？

把 partition 映射硬编码进应用代码
只依赖 DNS 解析 key 找到节点
options_en: Keep the authoritative mapping in ZooKeeper and notify subscribers.
Let each client keep a local cache that never refreshes.
Hard-code the partition mapping into application code.
Rely on DNS alone to resolve a key to a node.
whenOtherWins: 小集群且变更很少时，人工配置或简单管理连接可能足够。
tradeoff: 权威元数据 vs 外部依赖

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是协调服务，可保存集群成员和分区归属等元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a coordination service for metadata such as cluster membership and partition ownership.

termDefinitions.meaning: Domain Name System（DNS）：把域名解析到网络地址的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to network addresses.

optionExplanations: 用 ZooKeeper 这样的协调服务保存哪个 key range 归哪个节点的权威映射，节点和 partition 变化时通知订阅它的 routing tier，映射始终有一个可信来源。
让客户端缓存永不更新，一旦发生 rebalancing 就会一直把请求路由到错误的旧节点，跟“映射会频繁变化”这个前提直接冲突。
把映射硬编码进应用代码，每次 partition 变化都要重新发布代码，完全跟不上频繁变化的节奏。
DNS 只擅长解析少量相对稳定的服务入口，没法表达每个 key range 具体归哪个节点这种细粒度、高频变化的信息。
optionExplanations_en: Using a coordination service like ZooKeeper to hold the authoritative mapping of which node owns which key range, and notifying subscribers like the routing tier when it changes, gives everyone one trustworthy source of truth.
Letting clients cache the map forever means every rebalance leaves them routing requests to the wrong, now-outdated node, directly conflicting with the premise that the mapping changes frequently.
Hard-coding the map into application code would require a redeploy every time a partition moves, far too slow to keep up with frequent changes.
DNS is good at resolving a handful of relatively stable service entrypoints; it can't express fine-grained, fast-changing ownership of every key range down to the node.

q: ZooKeeper 路由和 gossip 路由的取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the tradeoff between ZooKeeper-based routing and gossip-based routing?
why: 外部协调服务给路由层一个权威来源，但多了依赖；gossip 少一个外部系统，却要求数据库节点自己传播并收敛状态。
why_en: An external coordinator gives routers an authority but adds a dependency; gossip removes that dependency and moves convergence into database nodes.
scenario: 数据库要传播 partition ownership 变化，团队在外部协调服务和节点间 gossip 之间选择。
scenario_en: A database must propagate partition ownership changes, and the team is choosing between an external coordinator and node gossip.
options: ZooKeeper 集中元数据，gossip 把复杂度放进节点
ZooKeeper 不需要一致性，gossip 必须整体停机
二者都不需要映射
DNS 能替代两者的 partition map
options_en: ZooKeeper centralizes metadata; gossip puts complexity in nodes
ZooKeeper needs no consistency, and gossip must stop the whole cluster.
Neither needs a map
DNS replaces the partition map for both
tradeoff: 集中协调依赖 vs 节点内复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是协调服务，可保存集群成员和分区归属等元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a coordination service for metadata such as cluster membership and partition ownership.

termDefinitions.meaning: Domain Name System（DNS）：把域名解析到网络地址的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to network addresses.

optionExplanations: ZooKeeper 这类外部协调服务集中存一份归属信息，路由层查它就好，但多一个外部依赖；gossip 让节点互相传播、自己收敛，省外部依赖但复杂度转到了节点内部。
ZooKeeper 本身恰恰需要保证元数据的一致性才有意义，gossip 也不要求停机才能传播状态，这两个说法都不成立。
两种方案都需要一份 partition ownership 的映射，只是维护和传播它的方式不同，说都不需要映射不成立。
DNS 适合解析少量相对稳定的服务入口，替代不了细粒度、频繁变化的 partition 归属映射，两种方案都不会靠 DNS 解决这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: An external coordinator like ZooKeeper centralizes partition ownership so the routing layer just queries it, at the cost of one more external dependency to maintain; gossip lets database nodes propagate ownership info among themselves and converge on their own, removing that dependency but pushing the complexity into every node.
ZooKeeper's whole value depends on keeping its metadata consistent, and gossip doesn't require downtime to propagate state — neither claim holds.
Both approaches still need a partition-ownership map somewhere; they just differ in how it's maintained and propagated, so claiming neither needs one is incorrect.
DNS is good for resolving a small set of relatively stable service entrypoints; it can't substitute for a fine-grained, fast-changing partition-ownership map in either approach.

q: 为什么 DNS 通常只适合找入口，不适合找 partition？
q_en: Why is DNS usually enough for entrypoints but not partition ownership?
why: DNS 适合发现少量服务入口；key 到 partition 到节点的映射需要专门的集群元数据。
why_en: DNS is good for finding a small set of service entrypoints, while key-to-partition ownership needs cluster metadata.
scenario: 客户端需要先找到 routing tier 的地址，也需要知道 key foo 当前归哪个 partition leader。
scenario_en: A client needs the routing tier address and also needs to know which partition leader owns key foo.
options: 机器入口变化慢，partition 归属变化更细更快
DNS 能精确表达每个 key 的 owner 归属
partition 映射永远不变
routing tier 不需要地址
options_en: Machine entrypoints change slowly; partition ownership is finer and faster
DNS can express the owner of each individual key.
Partition maps never change
The routing tier needs no address
tradeoff: 通用服务发现 vs 精细分区路由

termDefinitions.meaning: Domain Name System（DNS）：把域名解析到网络地址的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DNS maps domain names to network addresses.

optionExplanations: 这类服务入口数量少、变化也慢，DNS 记录足够应付；但某个 key 具体挂在哪个 partition leader 下，会随 rebalancing 频繁细粒度地变化，DNS 记录粒度和更新速度都跟不上。
DNS 记录的是域名到 IP 的映射，没有办法表达“某个具体 key 归哪个 partition”这么细的信息。
partition 映射恰恰会随节点增减和 rebalancing 经常变化，说它永远不变不成立。
它自己也是一个服务，同样需要一个地址才能被客户端找到，这个说法站不住脚。
optionExplanations_en: A service entrypoint like this is small in number and changes slowly, so a DNS record is plenty; but which partition leader a given key falls under changes frequently and finely with rebalancing, at a granularity and speed DNS records cannot track.
A DNS record maps a hostname to an IP; it has no way to express something as fine-grained as which partition a specific key belongs to.
Partition ownership does change often as nodes come and go and rebalancing happens, so claiming it never changes doesn't hold.
It is itself a service and still needs an address to be found by clients, so this claim does not hold up.

q: 分析型大查询为什么需要 MPP 执行？
q_en: Why do analytic queries need MPP execution?
why: MPP 利用分区并行扫描和计算，适合大范围分析；普通 key-value 路由只解决单 key 请求。
why_en: MPP uses partitioned parallel scans and computation for large analytics, while key-value routing only solves single-key requests.
scenario: 数据仓库查询要扫描大量数据、做 join、group by 和聚合，结果不是单 key 点查。
scenario_en: A warehouse query scans lots of data and performs joins, grouping, and aggregation rather than one-key lookup.
options: 优化器把查询拆成多阶段在多节点并行跑
把所有数据先拉到客户端循环
只查询一个随机 partition
禁用所有索引
options_en: The optimizer splits the query into stages that run across nodes
Pull all data to the client loop
Query one random partition
Disable every index
whenOtherWins: 在线点查和小范围写入不需要完整 MPP 引擎，简单路由更低延迟。
tradeoff: 复杂查询吞吐 vs 点查延迟/复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: Massively Parallel Processing（MPP）：把分析查询拆成多个阶段并行跑在多节点上的执行方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MPP executes analytic queries in parallel across many nodes and stages.

optionExplanations: 优化器把一个大查询拆成扫描、过滤、join、聚合这些阶段，分别在多个节点上并行跑，再把中间结果汇总，这正是 MPP 处理大范围分析查询的方式。
把所有数据先拉到客户端再循环处理，等于放弃了分区并行计算的优势，数据量一大客户端根本处理不过来。
分析查询要覆盖大量数据做聚合，只查一个随机分区连需要的数据都凑不齐，结果是不完整的。
禁用所有索引跟需不需要多节点并行执行是两回事，这个说法答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: The optimizer splits a large query into stages — scan, filter, join, aggregate — that run in parallel across nodes and then get combined, exactly how MPP handles a large analytic query.
Pulling all the data to the client and looping through it gives up the advantage of partitioned parallel computation entirely, and the client can't keep up once data volume grows.
An analytic query aggregating across a large volume of data can't even gather what it needs from a single random partition, giving an incomplete result.
Disabling every index is unrelated to whether multi-node parallel execution is needed, so this option doesn't address the question.

q: 为什么分区能扩展？
q_en: Why does partitioning scale?
why: 一旦操作跨多个 partition，就会重新引入协调、事务和尾延迟问题。
why_en: Once operations span partitions, coordination, transactions, and tail latency return.
text: 分区扩展依赖一个前提：大多数单 key 操作只触碰{{一个 partition}}，因此多个 partition 可以{{相互独立}}处理请求。
text_en: Partitioning scales when most single-key operations touch {{one partition}}, so partitions can operate {{mostly independently}}.

q: local index 和 global index 的一句话取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the one-line tradeoff between local and global indexes?
why: local 把索引跟文档放一起，写局部；global 把同一 term 放一起，读局部。
why_en: Local indexes colocate index entries with documents for local writes; global indexes colocate a term for local reads.
scenario: 面试中要解释二级索引在分区数据库里的两种放置方式。
scenario_en: In an interview, you need to explain the two ways to place secondary indexes in a partitioned database.
options: local 写优，global 读优
local/global 都只改一分区
global 不能按 term 查询
local 强一致且完全无代价
options_en: Local favors writes; global favors reads
Both local and global touch one partition
Global cannot query by term
Local is strongly consistent for free
tradeoff: 写局部性 vs 读局部性
optionExplanations: local index 把索引条目和文档放一起，写一条数据只改一个分区，代价是读要查多个分区；global index 把同一 term 聚在一起，读只查少数分区，代价是写要触及多个索引分区，正好是相反的取舍。
local index 写只碰一个分区没错，但 global index 恰恰因为把同一 term 聚在一起，读时才少碰分区，这个说法混淆了两者的代价方向。
global index 正是按搜索词（term）组织的索引，说它不能按 term 查询正好说反了它存在的意义。
local index 依然要靠底层复制机制保证一致性，也不是没有代价，只是代价体现在读放大上，这个说法过于绝对。
optionExplanations_en: A local index keeps index entries with the document, so a write only touches one partition, at the cost of reads spanning many partitions; a global index groups the same term together, so reads touch few partitions, at the cost of writes touching multiple index partitions — the tradeoffs run in opposite directions.
It's true a local index write touches one partition, but a global index specifically groups a term together so reads touch fewer partitions — this option confuses which side each tradeoff falls on.
A global index is precisely organized by search term, so claiming it can't query by term has it exactly backwards from why it exists.
A local index still relies on the underlying replication for consistency and isn't free either — its cost just shows up as read amplification, so this claim is too absolute.

q: 新增节点的 rebalancing 状态链是什么？
q_en: What is the rebalancing state chain when adding a node?
why: 固定 partition 的关键是搬 partition 而不是重算每个 key；最后一步必须更新所有路由决策者。
why_en: With fixed partitions, the system moves partitions rather than remapping every key, and routing metadata must change last.
scenario: hash 分区集群新增一台机器，系统采用固定数量 partition。
scenario_en: A hash-partitioned cluster adds one machine and uses a fixed number of partitions.
steps: 计算新的 partition 分配
从多个旧节点迁移少量完整 partition
迁移期间旧归属继续服务或转发
切换路由元数据到新归属
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[new assignment] --> B[move whole partitions]
  B --> C[serve during copy]
  C --> D[publish routing map]

q: 选择分区方案时的面试决策链是什么？
q_en: What is the interview decision chain for choosing a partitioning scheme?
why: 分区不是先选算法名，而是从访问模式和热点开始；之后才补索引、迁移和路由。
why_en: Partitioning starts from access patterns and hot spots, then adds index, rebalancing, and routing design.
scenario: 你要为一个新存储服务选择 partition key 和路由方式，需求包含点查、范围查和二级搜索。
scenario_en: You need to choose a partition key and routing approach for a new storage service with point lookups, range scans, and secondary search.
steps: 先列主查询：点查、范围查、二级索引
按主查询选择 range、hash 或复合 key
检查热 key 和 secondary index 的读写 fan-out
设计 rebalancing 和路由元数据更新
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单机数据量和简单点查，先不分区会让实现和运维都更简单。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Q[access patterns] --> P[partition key]
  P --> H[hot key plan]
  H --> I[index strategy]
  I --> R[rebalance + routing]

q: ACID 四个字母分别指什么？
q_en: What do the four ACID letters stand for?
text: ACID = {{Atomicity 原子性}}、{{Consistency 一致性}}、{{Isolation 隔离性}}、{{Durability 持久性}}。
text_en: ACID = {{Atomicity}}, {{Consistency}}, {{Isolation}}, and {{Durability}}.
why: ACID 是事务讨论的入口，但不是完整规格。面试里要继续问隔离级别、复制方式和落盘策略。
why_en: ACID is a starting label, so in interviews you still need to ask about isolation level, replication, and durability details.

termDefinitions.meaning: ACID 是事务常见安全保证的缩写：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID names the common transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

scenario: 订单服务一次要写订单、扣库存、记审计；任一步失败都不能留下半成品。
scenario_en: An order service writes an order, reserves inventory, and appends an audit record; a failure must not leave partial state.
q: 订单多步写为什么先要原子事务？
q_en: Why ask for an atomic transaction for multi-step order writes?
options: 原子事务，失败时整体回滚
只在应用里重试每个写入
读副本做最终一致同步
把三次写拆到三个队列
options_en: An atomic transaction that rolls back all writes on failure
Retry each write separately in application code
Replicate through eventually consistent read replicas
Split the three writes into three independent queues
why: 原子性把多步写变成同成同败，调用方可以按“成功或重试”处理。代价是写路径要经过事务管理。
why_en: Atomicity turns several writes into an all-or-nothing unit, with the cost of transaction management on the write path.
whenOtherWins: 如果每一步都有幂等补偿，并且业务允许短暂半完成状态，拆成 saga 或队列会更灵活。
tradeoff: 简单错误处理 vs 写路径协调成本

termDefinitions.meaning: Saga：把一个大事务拆成多步本地事务，每步失败时靠补偿动作修正。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A saga splits a large transaction into local steps and uses compensating actions when a later step fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等性：同一操作执行多次，最终可见结果仍像执行一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotence means repeating the same operation leaves the visible result as if it ran once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读副本：从主库复制数据、主要承担读请求的副本，可能有复制延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica copies data from the primary and serves reads, often with replication lag.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子更新：把条件检查和修改放在数据库一条写语句里完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic update performs the condition check and modification inside one database statement.

optionExplanations: 把写订单、扣库存、记审计三步包进一个原子事务，失败时整体回滚，调用方只需要面对成功或整体重试两种结果。
只在应用里挨个重试每个写入，某一步失败重试时前面几步可能已经生效，很容易留下半成品状态。
读副本做最终一致同步解决的是读扩展和读新鲜度问题，不能保证这三步写入本身要么全成要么全不成。
把三次写拆到三个队列，各自独立消费、独立失败，反而更难保证三步要么一起成功要么一起不生效。
optionExplanations_en: Wrapping the order write, stock decrement, and audit log in one atomic transaction rolls everything back on failure, so the caller only ever sees success or a clean retry.
Retrying each write separately in application code risks earlier steps already taking effect while a later step fails, easily leaving a half-finished state.
Eventually consistent read replicas address read scaling and freshness, not whether these three writes succeed or fail together.
Splitting the three writes into three independent queues, each consumed and failing on its own, makes it harder to guarantee all three succeed or none do.

scenario: 支付接口先扣余额再写流水，进程在两步之间崩溃。
scenario_en: A payment handler debits an account and then writes a ledger row, but the process crashes between the two writes.
q: ACID 原子性在这里保证什么？
q_en: What does ACID atomicity guarantee here?
options: 并发事务之间互相完全看不见
两步写要么都保留要么都撤销
提交后数据不会丢
账户总额永远正确
options_en: Concurrent transactions are completely invisible to each other.
Both writes are kept or both are undone
Committed data cannot be lost
The account total is always correct
why: 原子性处理的是故障打断多步写，不是并发和业务规则。它让重试不会在未知半状态上叠加错误。
why_en: Atomicity is about failures during a multi-write unit, not concurrency or business invariants.
tradeoff: 故障回滚 vs 并发隔离

termDefinitions.meaning: ACID 是事务常见安全保证的缩写：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID names the common transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

optionExplanations: 这里问的是崩溃打断多步写的问题，不是并发事务之间能不能互相看见，隔离性才管这件事。
扣余额和写流水是同一个原子事务里的两步，进程在中间崩溃时，原子性保证这两步要么都被保留、要么都被撤销，不会留下只扣钱没记账的半成品。
提交后数据不丢是持久性关心的事，这里描述的是提交前进程崩溃，还没到持久性要保证的那个阶段。
账户总额永远正确是业务不变量，属于一致性（ACID 的 C）范畴，原子性本身不检查业务规则对不对。
optionExplanations_en: The question here is about a crash interrupting a multi-step write, not whether concurrent transactions can see each other — that's isolation's job.

Debiting the balance and writing the ledger are two steps of the same atomic transaction, and if the process crashes between them, atomicity guarantees both are kept or both undone, never a half-done state with money debited but no record.
Data not disappearing after commit is what durability covers; this scenario describes a crash before commit, before durability's guarantee even applies.
The account total always being correct is a business invariant, which falls under consistency (the C in ACID); atomicity itself doesn't check whether business rules hold.

scenario: 一个钱包系统要求所有账户余额之和不能凭空变化；数据库只知道行和约束，不懂业务含义。
scenario_en: A wallet system requires total balances not to change out of thin air; the database sees rows and constraints, not business meaning.
q: ACID 一致性主要是谁的责任？
q_en: Who mainly owns ACID consistency?
options: 数据库完全自动保证
应用定义事务和不变量
网络层保证消息顺序
备份系统定期校验
options_en: The database guarantees it automatically
The application defines transactions and invariants
The network layer guarantees message order
The backup system checks it periodically
why: ACID 里的 C 指业务“好状态”，数据库只能帮你执行约束和事务。写错业务事务，数据库也可能忠实保存坏结果。
why_en: ACID consistency is mostly the application preserving invariants, with the database enforcing only the constraints it knows.
tradeoff: 业务语义 vs 存储机制

termDefinitions.meaning: ACID 是事务常见安全保证的缩写：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID names the common transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

optionExplanations: 数据库只认识行和约束这些它能理解的规则，账户总和这种业务含义它自己判断不了，说它能完全自动保证是不成立的。
数据库只知道行和约束，真正定义“事务该怎么划分”“余额之和不能变”这些业务不变量的是应用；数据库负责忠实执行应用交给它的约束和事务边界。
网络层保证的是消息顺序和可靠传输，跟账户余额总和这种业务不变量没有关系。
备份系统定期校验发现的是过去已经发生的问题，不能在写入发生的那一刻阻止业务不变量被破坏。
optionExplanations_en: The database only understands rows and constraints it's told about; it can't judge whether the sum of account balances makes business sense, so claiming it guarantees this automatically doesn't hold.

The database only knows rows and constraints — it's the application that defines what a transaction boundary means and what invariant, like the balance sum, must hold; the database just faithfully enforces whatever constraints and boundaries it's given.
The network layer guarantees message ordering and delivery, which has nothing to do with a business invariant like an account balance sum.
A backup system's periodic checks catch problems after the fact; they can't stop a business invariant from being violated at the moment a write happens.

scenario: 两个客户端同时读计数器 42，各自加 1 后写回；最终只到 43。
scenario_en: Two clients read counter value 42, each adds one, and both write back; the final value becomes 43.
q: 这暴露了哪类隔离问题？
q_en: Which isolation problem does this expose?
options: 脏读
丢失更新
幻读
持久性失败
options_en: Dirty read
Lost update
Phantom read
Durability failure
why: 这是典型读-改-写竞争：两个事务都基于旧值计算，后写覆盖前写。用原子更新、锁或冲突检测处理。
why_en: This is a read-modify-write race where the later write overwrites the earlier one, so use atomic updates, locks, or conflict detection.
whenOtherWins: 如果每次写的是独立追加事件而不是覆盖同一值，事件流合并可能比锁更合适。
tradeoff: 并发吞吐 vs 更新不丢
optionExplanations: 脏读指的是读到了另一个事务还没提交的数据，这里两个客户端各自读到的 42 都是已经提交的值，不是脏读。
两个客户端都基于同一个旧值 42 各自加 1 再写回，后写的那个覆盖了先写的那个，中间那次加一凭空消失了，这正是丢失更新。
幻读指的是范围查询前后看到不同的匹配行集合，这里只是一个计数器的读改写，不涉及范围查询。
持久性失败指的是已提交数据在崩溃后消失，这里两次写都正常提交了，只是其中一次的效果被覆盖，不是持久性问题。
optionExplanations_en: A dirty read means reading data from another transaction that hasn't committed yet; here both clients read a value of 42 that was already committed, so this isn't a dirty read.
Both clients compute from the same old value of 42 and write back, and the later write overwrites the earlier one, silently erasing one increment — that's exactly a lost update.
A phantom read means a range query sees a different set of matching rows on a later read; this is just a read-modify-write on one counter, no range query involved.
A durability failure means committed data vanishes after a crash; both writes here committed fine, one's effect was just overwritten, not a durability problem.

scenario: 审计系统收到“提交成功”后，机房立刻断电。
scenario_en: An audit system returns commit success, and the datacenter loses power immediately after.
q: 事务持久性最关心哪件事？
q_en: What does transaction durability mainly protect?
options: 提交成功的数据不能因为崩溃消失
读取期间看不到别人的中间写
每个业务约束都自动成立
所有副本立刻完全一致
options_en: Committed data should not disappear because of a crash
Reads cannot see another transaction’s partial writes
Every business invariant is automatic
All replicas are immediately identical
why: 持久性关注提交后的生存能力，常靠 WAL、fsync、复制或组合策略。更强持久性通常增加提交延迟。
why_en: Durability is about committed data surviving failures, often through WAL, fsync, replication, or a combination.
tradeoff: 提交延迟 vs 崩溃后可恢复性

termDefinitions.meaning: WAL 是先记录意图再改数据页的日志，用于崩溃恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records changes before data pages are updated so the database can recover after a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: fsync：要求操作系统把文件变更刷到持久介质，降低断电丢提交的风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: fsync asks the operating system to flush file changes to durable storage.

optionExplanations: 持久性关心的正是这件事：一旦告诉客户端“提交成功”，这份数据就不能因为断电、崩溃这类故障而消失，通常靠 WAL、fsync 或复制来保证。
读取期间看不到别人的中间写属于隔离性的范畴，不是持久性关心的问题。
每个业务约束自动成立属于一致性（C），持久性只关心提交后数据的生存能力，不检查业务规则。
所有副本立刻完全一致是同步复制才可能追求的强一致目标，持久性本身不要求这个，也不是它的定义。
optionExplanations_en: Durability specifically covers this: once the client is told the commit succeeded, that data must not disappear because of a crash or power loss, typically ensured through WAL, fsync, or replication.
Not seeing another transaction's partial writes during a read falls under isolation, not what durability is concerned with.
Every business invariant automatically holding is consistency's job (the C); durability only cares about committed data surviving failures, not whether business rules are correct.
All replicas being immediately identical is a strong-consistency goal only synchronous replication might chase; durability itself doesn't require this and isn't defined by it.

scenario: 面试官说“我们数据库 ACID compliant”，但没有说明隔离级别和复制方式。
scenario_en: The interviewer says the database is ACID compliant but does not specify isolation level or replication.
q: ACID 标签后还该追问哪些事务边界？
q_en: What transaction boundaries should you ask about after hearing “ACID”?
options: 默认隔离级别是什么
提交要等几份副本确认
业务不变量由谁检查
是否支持全文索引查询
options_en: What is the default isolation level?
How many replicas acknowledge a commit?
Who checks business invariants?
Does it support full-text index queries?
why: ACID 标签太粗，真正影响设计的是隔离、持久化和不变量边界。全文索引是查询能力，不说明事务安全。
why_en: The ACID label is too coarse; isolation, durability, and invariant ownership are what shape the transaction design.

termDefinitions.meaning: ACID 是事务常见安全保证的缩写：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID names the common transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 隔离级别：数据库允许或阻止哪些并发异常的事务设置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An isolation level defines which concurrency anomalies a database prevents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 业务不变量：系统必须始终维护的业务规则，例如库存不能为负。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A business invariant is a rule the system must preserve, such as inventory never going negative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 副本确认：提交路径上至少多少副本确认写入后才向客户端返回成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replica acknowledgement is a replica confirming a write before the client sees success.

optionExplanations: 默认隔离级别直接决定会不会出现脏读、不可重复读或幻读这类竞态，是判断事务安全边界的核心问题。
提交要等几份副本确认决定的是持久性强度和写延迟，同样是“ACID compliant”这个标签背后需要问清楚的边界。
业务不变量由谁检查决定了跨行规则（比如余额不能为负）是数据库约束保证的，还是完全靠应用代码自己保证的，这直接影响设计。
全文索引查询是一种查询能力，跟事务安全性、隔离级别、持久化策略这些边界完全无关，不该混进这个问题里。
optionExplanations_en: The default isolation level directly determines whether dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, or phantoms can happen, a core question for understanding the transaction safety boundary.
How many replicas must acknowledge a commit determines durability strength and write latency, another boundary worth clarifying behind the ACID compliant label.

Who checks business invariants determines whether cross-row rules like a balance never going negative are enforced by database constraints or left entirely to application code, which directly shapes the design.
Full-text index query support is a query capability, unrelated to transaction safety, isolation level, or durability strategy, so it doesn't belong in this question.

scenario: 社交图服务要同时插入 A 关注 B 和 B 被 A 关注两个索引行，读者不能看到只更新一边。
scenario_en: A social graph service writes both “A follows B” and “B is followed by A” index rows, and readers must not see only one side.
q: 为什么需要多对象事务？
q_en: Why use a multi-object transaction?
options: 它把相关多行更新放进一个提交边界
它让单行写入更快
它取消所有唯一约束
它把所有读请求自动发到缓存层
options_en: It puts related multi-row updates in one commit boundary
It makes single-row writes faster
It removes all uniqueness constraints
It automatically routes all reads to the cache layer.
why: 多对象事务保护跨行不变量，避免读到一半更新。代价是事务管理器要追踪一组读写，而不是一条记录。
why_en: A multi-object transaction protects cross-row invariants by committing related rows together.
whenOtherWins: 如果读模型能从单一事件流重建，且允许异步投影，追加事件再修复索引会更容易扩展。
tradeoff: 跨行一致性 vs 写入协调范围
optionExplanations: 关注关系要同时插入两条索引行，多对象事务把这两行更新放进同一个提交边界，读者不会看到只更新了一半的状态。
多对象事务管理的是跨行的一致性边界，不是让单行写入本身跑得更快，这个说法答非所问。
多对象事务本身不会取消任何唯一约束，约束该生效还是照常生效。
多对象事务发生在写路径，跟读请求要不要自动路由到缓存完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Inserting both relationship index rows for a follow needs to land in the same commit boundary, so readers never see a state where only one row was updated.
A multi-object transaction manages a cross-row consistency boundary; it doesn't make a single-row write itself run faster, so this doesn't address the question.
A multi-object transaction doesn't remove any uniqueness constraint on its own — constraints still apply exactly as before.
A multi-object transaction happens on the write path, which is unrelated to whether reads get automatically routed to cache.

scenario: 库存服务只需要把同一个 SKU 的 available 数量减 1。
scenario_en: An inventory service only needs to decrement the available count for one SKU.
q: 单 SKU 扣减何时用 atomic update？
q_en: When should a single-SKU decrement use an atomic update?
options: 单条条件原子 UPDATE
本地完整事务包住多条读写
跨分区两阶段提交（2PC）
先读 read replica 再写主库
options_en: A single conditional atomic UPDATE
A full local transaction around several reads and writes
Cross-partition two-phase commit (2PC)
Read from a read replica before writing the primary
why: 单对象原子 UPDATE 把条件检查和扣减留在数据库一条写里，避免读旧值后覆盖。它不解决跨 SKU 或跨表不变量。
why_en: For one SKU, a conditional atomic UPDATE keeps the check and decrement inside one database write.
tradeoff: 单对象简洁性 vs 跨对象表达力
whenOtherWins: 如果一次操作要同时保护多个对象，就需要完整事务；跨分区同时提交才考虑 2PC。
codeSample:
UPDATE inventory
SET available = available - 1
WHERE sku = $1 AND available > 0;
-- 一条语句内完成检查和扣减。

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子更新：把条件检查和修改放在数据库一条写语句里完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic update performs the condition check and modification inside one database statement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 完整事务：把多条读写放进一个提交边界，失败时整体回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full transaction groups several reads and writes into one commit boundary that rolls back on failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交（2PC）：先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者统一 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then a coordinator tells them to commit or abort.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读副本：从主库复制数据、主要承担读请求的副本，可能有复制延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica copies data from the primary and serves reads, often with replication lag.

optionExplanations: 只涉及同一个 SKU 的一个字段扣减时，一条带条件的原子 UPDATE 就能把检查和扣减合成数据库内的一次写，不用先读再算再写。
本地完整事务包住多条读写是给跨多行、多表的场景准备的，对单个字段的简单扣减来说是多余的重量级方案。
跨分区两阶段提交（2PC）是协调多个分区一起提交时才需要的机制，这里只涉及一个 SKU 的一条记录，完全用不上。
先读 read replica 再写主库会读到可能落后的旧值，再拿这个旧值去扣减主库，正是丢失更新的典型诱因。
optionExplanations_en: For decrementing one field on a single SKU, a single conditional atomic UPDATE folds the check and the decrement into one database write, no separate read-then-write needed.
Wrapping a full local transaction around several reads and writes is meant for scenarios spanning multiple rows or tables, overkill for a simple single-field decrement.
Cross-partition two-phase commit is needed when coordinating a commit across multiple partitions; this only involves one record on one SKU, so it doesn't apply.
Reading from a replica and then writing the primary risks reading a stale value and decrementing against it on the primary — a classic setup for a lost update.

scenario: 报表查询不能看见另一个事务尚未提交的价格修改。
scenario_en: A reporting query must not see another transaction’s uncommitted price update.
q: 最低要哪种常见隔离保证？
q_en: What common isolation guarantee is the minimum?
options: 读未提交
读已提交
可串行化
无隔离，只靠缓存
options_en: Read uncommitted
Read committed
Serializable
No isolation, only cache
why: 读已提交至少挡住脏读：未提交写不会被其他事务读到。它仍可能允许不可重复读和丢失更新。
why_en: Read committed blocks dirty reads, though it can still allow non-repeatable reads and lost updates.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询要跨多行保持同一时间点视图，快照隔离会比读已提交更稳。
tradeoff: 低开销可见性规则 vs 稳定快照
optionExplanations: 读未提交连未提交的写都能读到，报表恰恰不能看见尚未提交的价格修改，这个级别达不到要求。
读已提交保证只能读到已经提交的数据，价格修改还没提交时报表看不到它，正好挡住了这里描述的脏读风险，是满足要求的最低级别。
可串行化能挡住更多异常，但题目只要求“最低”要哪种保证，读已提交已经足够满足这里的需求，不需要用到最强级别。
没有隔离、只靠缓存完全无法阻止读到未提交数据，跟“不能看见未提交修改”这个要求正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Read uncommitted can see even uncommitted writes, and the report specifically must not see the uncommitted price change, so this level falls short.

Read committed guarantees only committed data is visible, so the report never sees the price change before it commits — exactly blocking the dirty-read risk described, and the minimum level that meets the requirement.
Serializable blocks even more anomalies, but the question only asks for the minimum needed here, and read committed already suffices without reaching for the strongest level.
