No isolation with only a cache offers no protection against reading uncommitted data, the opposite of the requirement not to see unpublished changes.

scenario: 两个管理员同时改同一用户邮箱；后提交的事务覆盖了先提交的一半字段。
scenario_en: Two admins update the same user profile; the later transaction overwrites part of the earlier one.
q: 脏写为什么危险？
q_en: Why are dirty writes dangerous?
options: 把并发写拼成没人提交过的状态
只会让读请求变慢一点
只影响只读备份的内容
只在数据库没有二级索引时才发生
options_en: It stitches concurrent writes into a state nobody actually committed.
It only makes reads a little slower.
It only affects read-only backups.
It only happens when the database has no secondary index.
why: 脏写允许覆盖未提交写，会破坏事务边界。多数读已提交实现会用写锁阻止同一对象的并发脏写。
why_en: Dirty writes break transaction boundaries by overwriting uncommitted writes, so databases usually block them with write locks.

termDefinitions.meaning: ACID 是事务常见安全保证的缩写：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID names the common transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

optionExplanations: 两个管理员的写都还没真正提交完成，脏写让后提交的事务的部分字段和先提交的部分字段拼在一起，最终留下的是一个谁都没有真正确认提交过的混合状态。
脏写的危险在于数据正确性被破坏，不只是让读请求慢一点这么轻，这个说法严重低估了后果。
脏写发生在主库的写路径上，只读备份同样会复制到这个被破坏的状态，不是只影响备份不影响主库。
脏写和有没有索引没有关系，它是并发写事务之间缺少写锁保护造成的，跟索引这个查询优化机制是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: With neither administrator's write fully committed, a dirty write can splice the later transaction's partial fields together with the earlier one's, leaving a mixed state nobody actually committed.
The real danger of a dirty write is broken data correctness, far worse than just slightly slower reads — this option badly understates the consequence.
A dirty write happens on the primary's write path, and a read-only backup would just replicate that corrupted state too, not be spared from it.
A dirty write is about missing write-lock protection between concurrent write transactions, unrelated to whether an index exists on the table.

scenario: 数据库要实现读已提交，同时避免读者被长写事务长期阻塞。
scenario_en: A database wants read committed while avoiding long blocking of readers behind a writer.
q: 常见实现思路是什么？
q_en: What is a common implementation approach?
options: 读旧的已提交版本，写同一行时加写锁
所有读都等写事务结束
读未提交版本再之后修正
把事务日志直接发给客户端自己判断
options_en: Readers see the old committed version, while writers lock the row
All reads wait until the write transaction ends
Readers see uncommitted versions and fix them later
Send the transaction log to the client to decide itself.
why: 读旧已提交版本能挡脏读，也减少读写互相阻塞。写锁仍要阻止两个写事务同时改同一行。
why_en: Serving the last committed version blocks dirty reads without making readers wait for the writer.
tradeoff: 读延迟稳定 vs 读到最新未提交变化

rows: 读旧的已提交版本，写同一行时加写锁
必须保护最新读或不变量时
读旧的已提交版本，写同…成本
所有读都等写事务结束
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
所有读都等写事务结束成本
读未提交版本再之后修正
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
读未提交版本再之后修正成本
把事务日志发给客户端判断
高随机写吞吐更重要时
把事务日志发给客户端判断成本

optionExplanations: 读者只看上一个已提交的旧版本，不用等写事务结束，天然挡住脏读；同时对同一行的两个并发写事务之间还是要靠写锁互斥，防止脏写。
要求所有读都等写事务结束会让读写互相严重阻塞，读已提交恰恰是想避免这种情况才让读者读旧版本。
读未提交版本再之后修正正是脏读会发生的方式，跟读已提交想要挡住脏读的目标相反。
把事务日志发给客户端让它自己判断，既不现实也不是数据库通常实现隔离级别的方式。
optionExplanations_en: Readers just see the last committed version and don't wait for the writer to finish, which naturally blocks dirty reads, while a write lock still keeps two concurrent writers on the same row from stepping on each other, preventing dirty writes.
Requiring all reads to wait until the writer finishes would badly block readers and writers against each other — exactly what serving the old version is meant to avoid.
Letting readers see uncommitted versions and fix them later is exactly how a dirty read happens, the opposite of what read committed is trying to block.
Sending the transaction log to clients to decide for themselves isn't realistic and isn't how databases actually implement isolation levels.

scenario: 备份任务要扫完整库几十分钟，同时线上写入继续进行；备份必须自洽。
scenario_en: A backup scans the whole database for tens of minutes while production writes continue, and the backup must be self-consistent.
q: 应该优先使用哪种隔离？
q_en: Which isolation level should you prefer?
options: 读已提交
快照隔离
读未提交
只读缓存
options_en: Read committed
Snapshot isolation
Read uncommitted
Read-only cache
why: 快照隔离让长读事务看到同一时间点的版本集合，线上写入可以继续。代价是要保留旧版本直到读完成。
why_en: Snapshot isolation lets a long read see one consistent point-in-time view while writes continue.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询只读单行且不需要跨语句一致，读已提交更省版本保留成本。
tradeoff: 稳定读视图 vs 旧版本存储成本

termDefinitions.meaning: MVCC 为同一数据保留多个版本，让读事务看到稳定快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVCC keeps multiple versions of data so a transaction can read a stable snapshot.

optionExplanations: 读已提交只保证单条语句层面不读到脏数据，扫描几十分钟的过程中，早查过的行和晚查的行可能来自不同的提交点，备份内部会自相矛盾。
快照隔离让这次长时间扫描全程看着同一个时间点的版本集合，线上写入照常进行，备份读到的数据自洽一致，正好满足这里的需求。
读未提交连未提交的数据都能读到，备份的自洽性完全没有保障，风险比读已提交还大。
只读缓存拿到的是缓存里的旧快照，不是数据库本身给出的隔离保证，也没法覆盖几十分钟持续进行的全库扫描。
optionExplanations_en: Read committed only guarantees each individual statement avoids dirty data — across a scan lasting tens of minutes, earlier rows and later rows could come from different commit points, leaving the backup internally inconsistent.

Snapshot isolation lets this long-running scan see one consistent point-in-time set of versions throughout, while online writes keep happening, giving the backup a self-consistent view — exactly what's needed here.
Read uncommitted can read even uncommitted data, offering no guarantee of internal consistency at all, riskier than read committed.
A read-only cache serves whatever stale snapshot happens to be cached, not a database-level isolation guarantee, and can't cover a tens-of-minutes full scan reliably.

scenario: 数据库用 MVCC 支持快照隔离。
scenario_en: A database uses MVCC to provide snapshot isolation.
q: 读事务如何拿到稳定视图？
q_en: How does a read transaction get a stable view?
options: 选择对自己可见的数据版本
暂停所有写事务
只读最新物理页
把数据复制到客户端内存
options_en: It chooses the data versions visible to that transaction
It pauses all write transactions
It reads only the latest physical page
It copies the database into client memory
why: MVCC 给版本打上创建/删除边界，读事务按自己的快照选择可见版本。这样读者通常不阻塞写者。
why_en: MVCC gives versions visibility boundaries so a transaction can read the versions that belong to its snapshot.

termDefinitions.meaning: MVCC 为同一数据保留多个版本，让读事务看到稳定快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVCC keeps multiple versions of data so a transaction can read a stable snapshot.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  W1[write v1] --> S[reader snapshot]
  S --> R[read v1]
  W2[concurrent write v2] --> R2[later readers see v2]
optionExplanations: 每个版本都带着创建和删除的边界信息，读事务按照自己启动时那个快照的可见性规则，从多个版本里挑出对自己可见的那一份。
暂停所有写事务会让写入完全停摆，跟 MVCC 想要读写互不阻塞的设计目标正相反。
只读最新物理页会直接读到还没提交或比自己快照更新的数据，破坏了快照该看到的固定视图。
把数据复制到客户端内存不是 MVCC 的做法，MVCC 的版本选择发生在数据库内部，不涉及把整份数据搬到客户端。
optionExplanations_en: Every version carries creation and deletion boundaries, and a read transaction picks out whichever versions are visible under the snapshot rule it started with.
Pausing all write transactions would stop writes entirely, the opposite of MVCC's goal of keeping readers and writers from blocking each other.
Reading only the latest physical page would expose data that's uncommitted or newer than the transaction's own snapshot, breaking the fixed view a snapshot is supposed to give.
Copying the database into client memory isn't how MVCC works — version selection happens inside the database, not by moving the whole dataset to the client.

scenario: 同一个事务先查订单总数，几秒后又查一次；中间有人提交了新订单。
scenario_en: A transaction reads an order count, then reads it again seconds later; another transaction commits a new order in between.
q: 读已提交和快照隔离差别在哪？
q_en: How do read committed and snapshot isolation differ?
options: 读已提交每次读都会变，快照隔离全程稳定
两者都能保证完整可串行化的隔离级别
快照隔离一定会阻塞所有写
读已提交就能防住写偏斜
options_en: Read committed can change between reads; snapshot isolation stays stable all transaction long.
Both guarantee full serializable isolation.
Snapshot isolation always blocks every write.
Read committed already prevents write skew.
why: 读已提交通常按语句取视图，快照隔离按事务取视图。稳定视图不等于可串行化。
why_en: Read committed often gives each statement a fresh view, while snapshot isolation gives the whole transaction one stable view.
tradeoff: 新鲜读 vs 一致快照

termDefinitions.meaning: MVCC 为同一数据保留多个版本，让读事务看到稳定快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVCC keeps multiple versions of data so a transaction can read a stable snapshot.

optionExplanations: 读已提交通常按每条语句各自取一次视图，两次查询之间如果有人提交了新订单，第二次查询就能看到它；快照隔离在整个事务开始时定住一个视图，同一事务内两次查询看到的是同一批数据。
两者都不承诺可串行化，读已提交和快照隔离都只是隔离级别的一种，不是最高保证。
快照隔离只是给读事务一个固定的历史视图，不代表它会阻塞所有并发写入，写入仍然可以继续进行。
读已提交防不住写偏斜，写偏斜恰恰更容易在快照隔离下悄悄发生，这个说法把两者的能力搞反了。
optionExplanations_en: Read committed typically gives each statement its own fresh view, so a second query in the same transaction can see an order committed in between; snapshot isolation fixes one view at the start of the whole transaction, so both queries within it see the same data.
Neither guarantees serializability — both read committed and snapshot isolation are just isolation levels short of the strongest guarantee.
Snapshot isolation just gives a read transaction a fixed historical view; it doesn't block all concurrent writes, which can still proceed.
Read committed doesn't prevent write skew — write skew is actually more likely to slip through under snapshot isolation, so this option has the two capabilities backwards.

scenario: 点赞计数是热点字段，客户端不能先读值再把 value+1 写回。
scenario_en: A like counter is a hot field, and clients should not read the value and write value+1 back.
q: 最简单的数据库侧修复是什么？
q_en: What is the simplest database-side fix?
options: 数据库原子加一更新
先读副本再写主库
把计数缓存在每台 Web 服务器
用读未提交减少等待
options_en: An atomic increment in the database
Read from a replica and then write to the leader
Cache the counter on every web server
Use read uncommitted to wait less
why: 原子更新把计算放在数据库内部，避免两个客户端基于同一个旧值写回。热点很高时还要分片计数。
why_en: An atomic update keeps the increment inside the database so two clients do not overwrite each other’s read-modify-write result.
whenOtherWins: 如果计数可以短暂不准，分片计数器或异步聚合会比强原子更新更能扛热点。
tradeoff: 精确更新 vs 热点吞吐
codeSample:
UPDATE counters
SET value = value + 1
WHERE id = ?;
-- 加一在数据库内完成，避免读后写覆盖。
optionExplanations: 让数据库直接对这一行执行原子加一，把读值和加值这两步合并成数据库内部的一次操作，两个客户端都不会拿着同一个旧值覆盖对方。
先读副本再写主库，读到的副本值可能已经落后，两个客户端很可能基于同一个旧值各自加一再写回，恰恰会制造丢失更新。
把计数缓存在每台 Web 服务器上，各个服务器之间的计数互不同步，最后合并起来同样会互相覆盖，问题没有解决。
读未提交只是放宽了能看到什么数据，跟“两个客户端基于旧值同时写回”这个丢失更新的成因完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Letting the database do the atomic increment directly folds reading and incrementing into one database operation, so two clients can never both grab the same stale value and overwrite each other.

Reading from a replica and writing to the leader risks the replica value already being stale, so two clients are likely to increment the same old value and overwrite each other — creating exactly a lost update.
Caching the counter on every web server leaves each server's count out of sync with the others, and merging them later still overwrites data, the problem isn't solved.
Read uncommitted only loosens what data is visible; it has nothing to do with the two-clients-writing-from-the-same-stale-value cause of a lost update.

scenario: 转账事务要先读账户余额，再根据余额决定是否扣款；不希望另一个事务同时改这行。
scenario_en: A transfer transaction reads an account balance, decides whether to debit, and must prevent another transaction from changing that row meanwhile.
q: 应该用哪种机制？
q_en: Which mechanism fits this case?
options: FOR UPDATE 行锁
普通 SELECT 后在应用里睡眠
读副本检查余额
只靠 HTTP 请求重试
options_en: A FOR UPDATE row lock
A normal SELECT followed by sleeping in the app
Read a replica to check the balance
Rely only on HTTP request retries
why: 显式行锁把“读余额”和“扣款”连成一个受保护区间。代价是并发事务可能等待或死锁后重试。
why_en: A row lock protects the interval between checking the balance and writing the debit, at the cost of waits or retries.
whenOtherWins: 如果逻辑能写成单条条件更新，直接 UPDATE ... WHERE balance >= amount 通常更短。
tradeoff: 显式保护区间 vs 锁等待成本
optionExplanations: FOR UPDATE 行锁把这一行从读到扣款这段时间锁住，另一个事务想改同一行时会被挡住等待，读余额和扣款之间不会被插队。
普通 SELECT 后在应用里睡眠不会阻止别的事务在这段等待期间修改同一行余额，睡眠只是消耗时间，没有真正加锁。
读副本上的余额可能落后于主库，用它来判断要不要扣款，本身就可能基于过时数据做出错误决定。
只靠 HTTP 请求重试解决的是网络层面的失败，不能阻止另一个数据库事务在这期间并发修改同一行。
optionExplanations_en: A FOR UPDATE row lock holds the row from the moment it's read through the debit, so another transaction trying to touch the same row has to wait, closing the window between checking and debiting.
A normal SELECT followed by sleeping in the app doesn't stop another transaction from modifying the same row balance during that wait — sleeping just burns time without actually locking anything.
A replica's balance can lag behind the primary, so basing the decision to debit on it risks acting on stale data.
Relying only on HTTP request retries addresses network-level failures; it doesn't stop another database transaction from concurrently modifying the same row in the meantime.

scenario: 应用用 CAS 防丢失更新，但数据库的 WHERE 条件可能在旧快照上判断。
scenario_en: An app uses compare-and-set to prevent lost updates, but the database may evaluate the WHERE condition on an old snapshot.
q: 这个方案的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the risk in this approach?
options: 条件看起来成立，实际仍覆盖并发更新
所有并发事务最终都会退化成只读
提交后一定丢失日志
它只能用于网络超时
options_en: The condition appears true while a concurrent update is still overwritten
All concurrent transactions eventually degrade to read-only.
Commit logs are always lost
It only applies to network timeouts
why: CAS 只有在条件按最新已提交值检查时才可靠。隔离语义不清时，要验证数据库是否真正检测冲突。
why_en: CAS only works if the condition is checked against the current committed value, so verify the database’s conflict behavior.
tradeoff: 乐观条件写 vs 隐含快照语义

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS 只有在当前值仍等于预期值时才写入新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set writes a new value only if the current value still equals the expected value.

optionExplanations: 如果数据库的 WHERE 条件判断依赖的是一个旧快照而不是最新已提交值，条件表面上看起来成立，实际执行时并发的另一次更新已经悄悄被覆盖掉了。
这个风险跟事务是不是只读没有关系，CAS 本身既用于读也用于写，不会让所有事务都变成只读。
这里描述的是条件判断可能基于旧快照这个逻辑风险，跟提交后日志会不会丢失是完全不同的问题。
CAS 是一种通用的条件更新技巧，不是专门为网络超时设计的，这个说法把它的用途说窄了。
optionExplanations_en: If the database's WHERE condition is evaluated against a stale snapshot instead of the current committed value, the condition can look satisfied while a concurrent update actually gets silently overwritten underneath it.
This risk has nothing to do with whether transactions are read-only — CAS is used for both reading and writing, it doesn't turn every transaction read-only.
This is a logical risk about the condition being checked against a stale snapshot, a completely different issue from whether commit logs get lost.
CAS is a general conditional-update technique, not something designed specifically for network timeouts — this option narrows its purpose incorrectly.

scenario: 数据库在快照隔离下发现两个事务写同一对象，选择中止其中一个。
scenario_en: Under snapshot isolation, a database detects that two transactions wrote the same object and aborts one.
q: 这属于什么防护？
q_en: What protection is this?
options: 自动丢失更新检测
谓词锁
两阶段提交协议
物化冲突
options_en: Automatic lost update detection
Predicate locking
two-phase commit protocol
Materializing conflicts
why: 自动检测让读改写先并发执行，提交时发现覆盖风险再中止。应用必须准备好重试事务。
why_en: Automatic lost-update detection lets work run optimistically and aborts a transaction at commit time if overwrite risk appears.
tradeoff: 并发执行 vs 提交时重试

rows: 前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
自动丢失更新检测成本
必须保护最新读或不变量时
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适

optionExplanations: 两个事务先并发跑起来，数据库在提交时发现它们写了同一个对象，于是中止其中一个，这正是自动丢失更新检测的工作方式。
谓词锁保护的是符合某个查询条件、可能包括还不存在的行的整个范围，跟这里“发现同一对象被两个事务写”这种具体行冲突不是一回事。
两阶段提交是协调多个参与者一起提交或一起回滚的协议，跟单个数据库内部检测到同一对象写冲突没有关系。
物化冲突是把原本无法上锁的谓词冲突转成可以上锁的具体行，跟这里数据库自动检测到写写冲突后中止事务的机制不同。
optionExplanations_en: The two transactions ran concurrently first, and the database discovered at commit time that they wrote the same object, so it aborted one — exactly how automatic lost-update detection works.
A predicate lock protects a whole range matching a query condition, possibly including rows that don't exist yet — different from this specific same-object write conflict.
Two-phase commit coordinates multiple participants to commit or roll back together; it has nothing to do with detecting a same-object write conflict inside one database.

Materializing conflicts turns an otherwise unlockable predicate conflict into a concrete lockable row, a different mechanism from the database automatically detecting and aborting on a write-write conflict.

scenario: 排班系统要求至少一名医生值班；两个医生同时看到还有两人值班，于是各自把自己设为休假。
scenario_en: A rota system requires at least one doctor on call; two doctors each see two doctors on call and independently mark themselves off duty.
q: 这是什么异常？
q_en: Which anomaly is this?
options: 丢失更新
写偏斜
脏写
持久性失败
options_en: Lost update
Write skew
Dirty write
Durability failure
why: 两个事务读同一组行，却写不同的行，所以没有同一对象覆盖。快照隔离可能放过它，结果破坏跨行不变量。
why_en: Write skew happens when transactions read the same predicate but update different rows, breaking a cross-row invariant.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有事务都更新同一汇总行，丢失更新检测或行锁就可能足够。
tradeoff: 非阻塞快照读 vs 跨行不变量

termDefinitions.meaning: MVCC 为同一数据保留多个版本，让读事务看到稳定快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVCC keeps multiple versions of data so a transaction can read a stable snapshot.

optionExplanations: 丢失更新指两个事务基于同一个值各自计算再写回同一个对象，这里两个医生写的是各自不同的行（自己的排班），不是同一行被覆盖。
两个事务都读了同一组行（当前值班人数），却各自更新了不同的行（自己请假），谁都没有覆盖对方的写，但两人一起请假打破了“至少一人值班”这个跨行不变量，这正是写偏斜。
脏写指的是覆盖了另一个事务尚未提交的写，这里两个事务各自提交的是自己那一行，互不覆盖，不是脏写。
持久性失败指提交后数据因崩溃消失，这里的问题出在业务规则被破坏，跟数据有没有在崩溃中丢失无关。
optionExplanations_en: A lost update means two transactions compute from the same value and overwrite the same object; here the two doctors wrote different rows (their own schedules), not the same row being overwritten.

Both transactions read the same set of rows (the current on-call count) but each updated a different row (their own leave), so neither overwrote the other's write, yet both taking leave together broke the cross-row invariant of at least one doctor on call — exactly write skew.
A dirty write means overwriting another transaction's uncommitted write; here each transaction committed its own row without overwriting the other, not a dirty write.
A durability failure means committed data vanishing after a crash; the problem here is a broken business rule, unrelated to data being lost in a crash.

scenario: 两个事务都读同一条件，但分别更新不同记录。
scenario_en: Two transactions read the same condition but update different records.
q: 为什么丢失更新检测不够？
q_en: Why is lost-update detection insufficient?
options: 它通常只发现同一对象被覆盖
它只检查磁盘是否 fsync
它只用于只读事务
它会禁止所有并发读
options_en: It usually detects overwrites of the same object
It only checks whether disk fsync happened
It only applies to read-only transactions
It forbids all concurrent reads
why: 写偏斜的冲突在“读集合”和“写集合”的关系里，不一定有同一行写写冲突。要靠可串行化或显式物化冲突。
why_en: Write skew can have no same-row write conflict, so lost-update detection alone misses it.
tradeoff: 对象级冲突检测 vs 谓词级不变量

rows: 它通常只发现同一对象被覆盖
它通常只发现同一对…场景
它通常只发现同一对象被…成本
它只检查磁盘是否 fsync
它只检查磁盘是否 …场景
它只检查磁盘是否 fs…成本
它只用于只读事务场景
它只用于只读事务成本
它会禁止所有并发读场景
它会禁止所有并发读成本

optionExplanations: 丢失更新检测的核心逻辑是看有没有同一个对象被两次写覆盖，而写偏斜里两个事务写的是不同的行，压根不存在同一对象被覆盖这回事，所以这套检测抓不到它。
丢失更新检测跟磁盘有没有 fsync 是完全不同的机制，不该混为一谈。
丢失更新检测同样适用于写事务，不是只用于只读事务，这个说法不成立。
丢失更新检测不会禁止并发读，它只是在提交时检查有没有同对象写冲突，跟读并发无关。
optionExplanations_en: Lost-update detection's core logic looks for the same object being overwritten by two writes, but write skew involves two transactions writing different rows, so there's no same-object overwrite to catch at all — that's why the detection misses it.
Lost-update detection is a completely different mechanism from checking whether a disk fsync happened, so the two shouldn't be conflated.
Lost-update detection applies to write transactions too, not only read-only ones, so this claim doesn't hold.
Lost-update detection doesn't forbid concurrent reads at all; it only checks for same-object write conflicts at commit time, unrelated to read concurrency.

scenario: 用户名必须唯一；两个请求同时注册同一个用户名。
scenario_en: Usernames must be unique, and two requests concurrently register the same username.
q: 最合适的数据库防线是什么？
q_en: What is the best database defense?
options: 唯一约束或唯一索引
后台批处理去重
读副本先查有没有
把用户名放进缓存 set
options_en: A uniqueness constraint or unique index
A background deduplication job
Check a read replica first
Put usernames into a cached set
why: 唯一约束把不变量交给数据库提交路径检查，能挡住并发插入。读副本和缓存都会受延迟或失效影响。
why_en: A uniqueness constraint checks the invariant on the commit path, so concurrent inserts cannot both win.
whenOtherWins: 如果冲突很少且重复可人工修复，异步去重会更便宜但用户体验更差。
tradeoff: 提交时拒绝冲突 vs 异步修复成本
optionExplanations: 唯一约束或唯一索引把“用户名不能重复”这条规则交给数据库的提交路径检查，两个并发插入同一用户名的请求里只会有一个真正提交成功，另一个会被拒绝。
后台批处理去重是在数据已经写进去、可能已经重复之后才补救，防不住这一刻两个并发请求都成功写入。
读副本可能落后于主库，先查读副本有没有这个用户名，判断出的结果可能是过时的，挡不住真正的并发插入。
缓存 set 里的数据同样可能落后或者跟数据库不同步，靠它判断唯一性也无法真正阻止两个并发请求都写进数据库。
optionExplanations_en: A uniqueness constraint or unique index puts the no-duplicate-usernames rule on the database's commit path, so of two concurrent inserts for the same username, only one can actually commit and the other gets rejected.
A background deduplication job only cleans up after data has already been written and possibly duplicated, it can't stop both concurrent requests from succeeding in the first place.
A read replica can lag behind the primary, so checking it for an existing username can give a stale answer that doesn't actually block real concurrent inserts.
Data in a cached set can also be stale or out of sync with the database, so relying on it for uniqueness can't truly prevent both concurrent requests from writing to the database.

scenario: 会议室预订事务先查 10 点到 11 点无人预订，再插入自己的预订；两个事务都这样做。
scenario_en: A room-booking transaction checks that 10-11 is free and then inserts a booking; two transactions do this concurrently.
q: 这里的幻读风险是什么？
q_en: What is the phantom risk here?
options: 要锁的行还不存在，行锁无从下手
提交日志有可能被重复地写入两次
单行更新会自动失败回滚
读副本会变得线性化一致
options_en: The rows to lock do not exist yet, so row locks have nothing to hold.
The commit log may be written twice by duplication.
Single-row updates automatically fail and roll back.
Read replicas become linearizable.
why: 幻读来自谓词范围：事务读的是“没有匹配行”，另一个事务却插入了匹配行。普通行锁抓不到不存在的行。
why_en: A phantom appears when the transaction depends on absence in a predicate range and another transaction inserts a matching row.
tradeoff: 行级锁简单性 vs 范围谓词保护
optionExplanations: 两个事务查询的是“这段时间没有预订”，此刻符合条件的记录根本不存在，普通行锁只能锁住已经存在的行，锁不住一个还没出现的东西，所以两边都查到了空结果并各自插入。
提交日志重复写入是持久化实现层面的问题，跟这里查询空结果后并发插入导致的幻读没有关系。
单行更新不会因为这里的场景就自动失败，问题恰恰在于两个事务各自插入的是不同的新行，不存在单行冲突让它失败。
读副本会不会变成线性化和这里描述的幻读现象毫无关系，答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Both transactions query for no existing booking in that slot, and at that moment no matching row actually exists — a plain row lock can only lock rows that exist, not something that hasn't appeared yet, so both see an empty result and both insert.
Commit logs being written twice is a durability-implementation concern, unrelated to the phantom caused here by an empty-query-then-insert race.
A single-row update doesn't automatically fail in this scenario — the real issue is that each transaction inserts a different new row, so there's no single-row conflict to fail on.
Whether read replicas become linearizable has nothing to do with the phantom described here, so this option doesn't address the question.

scenario: 会议室系统没有可锁的“空时间段”行，但必须防止同一房间同一小时双订。
scenario_en: A room-booking system has no row for an empty slot, but must prevent double booking for the same room-hour.
q: 物化冲突怎么帮忙？
q_en: How does materializing conflicts help?
options: 建立可锁的槽位行
把查询改成读未提交
把所有预订只写日志不查询
把房间名随机打散
options_en: Create a lockable slot row
Change the query to read uncommitted
Only append bookings without querying
Randomly shard room names
why: 物化冲突把“没有行”的谓词冲突变成“锁同一槽位行”的写写冲突。代价是要维护额外的槽位模型。
why_en: Materializing conflicts turns an absence-based predicate conflict into a concrete row conflict that can be locked.
whenOtherWins: 如果数据库有可靠谓词锁或可串行化隔离，额外槽位行可能不值得。
tradeoff: 额外建模复杂度 vs 可锁冲突点
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[check room-hour slot] --> B[lock slot row]
  B --> C[insert booking]
  C --> D[commit or abort]
optionExplanations: 没有可锁的空槽位行时，先建出一行代表这个房间这个小时的槽位，两个事务都要先锁这一行才能插入预订，谁先锁到谁能继续，把原本锁不住的“空”变成了能锁的具体行。
把查询改成读未提交只会让隔离更弱，反而更容易读到脏数据，不能防止双订。
只写日志不查询会让系统完全无法判断某个时间段有没有被预订过，根本没有防止双订的机制。
把房间名随机打散跟这里“同一房间同一小时不能双订”这个不变量的检测机制没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: With no lockable empty-slot row to begin with, creating a row representing this room's hour ahead of time means both transactions must lock that row before inserting a booking, so whoever locks it first proceeds — turning an unlockable absence into a lockable concrete row.
Changing the query to read uncommitted just weakens isolation further and makes dirty reads more likely, it doesn't prevent double booking.
Only appending bookings without querying leaves the system with no way to tell whether a slot was already booked, no double-booking protection at all.
Randomly sharding room names has nothing to do with the mechanism for detecting the same-room-same-hour invariant here.

scenario: 金融系统有跨多行余额、额度和风控规则；错误比少量重试更贵。
scenario_en: A financial system has cross-row balance, limit, and risk rules; a wrong result is more expensive than some retries.
q: 应优先考虑哪种隔离？
q_en: Which isolation level should you consider first?
options: 读未提交
读已提交
快照隔离
可串行化隔离
options_en: Read uncommitted
Read committed
Snapshot isolation
Serializable isolation
why: 可串行化给出结果等价于事务逐个运行，最适合保护复杂不变量。代价是锁等待、重试或单线程瓶颈。
why_en: Serializable isolation makes the result equivalent to running transactions one at a time, which protects complex invariants.
whenOtherWins: 如果不变量局限在单行或唯一索引，较弱隔离加约束通常更便宜。
tradeoff: 不变量安全 vs 并发成本
optionExplanations: 读未提交连没提交的数据都能读到，对金融系统这种错误代价极高的场景来说风险太大，完全不合适。
读已提交只挡脏读，挡不住丢失更新和写偏斜，跨多行余额、额度、风控规则这类复杂不变量很容易被绕过。
快照隔离能给一致的视图，但仍然可能放过写偏斜这类跨行竞态，对“错误比重试更贵”的场景保护不够。
可串行化让结果等价于事务逐个顺序执行，能同时守住跨行余额、额度和风控这些复杂不变量，虽然有锁等待或重试的代价，但换来的正确性对金融系统来说更值得。
optionExplanations_en: Read uncommitted can even see uncommitted data, far too risky for a financial system where an error is much more expensive than a retry.
Read committed only blocks dirty reads — it doesn't stop lost updates or write skew, so complex invariants spanning balance, credit limit, and risk rules across rows can easily slip through.
Snapshot isolation gives a consistent view but can still let write skew slip through across rows, not enough protection for a system where errors cost more than retries.

Serializable isolation makes the outcome equivalent to running transactions one at a time, protecting complex cross-row invariants for balance, credit, and risk together, and the lock waits or retries it costs are worth it here.

scenario: 数据库实际并发执行事务，但承诺结果像某个顺序逐个执行。
scenario_en: A database runs transactions concurrently but promises the result is as if they ran one at a time in some order.
q: 这个承诺叫什么？
q_en: What is this guarantee called?
options: 实际串行执行
可串行化
线性化
最终一致
options_en: Actual serial execution
Serializability
Linearizability
Eventual consistency
why: 可串行化关心结果是否等价于某个串行顺序，不要求物理上真的一个接一个执行。线性化是单对象新鲜度保证。
why_en: Serializability is about equivalence to some serial order, not necessarily physically executing one transaction at a time.
tradeoff: 结果等价性 vs 实际执行方式
optionExplanations: 实际串行执行是指数据库物理上真的一个接一个跑事务，不并发，这跟场景描述的“实际并发执行”正相反。
可串行化关心的是结果看起来是不是等价于某种顺序逐个执行，不要求物理上真的串行跑，这正是场景描述的情况。
线性化保证的是单个对象的读写看起来像是瞬时发生、全局有序，讨论的是不同层面的问题，不是这里描述的多事务顺序等价性。
最终一致只保证副本之间迟早收敛到同一状态，跟“结果等价于某个顺序执行”这种事务级别的保证不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Actual serial execution means the database physically runs transactions one after another with no concurrency, the opposite of the actual concurrent execution described here.
Serializability is about the result being equivalent to some serial order, without requiring physically sequential execution — exactly what's described here.
Linearizability guarantees a single object's reads and writes appear to happen instantaneously in a global order, a different concern from the multi-transaction ordering equivalence described here.
Eventual consistency only guarantees replicas eventually converge to the same state, a different kind of guarantee from result-equivalent-to-some-order at the transaction level.

scenario: 内存数据库把每个分区的事务逻辑作为短小存储过程执行，事务都很快且不等待外部 API。
scenario_en: An in-memory database executes short stored procedures per partition, and transactions are fast with no external API waits.
q: 实际串行执行何时可行？
q_en: When is actual serial execution feasible?
options: 事务短、数据在内存、分区能限制热点
事务中途常常要停下来等人工审批
每个事务都要跨所有分区
每个查询都要扫描冷数据
options_en: Transactions are short, data fits in memory, and partitioning caps the hot spots.
Transactions often pause mid-way to wait for human approval.
Every transaction spans all partitions.
Every query scans cold data.
why: 单线程串行靠避免并发控制换简单性，但只能吃下单核/单分区吞吐。长事务或跨分区会拖住队列。
why_en: Actual serial execution is attractive for short in-memory transactions, but long or cross-partition work blocks the queue.
whenOtherWins: 如果事务包含慢 I/O 或跨很多分区，2PL 或 SSI 这类并发方案更实际。
tradeoff: 无并发控制开销 vs 单执行队列瓶颈
optionExplanations: 事务短、数据都在内存里不用等磁盘 I/O、又靠分区把热点限制在各自范围内，单线程一个接一个执行也能吃下不错的吞吐，不会互相拖长队。
事务要是常等人工审批，队列里的其它事务都要陪着一起等，这正是实际串行执行最怕遇到的场景，不是它可行的条件。
每个事务都跨所有分区意味着单线程要为每笔事务都协调全部分区，完全失去了分区限制热点这个优势。
每次查询都扫冷数据意味着单次执行时间被拉长，跟“事务短”这个前提直接矛盾，会拖垮整个串行队列。
optionExplanations_en: With short transactions, data already in memory with no disk I/O to wait on, and partitioning containing hotspots to their own range, running them one at a time on a single thread can still hit decent throughput without piling up a long queue.
If transactions often wait on human approval, everything else in the queue waits along with it — exactly the scenario actual serial execution can't tolerate, not a condition that makes it viable.
Every transaction spanning all partitions means the single thread has to coordinate across every partition for every transaction, losing the whole advantage of partitioning to contain hotspots.
Every query scanning cold data stretches out each execution, directly contradicting the short-transaction premise and clogging the entire serial queue.

scenario: 单线程事务引擎要求业务逻辑在数据库内执行。
scenario_en: A single-threaded transaction engine requires business logic to run inside the database.
q: 为什么不适合交互式多轮事务？
q_en: Why is it a poor fit for interactive multi-round transactions?
options: 事务等客户端时会堵住后面所有事务
它无法写入内存里的数据
它天然不支持任何索引
它会让事务日志变得彻底不可恢复
options_en: While a transaction waits on the client, everything behind it stalls.
It cannot write data held in memory.
It inherently supports no indexes.
It makes the transaction log entirely unrecoverable.
why: 实际串行执行的队列里不能夹长等待。存储过程把读写逻辑一次发进数据库，避免事务边执行边等客户端。
why_en: A serial execution queue cannot afford client think time, so stored procedures send the transaction logic in one shot.
optionExplanations: 单线程串行执行的队列里，一个事务要是卡在等客户端下一步输入，后面排队的所有事务都要跟着一起干等，整个系统的吞吐会被这一次交互拖垮。
能不能写内存数据跟事务要不要在多轮里等客户端完全是两回事，不成立。
支不支持索引是存储引擎层面的能力，跟单线程执行模型要不要等客户端输入没有关系。
日志能不能恢复是持久化层面的问题，跟这里讨论的“队列里能不能夹长时间等待”不是同一个问题。
optionExplanations_en: In a single-threaded serial execution queue, if one transaction sits waiting on the client's next input, every transaction queued behind it has to wait too, and that one interaction can tank the whole system's throughput.
Whether it can write in-memory data has nothing to do with whether a transaction needs to wait on the client across multiple round trips, so this doesn't hold.
Index support is a storage-engine capability, unrelated to whether a single-threaded execution model can afford to wait on client input.
Whether the log is recoverable is a durability concern, a different question from whether the queue can tolerate a long wait in the middle.

scenario: 数据库要用锁实现可串行化，并允许读读并发但阻止冲突读写。
scenario_en: A database wants lock-based serializability, allowing read-read concurrency while blocking conflicting reads and writes.
q: 核心机制是什么？
q_en: What is the core mechanism?
options: 两阶段锁：读锁/写锁按规则持有到事务结束
只给每条语句一个新快照
用 NTP 墙钟时间戳决定全局提交顺序
只在应用层加互斥锁
options_en: Two-phase locking with read/write locks held by rule until transaction end
Give every statement a fresh snapshot
Use NTP wall-clock timestamps to decide global commit order.
Use only application-level mutexes
why: 2PL 用共享读锁和独占写锁控制冲突，锁通常持有到事务结束。代价是阻塞和死锁检测。
why_en: Two-phase locking controls conflicts with shared and exclusive locks, at the cost of blocking and deadlock handling.
whenOtherWins: 如果读多且不能接受读写互相阻塞，SSI 可能更适合。
tradeoff: 阻塞式安全 vs 读写并发

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PL 先获取需要的锁，提交或回滚后再释放，用锁顺序实现可串行化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase locking acquires locks before releasing them at commit or abort to enforce serializability.

optionExplanations: 两阶段锁按规则给读操作加共享锁、给写操作加独占锁，锁通常一直持有到事务结束才释放，靠这套规则控制哪些操作能并发、哪些要互相等待。
只给每条语句一个新快照是 MVCC 或读已提交类实现的做法，不是两阶段锁的核心机制。
用 NTP 时间戳决定提交顺序是另一类基于时钟的并发控制思路，不是两阶段锁依赖的机制。
只在应用层加互斥锁没法覆盖数据库内部多个事务、多张表之间的并发控制，达不到这里要的效果。
optionExplanations_en: Two-phase locking follows a rule of shared locks for reads and exclusive locks for writes, usually held until the transaction ends, and uses that rule to control which operations can run concurrently and which must wait.
Giving each statement a fresh snapshot is how MVCC or read-committed-style implementations work, not the core mechanism of two-phase locking.
Using NTP timestamps to decide commit order is a different, clock-based concurrency-control idea, not what two-phase locking relies on.
Using only application-level mutexes can't cover concurrency control across multiple transactions and tables inside the database, falling short of what's needed here.

scenario: 系统读多写少，长报表不应阻塞在线更新。
scenario_en: A system is read-heavy, and long reports should not block online updates.
q: 2PL 与 MVCC 的关键差别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between 2PL and MVCC?
options: 2PL 冲突就等待，MVCC 让读者读旧版本
MVCC 会彻底禁止任何并发进行的写入事务
2PL 完全不支持写事务并发
两者都只能读到未提交的数据
options_en: 2PL makes conflicting transactions wait; MVCC lets readers read an older version.
MVCC completely forbids any concurrent write transaction.
2PL cannot run write transactions concurrently at all.
Both can only read uncommitted data.
why: 2PL 靠等待保护顺序，MVCC 靠版本让读写少互相卡住。MVCC 仍要处理写写冲突和写偏斜。
why_en: 2PL protects order by waiting, while MVCC reduces read-write blocking through versions.
tradeoff: 等待锁 vs 版本存储

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PL 先获取需要的锁，提交或回滚后再释放，用锁顺序实现可串行化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase locking acquires locks before releasing them at commit or abort to enforce serializability.

termDefinitions.meaning: MVCC 为同一数据保留多个版本，让读事务看到稳定快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVCC keeps multiple versions of data so a transaction can read a stable snapshot.

optionExplanations: 2PL 遇到冲突时让后来者等待前面持锁的事务释放，MVCC 靠版本让读者去看一个旧的已提交版本，读多写少、长报表也不用等在线更新，两者的策略方向完全不同。
MVCC 不禁止并发写，它只是让读者不必因为写者在改而阻塞，写写之间该有的冲突处理照样存在。
2PL 同样支持写事务，只是写锁会让冲突的操作互相等待，说它不支持写是不成立的。
两者都不是只能读未提交，2PL 和 MVCC 都是为了提供比读未提交更强的隔离保证而设计的。
optionExplanations_en: 2PL makes a later conflicting operation wait for the lock holder to release, while MVCC lets readers see an older committed version, so a read-heavy long report doesn't have to wait on an online update — the two take fundamentally different approaches.
MVCC doesn't forbid concurrent writes; it just lets readers avoid blocking on an in-progress writer, while write-write conflicts still need their own handling.
2PL supports writes just fine — write locks just make conflicting operations wait for each other, so claiming it doesn't support writes is incorrect.
Neither is limited to dirty reads only; both 2PL and MVCC exist precisely to provide stronger isolation than read uncommitted.

scenario: 事务 A 锁住行 1 等行 2，事务 B 锁住行 2 等行 1。
scenario_en: Transaction A locks row 1 and waits for row 2; transaction B locks row 2 and waits for row 1.
q: 2PL 必须处理什么？
q_en: What must 2PL handle?
options: 死锁检测并中止一个事务
自动把事务改成最终一致
删除所有索引
关闭事务日志
options_en: Deadlock detection and aborting one transaction
Automatically switch transactions to eventual consistency.
Delete all indexes
Disable the transaction log
why: 锁等待可能形成环，数据库要检测或超时后中止一方。应用要把可重试事务当正常路径。
why_en: Lock waits can form cycles, so the database must abort one transaction and the application must retry.
optionExplanations: 两个事务互相等着对方手里的锁，形成一个环，数据库要检测出这种循环等待，或者靠超时判断出来，然后中止其中一个事务打破僵局。
死锁跟一致性模型的强弱没有关系，数据库不会因为出现死锁就自动切换成最终一致。
删除所有索引不会解开两个事务互相等待对方锁的僵局，跟死锁的成因和解法都无关。
关闭事务日志跟锁等待环没有关系，也不是处理死锁的方式，反而会危及持久性。
optionExplanations_en: Two transactions waiting on each other's locks form a cycle, and the database has to detect that circular wait, or time it out, then abort one transaction to break the deadlock.
A deadlock has nothing to do with how strong the consistency model is; a database doesn't automatically switch to eventual consistency just because a deadlock occurred.
Deleting all indexes doesn't resolve two transactions waiting on each other's locks — it's unrelated to both the cause and the fix for a deadlock.
Disabling the transaction log is unrelated to a lock-wait cycle and isn't how deadlocks are handled — it would actually endanger durability.

scenario: 可串行化数据库要防止“查无预订后插入预订”的幻读。
scenario_en: A serializable database must prevent a transaction from checking for no booking and another transaction inserting one.
q: 最精确的锁是什么？
q_en: What is the most precise lock?
options: 谓词锁，锁住查询条件匹配的范围
只锁住当前已经存在的那些行
只锁住整张表
只锁住客户端连接
options_en: A predicate lock on the range matched by the query condition
Lock only the rows that currently already exist.
Lock the entire table only
Lock only the client connection
why: 谓词锁保护“这个条件下会出现的行”，所以能挡住未来插入的幻影。实现精确但成本高。
why_en: Predicate locks protect rows that would match a condition, including future inserts, but they are expensive to implement.
whenOtherWins: 如果可接受更粗粒度，索引范围锁或物化冲突通常更容易落地。
tradeoff: 精确谓词保护 vs 锁管理成本
optionExplanations: 谓词锁锁住的是“符合这个查询条件的范围”本身，不管匹配的行现在存不存在，之后有人想插入一条符合条件的新行也会被这把锁挡住，能真正防住幻读。
只锁住已经存在的行拦不住插入一条全新的、之前不存在的匹配行，正是幻读能钻的空子。
只锁整张表虽然也能挡住幻读，但代价是把所有并发都堵死，粒度太粗，不是这里说的“最精确”。
只锁客户端连接跟数据库内部的行、范围完全不是一回事，起不到保护数据的作用。
optionExplanations_en: A predicate lock locks the range matching the query condition itself, regardless of whether a matching row currently exists, so a later insert of a new matching row still gets blocked by it, genuinely preventing the phantom.
Locking only rows that already exist can't stop someone from inserting a brand-new matching row that didn't exist before — exactly the gap a phantom exploits.
Locking the entire table would also block phantoms, but at the cost of serializing all concurrency, far too coarse to be called the most precise option here.
Locking only the client connection has nothing to do with rows or ranges inside the database and does nothing to protect the data.

scenario: 数据库用索引支持房间和时间范围查询。
scenario_en: A database has an index for room and time-range booking queries.
q: 索引范围锁为什么常用？
q_en: Why are index-range locks commonly used?
options: 比谓词锁粗一些，但执行更便宜
它完全不需要依赖任何索引
它只保护单行主键记录
它把写入变成异步复制
options_en: It is coarser than a predicate lock but much cheaper to run.
It needs no index at all.
It only protects a single primary-key row.
It turns writes into asynchronous replication.
why: 索引范围锁把谓词映射到索引区间，能防许多幻读。范围太粗时会误伤不冲突的并发写。
why_en: Index-range locks map predicates to index intervals, preventing many phantoms while sometimes blocking non-conflicting writes.
tradeoff: 实现效率 vs 误阻塞

rows: 比谓词锁粗一些，但实现和执行更便宜
必须保护最新读或不变量时
比谓词锁粗一些，但实现…成本
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
它完全不需要索引成本
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
它只保护单行主键成本
它把写入变成异步复制
能接受短暂滞后、想降延迟时

optionExplanations: 索引范围锁把查询条件映射到索引上的一个区间去锁，粒度比精确的谓词锁粗一些，但实现和运行的开销小得多，是常见的折中方案。
索引范围锁恰恰是建立在索引之上的，锁的是索引里的一段区间，没有索引就没有区间可锁。
它保护的是一段索引区间，可能覆盖多行，不是只保护单一的主键行，这个说法把它的粒度说错了。
索引范围锁是并发控制机制，跟写入要不要走异步复制是两回事，不会把写入变成异步复制。
optionExplanations_en: An index-range lock maps the query condition onto a range in the index and locks that, coarser than a precise predicate lock but far cheaper to implement and run — a common tradeoff.
An index-range lock is built directly on top of an index, locking a span within it, so without an index there's no range to lock.
It protects a span of the index that can cover multiple rows, not just a single primary-key row, so this option misstates its granularity.
An index-range lock is a concurrency-control mechanism, unrelated to whether writes go through asynchronous replication — it doesn't turn writes into that.

scenario: 在线业务读多写少，偶发冲突可以重试，但不想让读事务阻塞写事务。
scenario_en: An online workload is read-heavy; occasional conflicts can retry, but reads should not block writes.
q: 哪种可串行化实现更合适？
q_en: Which serializable implementation fits better?
options: SSI，基于快照并在危险依赖时中止
严格 2PL，所有冲突读写都等待
读未提交，完全不做隔离
客户端本地锁
options_en: SSI, using snapshots and aborting dangerous dependencies
Strict 2PL, making conflicting reads and writes wait
Read uncommitted with no real isolation
Client-side local locks
why: SSI 保留快照隔离的读写并发，再用依赖跟踪发现可能的写偏斜。代价是冲突事务要重试。
why_en: SSI keeps snapshot-style read-write concurrency and aborts transactions when dependency tracking finds a serializability risk.
whenOtherWins: 如果冲突率很高，阻塞式 2PL 可能比大量乐观重试更稳定。
tradeoff: 乐观并发 vs 重试开销

termDefinitions.meaning: SSI 在快照隔离上跟踪读写依赖，发现危险结构时中止事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializable Snapshot Isolation tracks read-write dependencies on snapshots and aborts dangerous transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: MVCC 为同一数据保留多个版本，让读事务看到稳定快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVCC keeps multiple versions of data so a transaction can read a stable snapshot.

optionExplanations: SSI 保留了快照隔离下读写正常并发的能力，只在检测到可能导致写偏斜的危险依赖时才中止事务，读事务不会被写事务硬生生挡住。
严格 2PL 要求所有冲突的读写都互相等待，读多写少场景下大量读事务会被写事务频繁卡住，跟这里“不想让读阻塞写”的要求相反。
读未提交完全不做隔离，防不住脏读、丢失更新、写偏斜这些问题，风险太高不适合正经业务。
客户端本地锁只在单个客户端进程内有效，管不住其它客户端或其它服务实例的并发操作，起不到数据库级别的保护作用。
optionExplanations_en: SSI keeps the normal read-write concurrency snapshot isolation allows, only aborting a transaction when dependency tracking finds a dangerous pattern that could cause write skew, so reads are never simply blocked by writes.

Strict 2PL makes every conflicting read and write wait on each other, so in a read-heavy workload readers would frequently get stuck behind writers — the opposite of not wanting reads to block writes here.
Read uncommitted offers no real isolation at all, leaving dirty reads, lost updates, and write skew all possible, too risky for real business logic.
A client-side local lock only works within one client process and can't control concurrent operations from other clients or service instances, offering no database-level protection.

scenario: SSI 在快照隔离上寻找会导致非串行结果的依赖结构。
scenario_en: SSI looks for dependency patterns on top of snapshot isolation that could lead to non-serializable results.
q: 它通常在发现风险后怎么做？
q_en: What does it usually do after finding risk?
options: 中止一个相关事务，让应用重试
悄悄返回旧数据
永久关闭索引
把所有并发事务都改成只读
options_en: Abort one related transaction and let the application retry
Silently return old data
Permanently disable indexes
Turn all concurrent transactions read-only.
why: SSI 是乐观控制：先允许并发，提交附近再打断危险组合。应用的事务函数必须能安全重跑。
why_en: SSI is optimistic: it allows concurrency first and aborts dangerous combinations near commit time.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSI 在快照隔离上跟踪读写依赖，发现危险结构时中止事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializable Snapshot Isolation tracks read-write dependencies on snapshots and aborts dangerous transactions.

optionExplanations: SSI 发现某个依赖组合可能导致最终结果不等价于任何串行顺序时，会中止其中一个相关的事务，交给应用重新跑一遍来解决冲突。
悄悄返回旧数据会隐藏问题而不是解决它，跟发现风险后应该主动处理的做法相反。
永久关闭索引跟发现一次危险的依赖结构没有关系，也不是数据库在这种情况下的正常反应。
把事务改成只读会改变事务本身的语义，不是数据库检测到风险后会擅自做的事，那样会破坏调用方的预期。
optionExplanations_en: When SSI finds a dependency pattern that could make the outcome not equivalent to any serial order, it aborts one of the related transactions and hands it back to the application to retry.
Silently returning old data would hide the problem instead of addressing it, the opposite of proactively handling a detected risk.
Permanently disabling indexes has nothing to do with detecting one dangerous dependency structure and isn't a normal database response to it.

Turning the transaction into read-only mode would change its semantics on its own, not something the database would do unilaterally after detecting a risk, since that would break the caller's expectations.

scenario: 事务基于一个过时快照做决定，同时另一个事务改了它读过的条件结果。
scenario_en: A transaction makes a decision from an old snapshot while another transaction changes the predicate it read.
q: SSI 为什么要跟踪读集合？
q_en: Why does SSI track read sets?
options: 为了知道后续写入是否让先前读失效
为了把所有读请求都转发到只读副本
为了压缩 WAL 日志体积
为了选择缓存的过期时间
options_en: So it can tell whether a later write invalidated what this transaction read.
To route all reads to read-only replicas.
So the WAL can be compressed.
So cache expiry times can be chosen.
why: 写偏斜常从“我读到的前提后来被改了”开始。跟踪读集合能让数据库在提交时发现危险依赖。
why_en: Write skew often starts with a decision based on a predicate that another transaction changes, so SSI tracks those dependencies.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSI 在快照隔离上跟踪读写依赖，发现危险结构时中止事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializable Snapshot Isolation tracks read-write dependencies on snapshots and aborts dangerous transactions.

optionExplanations: 写偏斜常常起于“我读到的这个前提，后来被另一个事务改了”，跟踪读集合能让数据库在提交时判断出这种依赖，发现前提已经变化就中止相关事务。
跟踪读集合是内部并发控制的机制，跟把读请求发到哪个副本这种路由决定没有关系。
跟踪读集合是为了识别危险依赖，不是为了压缩 WAL 这种存储优化目的。
跟踪读集合跟选择缓存过期时间是完全不同层面的问题，一个是事务安全，一个是缓存策略。
optionExplanations_en: Write skew often starts with a decision based on a premise another transaction later changes, and tracking the read set lets the database recognize that dependency at commit time and abort when the premise has shifted.
Tracking the read set is an internal concurrency-control mechanism, unrelated to routing decisions like which replica a read goes to.
Tracking the read set exists to spot dangerous dependencies, not for a storage optimization goal like compressing the WAL.
Tracking the read set and choosing cache TTLs sit at completely different layers — one is transaction safety, the other is caching policy.

scenario: 产品分析查询只读历史数据，可以晚几分钟，但一次导出内部必须自洽。
scenario_en: A product analytics export reads historical data, can be a few minutes stale, but must be internally consistent.
q: 最合适的事务语义是什么？
q_en: Which transaction semantics fit best?
options: 只读快照事务
可串行化写事务
读未提交扫描
每行单独读最新
options_en: A read-only snapshot transaction
A serializable write transaction
A read-uncommitted scan
Read the latest value row by row
why: 只读快照给导出一个固定视图，通常不需要可串行化写冲突检测。它牺牲的是最新性。
why_en: A read-only snapshot gives the export one stable view without needing full serializable write conflict checks.
whenOtherWins: 如果导出结果要触发资金或库存决策，就要升级到可串行化或锁定相关范围。
tradeoff: 导出自洽 vs 最新性
optionExplanations: 只读快照事务给这次导出一个固定的历史视图，全程自洽，不需要处理写事务那套冲突检测，正好匹配“可以晚几分钟、但内部必须自洽”的需求。
可串行化写事务是为了保护写入之间的冲突设计的，这里只是只读导出，用不上写事务那套机制，也是不必要的开销。
读未提交扫描随时可能读到还没提交、之后会回滚的数据，导出内部很可能自相矛盾，不满足自洽的要求。
每行单独读最新会让导出过程中前后读到的数据来自不同时间点，同样破坏了导出内部要自洽这个要求。
optionExplanations_en: A read-only snapshot transaction gives this export one fixed historical view throughout, self-consistent by construction, with no need for write-transaction conflict checks — exactly matching a few-minutes-stale-but-internally-consistent requirement.
A serializable write transaction exists to protect against write-write conflicts, unnecessary machinery and overhead for a read-only export.
A read-uncommitted scan can read data that hasn't committed yet and might later roll back, likely making the export internally contradictory, failing the self-consistency requirement.
Reading the latest value row by row means different rows in the export come from different points in time, also breaking the internal self-consistency requirement.

scenario: 团队把隔离级别从可串行化降到快照隔离以提升吞吐。
scenario_en: A team lowers isolation from serializable to snapshot isolation to improve throughput.
q: 最需要重新检查什么？
q_en: What must be rechecked first?
options: 跨多行不变量是否会被写偏斜破坏
磁盘是否支持压缩
表名是否足够短
数据库连接池是否启用了 TLS 加密
options_en: Whether cross-row invariants can be broken by write skew
Whether disks support compression
Whether table names are short enough
Whether the connection pool has TLS enabled.
why: 降低隔离通常不是纯性能开关，它会把某些竞态交回应用。跨行规则、唯一性和范围查询要重点审。
why_en: Lowering isolation hands some race conditions back to the application, so cross-row invariants and range predicates need review.
tradeoff: 吞吐提升 vs 异常风险

rows: 跨多行不变量是否会被写偏斜破坏
跨多行不变量是否会…场景
跨多行不变量是否会被写…成本
磁盘是否支持压缩场景
磁盘是否支持压缩成本
连接池是否启用 T…场景
连接池是否启用 TLS成本

optionExplanations: 从可串行化降到快照隔离，原本靠强隔离防住的写偏斜风险现在要重新暴露出来审查，尤其是那些依赖跨多行不变量的逻辑，很可能会被打破。
磁盘压不压缩是存储层面的配置，跟隔离级别高低没有关系，不是降级后要重新检查的重点。
表名长度跟事务隔离级别完全无关，不需要因为降级而重新检查。
连接池要不要用 TLS 是网络安全层面的配置，跟隔离级别从可串行化降到快照隔离没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping from serializable to snapshot isolation means the write-skew risk that stronger isolation used to block now needs re-examining, especially logic depending on cross-row invariants, which can genuinely break.
Whether disks support compression is a storage-layer setting, unrelated to isolation level and not something the downgrade requires re-checking.
Table name length has nothing to do with the transaction isolation level and doesn't need re-checking because of this downgrade.
Whether the connection pool uses TLS is a network-security setting, unrelated to dropping from serializable to snapshot isolation.

scenario: 日志收集管线只追加事件，重复事件可用 idempotency key 去重，短暂乱序可接受。
scenario_en: A log ingestion pipeline only appends events, duplicates can be removed by idempotency keys, and short reordering is acceptable.
q: 可以怎样弱化事务需求？
q_en: How can the design weaken transaction needs?
options: 用幂等追加和异步去重替代跨对象事务
强制把所有事件塞进同一个全局事务
每次写前锁全表
让客户端缓存唯一真相
options_en: Use idempotent appends and async deduplication instead of cross-object transactions
Force all events into one global transaction.
Lock the whole table before every write
Make client cache the source of truth
why: 追加型、可重放的工作流可以把正确性放到幂等键和后台修复上。代价是读侧要接受短暂重复或乱序。
why_en: Append-only replayable workflows can move correctness to idempotency and repair, with temporary duplicates or reordering on reads.
whenOtherWins: 如果写入同时改变用户余额或库存，事务边界不能轻易拿掉。
tradeoff: 高可用吞吐 vs 即时强不变量
optionExplanations: 事件只追加、不需要跨对象改动，用幂等键让重复事件在异步去重时被识别出来，短暂乱序也能被业务接受，跨对象事务的强保证在这里就不是必需的了。
强制所有事件进一个全局事务，会把本来轻量的追加型工作流硬套上事务协调的重量级开销，跟这里想弱化事务需求的方向相反。
每次写前锁全表是最重的并发控制手段，用在只是追加事件这种轻量场景上完全不成比例。
让客户端缓存唯一真相意味着数据的权威版本分散在各个客户端手里，容易互相矛盾，不是弱化事务的合理替代方案。
optionExplanations_en: Events are append-only with no cross-object changes needed, so an idempotency key lets duplicate events be recognized during async dedup, and brief reordering is tolerable — the strong guarantees of a cross-object transaction just aren't necessary here.
Forcing every event into one global transaction saddles an otherwise lightweight append-only workflow with heavy transaction-coordination overhead, the opposite of the direction this scenario wants.
Locking the whole table before every write is the heaviest form of concurrency control, wildly disproportionate for a workload that's just appending events.

Making the client cache the source of truth scatters the authoritative version of the data across many clients, inviting contradictions — not a reasonable substitute for weakening the transaction requirement.

scenario: 你在设计订单数据库，需要把异常名和现象对应起来。
scenario_en: You are designing an order database and need to map anomaly names to symptoms.
q: 哪些配对是正确的？
q_en: Which mappings are correct?
options: 脏读：读到后来回滚的数据
丢失更新：读改写覆盖别人的改动
写偏斜：读同一组条件但写不同记录破坏规则
持久性：并发读写互相阻塞
options_en: Dirty read: seeing data that later rolls back
Lost update: read-modify-write overwrites another change
Write skew: same predicate, different rows, invariant broken
Durability: concurrent reads and writes block each other
why: 前三个是隔离异常，持久性讨论的是提交后能否从崩溃中保住数据。
why_en: The first three are isolation anomalies; durability is about committed data surviving crashes.
optionExplanations: 脏读确实就是读到了另一个事务后来回滚掉的数据，这条配对是对的。
丢失更新确实就是读改写的过程中，后写覆盖了先写的改动，这条配对是对的。
写偏斜确实就是两个事务读的是同一组条件，却各自更新了不同的记录，结果破坏了本该跨行成立的规则，这条配对是对的。
持久性讨论的是提交后的数据能不能扛过崩溃，不是并发读写之间会不会互相阻塞，这条配对把持久性的定义说错了。
optionExplanations_en: A dirty read really is seeing data that another transaction later rolls back, so this pairing is correct.
A lost update really is a read-modify-write where a later write overwrites an earlier one's change, so this pairing is correct.
Write skew really is two transactions reading the same predicate but each updating a different row, breaking a rule meant to hold across rows, so this pairing is correct.
Durability is about whether committed data survives a crash, not whether concurrent reads and writes block each other, so this pairing misstates what durability means.

q: 快照隔离的核心心智模型是什么？
q_en: What is the core mental model of snapshot isolation?
text: 快照隔离让一个事务读取{{同一时间点的已提交版本集合}}，通常通过 {{MVCC}} 实现。
text_en: Snapshot isolation lets a transaction read {{one point-in-time set of committed versions}}, usually implemented with {{MVCC}}.
why: 这就是为什么长读不会拼出前后不一致的结果。它仍不是完整可串行化。
why_en: That is why long reads stay internally consistent, but snapshot isolation is still not full serializability.

termDefinitions.meaning: MVCC 为同一数据保留多个版本，让读事务看到稳定快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MVCC keeps multiple versions of data so a transaction can read a stable snapshot.

q: 读已提交与可串行化分别挡住什么？
q_en: What do read committed and serializable isolation each block?
text: 读已提交至少挡住{{脏读和脏写}}；可串行化要求结果等价于{{某个串行执行顺序}}。
text_en: Read committed blocks at least {{dirty reads and dirty writes}}; serializable isolation requires equivalence to {{some serial execution order}}.
why: 中间隔离级别能提高并发，但会留下需要应用理解的竞态。
why_en: Intermediate isolation levels improve concurrency but leave races the application must understand.

scenario: 数据库可能因死锁或 SSI 冲突中止事务。
scenario_en: The database may abort a transaction because of a deadlock or SSI conflict.
q: 应用事务函数应满足什么？
q_en: What property should the application transaction function have?
options: 可安全重试，外部副作用放到提交后
在事务中直接发不可撤销邮件
失败后忽略错误继续返回成功
重试时复用第一次读到的旧判断
options_en: Make it safe to retry and move external side effects after commit
Send irreversible email directly inside the transaction
Ignore the error and return success after failure
Reuse the stale decision from the first attempt on retry
why: 事务函数要能被数据库中止后重跑，所以内部逻辑不能依赖一次性副作用。重试时还要重新读取数据，避免拿旧判断硬提交。
why_en: A retryable transaction function must tolerate reruns and avoid one-shot side effects or stale decisions.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作不可重试，就要用幂等外部消息或 outbox 把副作用纳入提交边界。
tradeoff: 数据库安全中止 vs 应用重试设计
optionExplanations: 事务函数要能被数据库中止后安全地重新跑一遍，所以像发邮件这类不可撤销的外部动作要放到提交确认之后再做，重跑内部逻辑本身不会产生额外副作用。
在事务中直接发不可撤销邮件，一旦事务后来被中止重试，同一封邮件可能被发送多次，这正是应该避免的做法。
失败后忽略错误直接返回成功，会让调用方误以为操作真的完成了，跟“可安全重试”的要求背道而驰。
重试时复用第一次读到的旧判断，等于用过时的前提去提交，跟需要重新读取最新数据再判断的要求相反。
optionExplanations_en: A transaction function needs to be safely rerunnable after a database abort, so irreversible external actions like sending an email should happen only after commit is confirmed, while rerunning the internal logic itself shouldn't create extra side effects.
Sending an irreversible email directly inside the transaction risks sending it multiple times if the transaction later gets aborted and retried — exactly what should be avoided.
Ignoring the error and returning success after a failure would make the caller wrongly believe the operation actually completed, working against the safe-to-retry requirement.
Reusing the stale decision from the first attempt on retry means committing against an outdated premise, the opposite of needing to re-read fresh data before deciding again.

scenario: 多主复制中两个地区同时更新同一购物车字段。
scenario_en: Two regions in a multi-leader setup update the same shopping-cart field at the same time.
q: 为什么单节点丢失更新技巧不够？
q_en: Why are single-node lost-update techniques insufficient?
options: 不同副本会并发接受写，事后才发现冲突
所有副本共享同一把行锁
读已提交能自动跨地区串行化
WAL 复制会自动合并所有业务语义冲突
options_en: Different replicas accept writes concurrently and only discover the conflict later.
All replicas share one row lock.
Read committed serializes across regions automatically.
WAL replication auto-merges all business-semantic conflicts.
why: 复制把“同时写”扩展到多个主节点，单机锁看不到远端并发。需要冲突解决、合并数据结构或更强协调。
why_en: Replication lets different leaders accept concurrent writes, so single-node locks cannot see all conflicts.
optionExplanations: 多主复制下，两个地区各自的 leader 都能独立接受写入，本地写入时看不到对方那边正在发生的并发写，冲突要等复制到达后才被发现，单机上的行锁完全看不到远端的并发操作。
不同数据中心的副本各自持有自己的本地状态，并不共享同一把行锁，这个说法不成立。
读已提交是单机隔离级别的概念，不会跨地区自动把并发写变成串行执行。
WAL 只是记录底层的字节或行级变化，它不理解购物车字段这种业务语义，更不会替你合并冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Under multi-leader replication, each region's leader can accept writes independently, with no visibility into what's concurrently happening in the other region until replication catches up, so a single-node lock simply cannot see the remote concurrent write.
Replicas in different datacenters each hold their own local state and don't share the same row lock, so this claim doesn't hold.
Read committed is a single-node isolation concept; it doesn't automatically serialize concurrent writes across regions.
The WAL just records low-level byte or row changes; it has no understanding of business meaning like a shopping-cart field, let alone merging conflicts for you.

scenario: 系统只有一个跨事务规则：email 全局唯一。其他字段彼此独立。
scenario_en: The system has one cross-transaction rule: email must be globally unique; other fields are independent.
q: 比全局可串行化更聚焦的做法是什么？
q_en: What is a more focused alternative to global serializability?
options: 对 email 建唯一索引并处理冲突错误
把所有的用户写入都串进一个单线程队列
降低到读未提交
用缓存先查再插入
options_en: Create a unique index on email and handle conflict errors
Serialize all user writes into one single-threaded queue.
Lower isolation to read uncommitted
Check cache before insert
why: 如果不变量能落成数据库约束，就让提交路径直接拒绝冲突。全局可串行化可能保护了太多不需要的东西。
why_en: If the invariant can be expressed as a database constraint, enforce it there instead of serializing unrelated work.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则是“每个组织至少一个管理员”这类跨行存在性条件，唯一索引通常不够。
tradeoff: 局部约束 vs 全局事务顺序
optionExplanations: 既然唯一需要的跨事务规则就是 email 全局唯一，直接在 email 上建唯一索引，让数据库在提交路径上拒绝重复值，比为了这一条规则去做全局可串行化要轻得多。
把所有用户写入放进单线程队列，等于为了一条唯一性规则牺牲了所有用户写入之间原本可以并行的部分，代价过大。
降低到读未提交只会让隔离更弱，完全挡不住两个并发注册请求都写入同一个 email。
用缓存先查再插入的检查和写入之间存在时间差，两个并发请求都可能查到「不存在」然后都成功插入，防不住重复。
optionExplanations_en: Since the only cross-transaction rule needed is a globally unique email, putting a unique index directly on email lets the database reject duplicates right on the commit path, far lighter than serializing everything just for this one rule.
Putting all user writes through a single-threaded queue sacrifices all the parallelism between unrelated user writes just to enforce one uniqueness rule, disproportionately expensive.
Lowering isolation to read uncommitted only weakens things further and does nothing to stop two concurrent registrations from both writing the same email.
Checking a cache before insert leaves a gap between the check and the write, so two concurrent requests can both see not found and both insert successfully, failing to prevent the duplicate.

scenario: 某数据库把隔离级别命名为 serializable，但实际行为更像快照隔离。
scenario_en: A database names an isolation level serializable, but its behavior is closer to snapshot isolation.
q: 设计评审时应该怎么处理？
q_en: How should you handle this in design review?
options: 按实测异常和文档保证判断，不只看名字
完全相信隔离级别名称并跳过并发测试
把所有一致性问题交给缓存
只增加连接池大小
options_en: Judge by documented guarantees and anomaly tests, not the name alone
Trust the isolation-level name and skip concurrency tests.
Delegate all consistency to cache
Only increase connection-pool size
why: 隔离级别名称在数据库之间并不总一致。关键路径要用文档和小型并发测试确认真实行为。
why_en: Isolation names vary across databases, so verify the documented behavior and test the anomalies that matter.
optionExplanations: 隔离级别的名字在不同数据库之间并不总是意味着同一件事，评审时应该拿实测的异常表现和文档承诺去核实，而不是单看名字就当真。
相信名称、跳过并发测试正是这里要避免的做法，名字叫 serializable 不代表真的按可串行化行为。
把所有一致性问题都交给缓存解决，跟名字和实际行为不符这个问题本身没有关系，也解决不了它。
只增加连接池大小是性能层面的调整，不会改变隔离级别名字和真实行为之间的落差。
optionExplanations_en: An isolation level's name doesn't always mean the same thing across different databases, so a review should verify actual measured anomaly behavior and documented guarantees, not just take the name at face value.
Trusting the name and skipping concurrency tests is exactly what should be avoided here — a name of serializable doesn't guarantee it actually behaves that way.
Delegating all consistency problems to cache has nothing to do with fixing a mismatch between a name and its real behavior, and it doesn't solve it either.
Only increasing connection-pool size is a performance tweak; it doesn't close the gap between what the isolation level is named and what it actually does.

scenario: 用户更新个人资料后，同一事务内马上读取资料用于生成确认页。
scenario_en: A user updates a profile and immediately reads it in the same transaction to render a confirmation page.
q: 事务隔离至少应保证什么？
q_en: What should transaction isolation at least guarantee?
options: 本事务能看到自己的写入
所有其他用户立刻看到写入
所有副本永远同步
历史备份马上更新
options_en: The transaction can read its own writes
All other users see the write immediately
All replicas are always synchronized
Historical backups update immediately
why: 事务内读己之写是基本编程模型，否则确认页可能自相矛盾。对其他客户端的新鲜度是另一个问题。
why_en: A transaction should read its own writes; visibility to other clients is a separate recency question.
whenOtherWins: 如果要让其他客户端立刻读到新值，需要线性化读或读主路径，而不只是事务内隔离。
tradeoff: 事务内一致性 vs 跨客户端新鲜度
optionExplanations: 事务内读己之写是最基本的编程模型：刚更新完资料，同一个事务里立刻读出来生成确认页，理应看到自己刚写的内容，不然确认页可能显示旧数据，自相矛盾。
其他用户能不能立刻看到这次写入是另一个新鲜度问题，跟本事务能不能看到自己的写是两件事，不是这里的最低要求。
所有副本永远同步是一个很强的复制保证，跟这里“同一事务内能读到自己刚写的东西”这个基本要求不是同一个层面的问题。
历史备份马上更新跟这次事务内部的读写自洽完全无关，备份通常有自己的延迟和节奏。
optionExplanations_en: Reading your own writes within a transaction is the most basic programming model: right after updating the profile, reading it back in the same transaction to build the confirmation page should see what was just written, otherwise the page could show stale data and contradict itself.
Whether other users see the write immediately is a separate freshness question, distinct from whether this transaction can see its own write — not the minimum requirement being asked about here.
All replicas being always synchronized is a very strong replication guarantee, a different level of problem from this basic within-transaction read-your-own-write requirement.
Historical backups updating immediately has nothing to do with this transaction's internal read-write consistency; backups usually run on their own delayed schedule.

scenario: 票务系统用范围查询判断同一区域是否还有可售座位，错误超卖不可接受。
scenario_en: A ticketing system uses range queries to decide whether seats remain in an area, and overselling is unacceptable.
q: 应避免只依赖什么？
q_en: What should you avoid relying on alone?
options: 普通快照隔离下的范围查询
可串行化的范围谓词保护
唯一座位约束
显式锁定库存槽位
options_en: A range query under plain snapshot isolation
Serializable range-predicate protection.
A unique seat constraint
Explicitly locking an inventory slot
why: 普通快照隔离能让每个事务自洽地读旧范围，但可能放过并发插入或更新导致的写偏斜。要加约束、锁或可串行化。
why_en: Plain snapshot isolation can make each transaction’s range read consistent while still allowing write skew, so add constraints, locks, or serializability.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务能容忍偶发超卖并人工补偿，弱隔离加修复会更省吞吐成本。
tradeoff: 强防超卖 vs 写入吞吐
optionExplanations: 普通快照隔离下，每个事务各自看到的范围查询结果在自己内部是自洽的，但两个事务可能各自基于看似没超卖的旧范围各自卖出座位，写偏斜悄悄就发生了，光靠它防不住超卖。
可串行化的范围保护能真正挡住这种基于范围判断的并发写偏斜，是更可靠的防线之一。
唯一座位约束能让同一个座位不会被卖给两个人，是另一层可靠的防线。
显式锁定库存槽位能把这段判断和扣减的过程串起来，同样是可靠的防线之一。
optionExplanations_en: Under plain snapshot isolation, each transaction's own range query looks internally consistent, but two transactions can each act on a seemingly not-oversold range and both sell a seat, letting write skew slip through unnoticed — this alone can't prevent overselling.
Serializable range protection can genuinely block this kind of range-based concurrent write skew, one of the more reliable defenses here.
A unique seat constraint keeps the same seat from being sold to two people, another reliable layer of defense.
Explicitly locking an inventory slot ties the check and the decrement together into one protected interval, also a reliable defense here.

scenario: 架构讨论中有人说“我们是 BASE，所以不用管事务”。
scenario_en: Someone says, “We are BASE, so we do not need to think about transactions.”
q: 这句话的问题是什么？
q_en: What is wrong with this statement?
options: BASE 太宽泛，仍要明确哪些不变量要保护
BASE 自动提供可串行化
BASE 只适合单机数据库
BASE 比 ACID 有更严格更精确的定义
options_en: BASE is broad, and invariants still need explicit protection
BASE automatically gives serializability
BASE only applies to single-node databases
BASE has a stricter, more precise definition than ACID.
why: 弱化事务不是免设计，而是把哪些错误可接受、哪些要补偿说清楚。BASE 不能替代具体保证。
why_en: Weakening transactions is a design choice; BASE does not replace explicit decisions about invariants and compensation.

termDefinitions.fullName: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency
termDefinitions.meaning: BASE 常被用来粗略表示弱于 ACID 的系统，但定义很松。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BASE is a loose label for systems with weaker guarantees than ACID.

termDefinitions.meaning: ACID 是事务常见安全保证的缩写：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID names the common transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

tradeoff: 弱保证自由度 vs 不变量明确性

rows: BASE 太宽泛，仍要明确哪些不变…
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
BASE 自动提供可串行化
必须保护最新读或不变量时
BASE 只适合单机数据库
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
BASE 只适合单机数…成本
BASE 比 ACID 有更严格定义
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适

optionExplanations: BASE 本身是一组很宽泛的原则，说“我们是 BASE 所以不用管事务”跳过了具体该保护哪些不变量、哪些错误可以接受这些真正要做的设计决定。
BASE 完全不提供可串行化，它恰恰是放弃强一致性、接受最终一致的一套思路，跟可串行化方向相反。
BASE 同样可以用在分布式系统里，不是只适合单机数据库，这个说法把它的适用范围说窄了。
BASE 相比 ACID 反而是更宽泛、更不精确的一组原则，说它定义更严格正好说反了。
optionExplanations_en: BASE itself is a broad set of principles, and saying we're BASE so we don't need transactions skips the actual design work of deciding which invariants to protect and which errors are acceptable.
BASE provides no serializability at all — it's precisely a philosophy of giving up strong consistency for eventual consistency, the opposite direction from serializability.
BASE can be used in distributed systems too, not just single-node databases, so this option narrows its applicability incorrectly.
BASE is actually broader and less precise than ACID, not more strictly defined, so this claim has it backwards.

scenario: 售票服务必须避免同一座位被卖两次，同时高峰期会有大量并发请求。
scenario_en: A ticket service must avoid selling the same seat twice while handling many concurrent requests.
q: 把隔离选择推理排好序。
q_en: Order the reasoning for choosing isolation.
steps: 选择唯一约束或行锁保护 seatId
允许失败事务返回冲突并让用户重选
识别不变量：一个 seatId 只能成功售出一次
避免只用读副本检查可售状态
why: 先说清不变量，再排除会读旧状态的方案，最后把冲突放到提交路径处理。这样并发高也不会超卖。
why_en: Start from the invariant, avoid stale read checks, and enforce conflict on the commit path so concurrency does not oversell.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务允许偶发超卖后人工补偿，弱一致读加异步修复能换来更高吞吐。
tradeoff: 提交时防超卖 vs 异步补偿吞吐
diagram:
flowchart LR
  I[invariant: one seat one sale] --> R[avoid stale read check]
  R --> E[unique constraint or lock]
  E --> C[conflict response]

scenario: 两个快照事务都按同一条件读数据，再分别写不同记录。
scenario_en: Two snapshot transactions read the same predicate and then write different records.
q: 把 SSI 处理链排好序。
q_en: Order the SSI handling chain.
steps: 数据库中止其中一个事务
两个事务读取各自快照
提交前发现危险读写依赖
应用重试被中止的事务
why: SSI 不先阻塞读写，而是在提交附近发现危险依赖并中止。正确性依赖应用把中止当可重试结果。
why_en: SSI does not block first; it detects dangerous dependencies near commit, aborts one transaction, and relies on retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSI 在快照隔离上跟踪读写依赖，发现危险结构时中止事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializable Snapshot Isolation tracks read-write dependencies on snapshots and aborts dangerous transactions.

scenario: 下单事务提交后必须发一条消息给履约系统；不能出现订单已提交但消息永久丢失。
scenario_en: After an order commits, a message must reach fulfillment; the system must not commit the order while losing the message forever.
q: 事务内外部副作用怎么设计？
q_en: How should the side effect be designed?
options: 把待发送消息写入同一数据库 outbox，再异步投递
在数据库事务里直接调用履约 HTTP 接口并忽略失败
先发消息再写订单
只靠进程内内存队列
options_en: Write an outbox row in the same transaction, then deliver asynchronously
Call the fulfillment HTTP endpoint inside the DB transaction and ignore failures.
Send the message before writing the order
Use only an in-process memory queue
why: outbox 把“订单”和“要发的消息”放进同一原子提交边界。投递可能重复，所以消费者仍要幂等。
why_en: The outbox pattern puts the order and the intent to send in one atomic commit, while delivery remains retryable.
whenOtherWins: 如果下游也参与同一个可信事务管理器，分布式事务可以更直接但更重。
tradeoff: 本地原子提交 vs 异步投递重复
optionExplanations: 把要发送的消息作为一行写进同一个数据库、同一个事务里的 outbox 表，跟订单写入共享同一次原子提交，之后再由单独的进程异步把它投递出去，订单和消息意图要么一起提交要么一起不提交。
在事务内直接调用履约 HTTP 并忽略失败，会让订单已经提交但消息实际没送达的情况完全无法被发现或补救。
先发消息再写订单，如果消息发出去后订单写入失败，履约系统会收到一个根本不存在的订单消息。
只靠进程内内存队列，一旦进程重启或崩溃，队列里还没投递的消息就彻底丢了，保证不了消息最终一定被发出去。
optionExplanations_en: Writing the outgoing message as a row in an outbox table within the same database transaction as the order write means both share the same atomic commit, and a separate process delivers it asynchronously afterward — the order and the intent to send commit together or not at all.

Calling the fulfillment HTTP endpoint directly inside the transaction and ignoring failures leaves no way to detect or recover from a case where the order committed but the message never actually arrived.
Sending the message before writing the order risks the fulfillment system receiving a message for an order that then fails to write and doesn't actually exist.
Relying only on an in-process memory queue means any undelivered message is lost outright if the process restarts or crashes, offering no guarantee the message ever eventually goes out.

scenario: 一次可串行化事务要协调 3 个分区，而单分区事务只进一个分区队列。
scenario_en: A serializable transaction must coordinate 3 shards, while a single-shard transaction enters one shard queue.
q: 跨 3 个分区的事务成本怎么估？
q_en: How should you estimate the cost of touching 3 shards?
options: 扇出 = 触达分区数 = 3
分区数完全不影响等待时间
3 个分区会让事务自动变成只读
协调者可以直接忽略最慢参与者
options_en: Fan-out = partitions touched = 3.
The partition count does not affect wait time.
Three partitions make the transaction read-only.
The coordinator can just ignore the slowest participant.
why: 公式是 fanout = touched partitions = 3；这个数会进入延迟预算、锁持有时间和部分失败处理。分区数不是背诵点，是协调参与者数量。
why_en: fanout equals touched partitions, so 3 participants feed latency, lock-hold time, and partial-failure handling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可串行化：并发事务的结果等价于某个串行执行顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializable isolation makes concurrent transactions behave like some serial order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区：按 key 或范围把数据拆到不同节点或队列上的一份子集。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is a subset of data assigned to a node or queue by key or range.

termDefinitions.meaning: 扇出：一次请求需要同时触达的下游节点或分区数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fanout is the number of downstream nodes or partitions one request must touch.

optionExplanations: 扇出就是这次事务实际触达的分区数，这里是 3；这个数字直接进入延迟预算——要等 3 个分区分别响应，也直接影响持有锁的时间和这次事务可能部分失败的面有多大。
分区数正是决定要等多少个参与者响应的关键因素，分区越多通常等待越久，这个说法说反了。
3 个分区只是意味着协调者要跟 3 个参与者打交道，不会让事务因此自动变成只读，这两者没有因果关系。
协调者恰恰不能忽略任何一个参与者，可串行化事务要等所有涉及的分区都确认，忽略最慢的那个会破坏原子性保证。
optionExplanations_en: Fanout is simply how many partitions this transaction actually touches, 3 here, and that number directly feeds the latency budget by waiting on 3 partitions to respond, plus how long locks are held and how large the partial-failure surface is.
Partition count is exactly what determines how many participants must respond, and more partitions typically means more waiting, so this option has it backwards.
Touching 3 partitions just means the coordinator deals with 3 participants; it doesn't automatically turn the transaction read-only — the two are unrelated.

The coordinator can't afford to ignore any participant — a serializable transaction has to wait for every touched partition to confirm, and skipping the slowest one would break the atomicity guarantee.

scenario: 团队使用读已提交，但业务代码先查“是否存在未支付订单”，再插入一个新未支付订单。
scenario_en: A team uses read committed; code checks whether an unpaid order exists and then inserts a new unpaid order.
q: 应该补哪类保护？
q_en: What protection should be added?
options: 唯一部分索引或可串行化事务保护该谓词
只增加读副本数量
把查询缓存 5 分钟
把一条 SQL 拆成更多条独立语句
options_en: A partial unique index or serializable transaction for that predicate
Add more read replicas
Cache the query for five minutes
Split one SQL statement into more separate statements.
why: 读已提交不能保护“查无再插入”的谓词不变量。把规则落成约束，或升级隔离。
why_en: Read committed does not protect a check-then-insert predicate invariant; enforce it as a constraint or use stronger isolation.
whenOtherWins: 如果允许一个用户短暂有多个未支付订单，异步清理会更便宜。
tradeoff: 提交时保护谓词 vs 宽松业务修复
optionExplanations: 读已提交只挡脏读，挡不住“先查是否存在未支付订单、再插入一条”这种谓词竞态，要么用唯一部分索引把这条规则落成数据库约束，要么把这段逻辑升级到可串行化保护。
只增加读副本数量解决的是读扩展问题，不会改变两个并发事务都查到没有未支付订单、然后都插入的竞态。
把查询缓存 5 分钟只是让读到的数据可能更旧，跟阻止两个并发事务都通过检查再插入这个问题没有关系。
把 SQL 拆成更多语句只是改变了写法，读已提交下检查和插入之间的这个时间窗口依然存在，竞态没有被消除。
optionExplanations_en: Read committed only blocks dirty reads, not the check-then-insert predicate race of querying for an existing unpaid order and then inserting a new one — either enforce the rule with a partial unique index or upgrade that logic to serializable protection.
Adding more read replicas addresses read scaling, not the race where two concurrent transactions both find no unpaid order and both insert one.
Caching the query for five minutes just makes the read data staler; it does nothing to stop two concurrent transactions from both passing the check and inserting.
Splitting the SQL into more statements just changes how it's written; the window between checking and inserting under read committed is still there, and the race isn't eliminated.

scenario: 转账事务需要读余额后再扣款，不能让并发事务在检查和扣款之间改余额。
scenario_en: A transfer transaction must read a balance and then debit it without another transaction changing it between check and debit.
q: 这段 SQL 展示了哪种保护？
q_en: What protection does this SQL show?
options: 显式行锁防读改写竞态
读未提交提升吞吐
异步复制防崩溃
谓词锁防幻读
options_en: Explicit row locking for a read-modify-write race
Read uncommitted for throughput
Asynchronous replication for crash safety
Predicate locking for phantoms
why: FOR UPDATE 让读到的账户行在事务结束前保持锁定。它保护的是已有行，不自动锁住不存在的谓词范围。
why_en: FOR UPDATE locks the row that was read until the transaction ends; it protects existing rows, not arbitrary missing ranges.
whenOtherWins: 如果要保护“没有匹配行”这种条件，需要唯一约束、范围锁或可串行化。
tradeoff: 已有行保护 vs 谓词范围保护
optionExplanations: FOR UPDATE 把读到的这一行账户锁住直到事务结束，从检查余额到实际扣款之间不会有别的并发事务插进来改这一行，防住的是经典的读改写竞态。
读未提交是放宽隔离级别换吞吐的做法，跟这里用行锁保护余额检查这个目的正相反。
异步复制是复制层面用来保证容错的机制，跟单个事务内用行锁保护读改写完全是两回事。
谓词锁防的是幻读那种“查无、后来又出现”的问题，这里锁的是已经存在的一行具体账户记录，不是一个查询条件覆盖的范围。
optionExplanations_en: FOR UPDATE locks the account row that was read until the transaction ends, so no other concurrent transaction can slip in and change that row between checking the balance and actually debiting it — protecting against the classic read-modify-write race.
Read uncommitted is about trading isolation for throughput, the opposite purpose of using a row lock to protect a balance check here.
Asynchronous replication is a replication-layer mechanism for fault tolerance, a completely different concern from using a row lock inside one transaction to protect a read-modify-write.
A predicate lock protects against phantoms — rows that don't exist yet and later appear — while this locks one already-existing account row, not a range covered by a query condition.

scenario: 点赞接口只需要把同一行计数加一，不需要先把值返回给业务逻辑。
scenario_en: A like endpoint only needs to increment one row and does not need the old value in application logic.
q: 这段 SQL 为什么比读后写安全？
q_en: Why is this SQL safer than read-then-write?
options: 加法在数据库内原子完成
它绕过了数据库所有的锁
它让所有副本立即同步
它禁用了事务日志写入
options_en: The addition happens atomically inside the database.
It bypasses every database lock.
It makes all replicas sync immediately.
It disables transaction log writes.
why: 单条原子更新把读改写合成一个数据库操作。它适合简单同一行计算，不适合复杂跨行检查。
why_en: A single atomic update combines the read-modify-write inside the database, which fits simple one-row calculations.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要先检查多行规则，再决定是否更新，就需要事务和隔离。
tradeoff: 单行原子性 vs 跨行业务逻辑
optionExplanations: 加一这个动作完全在数据库内部原子执行，不用先把值读出来给业务逻辑算再写回去，两个并发点赞不会有一个的增量被另一个覆盖掉。
原子更新照样要靠底层的锁或等价机制保证同一行不会被两个写同时改坏，不是绕过了所有锁。
这条 SQL 只影响主库这一次写操作的执行方式，不会让副本因此立刻同步，复制延迟是另一个话题。
事务日志该记录还是会记录，原子更新不会因为写法简单就跳过日志记录，持久性保证照常存在。
optionExplanations_en: The increment runs entirely inside the database atomically, without first reading the value out to application logic and writing it back, so two concurrent likes never let one increment silently overwrite the other.
An atomic update still relies on underlying locking or equivalent mechanisms to keep the same row from being corrupted by two simultaneous writes, it doesn't bypass locking altogether.
This SQL only affects how the write executes on the primary; it doesn't make replicas synchronize immediately — replication lag is a separate topic.
The transaction log still gets written as usual; an atomic update doesn't skip logging just because the statement is simple, durability guarantees still apply.

scenario: 你在评估数据库如何提供可串行化。
scenario_en: You are evaluating how a database provides serializable isolation.
q: 哪些是常见实现路线？
q_en: Which are common implementation approaches?
options: 实际串行执行
两阶段锁
SSI
读未提交
options_en: Actual serial execution
Two-phase locking
SSI
Read uncommitted
why: 实际串行、2PL 和 SSI 都能提供可串行化，但成本形状不同。读未提交是弱隔离。
why_en: Actual serial execution, 2PL, and SSI can provide serializability, but read uncommitted is weak isolation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 2PL 先获取需要的锁，提交或回滚后再释放，用锁顺序实现可串行化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase locking acquires locks before releasing them at commit or abort to enforce serializability.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSI 在快照隔离上跟踪读写依赖，发现危险结构时中止事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializable Snapshot Isolation tracks read-write dependencies on snapshots and aborts dangerous transactions.

optionExplanations: 实际串行执行让事务真的一个接一个跑，天然没有并发冲突，是提供可串行化的一种实现路线。
两阶段锁靠共享锁和独占锁控制冲突操作互相等待，是另一条常见的可串行化实现路线。
SSI 让读写正常并发、在提交时检查危险依赖并中止有风险的事务，同样能达到可串行化的效果。
读未提交连脏读都挡不住，是最弱的隔离级别，跟可串行化完全是两个方向，不是它的实现路线之一。
optionExplanations_en: Actual serial execution really runs transactions one after another, inherently free of concurrency conflicts, and is one route to providing serializability.
Two-phase locking uses shared and exclusive locks to make conflicting operations wait for each other, another common route to serializability.
SSI lets reads and writes run concurrently as usual and checks for dangerous dependencies at commit time, aborting risky transactions — also achieving serializability.
Read uncommitted doesn't even block dirty reads, the weakest isolation level, going in the opposite direction from serializability rather than being one way to implement it.

scenario: 事务隔离选型会影响吞吐和延迟。
scenario_en: Transaction isolation choices affect throughput and latency.
q: 为什么很多系统默认不用可串行化？
q_en: Why do many systems not default to serializable isolation?
options: 它可能增加等待、重试或限制并行度
它根本不能保护任何业务不变量
它要求数据必须是 JSON
它不能和索引一起使用
options_en: It can increase waiting, retries, or limit parallelism
It cannot protect any business invariant at all.
It requires all data to be JSON
It cannot be used with indexes
why: 可串行化更容易推理，但数据库要付出协调成本。系统常把默认级别设弱，再让关键路径显式加保护。
why_en: Serializable isolation is easier to reason about, but it adds coordination cost, so many systems make critical paths opt in.
tradeoff: 推理简单性 vs 协调成本

rows: 它可能增加等待、重试或限制并行度
它可能增加等待、重…场景
它可能增加等待、重试或…成本
它不能保护任何不变量
它不能保护任何不变量场景
它不能保护任何不变量成本
它要求数据必须是 JSON
它要求数据必须是 …场景
它要求数据必须是 JS…成本
它不能和索引一起使用
它不能和索引一起使用场景
它不能和索引一起使用成本

optionExplanations: 可串行化为了保证结果等价于某个顺序执行，往往要让冲突的操作互相等待、或者在提交时中止重试，这些代价会增加延迟、降低并行度，所以很多系统默认选更弱的级别。
可串行化恰恰是保护不变量最强的隔离级别，说它不能保护任何不变量正好说反了。
隔离级别跟数据是不是 JSON 格式没有关系，这个说法不成立。
可串行化照样可以配合索引一起使用，索引该怎么用还是怎么用，这个说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: To make the outcome equivalent to some serial order, serializable isolation often makes conflicting operations wait on each other or aborts and retries at commit time, and that cost adds latency and limits parallelism, which is why many systems default to a weaker level.
Serializable isolation is precisely the strongest level for protecting invariants, so claiming it can't protect any invariant has it exactly backwards.
The isolation level has nothing to do with whether data is in JSON format, so this claim doesn't hold.
Serializable isolation works fine alongside indexes, which still function normally, so this claim doesn't hold.

scenario: 面试中被问“库存扣减怎么防并发错误”，你只能先给一个短答案。
scenario_en: In an interview, you are asked how to prevent concurrency bugs in inventory decrement and can give a short first answer.
q: 最好的开场是什么？
q_en: What is the best opening answer?
options: 先说不变量，再选保护提交路径的手段
先说把缓存和连接池调大
先说所有数据库默认就安全
先说去加更多的 Web 应用服务器
options_en: Name the invariant first, then pick what protects the commit path.
Start by enlarging the cache and connection pool.
Start by saying databases are safe by default.
Start by adding more web application servers.
why: 库存问题的核心是“不超卖”这个不变量。面试答案要把保护放在提交路径，而不是只优化读路径。
why_en: For inventory, the invariant is no overselling, and the protection must sit on the commit path rather than only on reads.
whenOtherWins: 如果库存只是近似展示，读路径缓存和异步刷新才是主要优化。
tradeoff: 提交路径正确性 vs 读路径速度
optionExplanations: 先说清楚要保护的不变量是“不能超卖”，再讲清楚具体用唯一约束、锁还是可串行化去把这条规则钉在提交路径上，这才是回答库存并发问题该有的结构。
直接说把缓存调大跟并发写入正确性没有关系，缓存解决的是读性能问题，答不到点子上。
说所有数据库都默认安全是不准确的，隔离级别和保护机制需要显式选择和配置，不能想当然。
加更多 Web 服务器只是提高了并发请求的数量，反而会让库存竞态问题暴露得更频繁，不是解决方案。
