optionExplanations_en: Starting by naming the invariant no overselling, then explaining whether a uniqueness constraint, a lock, or serializable isolation is what pins that rule down on the commit path — that's the right shape of answer for a concurrency question about inventory.
Jumping straight to increasing cache size has nothing to do with concurrent-write correctness; caching addresses read performance, missing the point entirely.
Claiming all databases are safe by default is inaccurate — isolation levels and protection mechanisms need to be explicitly chosen and configured, not assumed.
Adding more web servers just increases the number of concurrent requests, making the inventory race condition surface more often, not a solution.

q: 第 7 章的隔离主线是什么？
q_en: What is the main isolation storyline of Chapter 7?
text: 弱隔离提升并发，但会留下{{脏读、丢失更新、写偏斜、幻读}}等异常；可串行化用{{串行等价结果}}换取更简单的推理。
text_en: Weak isolation improves concurrency but leaves anomalies such as {{dirty reads, lost updates, write skew, and phantoms}}; serializability trades for {{serial-equivalent results}}.
why: 面试里不要只背级别名，要把异常、业务不变量和修复机制连起来。
why_en: In interviews, connect isolation names to anomalies, business invariants, and the mechanism that protects them.

q: 分布式系统为什么比单机难？
q_en: Why are distributed systems harder than single-machine software?
text: 单机常是{{正常或整体失败}}；分布式系统会出现{{部分失败}}，有些节点正常、有些节点或网络路径异常。
text_en: A single machine often is {{working or totally failed}}; a distributed system can have {{partial failure}}, where some nodes or network paths fail while others work.
why: 部分失败让调用结果变成“不知道成功还是失败”，所以必须把故障处理写进协议。
why_en: Partial failure makes outcomes uncertain, so fault handling must be part of the protocol design.

scenario: 在线服务要 24/7 响应用户，不能因为一台机器坏了就停全站维修。
scenario_en: An online service must respond 24/7 and cannot stop the whole service because one machine failed.
q: 应该采用哪种故障哲学？
q_en: Which fault-handling philosophy fits?
options: 容忍部分失败，服务降级或迁移流量
像批处理超算一样停掉整个作业
假设硬件永远可靠
只在周末手工恢复
options_en: Tolerate partial failures and degrade or move traffic
Stop the entire job like a batch supercomputer
Assume hardware never fails
Recover manually only on weekends
why: 在线云服务要从不可靠组件里拼可靠整体，不能把局部故障升级成全站不可用。代价是软件协议更复杂。
why_en: Online cloud services must build reliability from unreliable parts, rather than turning every local fault into a total outage.
whenOtherWins: 离线科学计算能从 checkpoint 重跑时，停全作业再恢复可能更简单。
tradeoff: 在线可用性 vs 协议复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: HPC 常指专用集群上的科学计算，故障处理更像整作业重启。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: High-performance computing often means scientific workloads on specialized clusters, where failures may restart the whole job.

optionExplanations: 容忍局部机器坏掉，让服务降级或把流量迁到其它节点，这样才能做到 24/7 响应，不用因为一台机器出问题就停全站。
像批处理超算那样直接停掉整个作业，会让在线服务因为一台机器坏掉就对所有用户不可用，跟 24/7 的要求正相反。
假设硬件永远可靠是不现实的前提，机器随时可能坏，按这个假设设计迟早会被现实打脸。
只在周末手工恢复意味着平时坏了没人管，在线服务显然等不了这么久。
optionExplanations_en: Tolerating a partial machine failure and degrading or moving traffic elsewhere is what lets the service run 24/7 without one broken machine taking down everyone.
Stopping the entire job like a batch supercomputer would make the online service unavailable to every user just because one machine failed, the opposite of the 24/7 requirement.
Assuming hardware never fails is an unrealistic premise; machines break at any time, and designing around that assumption eventually gets proven wrong.
Recovering manually only on weekends means nobody handles a failure during the week, clearly too slow for an online service.

scenario: 一个系统由会丢包的网络和会宕机的机器组成。
scenario_en: A system is built from a lossy network and machines that may crash.
q: 怎样仍能提高整体可靠性？
q_en: How can the overall system still be more reliable?
options: 在上层加入重试、校验、复制和多数派决策
假设最弱的那个组件决定了全部可靠性
关闭所有超时
只依赖单个最大机器
options_en: Add retries, checksums, replication, and majority decisions at higher layers
Assume the weakest component decides the whole reliability.
Disable all timeouts
Rely on one biggest machine
why: 上层协议可以屏蔽一部分底层错误，但不能消除物理极限。要同时说明还剩哪些失败会暴露给应用。
why_en: Higher-level protocols can mask some lower-level faults, but they cannot remove physical limits or every failure mode.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的最小节点集合，常用多数派让两个决定集合相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum set of nodes needed for a decision, often a majority so quorums overlap.

optionExplanations: 在丢包的网络和会宕机的机器之上，靠重试补丢包、校验和挡数据损坏、复制留住数据、多数派决策挡单点错误判断，上层能把这些不可靠拼成整体可靠。
假设最弱组件决定全部可靠性，等于放弃了上层能做的补救，跟“怎样仍能提高可靠性”这个问题的方向相反。
关闭所有超时会让客户端永远等一个可能已经死掉的节点，反而降低了系统的可用性。
只依赖单个最大机器放弃了冗余，这台机器一旦故障，整个系统直接不可用。
optionExplanations_en: On top of a lossy network and machines that can crash, retries cover lost packets, checksums catch corruption, replication keeps data around, and majority decisions guard against a single wrong judgment — together the upper layers build reliability from unreliable parts.
Assuming the weakest component fully determines reliability gives up on any upper-layer remedy, the opposite direction from how to still improve reliability.
Disabling all timeouts leaves a client waiting forever on a node that may already be dead, actually hurting availability.
Relying on one biggest machine gives up redundancy entirely — the moment that machine fails, the whole system goes down.

scenario: 服务 A 通过异步包网络调用服务 B。
scenario_en: Service A calls service B over an asynchronous packet network.
q: 一次请求可能发生哪些情况？
q_en: What can happen to one request?
options: 请求或响应丢失、延迟、重复或乱序
请求一定按发送顺序瞬时到达
B 一定知道 A 是否收到响应
网络能区分慢节点和死节点
options_en: The request or response may be lost, delayed, duplicated, or reordered
Requests always arrive instantly in send order
B always knows whether A received the response
The network can distinguish a slow node from a dead one
why: 异步网络只给尽力而为的传输，调用方看到超时也不知道哪一步丢了。协议要能处理重复和未知结果。
why_en: An asynchronous network is best-effort, so a timeout does not reveal which step failed.

termDefinitions.meaning: IP 是尽力而为的包传输协议，可能丢包、延迟、重复或乱序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is a best-effort packet protocol where packets may be lost, delayed, duplicated, or reordered.

optionExplanations: 异步包网络只提供尽力而为的传输，请求或响应都可能在路上丢失、被延迟、被重复递送，或者到达顺序被打乱，调用方对这些都要有准备。
实际情况恰恰相反，异步网络不承诺请求按发送顺序瞬时到达，这正是它跟同步网络的核心差别。
B 完全可能已经处理完并发出了响应，但这个响应本身在路上丢了，A 那边看到超时并不代表 B 知道 A 有没有收到。
网络本身分不清一个节点是真死了还是只是暂时变慢，这也是故障检测只能给怀疑而不是证明的原因。
optionExplanations_en: An asynchronous packet network only offers best-effort delivery, so the request or response can be lost, delayed, duplicated, or arrive out of order — the caller has to be ready for all of these.
It's actually the opposite — an asynchronous network makes no promise that requests arrive instantly in send order, which is exactly what separates it from a synchronous one.
B may well have finished processing and sent a response, only for that response itself to get lost in transit; A seeing a timeout doesn't tell B whether A ever received it.
The network itself can't tell a truly dead node from one that's just temporarily slow, which is exactly why failure detection can only offer suspicion, not proof.

scenario: 支付请求超时了，客户端不知道服务端是否已经扣款。
scenario_en: A payment request times out, and the client does not know whether the server already charged the card.
q: 客户端重试前最需要什么？
q_en: What is most needed before retrying?
options: 幂等请求 ID 或去重键
把超时设置得更短一些
读未提交隔离
随机换一个币种
options_en: An idempotency key or request deduplication ID
Set a shorter fixed timeout.
Read-uncommitted isolation
Randomly switch currency
why: 超时只说明“没及时收到回答”，不说明操作没发生。幂等键让重试不会重复扣款。
why_en: A timeout only means no answer arrived in time, so an idempotency key makes retry safe.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作本身是只读且无副作用，简单重试通常就足够。
tradeoff: 安全重试 vs 去重状态成本
optionExplanations: 超时只说明客户端没及时收到回答，不代表扣款没发生，带上幂等请求 ID 或去重键重试，服务端就能识别出这是同一次操作，不会重复扣款。
把超时设得更短只会让误判更频繁，不会告诉客户端这次扣款到底有没有真的执行。
读未提交放宽的是能看到什么数据，跟“超时后要不要安全重试”这个问题完全不是一回事。
随机换一个币种跟超时后该怎么安全重试没有任何关系，答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: A timeout only means the client didn't get an answer in time, not that the charge didn't happen — carrying an idempotency key or dedup ID on retry lets the server recognize it as the same operation and avoid charging twice.
Setting a shorter fixed timeout just makes false alarms more frequent; it doesn't tell the client whether the charge actually went through.
Read-uncommitted isolation loosens what data is visible, a completely different concern from whether it's safe to retry after a timeout.
Randomly switching currency has nothing to do with how to safely retry after a timeout, and doesn't address the question.

scenario: 服务的正常 p99 响应约 200ms，但网络偶尔排队到几秒。
scenario_en: A service has normal p99 latency around 200 ms, but network queues sometimes add seconds.
q: 超时值主要在权衡什么？
q_en: What is a timeout value mainly trading off?
options: 故障发现速度和误判健康节点的风险
数据库索引大小与缓存命中率高低
JSON 大小和压缩率
磁盘顺序写和随机写
options_en: Failure detection speed versus falsely suspecting a healthy node
Database index size versus cache hit rate.
JSON size versus compression ratio
Sequential versus random disk writes
why: 超时不是一个“正确数字”，而是用观测延迟分布选的工程取舍。设得太短会制造假故障。
why_en: A timeout is an engineering tradeoff based on observed latency, not a universally correct number.
optionExplanations: 超时设太短，正常波动到几秒的请求会被误判成故障；设太长，真正故障的节点又要等很久才被发现，这个数字本质上是在权衡这两者。
数据库索引大小和缓存命中率跟超时值该设多少没有关系，这个说法答非所问。
JSON 大小和压缩率是数据编码层面的事，跟超时权衡的是两个不同维度的问题。
磁盘顺序写和随机写是存储引擎的话题，跟网络请求的超时设置无关。
optionExplanations_en: Set the timeout too short and normal requests that occasionally take seconds get mistaken for failures; set it too long and a genuinely dead node takes forever to be noticed — the value is fundamentally a tradeoff between these two.
Index size and cache hit rate have nothing to do with how a timeout value should be set, so this option doesn't address the question.
JSON size and compression ratio are a data-encoding concern, a different dimension from the timeout tradeoff.
Sequential versus random disk writes is a storage-engine topic, unrelated to setting a network request timeout.

scenario: 跨地域 RPC 延迟随拥塞变化很大，固定 500ms 超时经常误杀请求。
scenario_en: Cross-region RPC latency changes with congestion, and a fixed 500 ms timeout often kills healthy requests.
q: 更稳的做法是什么？
q_en: What is a steadier approach?
options: 按近期延迟分布动态调整超时
把超时永久设成 1ms
删除所有重试
把业务数据塞进 DNS
options_en: Adapt timeout from recent latency distribution
Set the timeout permanently to 1 ms
Remove all retries
Put business data into DNS
why: 自适应超时跟着网络实际变化走，能减少误判。仍要有上限和熔断，避免无限等待。
why_en: Adaptive timeouts follow observed network behavior and reduce false suspicions, while still needing caps and circuit breakers.
whenOtherWins: 如果链路有硬实时上界，固定超时可以来自该上界；普通云网络通常没有。
tradeoff: 快速探测 vs 误判抖动
optionExplanations: 按最近观测到的延迟分布动态调整超时阈值，网络拥塞时超时跟着放宽，网络顺畅时收紧，比固定 500ms 更能贴合实际情况，减少误杀。
把超时永久设成 1ms 会让几乎所有正常请求都被判定为超时，比固定 500ms 误杀得更严重。
删除所有重试解决不了超时阈值设置不合理这个根本问题，只是放弃了失败后的补救手段。
把业务数据塞进 DNS 跟超时该怎么设置完全是两回事，不合理也不相关。
optionExplanations_en: Adapting the timeout from recent observed latency loosens it when the network is congested and tightens it when things are smooth, tracking reality far better than a fixed 500ms and cutting down false alarms.
Permanently setting the timeout to 1ms would flag nearly every normal request as timed out, an even worse false-alarm rate than the fixed 500ms.
Removing all retries doesn't fix the underlying problem of a badly chosen timeout threshold, it just gives up the recovery mechanism after a failure.
Putting business data into DNS has nothing to do with how the timeout should be set, neither reasonable nor relevant.

scenario: 一次请求本身处理很快，但排在交换机、网卡或接收端队列里很久。
scenario_en: A request is quick to process but waits in switch, NIC, or receiver queues for a long time.
q: 这对故障检测意味着什么？
q_en: What does this imply for failure detection?
options: 慢响应不一定是节点死了，可能只是排队
队列排队延迟能被 SQL 优化彻底消除
超时后可以断定操作没执行
TCP 会消除所有延迟
options_en: A slow response may be queueing, not node death
Queueing delay can be fully removed by SQL tuning.
After timeout the operation definitely did not run
TCP removes all delay
why: 网络和运行时队列会把健康节点伪装成故障节点。故障检测只能给怀疑，不是事实证明。
why_en: Queues can make a healthy node look failed, so failure detection gives suspicion rather than proof.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 在不可靠 IP 之上提供有序、去重、重传的字节流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP provides an ordered, deduplicated, retransmitted byte stream on top of unreliable IP.

optionExplanations: 请求本身处理得很快，只是被堵在交换机、网卡或接收端的队列里，从外部看响应慢，但节点本身完全健康，只是在排队。
队列延迟是网络和运行时层面排队造成的，SQL 优化针对的是数据库查询效率，两者不是一回事，SQL 调优消除不了排队。
超时只能说明没及时收到回答，操作到底有没有在远端执行完全不确定，不能断定它没执行。
TCP 能改善包传输的可靠性，但排队本身依然存在，TCP 不会让所有延迟都消失。
optionExplanations_en: The request itself may process quickly but sit stuck in a switch, NIC, or receive-side queue, so from the outside the response looks slow while the node is actually perfectly healthy, just queued up.
Queueing delay comes from network and runtime-level queues; SQL tuning targets database query efficiency — the two are unrelated, and tuning SQL won't remove queueing.
A timeout only shows an answer didn't arrive in time; whether the operation actually ran on the remote side is genuinely unknown, so it can't be declared as not having run.
TCP improves the reliability of packet transport, but the underlying queueing still exists — TCP doesn't make all delay disappear.

scenario: 应用说“TCP 是可靠的，所以不会有分布式故障”。
scenario_en: Someone says, “TCP is reliable, so distributed failures go away.”
q: 这句话漏了什么？
q_en: What does this miss?
options: TCP 能重传和排序，但不能消除无限延迟或对端崩溃
TCP 保证远端应用一定处理成功
IP 已经提供 exactly-once RPC
TCP 让时钟同步
options_en: TCP retransmits and orders bytes, but cannot remove unbounded delay or peer crashes
TCP guarantees the remote application succeeded
IP already provides exactly-once RPC
TCP synchronizes clocks
why: TCP 改善包传输语义，不等于应用级成功确认。你仍要处理连接断开、超时和重复请求。
why_en: TCP improves packet transport, but it is not an application-level success guarantee.
tradeoff: 传输可靠性 vs 应用语义

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP 在不可靠 IP 之上提供有序、去重、重传的字节流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP provides an ordered, deduplicated, retransmitted byte stream on top of unreliable IP.

termDefinitions.meaning: IP 是尽力而为的包传输协议，可能丢包、延迟、重复或乱序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IP is a best-effort packet protocol where packets may be lost, delayed, duplicated, or reordered.

optionExplanations: TCP 能重传丢包、把字节流按顺序交付，但它管不了对端进程崩溃、也管不了消息在应用层排队等到天荒地老，这些分布式层面的故障 TCP 消除不掉。
TCP 只保证字节可靠传输到对端内核缓冲区，不代表远端应用真的处理成功了，这中间还差应用层的确认。
IP 是网络层协议，连可靠传输都不保证，更谈不上提供 exactly-once 这种应用语义的 RPC 保证。
TCP 处理的是字节流的可靠传输和排序，跟不同机器之间的时钟同步完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: TCP retransmits lost packets and delivers bytes in order, but it can't do anything about the peer process crashing or a message sitting queued at the application layer indefinitely — those distributed-level failures aren't removed by TCP.
TCP only guarantees bytes reliably reach the peer's kernel buffer; it doesn't mean the remote application actually processed them successfully — that still needs an application-level acknowledgment.
IP is a network-layer protocol that doesn't even guarantee reliable transport, let alone an application-semantic guarantee like exactly-once RPC.
TCP handles reliable, ordered byte-stream transport, a completely different concern from synchronizing clocks across machines.

scenario: 库存服务收到扣减请求后网络断开，客户端没有收到响应。
scenario_en: An inventory service receives a decrement request, then the network disconnects before the client gets a response.
q: 客户端应该假设什么？
q_en: What should the client assume?
options: 结果未知，查询状态或幂等重试
一定失败，可以直接重发不同请求
一定成功，不必记录
网络会自动回滚数据库
options_en: The outcome is unknown, so query state or retry idempotently
It definitely failed, so send a different request
It definitely succeeded, so do not record it
The network automatically rolls back the database
why: 分布式调用的难点是“没回包”不等于“没执行”。要用操作 ID、状态查询或事务日志收敛。
why_en: No reply does not mean no execution, so use operation IDs, status lookup, or logs to converge.
whenOtherWins: 如果请求是无副作用只读查询，超时后直接重发查询通常就够。
tradeoff: 未知副作用安全 vs 简单重试
optionExplanations: 没收到响应不代表扣减一定没执行，也不代表一定执行了，客户端应该把结果当未知，靠查询操作状态或用幂等键重试来收敛到确定结果。
直接认定一定失败就发一个不同的请求，如果原请求其实已经成功执行，等于凭空多扣了一次，风险很大。
直接认定一定成功而不记录，如果原请求其实失败了，这次扣减就凭空丢失了，同样有风险。
网络本身不具备回滚数据库的能力，这个说法把两个不相关的层面混在了一起。
optionExplanations_en: No response doesn't prove the decrement failed, and it doesn't prove it succeeded either — the client should treat the outcome as unknown and converge on certainty by querying status or retrying idempotently.
Assuming it definitely failed and sending a different request risks double-decrementing if the original request actually did succeed.
Assuming it definitely succeeded and not recording it risks silently losing the decrement if the original request actually failed.
The network itself has no ability to roll back a database — this option conflates two unrelated layers.

q: time-of-day clock 和 monotonic clock 怎么分工？
q_en: How should time-of-day and monotonic clocks be used?
text: {{time-of-day clock}} 用来表示日期时间；{{monotonic clock}} 用来测量本机经过的时长。
text_en: A {{time-of-day clock}} represents calendar time; a {{monotonic clock}} measures elapsed time on one machine.
why: 超时和耗时统计应优先用单调时钟，因为墙上时间可能被 NTP 调整跳变。
why_en: Use a monotonic clock for timeouts and durations because wall-clock time can jump due to synchronization.

termDefinitions.meaning: NTP 用网络时间源校准机器时钟，但不能消除漂移和跳变风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes clocks to network time sources, but it cannot remove drift or clock-step risks.

scenario: 服务要测量一次 RPC 花了多久，并决定是否超时。
scenario_en: A service needs to measure how long an RPC took and decide whether it timed out.
q: 应该用哪种时钟？
q_en: Which clock should it use?
options: 本机单调时钟
跨机器 wall-clock 时间戳相减
数据库更新时间字段
用户浏览器时间
options_en: A local monotonic clock
Subtract wall-clock timestamps from different machines
A database updated_at field
The user browser’s clock
why: 单调时钟不会倒退，适合测本机时间间隔。不同机器的单调时钟值不能直接比较。
why_en: A monotonic clock does not go backward and is appropriate for measuring local elapsed time.
whenOtherWins: 如果要向用户展示日历时间，time-of-day clock 才是对的输入。
tradeoff: 本机时长测量 vs 全球日期时间
optionExplanations: 本机单调时钟只会往前走，不会因为系统时间被调整就倒退，正适合测量一次 RPC 在本机经过了多久。
不同机器的墙钟本身就可能有偏差和跳变，直接相减得到的时间差可能是负数或明显失真，不适合用来判断超时。
数据库的更新时间字段反映的是记录被修改的时刻，不是这次 RPC 调用本身经过了多久。
用户浏览器的时钟完全在客户端控制之下，既不准确也不能反映服务端这次调用实际花的时间。
optionExplanations_en: A local monotonic clock only moves forward and never jumps backward when system time gets adjusted, making it well suited for measuring how long an RPC took on this machine.
Wall-clock readings on different machines can themselves be skewed or jump, so subtracting them directly can give a negative or badly distorted duration, unsuitable for judging a timeout.
A database's updated_at field reflects when a record was last modified, not how long this particular RPC call took.
The user's browser clock is entirely under the client's control, neither accurate nor reflective of how long the server-side call actually took.

scenario: 定时任务用 wall-clock 判断“现在是否超过租约到期时间”，但机器时钟被 NTP 往回拨。
scenario_en: A scheduler uses wall-clock time to check lease expiry, but NTP steps the machine clock backward.
q: 可能发生什么？
q_en: What can happen?
options: 过期判断变慢，旧持有者继续行动
单调时间也会倒退
所有消息都会自动重排到正确顺序
数据库隔离级别升高
options_en: Expiry checks may be delayed, letting an old holder keep acting
Monotonic time also goes backward
All messages auto-reorder into the correct order.
Database isolation becomes stronger
why: 墙上时间会跳变，用它做租约边界会产生隐蔽错误。租约还需要下游 fencing token 防旧主写入。
why_en: Wall-clock jumps can break lease boundaries, so leases also need fencing tokens downstream.

termDefinitions.meaning: NTP 用网络时间源校准机器时钟，但不能消除漂移和跳变风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes clocks to network time sources, but it cannot remove drift or clock-step risks.

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token 是单调递增令牌，下游只接受更大的令牌来拒绝旧主。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing token; downstream systems accept only newer tokens to reject stale leaders.

optionExplanations: 机器时钟被 NTP 往回拨后，判断“现在是否超过租约到期时间”会用到这个变慢甚至倒退的墙钟，过期判断被推迟，旧持有者会以为租约还没到期而继续行动。
这里被往回拨的是墙钟，单调时钟专门被设计成不会倒退，两者不是同一回事。
墙钟跳变跟消息重排完全是两个机制，跳变不会让消息自动重排正确。
墙钟往回拨跟数据库隔离级别毫无关系，隔离级别不会因为时钟问题而升高。
optionExplanations_en: After NTP steps the machine clock backward, checking whether the lease has expired against that stalled or reversed wall clock delays the expiry check, letting the old holder believe the lease hasn't expired yet and keep acting.
It's the wall clock that gets stepped back here — a monotonic clock is specifically designed never to go backward, so these are not the same thing.
A wall-clock jump and message reordering are entirely different mechanisms; a jump doesn't make messages automatically reorder correctly.
A wall-clock step backward has nothing to do with database isolation level, which doesn't get stronger because of a clock issue.

scenario: 假设机器时钟漂移 200 ppm，30 秒校准间隔大约会漂 6ms。
scenario_en: Assume clock drift is 200 ppm; over a 30-second sync interval, drift is roughly 6 ms.
q: 这个量级对设计说明什么？
q_en: What does this order of magnitude imply?
options: 物理时钟读数应当看成有误差区间
机器时钟可当全局顺序源
30 秒内不会有任何时间误差
可以不用监控 NTP
options_en: Physical clock readings should be treated as intervals with uncertainty
Machine clocks can be a global ordering source
There is no time error within 30 seconds
NTP monitoring is unnecessary
why: 200 ppm × 30s 约等于 6ms，这还不含网络和配置问题。用时钟排序写入时要显式处理误差。
why_en: At 200 ppm, 30 seconds is about 6 ms of drift before other errors, so clock-based ordering must account for uncertainty.

termDefinitions.meaning: ppm 是百万分之一，常用来表示时钟频率漂移比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Parts per million is a ratio used to express clock frequency drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: NTP 用网络时间源校准机器时钟，但不能消除漂移和跳变风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes clocks to network time sources, but it cannot remove drift or clock-step risks.

optionExplanations: 200 ppm 漂移在 30 秒内累积出大约 6ms 的误差，这还不算网络和配置带来的额外误差，说明单点的物理时钟读数应该被当成一个有不确定范围的区间，而不是精确值。
漂移量级恰恰说明机器时钟不够精确，不能直接当作全局事件顺序的可靠来源，这个说法正好说反了。
6ms 的误差就是切实存在于 30 秒这个窗口内的，说完全没有误差跟给出的数字直接矛盾。
漂移会累积、又和网络及配置问题叠加，正说明需要持续监控 NTP，而不是可以不管它。
optionExplanations_en: 200 ppm drift accumulates to roughly 6ms over 30 seconds, before even counting network and configuration errors, which is why a single physical clock reading should be treated as an interval with uncertainty, not an exact value.
That amount of drift is exactly why a machine clock isn't precise enough to serve as a reliable global ordering source on its own — this option has it backwards.
The 6ms of error is a real, present quantity within that 30-second window, so claiming zero error directly contradicts the given numbers.
Drift accumulating and compounding with network and configuration issues is exactly why NTP needs ongoing monitoring, not a reason to ignore it.

scenario: 数据库依赖较准确的物理时钟给事务时间戳。
scenario_en: A database relies on reasonably accurate physical clocks for transaction timestamps.
q: 运维上必须加什么？
q_en: What operational control is required?
options: 监控节点时钟偏移，偏离过大就摘除
只监控 CPU 使用率
把所有节点的时钟手工设成一样
关闭时间同步避免跳变
options_en: Monitor clock offset and remove nodes that drift too far
Only monitor CPU utilization
Manually set every node's clock to the same value.
Disable time synchronization to avoid jumps
why: 时钟故障常常静默发生，应用还会继续跑。依赖时钟语义时，偏移监控就是正确性保护。
why_en: Clock faults can be silent, so systems that rely on clock semantics must monitor offset as a correctness guard.
whenOtherWins: 如果协议只用逻辑时钟排序事件，就不需要同样严格的物理时钟精度。
tradeoff: 物理时间语义 vs 运维约束

termDefinitions.meaning: NTP 用网络时间源校准机器时钟，但不能消除漂移和跳变风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes clocks to network time sources, but it cannot remove drift or clock-step risks.

optionExplanations: 时钟故障常常是悄无声息的，程序不会报错也不会崩溃，只有持续监控节点间的时钟偏移、发现偏离过大就摘除，才能在依赖时钟语义时守住正确性。
只监控 CPU 使用率看不出时钟偏移的问题，两者衡量的是完全不同的健康维度。
手工把所有节点时钟设成一样只是一次性动作，之后时钟照样会因为硬件漂移而重新出现偏差，不是长期方案。
关闭时间同步反而会让漂移不受控制地越积越大，跳变的风险不但没消除，长期偏差反而更严重。
optionExplanations_en: Clock faults often happen silently, with no crash or error message, so continuously monitoring the offset between node clocks and removing ones that drift too far is what protects correctness when the system depends on clock semantics.
Monitoring only CPU utilization says nothing about clock offset — the two measure completely different dimensions of health.
Manually setting all node clocks equal once is a one-time action; drift from hardware will reintroduce the skew over time, not a lasting solution.
Disabling time synchronization would let drift accumulate uncontrolled, not removing the risk of a jump but instead letting long-term skew get much worse.

scenario: 多主数据库要判断两个写入的因果先后，而不是日历时间。
scenario_en: A multi-leader database needs causal ordering of two writes, not calendar time.
q: 应优先考虑什么？
q_en: What should it prefer?
options: 逻辑时钟或版本向量
每台机器的 wall-clock 时间
用户本地时区
磁盘文件修改时间
options_en: Logical clocks or version vectors
Each machine’s wall-clock time
The user’s local timezone
Filesystem modification time
why: 逻辑时钟记录事件关系，不假装测量真实时间。它能帮助判断先后或并发，避免物理时钟漂移误导。
why_en: Logical clocks capture event relationships rather than real time, helping distinguish order from concurrency.
tradeoff: 因果排序 vs 物理时间便利

rows: 逻辑时钟或版本向量场景
逻辑时钟或版本向量成本
磁盘文件修改时间场景
磁盘文件修改时间成本

optionExplanations: 逻辑时钟或版本向量记录的是事件之间谁先谁后、谁看见了谁的因果关系，不依赖真实时间的准确性，正好适合判断多主写入的先后。
每台机器的墙钟本身可能有偏差和漂移，用它判断跨机器写入的因果先后并不可靠。
用户本地时区只影响显示格式，跟判断两个写入之间的因果关系毫无关系。
磁盘文件修改时间反映的是文件系统层面的时间戳，同样受墙钟不准的问题影响，也不携带因果信息。
optionExplanations_en: Logical clocks or version vectors record which event causally came before another, or who saw whom, without depending on real time being accurate — a good fit for judging the order of multi-leader writes.
Each machine's wall-clock time can itself be skewed or drifting, making it unreliable for judging the causal order of writes across machines.
The user's local timezone only affects display formatting, unrelated to determining the causal relationship between two writes.
A filesystem's modification time is just a timestamp at the filesystem level, subject to the same wall-clock inaccuracy and carrying no causal information.

scenario: 多主系统用物理时间戳做 last-write-wins 冲突解决。
scenario_en: A multi-leader system uses physical timestamps for last-write-wins conflict resolution.
q: 最大风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest risk?
options: 快时钟节点的旧写会覆盖较新的写
所有并发冲突都会被完整地保留
写入吞吐会直接降为零
网络分区会自动被修复
options_en: A node with a fast clock can overwrite a genuinely newer write.
All concurrent conflicts are fully preserved.
Write throughput drops straight to zero.
Network partitions heal automatically.
why: LWW 把“时间戳大”当“更晚”，但物理时钟可能错。结果是用户刚写的数据被无声丢掉。
why_en: Last-write-wins treats a larger timestamp as newer, but bad clocks can silently discard real updates.
optionExplanations: LWW 把时间戳更大的写当成更晚发生的，但如果某个节点的时钟本身跑得快，它上面较早的一次业务写反而会顶着一个更大的时间戳，覆盖掉另一个节点上真正更晚发生的写。
LWW 恰恰是靠丢弃其中一方来收敛的，不是保留所有冲突，这个说法说反了。
LWW 的冲突解决逻辑本身不会让写入吞吐降为零，它只是决定哪个值最终留下。
网络分区本身不会因为用了 LWW 冲突解决策略就自动修复，这两者没有因果关系。
optionExplanations_en: LWW treats the write with the larger timestamp as the later one, but if a node's clock runs fast, an earlier business write on it can carry a larger timestamp and overwrite a truly later write from another node.
LWW converges precisely by discarding one side, not by preserving all conflicts — this option has it backwards.
LWW's conflict-resolution logic by itself doesn't drop write throughput to zero, it just decides which value survives.
A network partition doesn't automatically repair itself just because LWW is used for conflict resolution — the two are unrelated.

scenario: 审计系统要回答“事件 B 是否看见了事件 A 的结果”。
scenario_en: An audit system must answer whether event B could have observed event A.
q: 哪种信息比墙上时间更关键？
q_en: Which information matters more than wall-clock time?
options: 因果依赖或消息传递关系
各个服务器所在的时区
日志文件名长度
磁盘序列号
options_en: Causal dependency or message-passing relationship
The time zone each server sits in.
Log filename length
Disk serial number
why: 分布式顺序首先是因果问题：谁读到谁、谁给谁发过消息。墙上时间只能作辅助线索。
why_en: Distributed ordering is mainly about causality: who observed or messaged whom, while wall-clock time is only a clue.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是给日志页面做近似排序，墙上时间可以用作展示键。
tradeoff: 因果正确性 vs 展示排序便利
optionExplanations: 事件 B 是否看见了事件 A 的结果，本质是因果依赖或消息传递关系的问题——谁读到了谁写的东西、谁给谁发过消息，这比墙上时钟的先后更可靠。
服务器所在时区只影响时间显示，跟判断一个事件有没有观察到另一个事件的结果无关。
日志文件名长度是纯粹的元数据细节，跟事件之间有没有因果关系没有任何联系。
磁盘序列号是硬件标识信息，同样跟事件间的因果依赖关系无关。
optionExplanations_en: Whether event B saw event A's result is fundamentally a question of causal dependency or message-passing — who read what someone else wrote, who sent whom a message — which is more reliable than wall-clock ordering.
The server's timezone only affects how time is displayed, unrelated to whether one event observed another's result.
Log filename length is a purely cosmetic metadata detail, unconnected to causal relationships between events.
Disk serial number is hardware identification information, likewise unrelated to causal dependency between events.

scenario: 一个时间 API 返回 now=[100ms,107ms] 这样的置信区间。
scenario_en: A time API returns an interval such as now=[100 ms, 107 ms].
q: 这种接口比单点时间戳多表达了什么？
q_en: What does this express beyond a point timestamp?
options: 本机对真实时间的不确定范围
事务的隔离级别
网络数据包的重试发送次数
磁盘队列深度
options_en: The local uncertainty range around real time
The transaction isolation level
The retry count of network packets.
The disk queue depth
why: 把时间当区间能让协议显式等待不确定性过去。单点时间戳容易让人忘掉误差。
why_en: Representing time as an interval lets protocols explicitly wait out uncertainty instead of pretending a point timestamp is exact.

termDefinitions.meaning: UTC 是常用的全球时间基准，机器本地时钟会近似它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UTC is a common global time reference that local machine clocks approximate.

optionExplanations: 返回一个区间而不是一个点，明确表达了本机对真实时间的不确定范围，协议看到这个区间就能显式地等待不确定性过去，而不是假装某个瞬间就是绝对精确的时间。
这个区间描述的是时间测量的不确定性，跟事务用什么隔离级别是完全不同的两件事。
网络包重试次数是网络层的统计信息，跟时间 API 返回的置信区间无关。
磁盘队列深度是存储层面的指标，跟时间不确定性区间是两个不相关的概念。
optionExplanations_en: Returning an interval instead of a point explicitly expresses the local uncertainty range around real time, letting a protocol explicitly wait out that uncertainty instead of pretending a single instant is exactly precise.
This interval describes measurement uncertainty in time, a completely different concern from what isolation level a transaction uses.
Packet retry count is a network-layer statistic, unrelated to a confidence interval returned by a time API.
Disk queue depth is a storage-layer metric, an unrelated concept to a time-uncertainty interval.

scenario: 全球数据库用带误差区间的物理时钟给事务排序，并要求外部一致性。
scenario_en: A global database uses physical clocks with uncertainty intervals to order transactions and wants external consistency.
q: 提交前为什么可能要等待？
q_en: Why might it wait before commit is visible?
options: 等时钟不确定区间过去再提交
等缓存 TTL 过期好省下内存
等客户端主动关闭连接
等所有旧日志被删除
options_en: Wait out the clock uncertainty window before committing.
Wait for the cache TTL to expire and free memory.
Wait for the client to close the connection.
Wait until all old logs are deleted.
why: 如果用物理时间给顺序背书，就要付出 commit wait。时钟越准，等待越短。
why_en: If physical time backs the ordering guarantee, commit wait pays for clock uncertainty; tighter clocks reduce the wait.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要因果一致或单分区顺序，逻辑时钟通常更便宜。
tradeoff: 外部时间顺序 vs 提交等待
optionExplanations: 要求外部一致性时，提交前必须等到这次事务的时钟不确定区间真正过去，才能保证按物理时间看起来晚发生的事务，不会被排到它前面，这段等待就是 commit wait。
等缓存 TTL 过期跟提交事务的顺序保证毫无关系，这是缓存策略层面的事。
等客户端关闭连接不是为了排序正确性，跟这里说的“等时钟不确定性过去”是不同的目的。
等所有旧日志删除是存储清理层面的操作，跟提交时为什么要等待没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: To provide external consistency, the transaction must wait out its own clock uncertainty interval before committing, so that a transaction that physically happened later can never be ordered before it — that wait is commit wait.
Letting cache TTLs lapse has nothing to do with the ordering guarantee of committing a transaction, that's a caching-policy concern.
Waiting for the client connection to close isn't about ordering correctness, a different purpose from waiting out clock uncertainty here.
Waiting for all old logs to be deleted is a storage-cleanup operation, unrelated to why commit needs to wait.

scenario: 持有锁的进程发生长时间 GC 暂停，恢复后以为租约还有效。
scenario_en: A lock holder pauses for a long GC stop and resumes thinking its lease is still valid.
q: 这会造成什么风险？
q_en: What risk does this create?
options: 旧持有者被替换后继续写，形成双主
GC 暂停期间会自动续约它持有的锁
其他节点会知道它只是暂停
网络协议会自动回滚旧写
options_en: The old holder keeps writing after being replaced, acting like a second leader.
A GC pause auto-renews all locks it holds.
Other nodes can tell it is merely paused.
The network protocol rolls back the stale writes.
why: 暂停中的进程无法观察世界变化，醒来后本地状态可能过期。下游要用 fencing token 拒绝旧令牌。
why_en: A paused process misses world changes, so downstream systems need fencing tokens to reject stale holders.

termDefinitions.meaning: GC 是运行时回收内存的过程，可能造成应用线程暂停。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Garbage collection reclaims memory and can pause application threads.

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token 是单调递增令牌，下游只接受更大的令牌来拒绝旧主。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing token; downstream systems accept only newer tokens to reject stale leaders.

optionExplanations: 暂停期间进程完全感知不到外界发生了什么，锁可能早已经被判定过期并转交给了别人，进程一恢复就以为自己还持有租约，继续写下去，跟新持有者一起变成了事实上的双主。
GC 暂停结束不代表任何锁会被自动续约，锁的状态取决于锁服务本身的判断，跟这次 GC 是否发生无关。
其他节点只会看到这个进程停止响应了一段时间，没有可靠办法分辨它是真的暂停还是已经死掉，不能假设它们知道真相。
网络协议不理解应用层的写入语义，不会替你回滚业务数据，这个说法混淆了协议和业务逻辑。
optionExplanations_en: During the pause, the process has no idea what happened in the world — its lock may already have been declared expired and handed to someone else, and on waking it still believes it holds the lease and keeps writing, effectively becoming a second leader alongside the new holder.
A GC pause ending doesn't automatically renew any lock; the lock's state is decided by the lock service itself, unrelated to whether this particular GC happened.
Other nodes only see this process stop responding for a while, with no reliable way to tell whether it merely paused or actually died — they can't be assumed to know the truth.
The network protocol has no understanding of application-level write semantics and won't roll back business data for you — this option conflates the protocol with business logic.

scenario: 作业调度器用分布式锁选主，旧主可能因暂停后恢复继续写共享存储。
scenario_en: A job scheduler uses a distributed lock for leadership; an old leader may resume after a pause and write shared storage.
q: 共享存储应要求什么？
q_en: What should shared storage require?
options: 写入携带递增 token
只检查客户端 IP 地址
只要锁服务返回 ok 就永远信任
把写入改成本地文件
options_en: Writes carry an increasing token
Check only the client IP address
Trust a past lock-service OK forever
Write to local files instead
why: 锁只能说明某一刻获得过资格，不能阻止旧进程复活。fencing token 让资源端自己挡掉旧主。
why_en: A lock proves eligibility at one moment; fencing tokens let the resource reject an old leader that comes back.
whenOtherWins: 如果资源本身只允许单连接独占且会断开旧连接，额外 token 可能不必自己实现。
tradeoff: 租约易用性 vs 资源端防旧主

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token 是单调递增令牌，下游只接受更大的令牌来拒绝旧主。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing token; downstream systems accept only newer tokens to reject stale leaders.

optionExplanations: 每次写入携带一个递增的 token，共享存储只接受比它见过的最大 token 更大的写入，旧主暂停后醒来带着旧 token 写进来，会因为 token 太小而被直接拒绝。
IP 地址不能区分同一台机器上先后不同任期的进程身份，一个恢复过来的旧主完全可能用同一个 IP 继续发送写入。
锁服务返回过 ok 只能说明当时那一刻确实拥有资格，不能保证持有者之后没有暂停、没有被替换，永远信任过去的 ok 正是问题所在。
把写入改成本地文件回避不了共享存储要面对多个写入者的问题，这不是解决方案。
optionExplanations_en: Attaching an increasing token to every write and having the shared storage only accept writes carrying a token larger than any it's already seen means a stale old leader waking up with an old token gets rejected outright.
An IP address can't distinguish which term or identity a process on that machine currently holds — a revived old leader could easily keep sending writes from the same IP.
A past OK from the lock service only proves eligibility at that one moment; it says nothing about whether the holder later paused or got replaced — trusting it forever is exactly the problem.
Writing to local files instead doesn't address the underlying issue of shared storage facing multiple potential writers, it isn't a solution.

scenario: 一个主节点拿到租约后长暂停，期间其他节点接任。
scenario_en: A leader obtains a lease, pauses for a long time, and another node takes over.
q: 把安全写入链排好序。
q_en: Order the safe write chain.
steps: 旧主醒来尝试写共享资源
锁服务给新主更大的 token
资源端拒绝较小 token 的写
旧主暂停导致租约过期
why: 链条关键是资源端检查单调 token，而不是相信旧主自己的本地时钟。这样暂停恢复也不会破坏数据。
why_en: The key is that the resource checks monotonically increasing tokens instead of trusting the old leader’s local clock.

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token 是单调递增令牌，下游只接受更大的令牌来拒绝旧主。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing token; downstream systems accept only newer tokens to reject stale leaders.

diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Old
  participant Lock
  participant New
  participant Store
  Old->>Lock: lease token 7
  Note over Old: long pause
  New->>Lock: lease token 8
  Old->>Store: write token 7
  Store-->>Old: reject

scenario: 团队想靠普通 Linux 进程保证“永远不会暂停超过 10ms”。
scenario_en: A team wants an ordinary Linux process to guarantee it never pauses for more than 10 ms.
q: 这个假设有什么问题？
q_en: What is wrong with this assumption?
options: 普通环境不是硬实时，随时可能暂停
TCP 会强制进程准时被调度
NTP 校时能阻止 GC 暂停
多数派投票能消除本机暂停
options_en: An ordinary environment is not hard real-time; it can pause at any moment.
TCP forces the process to be scheduled on time.
NTP time sync prevents GC pauses.
Majority voting removes local pauses.
why: 普通云主机没有硬实时上界。协议必须把长暂停当可能故障，而不是假设不会发生。
why_en: Ordinary cloud machines do not provide hard real-time bounds, so protocols must treat long pauses as possible.

termDefinitions.meaning: GC 是运行时回收内存的过程，可能造成应用线程暂停。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Garbage collection reclaims memory and can pause application threads.

rows: 普通环境不是硬实时，调度、GC、缺…
普通环境不是硬实时…场景
普通环境不是硬实时，调…成本
TCP 会强制进程准时运行
TCP 会强制进程准时…成本
多数派投票能消除本机暂停
多数派投票能消除本…场景
多数派投票能消除本机暂停成本

optionExplanations: 普通操作系统调度、垃圾回收、缺页中断都可能随时让进程暂停不确定的时长，这些都是普通云环境的常态，不是硬实时系统那种有严格上界保证的世界。
TCP 是传输层协议，管不了操作系统调度器什么时候真正运行这个进程。
NTP 只负责时钟同步，跟垃圾回收会不会暂停进程完全是两码事。
多数派投票解决的是分布式决策问题，它挡不住本机进程自己被调度器或 GC 暂停这件事。
optionExplanations_en: Ordinary OS scheduling, garbage collection, and page faults can all pause a process for an unpredictable duration at any time — that's the normal state of an ordinary cloud environment, not a hard real-time world with strict upper bounds.
TCP is a transport-layer protocol; it has no control over when the OS scheduler actually runs this process.
NTP only handles clock synchronization, completely unrelated to whether garbage collection pauses a process.
Majority voting solves a distributed-decision problem; it can't stop a local process from being paused by its own scheduler or GC.

scenario: 系统要决定两个并发写哪个应该胜出，但跨节点时钟最多只能“差不多同步”。
scenario_en: A system must decide which of two concurrent writes wins, but node clocks are only approximately synchronized.
q: 更稳的设计是什么？
q_en: What design is safer?
options: 用版本、因果或显式仲裁，不只用物理时间戳
直接比较本地 wall-clock 时间
让较快机器永远胜出
把时间戳截断到秒
options_en: Use versions, causality, or explicit arbitration, not only physical timestamps
Directly compare local wall-clock times
Let the faster machine always win
Round timestamps down to seconds
why: 近似同步不等于全局顺序。冲突解决要么保留并发信息，要么用明确的单点或多数派仲裁。
why_en: Approximate clock sync is not a global order, so conflict resolution needs causality, versions, or explicit arbitration.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务就是按用户看到的日历时间排序，物理时间可以展示，但不该单独决定冲突正确性。
tradeoff: 物理时间便利 vs 冲突正确性
optionExplanations: 跨节点时钟最多只能大致同步，不足以充当全局仲裁标准，用版本号、因果关系或明确的仲裁机制来决定哪个写赢，才不会被时钟误差带偏。
直接比较本地墙钟时间正是不可靠的做法，两台机器的时钟本来就可能有偏差，比较结果不能反映真实的先后关系。
让较快的机器永远胜出等于系统性地偏向某一台时钟跑得快的机器，跟哪个写真正发生得更晚没有关系。
把时间戳截断到秒只是降低了精度，没有解决时钟本身不同步、不能作为全局顺序依据这个根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: Clocks across nodes can only be roughly synchronized, not precise enough to serve as a global arbitration standard, so using versions, causality, or explicit arbitration to decide the winning write avoids being misled by clock error.
Directly comparing local wall-clock times is exactly the unreliable approach — two machines' clocks can already be skewed, so the comparison doesn't reflect the true order.
Letting the faster machine always win systematically favors whichever machine's clock happens to run fast, unrelated to which write genuinely happened later.
Rounding timestamps down to seconds just reduces precision; it doesn't fix the underlying problem that clocks aren't synchronized enough to serve as a global order.

scenario: 三节点集群中，一个节点觉得自己还是 leader，但另外两个节点已选出新 leader。
scenario_en: In a three-node cluster, one node believes it is still leader, but the other two have elected a new leader.
q: 系统应该相信谁？
q_en: Who should the system believe?
options: 多数派决定的新 leader
自称最久的旧 leader
时钟最快的节点
最近重启的节点
options_en: The new leader chosen by the majority
The old leader that has held leadership longest
The node with the fastest clock
The most recently restarted node
why: 分布式系统里的“事实”常由多数派定义。单个节点的自我认知不能覆盖多数派决定。
why_en: In many distributed systems, truth is defined by the majority; one node’s self-belief does not override it.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的最小节点集合，常用多数派让两个决定集合相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum set of nodes needed for a decision, often a majority so quorums overlap.

optionExplanations: 另外两个节点已经凑够多数派选出了新 leader，这个决定就是集群应该遵循的事实，单个节点自己觉得自己还是 leader 并不能推翻多数派已经做出的决定。
自称最久不是判断标准，一个节点主观认为自己仍是 leader，不能覆盖多数派已经选出新 leader 这个事实。
时钟最快跟谁是合法 leader 毫无关系，选主看的是多数派的决定，不是哪个节点计时更快。
最近重启跟是不是合法 leader 也没有关系，判断标准始终是多数派做出的决定。
optionExplanations_en: The other two nodes have already gathered a majority and elected a new leader, and that decision is what the cluster should follow — one node's private belief that it's still leader can't override what the majority has already decided.
Claiming the longest tenure isn't the deciding factor; one node's subjective belief that it's still leader can't override the fact that a majority already elected a new one.
Having the fastest clock has nothing to do with who the legitimate leader is; leadership is decided by majority vote, not by whose clock runs quickest.
Being the most recently restarted node is likewise unrelated to legitimacy — the deciding factor is always the majority's decision.

scenario: 旧 leader 和多数派失联，但它本地进程还健康。
scenario_en: An old leader loses contact with the majority, but its local process is still healthy.
q: 它应该怎么做？
q_en: What should it do?
options: 停止接受需要领导权的写入
继续写，直到自己崩溃
把本地时钟调快
要求客户端忽略错误
options_en: Stop accepting writes that require leadership
Keep writing until it crashes
Speed up its local clock
Ask clients to ignore errors
why: 领导权不是本地健康状态，而是多数派授予的资格。失去多数派时继续写会制造 split brain。
why_en: Leadership is granted by the majority, not by local health, so losing the majority should stop leader-only writes.
whenOtherWins: 如果该节点只服务本地只读缓存，并且读允许陈旧，可以继续返回带版本的弱一致结果。
tradeoff: 可用性 vs 防双主

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的最小节点集合，常用多数派让两个决定集合相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum set of nodes needed for a decision, often a majority so quorums overlap.

optionExplanations: 领导权是多数派授予的资格，一旦和多数派失联，就该主动停止接受需要领导权才能做的写入，等重新确认自己还被多数派承认再继续，不然容易和新 leader 一起制造双主。
本地进程健康不代表还拥有多数派授予的领导权，继续写下去直到崩溃只会让双主问题持续更久、造成更多冲突数据。
调快本地时钟跟能不能重新获得多数派的认可毫无关系，解决不了失联这个根本问题。
要求客户端忽略错误是在掩盖问题而不是解决问题，还会让客户端在双主状态下继续往一个不再合法的 leader 写数据。
optionExplanations_en: Leadership is a status granted by the majority, so the moment it loses contact with them, it should stop accepting writes that require leadership, and only resume once it reconfirms majority backing — otherwise it risks becoming a second leader alongside the new one.
Local process health doesn't mean it still holds majority-granted leadership; continuing to write until it crashes just prolongs the split-brain problem and creates more conflicting data.
Speeding up its local clock has nothing to do with regaining majority recognition, and doesn't fix the underlying loss of contact.
Asking clients to ignore errors papers over the problem instead of solving it, and would keep clients writing to a leader that's no longer legitimate.

scenario: 网络分区后两个节点都认为自己是主库并接受写入。
scenario_en: After a network partition, two nodes both believe they are primary and accept writes.
q: 最直接的后果是什么？
q_en: What is the immediate consequence?
options: split brain 双主
读延迟一定降低
所有客户端都会自动重试并成功
事务隔离自动增强
options_en: Split-brain dual primaries
Read latency always decreases
All clients automatically retry and succeed.
Transaction isolation automatically strengthens
why: 双主会让同一数据有两个合法历史，恢复网络后要么丢写，要么做复杂冲突合并。
why_en: Split brain creates two accepted histories, which later requires data loss or complex conflict resolution.
optionExplanations: 两个节点都以为自己是唯一的主库并各自接受写入，这就是典型的 split brain 双主，同一份数据出现了两条互不知情的历史。
分区期间两个节点各自独立处理写入，反而增加了之后要处理的冲突数据量，跟读延迟降低没有关系，这个说法答非所问。
客户端重试碰到的是两个都在接受写入、但互相不同步的主库，不会因为重试就自动获得正确、一致的结果。
事务隔离级别是单个数据库内部的并发控制设置，不会因为出现网络分区和双主就自动变强。
optionExplanations_en: Both nodes believing they're the one true primary and accepting writes independently is precisely split-brain dual primaries — the same data now has two histories that know nothing of each other.

During the partition, each node independently handling writes actually increases the volume of conflicting data to resolve afterward, unrelated to read latency, so this option doesn't address the question.
A retrying client is hitting two primaries that are both accepting writes but out of sync with each other; retrying doesn't automatically produce a correct, consistent result.
Transaction isolation level is a concurrency-control setting internal to one database; it doesn't automatically strengthen just because a network partition and dual primaries occurred.

scenario: 五节点协调服务要避免两个 leader 同时获得授权。
scenario_en: A five-node coordination service must avoid two leaders being authorized at the same time.
q: 为什么用多数派？
q_en: Why use a majority quorum?
options: 任意两个多数派必然相交，能看到彼此
多数派机制能让网络延迟直接降为零
少数派可以单独覆盖多数派
它能避免所有节点同时崩溃
options_en: Any two majorities must overlap, so they see each other's decision.
A majority quorum drives network latency to zero.
A minority can override a majority on its own.
It prevents all nodes from crashing at once.
why: 5 节点多数派是 3，两个 3 节点集合至少重叠 1 个节点。这个交集阻止两个互不知情的决定都成立。
why_en: In five nodes, two quorums of three must overlap in at least one node, preventing independent conflicting decisions.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单机本地决定，本地锁更简单，但它不提供节点故障后的集群一致性。
tradeoff: 多数派安全 vs 本地简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的最小节点集合，常用多数派让两个决定集合相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum set of nodes needed for a decision, often a majority so quorums overlap.

optionExplanations: 五节点里的多数派是三，任意两组三节点的集合按抽屉原理必然至少重叠一个节点，这个重叠节点见证过两次决定，能挡住两个互不知情的多数派同时成立。
多数派机制解决的是决策正确性问题，跟网络延迟本身没有关系，不会让延迟变成零。
少数派节点数量不够，按定义就凑不出多数派，说它能单独覆盖多数派的决定不成立。
多数派机制不能阻止个别节点崩溃，它解决的是崩溃发生后如何仍然做出正确、唯一的决定。
optionExplanations_en: With five nodes, a majority is three, and any two sets of three must overlap in at least one node by the pigeonhole principle; that overlapping node has witnessed both decisions, preventing two mutually unaware majorities from both succeeding.
The majority mechanism is about decision correctness, unrelated to network delay itself, and doesn't make latency zero.
A minority simply doesn't have enough nodes to form a majority by definition, so claiming it can override the majority's decision doesn't hold.
The majority mechanism doesn't prevent individual node crashes; it addresses how to still reach a correct, single decision after crashes happen.

scenario: 某节点不只是崩溃，而是给不同节点发送互相矛盾的假消息。
scenario_en: A node does not merely crash; it sends contradictory false messages to different peers.
q: 这属于什么故障？
q_en: What kind of fault is this?
options: Byzantine fault
crash-stop fault
clock drift
packet loss
options_en: Byzantine fault
Crash-stop fault
Clock drift
Packet loss
why: Byzantine 故障表示节点可以任意撒谎或作恶，普通崩溃容错算法通常不覆盖它。
why_en: A Byzantine fault means a node may lie or behave arbitrarily, which ordinary crash-fault algorithms do not handle.

termDefinitions.meaning: BFT 表示系统在部分节点任意作恶或撒谎时仍能保持正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Byzantine fault tolerance means a system remains correct even if some nodes lie or behave arbitrarily.

tradeoff: 崩溃故障模型 vs 恶意故障模型
optionExplanations: 节点没有单纯停止服务，而是主动给不同的对方发送互相矛盾的假消息，这种任意作恶、撒谎的行为正是 Byzantine fault 的定义。
crash-stop 指的是节点要么正常工作要么彻底停止，不会继续发消息更不会撒谎，跟这里描述的行为不符。
clock drift 只是时钟走得快慢有偏差，不涉及故意发送互相矛盾的假消息。
packet loss 只是网络丢包，跟节点主动构造矛盾假消息这种恶意行为是完全不同的故障类型。
optionExplanations_en: The node isn't simply stopping — it's actively sending different nodes contradictory, fabricated messages, and that arbitrary, deceptive behavior is exactly the definition of a Byzantine fault.
Crash-stop means a node either works correctly or halts entirely; it never keeps sending messages, let alone lying, which doesn't match the behavior described.
Clock drift is just a clock running fast or slow, unrelated to deliberately sending contradictory fabricated messages.
Packet loss is just the network dropping packets, a completely different failure type from a node maliciously fabricating contradictory messages.

scenario: 系统运行在互不信任的组织之间，节点可能故意签出冲突结果。
scenario_en: A system runs across mutually distrustful organizations, and nodes may intentionally sign conflicting results.
q: 应考虑哪类协议？
q_en: Which protocol family should be considered?
options: BFT 共识协议
只处理 crash-stop 的 Raft
单机互斥锁
NTP 时间排序
options_en: BFT consensus
Raft configured only for crash-stop faults
A single-machine mutex
NTP timestamp ordering
why: 互不信任环境不能只假设节点会安静崩溃。BFT 成本更高，但能处理撒谎节点。
why_en: Mutually distrustful environments cannot assume nodes only crash quietly; BFT costs more but handles lying nodes.
whenOtherWins: 同一团队控制的数据中心通常假设非 Byzantine，使用 crash-fault consensus 更简单。
tradeoff: 恶意容错 vs 协议成本

termDefinitions.meaning: BFT 表示系统在部分节点任意作恶或撒谎时仍能保持正确。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Byzantine fault tolerance means a system remains correct even if some nodes lie or behave arbitrarily.

optionExplanations: 互不信任的组织之间，节点可能故意作恶、签出矛盾结果，这正是 BFT 共识协议要处理的场景，代价是比普通崩溃容错更高的协调成本。
只处理 crash-stop 的 Raft 假设节点最多是安静地崩溃，不会防御节点故意撒谎，用在互不信任的环境里会被恶意节点钻空子。
单机互斥锁只解决同一台机器内部的并发问题，管不了跨组织、跨节点的恶意行为。
NTP 时间排序解决的是时钟同步问题，不能识别或阻止节点故意发送矛盾消息。
optionExplanations_en: Between mutually distrustful organizations, a node might deliberately misbehave and sign off on conflicting results, exactly the scenario BFT consensus is built for, at the cost of higher coordination overhead than ordinary crash tolerance.
Raft configured only for crash-stop faults assumes nodes at worst crash quietly and doesn't defend against deliberate lying, so a malicious node in a distrustful environment could exploit it.
A single-machine mutex only solves concurrency within one machine and has no bearing on cross-organization, cross-node malicious behavior.
NTP timestamp ordering addresses clock synchronization; it can neither detect nor prevent a node deliberately sending contradictory messages.

scenario: 所有节点部署同一个有 bug 的版本，都会对同一输入算错。
scenario_en: All nodes deploy the same buggy version and compute the same wrong result for the same input.
q: BFT 能救这个问题吗？
q_en: Can BFT save this?
options: 通常不能，因为多数节点会一致地产生同样错误
一定能，因为它能修复所有软件里的 bug
只要增加 NTP 就能解决
把网络变快就能解决
options_en: Usually no, because a majority may produce the same wrong result
Yes, because it fixes all software bugs.
Adding NTP solves it
A faster network solves it
why: BFT 处理的是部分节点任意偏离，不是所有副本共享同一个逻辑错误。多样化实现才可能缓解共享 bug。
why_en: BFT handles some nodes deviating arbitrarily, not every replica sharing the same logic bug.
optionExplanations: BFT 假设的是部分节点会任意偏离，但这里所有节点跑的是同一个有 bug 的版本，对同一输入会一致地算出同一个错误结果，多数派恰恰会认同这个错误答案，BFT 保护不了这种情况。
BFT 处理的是恶意或任意偏离行为，不是用来修复软件逻辑错误的工具，说它一定能解决正好说反了。
增加 NTP 只解决时钟同步问题，跟所有节点共享的同一个逻辑 bug 毫不相干。
网络变快只影响消息传递速度，不会改变所有节点对同一输入算出同样错误结果这件事。
optionExplanations_en: BFT assumes some nodes deviate arbitrarily, but here every node runs the same buggy version and computes the same wrong result for the same input, so the majority would actually agree on that wrong answer — BFT offers no protection here.
BFT handles malicious or arbitrary deviation, not a tool for fixing software logic errors, so claiming it always solves this has it backwards.
Adding NTP only addresses clock synchronization, unrelated to a logic bug shared by every node.
A faster network only affects message delivery speed; it doesn't change the fact that every node computes the same wrong result for the same input.

scenario: 你在读一个分布式算法证明，需要知道它假设网络和时钟有多可靠。
scenario_en: You are reading a distributed algorithm proof and need to know its timing assumptions.
q: 哪个模型最贴近普通云系统？
q_en: Which model best matches ordinary cloud systems?
options: 部分同步：大多数时候有界，偶尔界限失效
完全同步：延迟和暂停永远存在一个硬上界
完全异步：没有任何时钟或超时
单机模型：没有网络
options_en: Partial synchrony: bounds usually hold but sometimes fail
Fully synchronous: latency and pauses always have a hard bound.
Full asynchrony: no clocks or timeouts at all
Single-machine model: no network
why: 普通云环境通常有“平时还行，坏时很坏”的时间行为。部分同步承认这个现实。
why_en: Ordinary cloud systems usually behave with rough bounds most of the time and bad outliers sometimes, which is partial synchrony.

termDefinitions.meaning: 部分同步模型假设大多数时候有时间界限，但偶尔延迟、暂停和时钟误差会变得很大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partial synchrony assumes timing bounds usually hold, but delays, pauses, and clock error can sometimes become very large.

tradeoff: 真实部署弹性 vs 证明模型简化

rows: 部分同步：大多数时候有界，偶尔界限…
必须保护最新读或不变量时
完全同步：延迟和暂停永远有硬上界
必须保护最新读或不变量时
完全异步：没有任何时钟或超时
能接受短暂滞后、想降延迟时
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
单机模型：没有网络成本

optionExplanations: 普通云系统大多数时候延迟和暂停都在合理范围内，但偶尔会出现远超预期的极端情况，部分同步模型正是承认“平时还行、坏时很坏”这个现实。
完全同步要求延迟和暂停永远有硬上界，普通云环境做不到这种保证，跟真实情况不符。
完全异步没有任何时钟或超时概念，这比普通云系统实际能观察到的行为要悲观得多，不贴合实际。
单机模型压根没有网络，跟分布式云系统需要面对网络故障的现实完全不匹配。
optionExplanations_en: Ordinary cloud systems mostly keep latency and pauses within reasonable bounds, but occasionally hit extreme outliers far beyond expectation, and partial synchrony is precisely the model that admits things are usually fine but sometimes very bad.
Full synchrony requires delays and pauses to always have hard bounds, a guarantee ordinary cloud environments can't provide, mismatched with reality.
Full asynchrony assumes no notion of clocks or timeouts at all, far more pessimistic than what ordinary cloud systems actually exhibit, not a good fit.
A single-machine model has no network at all, completely mismatched with the reality that a distributed cloud system has to deal with network failures.

scenario: 一个算法声称在完全异步系统里用超时准确判断节点死亡。
scenario_en: An algorithm claims it can accurately detect node death with timeouts in a fully asynchronous system.
q: 你该怀疑什么？
q_en: What should you suspect?
options: 异步模型没有时间界限，超时证明不了死亡
完全异步的模型天生自带一个全局时钟
超时设得越短证明力越强
节点死亡会自动广播给所有人
options_en: An asynchronous model has no timing bound, so a timeout cannot prove death.
The fully asynchronous model comes with a global clock.
The shorter the timeout, the stronger the proof.
Node death is broadcast to everyone automatically.
why: 在没有时间界限的模型里，慢消息和死节点无法区分。超时只能是工程怀疑，不是证明。
why_en: Without timing bounds, a slow message and a dead node are indistinguishable, so timeout is suspicion, not proof.
whenOtherWins: 在有硬实时界限的专用同步系统里，超时判断可以更接近证明。
tradeoff: 模型严格性 vs 普通云现实
optionExplanations: 完全异步模型本身不承诺任何可靠的时间界限，这意味着一条消息慢到了和一个节点真的死了在这个模型里根本无法区分，用超时“准确”判断死亡这个说法站不住脚。
完全异步模型的定义恰恰是没有全局时钟或可靠的时间界限，这个说法把模型的定义说反了。
在没有可靠时间界限的模型里，超时长短本身证明不了什么，因为慢消息和死节点永远无法区分。
节点死亡不会在完全异步模型里自动广播，这个模型甚至不承诺消息一定会送达。
optionExplanations_en: A fully asynchronous model gives no reliable timing bound at all, meaning a slow message and a genuinely dead node are indistinguishable within it, so claiming a timeout can accurately prove death doesn't hold up.
A fully asynchronous model is defined precisely by the absence of a global clock or reliable timing bounds, so this option has the definition backwards.
In a model without reliable timing bounds, the length of the timeout proves nothing on its own, because a slow message and a dead node remain indistinguishable regardless.
Node death isn't automatically broadcast in a fully asynchronous model, which doesn't even promise messages will be delivered at all.

scenario: 协议文档说只处理 crash-stop，不处理 crash-recovery 或 Byzantine。
scenario_en: A protocol document says it handles crash-stop, not crash-recovery or Byzantine behavior.
q: 这意味着什么？
q_en: What does that imply?
options: 节点崩溃后不再回来，且不会撒谎
节点会恢复并带着旧状态一起回来
节点可以伪造任意消息
网络永远可靠
options_en: A crashed node does not return and does not lie
A node recovers and comes back carrying stale state.
A node may forge arbitrary messages
The network is always reliable
why: 故障模型定义了算法要防的世界。把模型看错，会把协议用到它没有承诺的场景。
why_en: The fault model defines the world an algorithm defends against; using the wrong model breaks the guarantee.
tradeoff: 故障假设范围 vs 协议保证
optionExplanations: crash-stop 假设节点一旦崩溃就永远不会回来，也不会伪造消息撒谎，协议只需要防这种“干净消失”的世界，不用考虑节点带着旧状态复活或恶意撒谎。
节点恢复后带着旧状态回来属于 crash-recovery 模型要处理的情况，跟只处理 crash-stop 的协议假设不同。
节点能伪造任意消息是 Byzantine 故障模型的范畴，crash-stop 明确不包含这种情况。
网络永远可靠是另一个独立的假设，跟节点是崩溃后不回来还是恢复回来是两个不同的维度。
optionExplanations_en: Crash-stop assumes a crashed node never comes back and never fabricates lies, so the protocol only has to defend against this clean-disappearance world, not nodes reviving with old state or maliciously lying.
A node recovering later with old state is what the crash-recovery model handles, different from an algorithm assuming only crash-stop.
A node forging arbitrary messages falls under the Byzantine fault model, explicitly excluded by crash-stop.
The network always being reliable is a separate, independent assumption, a different dimension from whether a crashed node returns or stays gone.

scenario: 一个协议永远不会选出两个 leader，但在网络抖动时可能很久选不出 leader。
scenario_en: A protocol never elects two leaders, but under network instability it may take a long time to elect any leader.
q: 这体现了什么区分？
q_en: What distinction does this show?
options: 安全性保持，活性受影响
活性保持，安全性受影响
两者都一定失败
这只和磁盘有关
options_en: Safety holds, liveness suffers
Liveness holds, safety suffers
Both necessarily fail
This is only about disks
why: 安全性是“不发生坏事”，活性是“好事最终发生”。故障期间很多协议宁可停住，也不做错。
why_en: Safety means bad things do not happen; liveness means good things eventually happen, and protocols often preserve safety by pausing.
tradeoff: 安全不出错 vs 活性继续前进

rows: 安全性保持，活性受影响
安全性保持，活性受…场景
安全性保持，活性受影响成本
活性保持，安全性受影响
活性保持，安全性受…场景
活性保持，安全性受影响成本

optionExplanations: 永远不会同时选出两个 leader，说明坏事没有发生，安全性守住了；但网络抖动时可能很久选不出任何 leader，说明好事没有及时发生，活性受到了影响。
这里的描述正好是安全性守住、活性受影响，说成活性守住、安全性受影响是把两者说反了。
协议只是活性暂时受影响，安全性一直守住，不能说两者都必然失败。
选主的安全性和活性讨论的是分布式协调层面的保证，跟磁盘没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Never electing two leaders at once means nothing bad happened, so safety holds; but going a long time without electing any leader during network jitter means something good didn't happen in time, so liveness suffers.
This scenario is exactly safety holding while liveness suffers — saying the reverse gets the two backwards.
The protocol's liveness is merely temporarily affected while safety holds throughout, so it's incorrect to say both necessarily fail.
Leader-election safety and liveness are guarantees at the distributed-coordination layer, unrelated to disks.

scenario: 客户端写入用户设置超时，但请求带了 operationId。
scenario_en: A client write for user settings times out, but the request included an operationId.
q: 恢复流程应先做什么？
q_en: What should recovery do first?
options: 用 operationId 查询服务器最终状态
立刻用同一个幂等键重试请求
先直接返回失败，再由后台任务去 reconcile
把超时当成功且不记录
options_en: Query the server’s final state by operationId
Retry immediately with the same idempotency key
Return failure first, then reconcile in a background task.
Treat the timeout as success without recording it
why: 超时后结果未知，先查状态能避免把已成功操作又执行一次。查不到再用同一个幂等键重试。
why_en: After a timeout the outcome is unknown, so check operation status before retrying the same side effect.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作是纯只读查询且无副作用，直接重发新查询也可以。
tradeoff: 操作收敛性 vs 客户端简化

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等性：同一操作执行多次，最终可见结果仍像执行一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotence means repeating the same operation leaves the visible result as if it ran once.

termDefinitions.meaning: operationId：一次业务操作的稳定标识，用来查询状态或去重重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An operationId is a stable identifier for one business operation, used for status lookup or retry dedupe.

optionExplanations: 超时后结果未知，先拿 operationId 去查服务器上这次操作最终到底是什么状态，能避免把一个已经成功的操作又执行一遍。
没查状态就立刻用同一个幂等键重试，如果服务端实现不完善或去重窗口有问题，仍有一定风险，不如先确认状态更稳妥。
先直接返回失败会误导用户以为操作没有发生，如果实际已经成功，用户可能会基于错误信息做出进一步的错误操作。
把超时直接当成功且不记录，一旦实际上失败了，这次操作就凭空消失了，没人知道要补救。
optionExplanations_en: With the outcome unknown after a timeout, querying the server's final state by operationId first avoids re-executing an operation that already succeeded.
Immediately retrying with the same idempotency key without checking status still carries some risk if the server's implementation or dedup window isn't airtight, so confirming status first is safer.
Returning failure right away misleads the user into thinking nothing happened, and if it actually succeeded, the user might take further incorrect action based on that wrong signal.
Treating the timeout as success without recording it means if it actually failed, the operation silently vanishes with nobody aware it needs fixing.

scenario: 两个服务隔着不可靠网络互相发送确认，想“绝对确定”双方都知道对方已收到。
scenario_en: Two services exchange acknowledgments over an unreliable network and want absolute certainty that both know the other received.
q: 为什么做不到绝对确定？
q_en: Why is absolute certainty impossible?
options: 最后一条确认本身也可能丢失
加一次确认就能无限确定
TCP 会证明应用处理完成
同步时钟能替代确认
options_en: The last acknowledgment can itself be lost
One extra acknowledgment gives infinite certainty
TCP proves application processing completed
Synchronized clocks replace acknowledgment
why: 每多一轮确认，最后一条消息仍可能丢。协议只能选择足够好的保证和超时策略。
why_en: Every extra acknowledgment leaves a final message that may be lost, so protocols choose practical guarantees rather than absolute knowledge.
optionExplanations: 不管加多少轮确认，总有最后一条消息，而这条消息本身照样可能在不可靠的网络上丢失，谁都没法拿到“双方都确认收到”这件事本身被确认的证据。
每多加一次确认，问题只是往后推了一层，最后一条确认依然可能丢，不会带来无限确定性。
TCP 只保证字节可靠传输，证明不了对端应用真的处理完成了这次业务逻辑。
同步时钟解决的是时间度量问题，不能替代确认消息本身要解决的“对方是否收到”这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: No matter how many rounds of acknowledgment you add, there's always a final message, and that message itself can still be lost on an unreliable network, so nobody ever gets proof that the fact both sides confirmed was itself confirmed.
Each extra acknowledgment just pushes the problem back one layer — the last acknowledgment can still be lost, never producing infinite certainty.
TCP only guarantees reliable byte delivery, not proof that the remote application actually finished processing the business logic.
Synchronized clocks solve a time-measurement problem; they can't substitute for what an acknowledgment itself is meant to answer — whether the other side received it.

scenario: 协调服务用心跳和超时怀疑 leader 故障。
scenario_en: A coordination service uses heartbeats and timeouts to suspect leader failure.
q: 把故障检测链排好序。
q_en: Order the failure-detection chain.
steps: 多数派在新任期投票
follower 超时未收到心跳
旧 leader 若失去多数派应停止写
新 leader 获得多数派授权
why: 超时只触发怀疑，真正的领导权来自多数派投票。旧 leader 继续写才是危险点。
why_en: Timeout only creates suspicion; leadership comes from majority votes, and the old leader must stop writing.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的最小节点集合，常用多数派让两个决定集合相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum set of nodes needed for a decision, often a majority so quorums overlap.

scenario: 你在给 RPC 协议做故障清单。
scenario_en: You are making a fault checklist for an RPC protocol.
q: 哪些情况必须考虑？
q_en: Which cases must be considered?
options: 请求包丢失
响应包丢失
远端处理成功但响应超时
消息重复到达
options_en: Request packet lost
Response packet lost
Remote side succeeded but response timed out
Message arrives more than once
why: 这些都会在真实网络或重试层出现。协议要靠幂等、去重和状态查询收敛。
why_en: All of these can occur in real networks or retry layers, so protocols need idempotency, deduplication, and status lookup.
optionExplanations: 请求包在到达服务端之前就可能在网络上丢失，这是真实网络会出现的基本故障之一。
响应包在服务端处理完之后返回客户端的路上同样可能丢失，客户端一样看不到结果。
远端可能已经成功处理了请求，但响应因为各种原因没能在超时窗口内送达，客户端只会看到一个超时。
网络重传或客户端重试都可能导致同一条消息被投递不止一次，协议要能应付重复。
optionExplanations_en: A request packet can get lost on the network before it even reaches the server — a basic failure mode of any real network.
A response packet can just as easily get lost on the way back to the client after the server finishes processing, leaving the client with no visible result either.
The remote side may have processed the request successfully, but the response failed to arrive within the timeout window for some reason, and the client only sees a timeout.
Network retransmission or client-side retries can both cause the same message to be delivered more than once, so the protocol has to tolerate duplicates.

scenario: 系统准备用物理时钟决定写入顺序。
scenario_en: A system plans to use physical clocks to order writes.
q: 哪些风险需要写进设计？
q_en: Which risks belong in the design?
options: 时钟漂移
NTP 跳变
不同机器读数不可精确比较
GC 暂停导致检查过期太晚
options_en: Clock drift
NTP clock steps
Readings on different machines are not exactly comparable
GC pause makes expiry checks late
why: 物理时钟问题不是小概率装饰，它会直接影响排序、租约和过期判断。
why_en: Physical-clock issues directly affect ordering, leases, and expiry checks, so they belong in the design.

termDefinitions.meaning: NTP 用网络时间源校准机器时钟，但不能消除漂移和跳变风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes clocks to network time sources, but it cannot remove drift or clock-step risks.

termDefinitions.meaning: GC 是运行时回收内存的过程，可能造成应用线程暂停。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Garbage collection reclaims memory and can pause application threads.

optionExplanations: 机器时钟本身会随时间缓慢跑偏，累积出实打实的误差，直接影响用它排序的写入顺序。
NTP 校准时可能让墙钟发生跳变，一旦跳到过去，正在用这个时钟判断顺序或过期的逻辑就会被打乱。
不同机器上读到的时钟数值即使都各自准确，也不能拿来精确比较大小，因为彼此之间总有一点误差。
GC 暂停会让进程在该检查过期的那一刻没能及时运行，等它醒来时判断已经晚了，过期检查因此被延后。
optionExplanations_en: Machine clocks slowly drift over time, accumulating real error that directly affects any ordering based on them.
NTP calibration can step the wall clock, and if it jumps backward, any logic relying on that clock for ordering or expiry gets thrown off.
Even if each machine's own clock reading is locally accurate, comparing readings across machines isn't precise, since there's always some residual skew between them.
A GC pause can keep the process from running exactly when it should check for expiry, so by the time it wakes up the check has already run late.

scenario: 一个协议要求消息一定在 50ms 内到达，否则就判定对方死了。
scenario_en: A protocol requires every message to arrive within 50 ms or the peer is declared dead.
q: 它适合什么环境？
q_en: What environment does it fit?
options: 有硬延迟上界的同步/实时系统
运行在普通公网上的互联网服务
跨洲的移动蜂窝网络
没有监控的多租户云
options_en: A synchronous or real-time system with a hard latency bound.
Internet services running over the ordinary public network.
A cross-continent mobile cellular network.
An unmonitored multi-tenant cloud.
why: 只有已知硬上界时，超时才接近证明。普通网络只能把超时当怀疑。
why_en: Only with known hard bounds does a timeout approach proof; ordinary networks make it a suspicion.
whenOtherWins: 普通云系统应使用部分同步假设、多数派和重试，而不是硬判死。
tradeoff: 强时间假设 vs 部署现实
optionExplanations: 只有在有硬性延迟上界保证的同步模型或专门的实时系统里，一条消息没在规定时间内到达才能被当作对方真的死了的可靠证据。
普通互联网服务的延迟波动很大，没有这种硬上界保证，用固定的 50ms 判死会经常误杀健康节点。
跨洲移动网络的延迟波动比普通互联网服务还要大，更加不适合用这种严格的固定阈值判断。
没有监控的多租户云环境延迟更加不可预测，同样不满足硬延迟上界这个前提。
optionExplanations_en: Only in a synchronous model or a dedicated real-time system with hard delay bounds can a message missing its deadline be reliably taken as proof the other side is truly dead.
An ordinary internet service has widely fluctuating latency with no such hard bound, so a fixed 50ms threshold would frequently misjudge healthy nodes as dead.
Cross-continent mobile networks fluctuate even more than an ordinary internet service, even less suited to this kind of strict fixed threshold.
An unmonitored multi-tenant cloud has even less predictable latency, also failing to meet the hard-delay-bound premise.

scenario: 网络短暂拥塞导致 follower 反复误判 leader 死亡。
scenario_en: Short network congestion repeatedly makes followers suspect the leader is dead.
q: 系统会出现什么症状？
q_en: What symptom can appear?
options: 频繁选主，时间花在协调而非请求
数据会自动变得更加线性化一致
所有请求的延迟变成零
磁盘空间会立刻被释放
options_en: Constant leader elections, with time spent coordinating instead of serving requests.
Data automatically becomes more linearizable.
Every request's latency drops to zero.
Disk space is freed immediately.
why: 误判不会必然破坏安全性，但会伤害活性和吞吐。选举退避和合理超时很重要。
why_en: False suspicions may preserve safety but hurt liveness and throughput, so election backoff and sane timeouts matter.
optionExplanations: follower 反复误判 leader 死亡就会反复触发选主，系统把大量时间花在协调新 leader 上，而不是真正处理业务请求，吞吐和响应都会受影响。
误判选主跟数据会不会变得更线性化没有关系，这个说法答非所问。
频繁选主期间协调开销增加，不会让所有请求延迟凭空变成零，这个说法不成立。
选主频率跟磁盘空间释放没有关系，这两者是完全不同的系统维度。
optionExplanations_en: Followers repeatedly misjudging the leader as dead keeps triggering new elections, so the system spends a lot of time coordinating a new leader instead of actually serving requests, hurting throughput and response time.
Mistaken elections have nothing to do with data becoming more linearizable, so this option doesn't address the question.
Coordination overhead rising during frequent elections doesn't make all request latency drop to zero out of nowhere, so this claim doesn't hold.
Election frequency has nothing to do with freeing up disk space — these are completely different system dimensions.

scenario: 三节点服务要滚动升级，每次重启一个节点，用户请求不能中断。
scenario_en: A three-node service needs rolling upgrades, restarting one node at a time without interrupting users.
q: 软件必须具备什么能力？
q_en: What ability must the software have?
options: 在少数节点不可用时继续服务
任何节点重启就全停
只支持手工切 DNS
要求所有请求粘到被重启节点
options_en: Continue serving while a minority of nodes is unavailable
Stop everything when any node restarts
Only support manual DNS cutover
Pin all requests to the restarting node
why: 滚动升级依赖部分失败容忍：一个节点离线时，其余节点仍能达成需要的决定。
why_en: Rolling upgrades rely on tolerating partial failure, so the remaining nodes can keep making required decisions.
whenOtherWins: 如果是离线批处理作业，停全作业并从 checkpoint 恢复会更简单。
tradeoff: 在线连续服务 vs 批处理简化

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的最小节点集合，常用多数派让两个决定集合相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum set of nodes needed for a decision, often a majority so quorums overlap.

optionExplanations: 滚动升级要一个接一个重启节点，软件必须能在少数节点暂时不可用的情况下继续对外服务，靠剩下多数节点撑住需要的决定。
任何节点重启就全停，会让滚动升级变成事实上的全站停机，跟“用户请求不能中断”的要求正相反。
只支持手工切 DNS 既慢又粗糙，达不到滚动升级过程中持续服务的细粒度要求。
要求所有请求粘到正在重启的节点，恰恰会在那个节点重启期间让所有请求都失败，这是最糟的做法。
optionExplanations_en: Rolling upgrades restart nodes one at a time, so the software must keep serving while a minority of nodes are temporarily unavailable, relying on the remaining majority to still make required decisions.
Stopping everything when any node restarts would turn a rolling upgrade into an effective full outage, the opposite of not interrupting user requests.
Only supporting manual DNS cutover is slow and coarse, falling short of the fine-grained continuous service a rolling upgrade needs.
Pinning all requests to the restarting node would make every single one of them fail exactly while that node is down, the worst possible approach.

scenario: 同样是很多机器，HPC 作业和在线云服务的故障策略为什么不同？
scenario_en: Why do HPC jobs and online cloud services use different fault strategies despite both using many machines?
q: 两类系统的故障策略为什么不同？
q_en: Why do these two system types use different fault strategies?
options: HPC 可重跑；在线要持续响应
HPC 从不发生硬件故障
在线服务不能使用复制
云网络一定比 HPC 专网更可靠
options_en: HPC can restart; online services must keep serving
HPC never has hardware failures
Online services cannot use replication
Cloud networks are always more reliable than HPC fabrics
why: 工作负载决定故障策略。离线计算能接受停顿，在线服务通常要在故障中继续提供有限服务。
why_en: The workload drives the fault strategy: offline computation can pause, while online services usually must keep serving.

termDefinitions.meaning: HPC 常指专用集群上的科学计算，故障处理更像整作业重启。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: High-performance computing often means scientific workloads on specialized clusters, where failures may restart the whole job.

tradeoff: 离线可暂停 vs 在线持续服务
optionExplanations: HPC 作业失败了可以直接重跑一次，代价是多花点计算时间；在线服务必须持续响应用户，不能因为要恢复而干脆停掉，这个工作负载差异决定了两者截然不同的故障策略。
HPC 环境同样会遇到硬件故障，只是它的应对方式是重跑而不是持续服务，说它从不发生硬件故障不成立。
在线服务恰恰经常依赖复制来提高可用性，说它不能使用复制正好说反了。
云网络和 HPC 专网各有各的可靠性特点，不能一概而论说云网络一定更可靠。
optionExplanations_en: An HPC job that fails can simply be rerun at the cost of some extra compute time; an online service must keep serving users and can't just stop to recover — this workload difference is what drives the two very different fault strategies.
HPC environments face hardware failures too, they just respond by rerunning rather than staying up continuously, so claiming HPC never has hardware failures doesn't hold.
Online services actually rely heavily on replication to boost availability, so claiming they can't use replication has it backwards.
Cloud networks and HPC-dedicated fabrics each have their own reliability characteristics; it isn't accurate to claim cloud networks are always more reliable.

scenario: DDIA 讨论的互联网服务通常假设 shared-nothing：机器只能通过网络请求通信。
scenario_en: The internet services in this scope usually assume shared-nothing machines that communicate by network requests.
q: 这排除了什么隐含能力？
q_en: What implicit ability is excluded?
options: 一台机器直接读写另一台机器内存或磁盘
机器之间通过 RPC 消息互相发送
服务通过负载均衡接收请求
节点有自己的本地磁盘
options_en: One machine directly reading or writing another machine’s memory or disk
Machines send messages to each other via RPC.
Services receiving requests through a load balancer
Nodes having their own local disk
why: shared-nothing 让故障边界更清楚：远端状态只能通过消息得知，而消息会丢、慢、重复。
why_en: Shared-nothing makes the failure boundary explicit: remote state is learned only through messages, which can fail.

termDefinitions.meaning: RDMA 允许一台机器直接访问另一台机器内存，用于低延迟专用网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Remote Direct Memory Access lets one machine access another machine’s memory over specialized low-latency networks.

optionExplanations: 无共享架构假设机器之间只能发网络请求，排除了直接读写另一台机器内存或磁盘的能力。
通过 RPC 发消息正是这个假设下机器互相通信的标准方式，不是被排除的能力。
服务经负载均衡接收请求同样是常规的网络通信方式，符合这个假设。
每个节点有自己的本地磁盘正是这类架构的典型特征，不是被排除的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Shared-nothing assumes machines can only communicate through network requests, ruling out the ability of one machine to directly read or write another machine's memory or disk as a shared physical resource.
Machines sending messages by RPC is exactly the standard way of communicating under the shared-nothing assumption, not something it excludes.
Services receiving requests through a load balancer is likewise a normal form of network communication, consistent with shared-nothing.
Nodes each having their own local disk is precisely a typical feature of shared-nothing, not something it excludes.

scenario: 团队声称系统能处理网络分区和长暂停，但从未测试过这些情况。
scenario_en: A team claims the system handles network partitions and long pauses, but has never tested those cases.
q: 应该补什么工程实践？
q_en: What practice should be added?
options: 故障注入和混沌测试验证真实行为
只写一份更长的 README
把所有超时都改成无穷大
关掉监控以减少告警噪声
options_en: Fault injection and chaos testing to see how the protocol really behaves.
Just write a longer README.
Set every timeout to infinity.
Turn monitoring off to cut alert noise.
why: 分布式故障很多只在边界条件出现。主动制造丢包、暂停和分区，才能知道系统真实反应。
why_en: Many distributed failures appear only in edge cases, so inject loss, pauses, and partitions to learn the real behavior.
whenOtherWins: 对极小低风险脚本，人工演练和 runbook 可能足够；核心服务要自动化验证。
tradeoff: 测试复杂度 vs 故障信心
optionExplanations: 很多分布式故障只在边界条件下才暴露出来，主动做故障注入和混沌测试，真正制造丢包、暂停和分区，才能验证协议在这些情况下到底是怎么表现的，而不是停留在声称。
只写更长的 README 不会验证系统的实际行为，纸面描述再详细也不等于系统真的能扛住这些场景。
把所有超时改成无穷大只会让系统在真正故障时永远卡住等待，不是验证行为的办法。
关闭监控只会让团队看不到问题发生，减少的是可见性而不是真实存在的风险。
optionExplanations_en: Many distributed failures only surface under edge conditions, so actively injecting faults and running chaos tests — genuinely causing packet loss, pauses, and partitions — verifies how the protocol actually behaves, instead of relying on claims.
Only writing a longer README doesn't verify actual system behavior; a more detailed document doesn't mean the system can actually withstand these scenarios.
Setting all timeouts to infinity would just leave the system stuck waiting forever during a real failure, not a way to verify behavior.
Turning off monitoring only blinds the team to problems as they happen, reducing visibility rather than the actual underlying risk.

q: 为什么多数派能避免两个互不知情的决定？
q_en: Why does a majority avoid two independent decisions?
text: 在固定节点集合里，任意两个{{多数派 quorum}} 必然有交集；交集节点能携带或拒绝冲突决定。
text_en: In a fixed node set, any two {{majority quorums}} must overlap; the shared node can carry or reject conflicting decisions.
why: 多数派不是为了快，而是为了让决定集合相交。少数派继续写通常要被禁止。
why_en: A majority is not about speed; it is about overlapping decision sets, so minority writes are usually forbidden.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的最小节点集合，常用多数派让两个决定集合相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum set of nodes needed for a decision, often a majority so quorums overlap.

scenario: 一个节点被多数派判死并移出服务，但它自己没崩溃，网络也稍后恢复。
scenario_en: A node is declared dead by the majority and removed from service, but it never crashed and later reconnects.
q: 这个节点最危险的行为是什么？
q_en: What is the most dangerous behavior by that node?
options: 继续按旧身份处理写入
清空本地指标
请求重新加入集群
停止对外服务并同步新状态
options_en: Continue processing writes under its old role
Clear local metrics
Ask to rejoin the cluster
Stop serving and sync new state
why: 被多数派否决的节点如果继续行动，就是旧主复活问题。恢复后必须先确认身份和任期。
why_en: A node rejected by the majority becomes dangerous if it keeps acting under the old role; it must revalidate its term and identity.
optionExplanations: 最危险的是它没意识到自己已经被多数派否决，还继续按旧身份接受写入，跟当前合法的主形成事实上的双主，把冲突数据写进系统。
清空本地指标只是清理监控数据，不会对集群状态或数据一致性造成风险。
请求重新加入集群是恢复后应该做的正确动作，前提是先确认自己被否决过、不能再假装拥有旧身份继续行动。
停止对外服务并同步新状态正是它恢复后应该做的安全行为，不是危险行为。
optionExplanations_en: The most dangerous thing is not realizing it's already been rejected by the majority and continuing to accept writes under its old role, effectively becoming a second leader alongside the current legitimate one and writing conflicting data.
Clearing local metrics is just cleaning up monitoring data and poses no risk to cluster state or data consistency.
Asking to rejoin the cluster is the correct action after recovery, provided it first confirms it was rejected and stops acting under its old assumed role.
Stopping serving and syncing new state is exactly the safe behavior it should take after recovering, not a dangerous one.

q: 第 8 章给系统设计的总提醒是什么？
q_en: What is Chapter 8’s main systems-design warning?
text: 网络可能{{丢、慢、重复、乱序}}；时钟可能{{漂移或跳变}}；进程可能{{暂停}}，所以分布式协议要围绕不确定性设计。
text_en: Networks can be {{lost, slow, duplicated, or reordered}}; clocks can {{drift or jump}}; processes can {{pause}}, so distributed protocols must be designed around uncertainty.
why: 面试里不要把超时、时钟或单个节点的自我判断当事实；要问多数派、幂等和 fencing。
why_en: In interviews, do not treat timeouts, clocks, or one node’s self-belief as truth; ask about quorums, idempotency, and fencing.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的最小节点集合，常用多数派让两个决定集合相交。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the minimum set of nodes needed for a decision, often a majority so quorums overlap.

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token 是单调递增令牌，下游只接受更大的令牌来拒绝旧主。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing token; downstream systems accept only newer tokens to reject stale leaders.

scenario: 用户写入资料后马上从另一个副本读取，可能读到旧值。
scenario_en: A user writes a profile and immediately reads from another replica, possibly seeing the old value.
q: eventual consistency 真正承诺什么？
q_en: What does eventual consistency actually promise?
options: 没有新写入时副本最终会收敛
每次读都能看到最新的写
所有写都按全局顺序提交
网络分区时仍然线性化
options_en: With no new writes, the replicas eventually converge.
Every read sees the latest write.
All writes commit in one global order.
It stays linearizable during a partition.
why: 最终一致只承诺最终收敛，不承诺多久收敛。应用要能处理窗口期的旧读。
why_en: Eventual consistency promises convergence eventually, not a bound on when reads become fresh.
optionExplanations: 最终一致只承诺：只要没有新写入进来、故障也修复了，所有副本迟早会收敛到同一个值，它不承诺具体多久，也不承诺中途读到的是最新值。
每次读都看到最新写正是线性化的定义，比最终一致强得多，最终一致明确不给这个保证。
所有写按全局顺序提交是全序广播或共识层面的保证，跟最终一致是完全不同的概念。
网络分区时仍线性化几乎不可能同时做到，最终一致恰恰是分区时牺牲新鲜度、换取继续可用的那种模型。
optionExplanations_en: Eventual consistency only promises that if no new writes arrive and faults heal, all replicas will eventually converge to the same value — it makes no promise about how long that takes or what a read sees in between.
Every read seeing the latest write is the definition of linearizability, far stronger than eventual consistency, which explicitly doesn't guarantee this.
All writes committing in one global order is a total-order-broadcast or consensus-level guarantee, a different concept from eventual consistency.
Staying linearizable during a partition is nearly impossible to combine with availability; eventual consistency is exactly the model that trades freshness for staying available during a partition.

scenario: 比分服务写入“比赛结束”成功后，所有后续刷新都必须看到最终比分。
