scenario_en: A score service successfully writes “game over,” and every later refresh must show the final score.
q: 需要哪种一致性？
q_en: Which consistency guarantee is needed?
options: 线性化
最终一致
读未提交
批量离线校正
options_en: Linearizability
Eventual consistency
Read uncommitted
Offline batch correction
why: 线性化是新鲜度保证：写成功返回后，后续读不能再看到旧世界。代价通常是读写要经过 leader 或 quorum。
why_en: Linearizability is a recency guarantee: once a write succeeds, later reads cannot see the old value.
whenOtherWins: 如果页面允许几秒延迟，例如点赞数，最终一致更便宜。
tradeoff: 读最新值 vs 延迟/可用性

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

optionExplanations: 写成功返回后，所有后续读都不能再看到旧世界，这正是线性化承诺的新鲜度保证，符合“看到最终比分”这个要求。
最终一致只承诺迟早收敛，不保证写成功后立刻就能被后续读看到，达不到这里“所有后续刷新都必须看到”的要求。
读未提交连提交过的数据都不一定保证读到，比最终一致还弱，更满足不了这里的需求。
批量离线校正是事后修正数据的手段，不是实时保证刷新就能看到最终结果的方式。
optionExplanations_en: Once a write returns success, no later read can see the old world — exactly linearizability's recency guarantee, matching the requirement that every subsequent refresh must see it.
Eventual consistency only promises convergence eventually, not that a read right after a successful write will see it, falling short of every subsequent refresh must see it.
Read uncommitted doesn't even reliably guarantee seeing committed data, weaker than eventual consistency, and even further from meeting this need.
Offline batch correction fixes data after the fact; it's not a way to guarantee a refresh sees the final result in real time.

scenario: Alice 看到最终比分并告诉 Bob；Bob 随后刷新却看到比赛还没结束。
scenario_en: Alice sees the final score and tells Bob; Bob refreshes afterward and sees the game still in progress.
q: 这违反了什么直觉？
q_en: What intuition is violated?
options: Bob 后来的读不该比 Alice 更旧
两个人同时刷新必须完全相同
Bob 的手机必须始终连到同一个副本
最终一致保证毫秒级就收敛
options_en: Bob's later read should not be older than what Alice already saw.
Two simultaneous refreshes must return identical results.
Bob's phone must always stay pinned to the same replica.
Eventual consistency guarantees millisecond convergence.
why: 线性化关心有先后关系的操作：Bob 的刷新发生在听到 Alice 之后，就不该回到更旧状态。
why_en: Linearizability cares about real-time order: Bob’s read happens after Alice observed the write, so it should not go backward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

optionExplanations: Bob 的刷新发生在他听 Alice 说了最终比分之后，按现实世界的先后关系，他这次读理应至少和 Alice 看到的一样新，结果却倒退回了旧状态，违反了这个直觉。
这里两次刷新并不是同时发生的，Bob 是在听说之后才刷新的，不是两个同时的操作需要完全相同这个问题。
Bob 的手机连到哪个副本是实现细节，线性化不要求连同一个副本，它要求的是不管连哪个副本都不能看到过时状态。
这里讨论的是线性化被违反的问题，跟最终一致收敛要花多久没有关系，也不是最终一致该保证毫秒级。
optionExplanations_en: Bob's refresh happens after he heard the final score from Alice, so by real-world ordering his read should be at least as fresh as what Alice saw — but it went backward instead, violating that intuition.
The two refreshes here aren't simultaneous; Bob refreshed after hearing about it, so this isn't about two simultaneous operations needing to be identical.

Which replica Bob's phone connects to is an implementation detail; linearizability doesn't require hitting the same replica, it requires that no replica shows a stale state regardless of which one is hit.
This is about a linearizability violation, unrelated to how long eventual consistency takes to converge, and eventual consistency was never claimed to converge within milliseconds.

scenario: 一个读请求和一个写请求时间窗口重叠。
scenario_en: A read request and a write request overlap in time.
q: 线性化允许这个读返回什么？
q_en: What may the read return under linearizability?
options: 旧值或新值，但不能倒退
只能返回新值
只能返回旧值
可以返回任意第三个值
options_en: Old or new value, but no going backward
Only the new value
Only the old value
Any unrelated third value
why: 并发操作没有确定先后，所以读可落在写前或写后。已经观察到新值后，后续读必须保持不倒退。
why_en: Concurrent operations can be ordered either way, but after the new value is observed, later reads must not go backward.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

tradeoff: 并发弹性 vs 读不倒退

rows: 旧值或新值，但不能倒退
旧值或新值，但不能…场景
旧值或新值，但不能倒退成本
可以返回任意第三个值
可以返回任意第三个值场景
可以返回任意第三个值成本

optionExplanations: 读写时间窗口重叠、没有明确先后关系时，这次读可以合理地返回写之前或写之后的值，但一旦某次读已经观察到了新值，后面的读就不能再倒退回旧值。
并发窗口内只能返回新值太严格了，线性化并不要求并发读一定看到刚好还没提交完成的新值。
只能返回旧值同样太严格，写操作可能已经在这个窗口内生效，读到新值也是允许的。
线性化承诺读到的一定是曾经写入过的某个真实值，不会凭空返回一个无关的第三个值。
optionExplanations_en: When a read and a write overlap in time with no clear ordering, the read can reasonably return either the value before or after the write, but once some read has already observed the new value, later reads must never go back to the old one.
Requiring the read to only return the new value during the overlap is too strict; linearizability doesn't force a concurrent read to see a write that may not have fully taken effect yet.
Requiring it to only return the old value is likewise too strict, since the write may have already taken effect within that window, and seeing the new value is also allowed.
Linearizability guarantees the read returns some real value that was actually written at some point, never an unrelated third value out of nowhere.

scenario: 数据库宣称事务可串行化，但读副本可能返回旧数据。
scenario_en: A database says transactions are serializable, but a read replica may return stale data.
q: 这里混淆了哪两个概念？
q_en: Which two concepts are being confused?
options: 可串行化管事务交错，线性化管读写新鲜度
线性化只管 SQL 语法
可串行化只管磁盘压缩
两者都只不过是最终一致性的另一个别名
options_en: Serializability is about transaction interleavings; linearizability is about recency
Linearizability is only SQL syntax
Serializability is only disk compression
Both are just another name for eventual consistency.
why: 可串行化不自动保证“读最新副本”。需要同时说明事务隔离和副本一致性。
why_en: Serializability does not automatically mean reads are fresh from replicas; isolation and replication consistency are separate.
tradeoff: 事务等价顺序 vs 单对象新鲜度

termDefinitions.meaning: 可串行化保证事务结果等价于某个串行执行顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializability guarantees that transactions produce a result equivalent to some serial order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

optionExplanations: 可串行化管的是并发事务执行顺序看起来像不像串行执行，线性化管的是读到的数据新不新鲜；数据库可串行化并不自动保证读副本读到的是最新数据，这里恰恰混淆了这两个概念。
线性化关心的是读写新鲜度这种语义保证，不是 SQL 语法层面的事，这个说法把它说窄了。
可串行化关心的是事务交错顺序等价性，跟磁盘压缩这种存储层面的话题毫无关系。
两者是完全不同的保证，都不是最终一致的别名，说是别名混淆了三个本该分开的概念。
optionExplanations_en: Serializability is about whether concurrent transaction execution looks equivalent to some serial order, while linearizability is about how fresh the data read is; a database being serializable doesn't automatically guarantee a read replica returns fresh data — that's exactly the confusion here.
Linearizability is concerned with read-write recency semantics, not SQL syntax, so this option undersells it.
Serializability is about transaction interleaving equivalence, completely unrelated to a storage-layer topic like disk compression.
Both are distinct guarantees, neither an alias for eventual consistency — calling them aliases conflates three concepts that should be kept separate.

scenario: 集群用分布式锁保证同一时刻只有一个 leader 能写主库。
scenario_en: A cluster uses a distributed lock so only one leader can write the primary store at a time.
q: 锁服务必须提供什么？
q_en: What must the lock service provide?
options: 线性化的加锁/续约操作
最终一致的缓存读
客户端本地互斥锁
只按 wall-clock 排序
options_en: Linearizable lock and renewal operations
Eventually consistent cached reads
A client-local mutex
Ordering only by wall-clock time
why: 选主锁必须让所有节点同意同一个持有者。否则两个节点可能都以为自己拿到锁。
why_en: A leader-election lock must make all nodes agree on one holder; otherwise two nodes can both think they hold it.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单进程内保护内存结构，本地互斥锁就足够。
tradeoff: 全局唯一持有者 vs 协调成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

optionExplanations: 所有节点必须就同一时刻只有一个持有者达成一致，加锁和续约操作必须是线性化的，不然两个节点可能各自认为自己拿到了锁，同时以 leader 身份写主库。
最终一致的缓存读可能让不同节点在不同时间看到不同的锁状态，很容易出现两个节点都以为自己持锁的情况。
客户端本地互斥锁只能约束同一个进程内部的并发，管不住跨机器、跨节点谁该是 leader 这个问题。
只按 wall-clock 排序没有一致性保证，不同机器的时钟本身就可能有偏差，选不出唯一确定的持有者。
optionExplanations_en: All nodes must agree on exactly one holder at any moment, so the lock and renewal operations must be linearizable, otherwise two nodes could each believe they hold the lock and both write as leader.
Eventually consistent cached reads can let different nodes see different lock states at different times, easily letting two nodes both think they hold the lock.
A client-local mutex only constrains concurrency within one process, powerless to decide who should be leader across machines.
Ordering only by wall-clock time offers no consistency guarantee, since different machines' clocks can themselves be skewed, failing to elect one definite holder.

scenario: 用户名注册要求全局唯一，两个请求不能同时抢到同名。
scenario_en: Username registration requires global uniqueness; two requests must not both claim the same name.
q: 需要把冲突放在哪里解决？
q_en: Where should the conflict be resolved?
options: 线性化提交路径或唯一约束
异步更新的搜索引擎索引
浏览器本地缓存
每日离线报表
options_en: A linearizable commit path or uniqueness constraint
An asynchronously updated search index.
Browser local cache
A daily offline report
why: 唯一性是提交时不变量，不能靠可能陈旧的读路径判断。提交路径要原子地检查并占用名字。
why_en: Uniqueness is a commit-time invariant, so the check-and-claim must be atomic on the write path.
whenOtherWins: 如果重复名字只是展示问题，异步检测和改名流程会更便宜。
tradeoff: 提交时唯一性 vs 异步修复

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

optionExplanations: 用户名唯一是提交时刻要守住的不变量，线性化的提交路径或唯一约束能把检查和占用名字合成原子的一步，两个同名请求里只有一个能真正抢到。
异步搜索索引本身就可能落后，用它判断名字有没有被占用会读到过时结果，防不住两个请求同时都以为名字可用。
浏览器本地缓存只在客户端本地有效，完全看不到别的用户此刻正在尝试注册的同一个名字。
每日离线报表只是事后统计，等它跑出来的时候两个人可能早就都注册成功了，来不及阻止冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Uniqueness is an invariant that must hold at commit time, and a linearizable commit path or uniqueness constraint fuses the check and the claim into one atomic step, so of two same-name requests only one can actually win.
An asynchronous search index can itself lag behind, so checking it for whether a name is taken can return a stale answer, failing to stop two requests from both thinking the name is free.
Browser-local cache only exists on that one client and has no visibility into another user attempting the same name right now.
A daily offline report is just an after-the-fact tally; by the time it runs, both people may already have registered successfully, too late to prevent the conflict.

scenario: ATM 显示余额后马上允许取款，不能基于过期余额超取。
scenario_en: An ATM shows a balance and immediately allows withdrawal; it must not overdraw based on stale balance.
q: 读余额应走哪条路径？
q_en: Which read path fits?
options: leader/quorum 读
从任意一个异步的副本直接读
CDN 缓存读
日志批处理结果
options_en: Read from leader or quorum
Read directly from any asynchronous replica.
A CDN cached read
A batch log result
why: 余额读会影响资金决策，所以不能接受复制滞后的旧值。最好把检查和扣款放进同一提交路径。
why_en: A balance read drives a money decision, so it cannot rely on a lagging replica; put check and debit on the same commit path.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是展示历史余额，带时间戳的陈旧读可能可接受。
tradeoff: 资金正确性 vs 读延迟
optionExplanations: 取款是资金决策，读余额必须走 leader 或凑够多数派的路径，最好把检查余额和实际扣款放在同一条提交路径里，才不会基于一个已经落后的旧值批准取款。
任意异步副本读到的余额可能已经落后于主库，用它决定能不能取款，正是导致超取的直接原因。
CDN 缓存读同样可能是过时数据，缓存本身就是为了降低延迟牺牲一部分新鲜度，不适合用来做资金决策。
日志批处理结果是事后汇总的产物，等它跑出来的时候取款可能早就已经完成了，来不及挡住超取。
optionExplanations_en: A withdrawal is a money decision, so the balance read must go through the leader or a quorum, and ideally the check and the actual debit sit on the same commit path, so the decision is never based on an already-stale value.
A balance read from any asynchronous replica can already be behind the primary, and using it to decide whether a withdrawal is allowed is exactly what causes overdrawing.
A CDN-cached read is also potentially stale — caching exists precisely to trade freshness for lower latency, unsuitable for a money decision.
A batch log result is an after-the-fact summary; by the time it's produced, the withdrawal may have already completed, too late to stop an overdraw.

scenario: 单主复制系统中，所有写到 leader。
scenario_en: In a single-leader replicated system, all writes go to the leader.
q: 什么时候可能线性化？
q_en: When can it be linearizable?
options: 读也走已确认的 leader 或同步副本
读总是从任意异步 follower 读取
允许两个 leader 同时接受写
leader 身份永远不需要确认
options_en: Reads also go to a confirmed leader or a synchronous follower.
Reads always go to any asynchronous follower.
Two leaders are allowed to accept writes at once.
Leadership never has to be confirmed.
why: 单主有潜力提供线性化，但前提是读路径不绕到落后副本，且 leader 身份没有 split brain。
why_en: Single-leader replication can be linearizable only if reads avoid stale followers and leadership is not split.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

tradeoff: 读最新副本 vs 读扩展

rows: 读也从确认的 leader 或同步…
必须保护最新读或不变量时
读总是从任意异步 follower…
能接受短暂滞后、想降延迟时
允许两个 leader 同时写
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
leader 身份永不需要确认
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适

optionExplanations: 所有写都到 leader 只是前提，读也要从确认的 leader 或者已经同步更新的 follower 读取，避免绕到落后副本，这样才有可能实现线性化。
读总是从任意异步 follower 读取，恰恰会读到可能落后于 leader 的旧数据，破坏了线性化要求的新鲜度。
允许两个 leader 同时写会直接产生冲突历史，跟“单主”这个前提本身就矛盾，更谈不上线性化。
leader 身份如果从不需要确认，就可能出现旧 leader 和新 leader 同时自认为合法的情况，也就是 split brain，破坏线性化。
optionExplanations_en: All writes going to the leader is just the premise; reads also need to come from the confirmed leader or synchronously updated followers, avoiding stale replicas, before linearizability is even possible.
Reads always going to any asynchronous follower risks returning data that's stale relative to the leader, breaking the recency linearizability requires.
Allowing two leaders to write concurrently directly produces conflicting histories, contradicting the single-leader premise itself, let alone linearizability.
If leader identity never needs confirmation, an old leader and a new leader could both believe they're legitimate at once — split brain — breaking linearizability.

scenario: 多主数据库允许两个地区在断网时都接受写入。
scenario_en: A multi-leader database lets two regions accept writes while disconnected.
q: 它通常牺牲什么？
q_en: What does it usually sacrifice?
options: 线性化的新鲜单副本语义
更好的本地写入可用性
低写延迟
地理容灾
options_en: Linearizable single-copy recency
Better local write availability.
Low local write latency
Geographic resilience
why: 多主保住本地可用性，但断网时没有一个全局单副本顺序。冲突要靠合并或业务规则处理。
why_en: Multi-leader replication preserves local write availability, but during disconnection there is no single global recency order.
tradeoff: 本地可用性 vs 单副本新鲜度

rows: 线性化的新鲜单副本语义
必须保护最新读或不变量时
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适

optionExplanations: 多主允许断网时两地各自继续接写，但这意味着不存在一条大家公认的单一最新副本顺序，牺牲的正是线性化承诺的这种新鲜单副本语义。
本地写可用性恰恰是多主想要保住的东西，不是它牺牲掉的部分。
低写延迟同样是多主想要争取的收益，不是代价。
地理容灾也是多主设计追求的目标之一，不是它放弃的东西。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-leader lets both regions keep accepting local writes during a disconnection, but that means there's no single agreed-upon latest-copy order — exactly the linearizable single-copy recency it gives up.
Local write availability is precisely what multi-leader is trying to preserve, not what it sacrifices.
Low local write latency is likewise a benefit multi-leader is chasing, not a cost.
Geographic resilience is also one of the goals multi-leader design pursues, not something it gives up.

scenario: Dynamo 风格读写使用多数派 quorum。
scenario_en: A Dynamo-style system uses majority quorums for reads and writes.
q: 为什么仍不能默认线性化？
q_en: Why is it not automatically linearizable?
options: 读修复和并发写细节可能仍让读看到旧值
多数派一定等于最新单副本
它不允许任何故障
quorum 交集只用于做磁盘压缩
options_en: Read repair and concurrent-write details may still allow stale reads
A majority always equals a latest single copy
It allows no failures
Quorum intersection is only for disk compaction.
why: quorum 交集是必要但不总是充分。要线性化还需处理读写并发、版本和读修复顺序。

The data model cannot be partitioned

why_en: Linearizability often puts coordination on the foreground path; cross-continent RTT is a physical-distance cost.
optionExplanations: 跨洲部署里，线性化的写和读都要真的跨海去联系 leader 所在的地区，这段长距离往返延迟会实实在在地进入用户请求路径，是物理距离带来的代价，调不掉。

optionExplanations_en: In a cross-continent deployment, linearizable writes and reads genuinely have to reach across the ocean to the leader's region, and that long round trip enters the user request path for real — a physical-distance cost that can't be tuned away.
How many indexes to build is unrelated to whether cross-continent RTT is paid, and doesn't double just because of linearizability.

What language the server is written in has nothing to do with the physical-distance latency cost being discussed here.

scenario: 库存详情页只展示大概剩余量，允许几秒旧；下单提交必须防超卖。

options_en: Display reads can be eventually consistent; the commit path needs a strong constraint.
Send both page reads and commits to any replica.
Move every read and write into offline batch jobs.
Let the commit path trust the CDN cache.
why: 不是每条路径都要最强一致性。把强保证放在保护不变量的提交路径，展示路径可换取速度。
why_en: Not every path needs the strongest consistency; put strong guarantees on invariant-protecting commits and keep display reads cheaper.
whenOtherWins: 如果展示数字本身会触发监管或资金动作，也要提高读路径保证。
tradeoff: 用户体验速度 vs 提交正确性
optionExplanations: 库存详情页只是展示，允许旧几秒完全没问题，可以走最终一致；但下单提交要防超卖，这条路径必须用强约束或者线性化，把强保证只放在真正需要它的地方。
页面读和提交都走任意副本，会让下单提交也可能基于过时库存做决定，防不住超卖。

Having both page reads and checkout hit any replica risks checkout deciding based on stale inventory, failing to prevent overselling.
Turning all reads and writes into offline batch jobs would make an operation like checkout, which needs immediate feedback, unworkable.
Checkout trusting only the CDN means the purchase decision is based on cached content, the opposite of the core requirement that checkout must prevent overselling.

There's an explicit read-then-happens dependency between A and C, not an independent concurrent pair of events.
C depends on having read A's write to happen at all, so C can't possibly be physically earlier than A — this directly contradicts the scenario.

A Lamport timestamp is a logical counter, not a measurement of real physical time, and makes no claim to perfect accuracy.

Compressed document size is a file attribute, unrelated to determining the causal relationship between two edits.

why: 全序广播给复制状态机同一条输入日志。每个副本按同顺序执行确定性操作，就能得到同状态。
why_en: Total order broadcast gives replicas the same input log, so deterministic execution keeps state equal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全序广播保证所有节点以同一顺序投递同一批消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Total order broadcast makes all nodes deliver the same messages in the same order.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[clients] --> L[ordered log]
  L --> A[replica A]
  L --> B[replica B]
  L --> D[replica C]
optionExplanations: 全序广播承诺的是：只要节点是正确运行的，它们看到的消息内容和顺序都完全一致，这才让每个副本按同样的输入执行确定性操作、得到同样的状态。
全序广播不承诺任何具体的到达时间上界，只承诺顺序一致，不是延迟保证。
全序广播只保证消息的传递顺序一致，不理解也不会自动合并消息内容本身的语义冲突。
全序广播是投递通道的性质，跟读请求要不要经过 leader 是两个不同层面的设计决定。
optionExplanations_en: Total order broadcast guarantees that as long as nodes are correct, they see the exact same messages in the exact same order — that's what lets every replica execute deterministic operations on the same input and reach the same state.
Total order broadcast makes no promise about any specific delivery time bound; it only guarantees consistent ordering, not a latency guarantee.
Total order broadcast only guarantees consistent delivery order; it doesn't understand or automatically merge semantic conflicts in the message content itself.
Total order broadcast is a property of the delivery channel, a different design decision from whether reads go through a leader.

scenario: 系统已经能对一个值达成共识。
scenario_en: A system can already reach consensus on one value.
q: 怎样得到全序广播？
q_en: How can it obtain total order broadcast?
options: 对日志的每个位置重复运行共识
让每个节点按本地接收顺序投递
用 wall-clock 排序所有消息
把消息随机打散
options_en: Run consensus repeatedly for each log position
Deliver messages in each node’s local receive order
Sort all messages by wall-clock time
Randomly shuffle messages
why: 一次共识决定一个槽位，重复共识形成有序日志。实际系统会优化成 leader 连续追加。
why_en: One consensus instance decides one log slot; repeated consensus forms an ordered log.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全序广播保证所有节点以同一顺序投递同一批消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Total order broadcast makes all nodes deliver the same messages in the same order.

tradeoff: 单槽共识 vs 连续日志优化

rows: 对日志的每个位置重复运行共识
高随机写吞吐更重要时
让每个节点按本地接收顺序投递
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
让每个节点按本地接收顺…成本
范围查询和稳定读延迟更重要时
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适

optionExplanations: 给日志的每一个位置分别跑一轮共识，就能确定这个位置该放哪条消息，把这些位置连起来就是一条大家公认顺序一致的全序日志。
让每个节点按自己本地接收到消息的先后顺序去投递，不同节点收到消息的先后本来就可能不一样，拼不出统一的全序。
用 wall-clock 给消息排序会受时钟偏差影响，不同机器的时钟本来就不完全同步，排不出可信的全序。
把消息随机打散跟“得到一致顺序”这个目标背道而驰，完全没有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Running one round of consensus for each position in the log decides which message goes there, and chaining these positions together forms a total-order log everyone agrees on.
Letting each node deliver messages in its own local arrival order fails because different nodes can receive the same messages in different orders, unable to produce a unified total order.
Sorting messages by wall-clock time is subject to clock skew, since different machines' clocks aren't perfectly synchronized, making the resulting order unreliable.
Randomly shuffling messages works directly against the goal of a consistent order, entirely pointless here.

scenario: 锁服务每次授予锁时都返回递增序号。
scenario_en: A lock service returns an increasing sequence number every time it grants a lock.
q: 这个序号应该怎么用？
q_en: How should the sequence number be used?
options: 作为 fencing token
只用于日志美化
只发给客户端但资源端从不检查
当作随机会话 ID
options_en: Use it as a fencing token
Use it only for prettier logs
Sent to the client but never checked by the resource.
Treat it as a random session ID
why: 全序服务给的递增号能挡旧主复活，但前提是共享资源也检查它。只发不验没有意义。
why_en: An increasing number from an ordered service can fence old leaders, but only if the shared resource checks it.
whenOtherWins: 如果资源天然由锁服务代理所有写入，外部 fencing 检查可能不需要。
tradeoff: 外部资源安全 vs 接口侵入

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token 是单调递增令牌，资源端用它拒绝旧 leader 的写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing token that lets a resource reject writes from an old leader.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全序广播保证所有节点以同一顺序投递同一批消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Total order broadcast makes all nodes deliver the same messages in the same order.

optionExplanations: 这个递增序号应该当作 fencing token 发给共享资源，让资源端只接受比它见过的最大 token 更大的写入，从而挡住旧持有者暂停后复活带来的写入。
只用于日志美化浪费了这个序号本该有的实际保护作用，它是能真正拦住旧主写入的机制，不只是好看。
发给客户端但资源端不检查，等于这个序号没有起到任何拦截作用，跟没有一样。
当作随机会话 ID 使用会丢掉它递增、可比较大小这个关键性质，fencing 恰恰依赖这个性质。
optionExplanations_en: This increasing number should be given to the shared resource as a fencing token, so the resource only accepts writes carrying a token larger than any it's already seen, blocking a revived old holder's stale writes.
Using it only for prettier logs wastes the real protective role this number could play — it's a mechanism that can actually block an old leader's writes, not just decoration.
Handing it to clients without the resource checking it means the number provides no protection at all, effectively the same as not having it.
Treating it as a random session ID throws away the crucial property of being increasing and comparable, which fencing depends on.

scenario: 一次事务要同时更新用户库和库存库；不能一个提交另一个回滚。
scenario_en: A transaction updates a user database and an inventory database; one must not commit while the other aborts.
q: 这是什么问题？
q_en: What problem is this?
options: 原子提交
线性化读
因果广播
缓存失效
options_en: Atomic commit
Linearizable reads
Causal broadcast
Cache invalidation
why: 原子提交要求所有参与者对提交或放弃达成同一决定。2PC 是经典但有阻塞风险的方案。
why_en: Atomic commit requires all participants to make the same commit-or-abort decision; 2PC is classic but can block.
whenOtherWins: 如果能改成单库事务加 outbox，通常比跨库原子提交更简单。
tradeoff: 跨资源原子性 vs 可用性/复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

optionExplanations: 一次事务要同时改动用户库和库存库这两个不同的资源，不能一个提交一个回滚，这正是原子提交问题——要求所有参与者对提交或放弃做出同一个决定。
线性化读关心的是读到的数据够不够新鲜，不是跨多个资源要不要同一个提交决定的问题。
因果广播关心的是消息之间的因果顺序，跟跨资源提交要不要一致没有关系。
缓存失效解决的是缓存和数据源不同步的问题，跟这里描述的跨库原子性问题不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: A transaction that must change both the user database and the inventory database at once, with neither one allowed to commit while the other rolls back, is exactly the atomic commit problem — requiring all participants to reach the same commit-or-abort decision.
Linearizable reads are about how fresh the data read is, not about whether multiple resources need one shared commit decision.
Causal broadcast is about causal ordering between messages, unrelated to whether a cross-resource commit needs to be unanimous.
Cache invalidation addresses cache-versus-source staleness, a different problem from the cross-database atomicity described here.

scenario: 协调者要在三个参与者之间执行 2PC。
scenario_en: A coordinator runs 2PC across three participants.
q: 把正常路径排好序。
q_en: Order the normal 2PC path.
steps: 协调者写 commit 决定并通知参与者
参与者进入 prepared 并回复 yes
协调者发送 prepare 请求
参与者提交并释放锁
why: 2PC 的关键断点是 prepared：参与者已承诺听协调者最终决定。之后协调者日志决定恢复结果。
why_en: The key point in 2PC is prepared state: participants promise to follow the coordinator’s final logged decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Coordinator
  participant P as Participants
  C->>P: prepare?
  P-->>C: yes, prepared
  C->>C: log commit
  C->>P: commit

scenario: 参与者在 2PC 中回复 yes 后，协调者暂时失联。
scenario_en: A participant votes yes in 2PC, then the coordinator becomes unreachable.
q: 参与者为什么不能自己放弃？
q_en: Why can’t the participant unilaterally abort?
options: 它已承诺服从协调者，自作主张会分裂
投出的 yes 票只是一条日志注释
参与者没有任何本地状态
网络会自动通知所有人结果
options_en: It already promised to follow the coordinator, so deciding alone would split the outcome.
The yes vote is just a log comment.
Participants hold no local state.
The network tells everyone the outcome automatically.
why: prepared 参与者既不能忘记事务，也不能随便提交或回滚。协调者失联会让资源被锁住。
why_en: A prepared participant cannot forget, commit, or abort on its own, so coordinator failure can hold resources locked.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

optionExplanations: 参与者投了 yes 就等于承诺服从协调者最终的决定，如果它自己擅自决定提交或回滚，可能跟其它参与者的选择不一致，让原本该原子的事务分裂成不一致的结果。
yes 票是一个正式的承诺，参与者要为此持久化状态、持锁等待，不只是一条无关紧要的日志注释。
参与者恰恰要保留自己 prepared 状态这份本地记录，直到收到最终决定才能释放，不是没有任何本地状态。
网络不会替协调者主动通知所有参与者最终决定，协调者失联时这条通道本身也断了。
optionExplanations_en: Voting yes is a commitment to follow whatever the coordinator finally decides; if the participant unilaterally commits or aborts on its own, it can disagree with what other participants chose, splitting an otherwise atomic transaction into inconsistent outcomes.
A yes vote is a real commitment the participant persists state and holds locks for, not just an inconsequential log comment.
The participant specifically has to keep its prepared-state record locally until the final decision arrives — it's not without any local state.
The network doesn't proactively inform every participant of the final decision on the coordinator's behalf; that channel is exactly what's down when the coordinator is unreachable.

scenario: 2PC 协调者在记录 commit 后崩溃，部分参与者没收到决定。
scenario_en: A 2PC coordinator crashes after logging commit, and some participants did not receive the decision.
q: 系统会怎样恢复？
q_en: How does the system recover?
options: 读日志并重发 commit
参与者立即全部 abort
少数派参与者投票覆盖决定
客户端用读副本猜结果
options_en: Read the log and resend commit
Participants immediately abort
A minority of participants overrides the decision
The client guesses from a read replica
why: 协调者日志是最终决定的来源，但协调者不可用时 prepared 参与者只能等待。阻塞是 2PC 的核心代价。
why_en: The coordinator log is the source of the final decision, but prepared participants may block while it is unavailable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

optionExplanations: 协调者把 commit 决定写进了持久日志，恢复后可以从日志里读出这个决定并重新发给还没收到的参与者，让他们完成提交。
参与者已经投了 yes、处于 prepared 状态，不能擅自全部 abort，那样可能跟协调者已经记录的 commit 决定不一致。
少数派参与者没有权力覆盖协调者已经持久化的决定，那样会破坏原子提交要求的统一结果。
客户端猜结果没有确定性保证，跟这里问的“系统会怎样恢复”这个正式恢复流程不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: The coordinator persisted the commit decision to its log, so on recovery it can read that decision back out and resend it to any participants that never got it, letting them finish committing.
Participants that already voted yes and are in the prepared state can't unilaterally abort, since that could conflict with the commit decision the coordinator already recorded.
A minority of participants has no authority to override a decision the coordinator already persisted, which would break the unified outcome atomic commit requires.
A client guessing the result offers no certainty and isn't the same as the formal recovery process the question is asking about.

scenario: 2PC 协调者准备告诉参与者 commit。
scenario_en: A 2PC coordinator is about to tell participants to commit.
q: 它为什么必须先持久化决定？
q_en: Why must it persist the decision first?
options: 崩溃后恢复决定
为了让网络更快
为了删除参与者日志
为了避免所有锁
options_en: Recover the decision after crash
To make the network faster
To delete participant logs
To avoid all locks
why: 如果决定只在内存里，协调者崩溃后就无法回答 prepared 参与者。持久日志让决定可恢复。
why_en: If the decision lived only in memory, a crash would leave prepared participants stuck without an answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

optionExplanations: 如果决定只存在协调者的内存里，一旦协调者崩溃重启，这个决定就彻底没了，prepared 状态的参与者会永远等不到答案；先持久化决定，崩溃后才能从日志里恢复它。
持久化决定这个动作本身跟网络快慢没有关系，它解决的是崩溃后能不能找回决定这个问题。
持久化协调者自己的决定日志，跟要不要删除参与者日志是两回事，参与者有自己独立的日志管理。
持久化决定不会让锁消失，prepared 参与者在收到决定之前照样要持锁等待。
optionExplanations_en: If the decision only lived in memory, a coordinator crash and restart would wipe it out entirely, leaving prepared participants stuck forever with no answer; persisting the decision first is what lets it be recovered from the log after a crash.
Persisting the decision has nothing to do with network speed; it addresses whether the decision can be recovered after a crash.
Persisting the coordinator's own decision log is unrelated to whether participant logs should be deleted — participants manage their own logs independently.
Persisting the decision doesn't make locks disappear; prepared participants still hold their locks until they receive the decision.

scenario: 单数据库事务只有一个参与者；跨两个数据库事务有两个参与者。
scenario_en: A single-database transaction has one participant; a cross-database transaction has two participants.
q: 为什么单参与者不需要 2PC？
q_en: Why does one participant not need 2PC?
options: 没有跨参与者决定，本地日志就够
单参与者不能回滚事务
单参与者没有崩溃风险
2PC 协议只能用在缓存系统上
options_en: There is no cross-participant decision, so the local commit log is enough.
A single participant cannot roll back.
A single participant cannot crash.
2PC can only be used on caches.
why: 2PC 是为“多个资源必须同一决定”付出的协调成本。只有一个资源时，本地事务日志已足够。
why_en: 2PC pays coordination cost for multiple resources sharing one decision; one resource only needs its local transaction log.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

tradeoff: 本地提交简单性 vs 跨资源一致决定

rows: 没有跨参与者一致决定，只需本地提交…
高随机写吞吐更重要时
没有跨参与者一致决定，…成本
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
单参与者不能回滚成本
单参与者没有崩溃风险
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
单参与者没有崩溃风险成本
能接受短暂滞后、想降延迟时

optionExplanations: 只有一个资源参与时，根本不存在“多个参与者要达成同一决定”这个问题，本地那一份事务日志自己就够用了，用不上跨参与者协调的 2PC。
单参与者事务照样能回滚，回滚能力是本地事务日志自带的能力，跟要不要 2PC 无关。
单参与者一样会崩溃，只是崩溃恢复只涉及它自己的本地日志，不需要协调别的参与者。
2PC 是通用的跨资源原子提交协议，能用在数据库和消息队列等各种资源上，不是只能用于缓存。
optionExplanations_en: With only one resource involved, there's no multiple-participants-must-agree problem at all — the local transaction log alone is sufficient, with no need for cross-participant coordination like 2PC.
A single-participant transaction can absolutely roll back; that's a capability of the local transaction log itself, unrelated to whether 2PC is used.
A single participant can still crash; recovery just involves only its own local log, with no need to coordinate other participants.
2PC is a general cross-resource atomic-commit protocol usable across databases, message queues, and other resources, not something limited to caches.

scenario: 服务把数据库和消息队列纳入 XA 分布式事务。
scenario_en: A service includes a database and message queue in an XA distributed transaction.
q: 主要运维风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main operational risk?
options: in-doubt 事务和锁等待
所有消息自动 exactly-once
网络分区时仍总是可用
不再需要监控
options_en: In-doubt transactions and held locks
All messages become exactly-once automatically
The system remains always available during partitions
Monitoring is no longer needed
why: XA 给跨资源原子性，但会把故障恢复和阻塞带到生产运维。很多系统宁可用 outbox。
why_en: XA gives cross-resource atomicity, but it brings blocking and recovery complexity into operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: XA 是跨资源管理器做分布式事务的一类标准接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XA is a standard interface family for distributed transactions across resource managers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

optionExplanations: 协调者失联时，prepared 的资源会一直卡在“不知道该提交还是回滚”的 in-doubt 状态，锁被一直持有，这份阻塞和恢复复杂度会实实在在地压在生产运维上。
XA 提供的是原子性协调，不会自动让每条消息都变成 exactly-once，去重和幂等仍要额外设计。
XA 恰恰在网络分区时更容易出现阻塞，not 总是可用，跟这个说法正相反。
XA 事务的 in-doubt 状态和阻塞风险需要持续监控和运维介入，不是可以不管的东西。
optionExplanations_en: When the coordinator is unreachable, prepared resources sit stuck in an in-doubt state, not knowing whether to commit or abort, holding locks the whole time — that blocking and recovery complexity lands squarely on production operations.
XA provides atomic coordination; it doesn't automatically turn every message into exactly-once, deduplication and idempotency still need separate design.
XA is actually more prone to blocking during a network partition, not always available, the opposite of this claim.
An XA transaction's in-doubt state and blocking risk require ongoing monitoring and operational intervention, not something that can be ignored.

scenario: 订单服务想同时写本地订单库和 Kafka 消息。
scenario_en: An order service wants to write a local order database and a Kafka message together.
q: 常见替代 2PC 的设计是什么？
q_en: What is a common alternative to 2PC?
options: 本地事务同时写 order 和 outbox
直接跨 DB 和 Kafka 做 XA 事务
先发 Kafka 再写库，且不重试
只把消息放进进程内队列
options_en: Write the order and an outbox row in one local transaction, then publish asynchronously.
Run an XA transaction across the DB and Kafka.
Publish to Kafka first, write the DB after, and never retry.
Keep the message in an in-process queue only.
why: outbox 把原子边界缩回单数据库，后台发布可重试。代价是消费者要处理重复消息。
why_en: The outbox pattern shrinks the atomic boundary to one database and makes publishing retryable, at the cost of duplicate handling.
whenOtherWins: 如果组织已有成熟事务协调器并能接受阻塞，2PC 可以更直接。
tradeoff: 本地原子性+幂等 vs 跨资源阻塞

termDefinitions.meaning: outbox 是和业务数据同库提交的待发布消息表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An outbox is a table of messages committed in the same database transaction as business data.

optionExplanations: 把订单和一条待发送的消息作为 outbox 记录，一起写进同一个本地数据库事务，之后再由一个独立的进程异步把它发布到 Kafka，重试也很自然，这就把原子边界收回到一个数据库内。
直接跨 DB 和 Kafka 做 XA 会把跨资源的阻塞和恢复复杂度带进生产环境，正是 outbox 想要绕开的问题。
先发 Kafka 再写库且不重试，一旦写库失败，消息已经发出去了，会造成消息和订单不一致，且没有重试兜底。
只把消息存在进程内队列，进程重启或崩溃时队列内容就没了，消息可能永久丢失。
optionExplanations_en: Writing the order and an outbox row for the pending message in the same local database transaction, then having a separate process publish it asynchronously and retryably, shrinks the atomic boundary back to one database.
Doing XA directly across the database and Kafka brings the blocking and recovery complexity of cross-resource coordination into production, exactly what the outbox pattern is meant to avoid.
Publishing to Kafka first and writing the database later with no retry risks the message going out while the database write fails, leaving the message and order inconsistent with no safety net.
Storing the message only in process memory means it's lost the moment the process restarts or crashes, risking permanent loss.

scenario: 一个共识算法要在若干节点提议值时决定一个值。
scenario_en: A consensus algorithm chooses one value among proposals from several nodes.
q: 哪些是核心性质？
q_en: Which are core properties?
options: 所有正确节点决定同一个值
决定值必须来自某个提议
一个节点不能决定两次
如果多数派可用，最终应能决定
options_en: All correct nodes decide the same value
The decided value must come from a proposal
A node must not decide twice
If a majority is available, it should eventually decide
why: agreement、validity、integrity 和 termination 一起定义了共识想解决的问题。实际系统常在故障模型内保证它们。
why_en: Agreement, validity, integrity, and termination together define what consensus is trying to provide.
optionExplanations: 所有正确节点决定同一个值是共识最核心的一致性要求（agreement），没有它共识就没有意义。
决定值必须来自某个提议是有效性要求（validity），保证结果不是凭空捏造出来的。
一个节点不能决定两次是完整性要求（integrity），保证决定一旦做出就不会反悔或改变。
如果多数派可用，最终应能决定是终止性要求（termination），保证算法不会永远卡住不给出结果。
optionExplanations_en: All correct nodes deciding the same value is consensus's core agreement requirement, without which consensus would be meaningless.
The decided value must come from a proposal is the validity requirement, ensuring the outcome isn't fabricated out of nowhere.
A node must not decide twice is the integrity requirement, ensuring a decision once made never flip-flops or changes.
If a majority is available, it should eventually decide is the termination requirement, ensuring the algorithm doesn't stall forever without producing a result.

scenario: 有人说 FLP 证明“共识永远不可能”。
scenario_en: Someone says FLP proves consensus is never possible.
q: 更准确的理解是什么？
q_en: What is the more accurate reading?
options: 异步且可能崩溃时不保证终止
任何真实系统都不可能选主
多数派投票其实没有意义
物理时钟可以完美解决全部问题
options_en: In a fully asynchronous, crash-prone model, no deterministic algorithm is guaranteed to terminate.
No real system can ever elect a leader.
Majority voting is pointless.
Physical clocks solve the whole problem perfectly.
why: FLP 限制的是模型内的必然终止。工程系统通过超时、随机化或部分同步假设在实践中取得进展。
why_en: FLP limits guaranteed termination in a model; practical systems make progress using timeouts, randomness, or partial synchrony.

termDefinitions.fullName: Fischer, Lynch, and Paterson impossibility result
termDefinitions.meaning: FLP 结果说明在完全异步且可能崩溃的模型里，确定性共识无法保证终止。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The FLP result says deterministic consensus cannot guarantee termination in a fully asynchronous model with possible crashes.

tradeoff: 理论终止限制 vs 工程进展假设

rows: 完全异步且可能崩溃时，确定性算法不…
能接受短暂滞后、想降延迟时
任何真实系统都不能选主
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
任何真实系统都不能选主成本
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
多数派投票没有意义成本
物理时钟可以完美解决全部问题
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
物理时钟可以完美解决全…成本

optionExplanations: FLP 限制的是一个特定模型：完全异步、节点可能崩溃的情况下，确定性算法不能保证一定会终止；这是模型内的理论限制，不是说现实系统一定选不出主。
真实系统靠超时、随机化或部分同步假设这些工程手段在实践中绕开了这个理论限制，说任何真实系统都不能选主是过度引申。
多数派投票依然是共识算法的核心机制，FLP 限制的是终止性，不是说投票本身没有意义。
物理时钟不能完美解决所有分布式一致性问题，这个说法跟 FLP 讨论的内容完全不相干。
optionExplanations_en: FLP limits one specific model: in a fully asynchronous, crash-prone setting, deterministic algorithms can't guarantee termination — a theoretical limit within that model, not proof that real systems can never elect a leader.

Real systems sidestep this theoretical limit in practice using engineering tools like timeouts, randomization, or partial-synchrony assumptions, so claiming no real system can elect a leader overextends the result.
Majority voting is still the core mechanism of consensus algorithms; FLP limits termination, not the meaningfulness of voting itself.
Physical clocks perfectly solving everything has nothing to do with what FLP is actually about.

scenario: 五节点共识组中两个节点宕机。
scenario_en: In a five-node consensus group, two nodes are down.
q: 为什么还能决定新日志项？
q_en: Why can it still decide a new log entry?
options: 剩下三个节点构成多数派 quorum
任意一个单独的节点都可以自行决定
宕机节点会自动投 yes
不需要持久日志
options_en: The remaining three nodes form a majority quorum
Any single node can decide on its own.
Crashed nodes automatically vote yes
No durable log is needed
why: 共识通常只需要多数派，而不是所有节点都同意。多数派交集保证新旧决定不会互相冲突。
why_en: Consensus usually needs a majority, not every node; quorum overlap prevents conflicting decisions.
whenOtherWins: 如果只剩两个节点，五节点组失去多数派，系统应停住而不是做错。
tradeoff: 容忍少数故障 vs 多数派不可用阻塞

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

optionExplanations: 五节点里的多数派是三个，两个节点宕机后剩下的三个节点刚好凑够一个多数派 quorum，仍然能就新日志项达成一致。
共识不允许任意一个节点单独决定，那样会失去 agreement 保证，谁都可能各自决定出不同的值。
宕机节点不会自动投任何票，它们是不可用的，票数只能靠还在线的节点凑。
共识需要持久日志来记录已经做出的决定，才能在节点重启后正确恢复，不是不需要日志。
optionExplanations_en: With five nodes, a majority is three, and after two nodes go down, the remaining three exactly form a majority quorum, still able to agree on a new log entry.
Consensus doesn't let any single node decide alone — that would break the agreement guarantee, letting different nodes potentially settle on different values.
Crashed nodes don't automatically vote for anything; they're simply unavailable, and the vote count can only come from nodes still online.
Consensus needs a durable log to record decisions already made, so nodes can correctly recover state after restarting — it isn't something that can be skipped.

scenario: 共识协议给每次选举一个递增 term/epoch。
scenario_en: A consensus protocol gives each election an increasing term or epoch.
q: 这个编号解决什么？
q_en: What does the number solve?
options: 区分新旧 leader，旧任期被拒绝
让网络延迟变成一个常数
让磁盘写入从此不再需要 fsync
保证集群里没有节点崩溃
options_en: It separates old from new leaders so stale-term requests get rejected.
It makes network latency constant.
It makes disk writes no longer need fsync.
It guarantees no node in the cluster crashes.
why: epoch 把领导权变成有版本的资格。看到更高 epoch 后，旧 leader 必须停止做决定。
why_en: An epoch versions leadership; once a higher epoch is seen, an old leader must stop deciding.

termDefinitions.meaning: epoch 是单调增加的任期编号，用来区分旧 leader 和新 leader。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An epoch is a monotonically increasing term number used to distinguish old leaders from newer leaders.

optionExplanations: 每次选举给一个递增的 term/epoch，把领导权变成有版本号的资格；一个节点一旦见过更高的 epoch，就知道自己那份旧任期的资格已经过期，可以据此拒绝旧任期发来的请求。
epoch 编号跟网络延迟本身没有关系，它解决的是身份和资格版本化的问题，不会让延迟变成常数。
epoch 跟磁盘写入需不需要 fsync 完全是两个不相关的机制。
epoch 不能保证节点不崩溃，它只是在崩溃或分区之后帮助系统分清谁的资格是过时的。
optionExplanations_en: Giving each election an increasing term or epoch versions leadership itself; once a node has seen a higher epoch, it knows its own old term's authority has expired and can reject requests carrying that stale term.
An epoch number has nothing to do with network latency itself; it solves versioning identity and authority, not making latency constant.
An epoch is entirely unrelated to whether disk writes need fsync.
An epoch doesn't guarantee nodes never crash; it only helps the system tell, after a crash or partition, whose authority is stale.

scenario: 两个候选 leader 在不同网络分区里同时请求投票。
scenario_en: Two leader candidates request votes in different network partitions.
q: 共识如何避免双主？
q_en: How does consensus avoid two leaders?
options: 多数派相交防双主
谁时钟快谁赢
每个分区都可独立选主
客户端投票决定
options_en: Majority overlap prevents dual leaders
The faster clock wins
Each partition may independently elect a leader
Clients vote to decide
why: 多数派交集让一个节点不能同时承诺两个同任期 leader。少数派应不可写。
why_en: Quorum overlap prevents two leaders in the same term from both being accepted; the minority should not write.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

termDefinitions.meaning: epoch 是单调增加的任期编号，用来区分旧 leader 和新 leader。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An epoch is a monotonically increasing term number used to distinguish old leaders from newer leaders.

optionExplanations: 两个候选者要各自拿到多数派的投票才能当选，五个节点里两组三节点的多数派必然重叠至少一个节点，这个重叠节点不可能同时把票投给两个同任期的候选者，从而挡住双主。
谁时钟快谁赢没有一致性保证，两个分区各自可能都觉得自己的候选者时钟更快，解决不了双主问题。
每个分区独立选主正是会导致双主的做法，跟“如何避免双主”这个问题的方向相反。
客户端不参与共识组内部的投票决策，让客户端投票不是共识协议解决双主的机制。
optionExplanations_en: Each candidate needs a majority of votes to win, and among five nodes any two sets of three majorities must overlap in at least one node, and that overlapping node can't cast its vote for two same-term candidates at once, blocking dual leaders.
The faster clock winning offers no consistency guarantee; each partition might believe its own candidate has the faster clock, failing to resolve dual leadership.
Each partition independently electing a leader is exactly what causes dual leaders, the opposite direction from how to avoid it.
Clients don't participate in the internal voting decisions of a consensus group; having clients vote isn't the mechanism consensus uses to prevent split brain.

scenario: leader 在提交一条日志前担心自己已被更高任期取代。
scenario_en: A leader worries it may have been replaced by a higher-term leader before committing a log entry.
q: 它应怎样确认？
q_en: How should it confirm?
options: 向多数派确认，并检查没有更高任期
只看自己节点的本地时钟
随便问任意一个 follower
相信上一次心跳成功过
options_en: Confirm with a majority and check that no higher term exists.
Just read its own local clock.
Ask any single follower.
Trust that the last heartbeat succeeded.
why: 多数派确认同时证明提议被足够节点看到，也会暴露更高任期。单个节点或本地时钟不够。
why_en: A majority confirmation both records the proposal and reveals a higher term if one exists.
whenOtherWins: 只读本地缓存且允许陈旧时，不必每次都确认领导权。
tradeoff: 提交安全 vs 前台协调

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

termDefinitions.meaning: epoch 是单调增加的任期编号，用来区分旧 leader 和新 leader。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An epoch is a monotonically increasing term number used to distinguish old leaders from newer leaders.

optionExplanations: leader 要把这条提议复制给多数派并拿到确认，这个过程既证明了提议被足够多节点看到，也会顺带暴露出是不是已经有更高任期的新 leader 存在。
只看自己的本地时钟没法知道集群里其他节点是不是已经选出了新 leader，这是本地信息解决不了的问题。
只问一个 follower 得到的只是单个节点的视角，不能代表多数派的真实状态。
上次心跳成功只能说明过去那一刻还连通，不能保证现在没有更高任期的 leader 已经出现。
optionExplanations_en: The leader has to replicate this proposal to a majority and get confirmation — that process both proves enough nodes have seen the proposal and would surface whether a higher-term new leader already exists.
Looking only at its own local clock tells it nothing about whether the rest of the cluster has already elected a new leader, information a local clock simply can't provide.
Asking just one follower only gives the perspective of a single node, which doesn't represent the true state of the majority.
A successful last heartbeat only proves connectivity at that past moment; it doesn't guarantee no higher-term leader has emerged since.

scenario: 系统要在故障中继续决定新值。
scenario_en: A system must keep deciding new values despite failures.
q: 2PC 和容错共识关键差别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between 2PC and fault-tolerant consensus?
options: 2PC 全员，共识多数派
2PC 比共识更能容忍协调者永久宕机
共识不需要任何日志
二者完全一样
options_en: 2PC needs all; consensus uses a majority
2PC tolerates permanent coordinator failure better than consensus
Consensus needs no log
They are identical
why: 2PC 的 prepared 参与者会等协调者，容易阻塞。共识用多数派和新 leader 恢复决策。
why_en: 2PC can block on a coordinator, while consensus uses majorities and new leaders to keep deciding.
tradeoff: 全参与者原子提交 vs 多数派容错

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

rows: 多个资源必须同一提交结果时
2PC 比共识更能容忍协调者永久宕机
多个资源必须同一提交结果时
高随机写吞吐更重要时
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适

optionExplanations: 2PC 需要所有参与者都投 yes 才能提交，任何一个失联都会卡住整个决定；容错共识通常只需要多数派同意就能继续做决定，剩下的少数派掉线也不影响。
2PC 恰恰更容易在协调者永久宕机时被卡住阻塞，容错共识用多数派和新 leader 接替能继续前进，这个说法说反了。
共识同样需要日志来记录已经达成的决定，不然节点重启后没法恢复到正确状态。
2PC 要求全体一致，共识只要多数派，两者在这个关键点上有本质差别，不是完全一样。
optionExplanations_en: 2PC needs every participant to vote yes before committing, so any single one going unreachable stalls the whole decision; fault-tolerant consensus usually only needs a majority to agree and keep making progress, with a minority offline having no effect.
2PC is actually more prone to blocking when the coordinator fails permanently, while fault-tolerant consensus keeps moving forward via majorities and new leaders — this option has it backwards.
Consensus still needs a log to record decisions already reached, otherwise nodes can't recover to the correct state after restarting.
2PC requires unanimity while consensus only needs a majority — a fundamental difference between the two, not identical at all.

scenario: 共识系统连续决定很多日志项。
scenario_en: A consensus system decides many log entries in sequence.
q: 为什么通常会稳定使用一个 leader？
q_en: Why does it usually keep a stable leader?
options: 避免每个日志项都重新完整选主，降低往返和冲突
因为 leader 是永远正确的
因为 follower 节点根本不能存储日志
因为共识只允许一个值
options_en: To avoid a full leader election for every log entry, reducing round trips and conflicts
Because the leader is always correct
Because follower nodes cannot store logs at all.
Because consensus allows only one value ever
why: 稳定 leader 把重复共识优化成连续追加日志。安全性仍依赖任期和多数派，而不是盲目信任 leader。
why_en: A stable leader optimizes repeated consensus into log appends, while safety still depends on terms and majorities.

termDefinitions.meaning: Raft 是一种实际常用的崩溃容错共识算法，用 term、leader 和日志复制组织决策。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Raft is a practical crash-fault consensus algorithm organized around terms, leaders, and replicated logs.

termDefinitions.meaning: epoch 是单调增加的任期编号，用来区分旧 leader 和新 leader。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An epoch is a monotonically increasing term number used to distinguish old leaders from newer leaders.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

optionExplanations: 稳定用一个 leader 能把重复的共识流程简化成连续追加日志，避免每写一条都要重新走一遍完整选主，省下大量往返和潜在的提议冲突。
leader 不是永远正确的，它也会崩溃或被更高任期取代，安全性靠的是任期和多数派机制，不是对 leader 的盲目信任。
follower 完全可以存日志，甚至是复制协议要求它们必须保存日志副本的核心职责之一。
共识在一个位置上只能决定一个值，但连续的日志项各自可以有不同的值，不是共识永远只允许一个值。
optionExplanations_en: Sticking with a stable leader turns repeated consensus into continuous log appending, avoiding a full leader election for every single write and saving a lot of round trips and potential proposal conflicts.
The leader isn't always correct — it can crash or get replaced by a higher term too; safety comes from terms and majority mechanisms, not blind trust in the leader.
Followers absolutely can store logs — keeping a copy of the log is actually one of their core responsibilities in the replication protocol.
Consensus only decides one value per log position, but successive log entries can each hold different values — it isn't true that consensus allows only one value ever.

scenario: 单主数据库平时所有写都走 leader，看起来不需要共识。
scenario_en: A single-leader database sends all writes to the leader, so it seems not to need consensus.
q: 共识最终出现在哪里？
q_en: Where does consensus still appear?
options: failover 选主时
每条普通 SQL 都必须运行 FLP 证明
所有读都要跨库 2PC
缓存淘汰必须共识
options_en: During failover leader election
Every SQL statement must run an FLP proof
All reads need cross-database 2PC
Cache eviction requires consensus
why: leader 简化写入顺序，但 leader 换人本身就是一致决定。自动故障转移绕不开共识问题。
why_en: A leader simplifies write ordering, but choosing the leader during failover is itself a consensus problem.

termDefinitions.fullName: Fischer, Lynch, and Paterson impossibility result
termDefinitions.meaning: FLP 结果说明在完全异步且可能崩溃的模型里，确定性共识无法保证终止。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The FLP result says deterministic consensus cannot guarantee termination in a fully asynchronous model with possible crashes.

tradeoff: 稳定 leader 写入 vs failover 一致选主

rows: 前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
每条普通 SQL 都必须运行 FL…
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
每条普通 SQL 都必…成本
多个资源必须同一提交结果时
能接受短暂滞后、想降延迟时

optionExplanations: 平时写入走 leader 看似简单，但一旦要 failover、需要在候选者里选出新 leader，这本身就是一个要节点达成一致的决定，共识问题就在这个环节冒出来了。
普通 SQL 语句只是走既定的写路径，不需要每条都跑一遍完整的 FLP 理论证明，这个说法夸张了。
读操作不需要跨库 2PC，2PC 是解决跨资源写入原子性的问题，跟普通读请求无关。
缓存淘汰是本地或独立的存储管理策略，不是需要跨节点达成一致的共识问题。
optionExplanations_en: Writes normally going through the leader looks simple enough, but the moment failover needs to pick a new leader from candidates, that choice itself is a decision nodes must agree on — that's exactly where the consensus problem surfaces.
An ordinary SQL statement just follows the established write path; it doesn't need to run a full FLP-style proof on every execution, an exaggerated claim.
Reads don't need cross-database 2PC — 2PC solves cross-resource write atomicity, unrelated to ordinary reads.
Cache eviction is a local or independent storage-management policy, not a cross-node agreement problem requiring consensus.

scenario: 数据库只能靠人工在故障后指定新 leader。
scenario_en: A database relies on a human to choose a new leader after failure.
q: 这为什么不满足共识终止性？
q_en: Why does this not satisfy consensus termination?
options: 无人介入会无限阻塞
人工选择总是比算法快
终止性只关心数据压缩
它会自动避免 split brain
options_en: It can block forever without intervention
Manual choice is always faster than algorithms
Termination only concerns compaction
It automatically prevents split brain
why: 人工 failover 可以实用，但终止性被移到系统外的人身上。共识算法要在模型内自动前进。
why_en: Manual failover can work operationally, but termination has been moved outside the system to a human.
tradeoff: 人工恢复简单性 vs 自动终止性

rows: 无人介入会无限阻塞场景
无人介入会无限阻塞成本
人工选择总是比算法快
人工选择总是比算法快场景
人工选择总是比算法快成本
终止性只关心数据压缩
终止性只关心数据压缩场景
终止性只关心数据压缩成本
它会自动避免 split brain
它会自动避免 sp…场景
它会自动避免 spli…成本

optionExplanations: 没有人介入的情况下，系统自己没有任何机制去挑出新 leader，会一直卡在故障后的状态，无限期地等着人来做决定，这就没有满足共识要求的终止性。
人工选择不见得比算法快，尤其是半夜出故障、没人及时响应的情况下，反而可能等得更久。
终止性讲的是“系统最终能不能自动做出决定”，跟数据压缩完全不是一回事。
人工 failover 完全可能因为操作失误让两个人同时指定了两个不同的新 leader，不会自动避免 split brain。
optionExplanations_en: With no one intervening, the system itself has no mechanism to pick a new leader and just sits stuck in the post-failure state, waiting indefinitely for a human decision — that's exactly failing the termination requirement consensus demands.
Manual choice isn't necessarily faster than an algorithm, especially if a failure happens at 2am with no one responding promptly, it could easily take even longer.
Termination is about whether the system can eventually make a decision automatically, completely unrelated to data compaction.
Manual failover can easily let two people mistakenly designate two different new leaders at once — it doesn't automatically prevent split brain.

scenario: 一个共识组频繁自动增删投票节点。
scenario_en: A consensus group frequently adds and removes voting nodes automatically.
q: 为什么成员变更要小心？
q_en: Why must membership changes be careful?
options: 保持新旧 quorum 相交
成员变更只影响 UI
节点越频繁变化越容易线性化
不需要记录成员配置
options_en: Keep old and new quorums overlapping
Membership only affects the UI
Frequent changes make linearizability easier
Membership configurations need not be logged
why: 共识安全依赖 quorum 交集。成员变更本身也要被有序记录，否则可能出现两个合法多数派。
why_en: Consensus safety depends on quorum overlap, so membership changes themselves must be ordered and recorded.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

optionExplanations: 共识的安全性依赖新旧配置的 quorum 必须相交，成员变更要小心地保证这一点，不然新加入的一批节点和原来的节点各自可能凑出互不相交的多数派，做出互相冲突的决定。
成员变更直接影响谁算在 quorum 里、谁的投票有效，远不止是 UI 展示层面的事。
节点越频繁变化，quorum 交集的保证反而越难维持，更不利于线性化，这个说法说反了。
成员配置本身必须像日志项一样被有序记录下来，不然节点重启后无法正确恢复当时的成员视图。
optionExplanations_en: Consensus safety depends on the old and new quorums overlapping, so membership changes must carefully preserve that, otherwise a newly added batch of nodes and the original nodes could each form majorities that never overlap, reaching conflicting decisions.
Membership changes directly affect who counts toward the quorum and whose votes are valid, far more than just a UI display concern.
The more frequently membership changes, the harder it actually gets to preserve quorum overlap, which works against linearizability — this option has it backwards.
Membership configuration itself must be ordered and recorded just like a log entry, otherwise a node can't correctly recover the membership view at that point after restarting.

scenario: 网络抖动导致共识组频繁重新选主。
scenario_en: Network instability makes a consensus group repeatedly elect new leaders.
q: 主要影响是什么？
q_en: What is the main impact?
options: 安全性通常保持，但活性和吞吐下降
一定产生两个已提交值
所有 follower 数据丢失
CAP 不再适用
options_en: Safety usually holds, but liveness and throughput drop
It must produce two committed values
All follower data is lost
CAP no longer applies
why: 频繁选主会打断日志复制，系统把时间花在投票上。超时和网络质量会直接影响活性。
why_en: Frequent elections interrupt log replication, so the system spends time voting rather than serving writes.
optionExplanations: 频繁重新选主会反复打断正在进行的日志复制，系统把大量时间花在投票协调上而不是真正处理写请求，安全性通常还守得住，但活性和吞吐明显下降。
频繁选主不会必然产生两个已提交的值，共识的安全性设计正是为了避免这种情况，即使选主很频繁。
重新选主不会导致所有 follower 数据丢失，follower 本地的数据仍然保留着，只是协调过程被打断了。
CAP 讨论的是分区场景下的取舍，这里描述的是选主频繁这个活性问题，CAP 框架依然适用，不是不再适用。
optionExplanations_en: Frequent re-elections keep interrupting ongoing log replication, and the system spends a lot of time on voting coordination instead of actually serving writes — safety usually still holds, but liveness and throughput clearly suffer.
Frequent elections don't necessarily produce two committed values; consensus's safety design exists precisely to prevent that, even amid frequent elections.
Re-elections don't cause all follower data to be lost — followers still keep their local data, only the coordination process gets interrupted.
CAP addresses the tradeoff under a partition; this scenario is about the liveness problem of frequent elections, and the CAP framework still applies, it hasn't stopped applying.

scenario: 调度平台需要存“分区 7 当前 leader 是谁”和少量租约状态。
scenario_en: A scheduler needs to store “who is leader for partition 7” and a small amount of lease state.
q: 为什么适合协调服务？
q_en: Why is a coordination service a good fit?
options: 小而关键的协调元数据
数据大且高吞吐，适合全量放 ZooKeeper
它能替代所有业务数据库
它让网络分区消失
options_en: Small but critical coordination metadata
The data is huge and high-throughput, so put it all in ZooKeeper
It replaces every business database
It makes network partitions disappear
why: 协调服务适合低吞吐、小元数据和强顺序需求。业务大数据不应塞进共识存储。
why_en: Coordination services fit small, low-throughput, correctness-critical metadata, not bulk business data.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是高 QPS 业务记录，普通分区数据库或日志系统更合适。
tradeoff: 强协调元数据 vs 业务数据吞吐

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是基于共识的协调服务，常用于小规模元数据、选主、锁和成员通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-backed coordination service for small metadata, leader election, locks, and membership notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd 是基于 Raft 的分布式键值协调存储，常用于 Kubernetes 等系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a Raft-backed distributed key-value coordination store used by systems such as Kubernetes.

optionExplanations: “分区 7 当前 leader 是谁”和少量租约状态数据量很小、但正确性极其关键，正好落在协调服务擅长的领域：小而关键的协调元数据。
协调服务通常只适合低吞吐、小数据量的场景，把大量高吞吐业务数据塞进去会拖垮它，跟它的设计初衷相反。
协调服务专注于协调元数据这个窄领域，不能替代日常业务数据库承担的全部职责。
协调服务能帮助系统更好地应对网络分区，但不会让网络分区这件事本身消失。
optionExplanations_en: Who's the current leader of partition 7 and a small amount of lease state is tiny in volume but extremely critical to correctness — exactly the sweet spot for a coordination service: small but critical coordination metadata.
Coordination services are typically suited to low-throughput, small-volume data; stuffing a lot of high-throughput business data in there would bog it down, against its design intent.
A coordination service focuses on this narrow domain of coordination metadata; it can't take over all the responsibilities of a regular business database.
A coordination service can help a system cope better with network partitions, but it doesn't make partitions themselves disappear.

scenario: 多个 worker 同时尝试创建 /leader 节点，只有一个能成功。
scenario_en: Several workers try to create /leader at the same time, and only one may succeed.
q: 协调服务需要提供什么操作？
q_en: What operation does the coordination service need?
options: 线性化条件创建
异步缓存刷新
每日批量去重
客户端本地随机数
options_en: Linearizable conditional create
Asynchronous cache refresh
Daily batch deduplication
Client-local randomness
why: 原子条件创建把“检查没人是 leader”和“占位”合成一个线性化写。失败者能安全退下。
why_en: Atomic conditional create combines checking no leader and claiming the slot into one linearizable write.
whenOtherWins: 如果多个 worker 同时工作也没关系，普通服务发现即可。
tradeoff: 唯一选主 vs 协调延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是基于共识的协调服务，常用于小规模元数据、选主、锁和成员通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-backed coordination service for small metadata, leader election, locks, and membership notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

optionExplanations: 多个 worker 同时抢一个节点，只能有一个成功，这需要把检查这个节点没被别人抢占和实际占用它合成同一个线性化操作，才能保证唯一确定的赢家。
异步缓存刷新可能让不同 worker 看到不同的检查结果，容易出现两个 worker 都以为自己抢到了。
每日批量去重是事后处理，等它跑的时候可能已经有多个 worker 都以为自己是 leader 很久了。
客户端本地随机数没有跨 worker 的协调能力，解决不了谁能真正抢到这个节点的问题。
optionExplanations_en: With multiple workers racing to create the same node and only one allowed to win, checking that nobody else holds it and actually claiming it must be fused into one linearizable operation to guarantee a single definite winner.
Asynchronous cache refresh can let different workers see different check results, easily letting two workers both believe they won.
Daily batch deduplication is after-the-fact; by the time it runs, multiple workers may have already believed they were leader for a long while.
Client-local randomness has no cross-worker coordination power and doesn't resolve who actually gets to claim the node.

scenario: worker 持有 ZooKeeper session，并创建 ephemeral leader 节点。
scenario_en: A worker holds a ZooKeeper session and creates an ephemeral leader node.
q: session 超时后发生什么？
q_en: What happens after session timeout?
options: 删临时节点，触发接任
节点永久保留直到手工删除
所有业务数据被清空
旧 worker 自动获得更高 token
options_en: Delete ephemeral node and trigger takeover
The node stays forever until manual deletion
All business data is cleared
The old worker automatically gets a higher token
why: ephemeral 节点把客户端存活和元数据生命周期绑在一起。长暂停仍要配合 fencing 防旧 worker 复活写。
why_en: Ephemeral nodes tie client liveness to metadata lifetime, but long pauses still need fencing against old workers.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是基于共识的协调服务，常用于小规模元数据、选主、锁和成员通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-backed coordination service for small metadata, leader election, locks, and membership notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: fencing token 是单调递增令牌，资源端用它拒绝旧 leader 的写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fencing token is a monotonically increasing token that lets a resource reject writes from an old leader.

optionExplanations: session 超时说明这个 worker 已经失联，ZooKeeper 会删掉它绑定的临时 leader 节点，其它候选者监听到节点消失，就会触发接任流程。
临时节点恰恰是绑定客户端存活状态的，session 一超时它就会被删除，不会永久保留。
ZooKeeper 删除的只是这一个临时节点，不会波及其他跟这次 session 无关的业务数据。
旧 worker 醒来后并不会自动获得更高的 token，它甚至可能已经不知道自己已经被移除，还要靠下游 fencing 挡住它。
optionExplanations_en: A session timeout means the worker has lost contact, so ZooKeeper deletes the ephemeral leader node it was bound to, and other candidates watching that node see it disappear and trigger takeover.
An ephemeral node is precisely tied to client liveness — the moment the session times out, it gets deleted rather than staying forever.
ZooKeeper only deletes this one ephemeral node; it doesn't touch other business data unrelated to this session.
A revived old worker doesn't automatically get a higher token — it may not even know it's been removed, which is exactly why downstream fencing is still needed to block it.

scenario: 配置中心里 leader 变化后，服务实例要尽快收到通知。
scenario_en: Services should be notified soon after the leader changes in a configuration store.
q: 协调服务的哪个能力有用？
q_en: Which coordination-service feature helps?
options: watch 通知机制
只读副本上的随机读延迟
离线的日志压缩任务
客户端浏览器本地缓存
options_en: A watch/notification mechanism.
Random read latency on read-only replicas.
An offline log compaction job.
The client browser's local cache.
why: watch 让客户端不用一直轮询所有 key。通知仍可能丢或需要重新读，所以客户端要按版本重查状态。
why_en: Watches reduce polling, but clients should still re-read versioned state because notifications can be missed or coalesced.
whenOtherWins: 如果变化很频繁且每次都不关键，普通 pub/sub 可能更便宜。
tradeoff: 及时成员通知 vs 协调服务负载

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是基于共识的协调服务，常用于小规模元数据、选主、锁和成员通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-backed coordination service for small metadata, leader election, locks, and membership notifications.

optionExplanations: watch/notification 机制让服务实例订阅感兴趣的 key，一旦它变化就能收到主动通知，不用一直去轮询每一个 key 有没有变化。
只读副本的随机延迟解决的是读扩展问题，跟“leader 变化后要尽快通知”这个及时性需求不是一回事。
离线压缩任务是存储层面的整理动作，跟实时通知配置变化毫不相关。
客户端浏览器缓存只在客户端本地生效，服务实例之间的配置同步用不上它。
optionExplanations_en: A watch/notification mechanism lets a service instance subscribe to a key it cares about and get actively notified when it changes, instead of constantly polling every key for updates.
Random delay from read replicas addresses read scaling, a different concern from the timely notify-me-when-the-leader-changes requirement here.
Offline compaction jobs are a storage-layer housekeeping task, entirely unrelated to real-time notification of a configuration change.
Browser cache only applies locally on a client and does nothing for configuration syncing between server-side service instances.

scenario: 普通无状态 Web 服务只需要找到一些健康实例，偶尔读到旧列表也能重试。
scenario_en: A stateless web client only needs some healthy instances, and can retry if it sees a slightly stale list.
q: 服务发现一定要共识吗？
q_en: Does service discovery necessarily require consensus?
options: 不一定，最终一致的注册表够用
一定需要线性化的写和读
必须用 2PC 保证一致
必须每次请求都重新选主
options_en: Not necessarily — DNS or an eventually consistent registry can be enough.
It always needs linearizable reads and writes.
It must use 2PC to stay consistent.
It must elect a leader on every request.
why: 服务发现通常能容忍旧列表和重试，不一定需要强一致。选主和锁这类唯一性问题才更需要共识。
why_en: Service discovery often tolerates stale lists and retries; uniqueness problems like leader election need consensus more.
whenOtherWins: 如果发现的是“当前唯一 leader 地址”，共识系统已经知道 leader，用它发布更合理。
tradeoff: 发现可用实例 vs 唯一角色正确性
optionExplanations: 普通无状态服务只是想找到一些健康实例，偶尔读到旧列表也能靠重试自己修复，这种场景用 DNS 或最终一致的注册表往往就够用，不必强上共识。
要求一定线性化读写会把服务发现这种低门槛需求硬升级成高成本操作，没有必要。
2PC 是解决跨资源原子提交的问题，跟找几个健康实例这种服务发现需求不是一回事。
每次请求都选主的开销极高，服务发现的正确性要求远没有严格到需要这个地步。
optionExplanations_en: An ordinary stateless service just wants to find a few healthy instances and can tolerate an occasional stale list by retrying — for this, DNS or an eventually consistent registry is usually enough, no need to force consensus.
Requiring linearizable reads and writes would needlessly upgrade this low-stakes service-discovery need into an expensive operation.
2PC solves cross-resource atomic commit, unrelated to a service-discovery need like finding a few healthy instances.
Electing a leader per request is prohibitively expensive, and service discovery's correctness requirement is nowhere near strict enough to need that.

scenario: 分布式任务系统要决定哪些 worker 当前属于活跃集合。
scenario_en: A distributed job system must decide which workers are currently active members.
q: 为什么成员关系常和共识绑在一起？
q_en: Why is membership often tied to consensus?
options: 死活判断影响分配，需多数派同一视图
成员列表只影响日志的格式
每个节点自己本地猜测就够
NTP 校时能直接给出活跃集合
options_en: Liveness calls drive assignment, so a majority must agree on one view.
The member list only affects the log format.
Each node guessing locally is good enough.
NTP time sync hands you the active set directly.
why: 成员关系不是事实探测那么简单，而是集群采纳的视图。任务分配要基于同一视图才不会重复或漏跑。
why_en: Membership is an adopted cluster view, not just local failure detection; assignments need one view to avoid duplicates or gaps.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务天然幂等且允许重复执行，本地探测加租约可能足够。
tradeoff: 统一成员视图 vs 协调开销

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

optionExplanations: 哪些 worker 算活跃直接决定任务该分给谁，如果不同节点各自判断出不同的活跃集合，同一个任务可能被重复分配或者干脆漏掉，所以要让多数派对同一个视图达成一致。
成员列表直接决定任务分配这种业务逻辑，远不止是影响日志怎么格式化。
每个节点本地猜测容易出现分歧，一个节点觉得某个 worker 活着、另一个节点觉得它死了，任务分配就会出错。
NTP 只负责时钟同步，不理解也不能直接判断哪些 worker 属于当前活跃集合。
optionExplanations_en: Which workers count as active directly decides who gets assigned tasks, so if different nodes independently judge different active sets, the same task can be duplicated or missed entirely — that's why a majority needs to agree on one view.
The membership list directly drives business logic like task assignment, far more than just affecting log formatting.
Each node guessing locally is prone to disagreement — one node thinks a worker is alive while another thinks it's dead, and task assignment goes wrong.
NTP only handles clock synchronization; it neither understands nor can directly determine which workers belong to the current active set.

scenario: 多个进程竞争 leader，想公平排队并在前一个挂掉时接任。
scenario_en: Several processes compete for leadership and want ordered takeover when the predecessor dies.
q: ZooKeeper 常用什么模式？
q_en: What ZooKeeper pattern is common?
options: 顺序临时节点+观察前驱
所有进程同时写同一个普通文件
每秒随机选一个 leader
只比较本机启动时间
options_en: Sequential ephemeral node plus predecessor watch
All processes write the same normal file
Randomly choose a leader every second
Compare only local start time
why: 顺序节点给每个候选者一个全序位置，ephemeral 处理会话死亡。观察前驱能避免所有客户端同时惊群。
why_en: Sequential nodes give candidates an order, ephemeral nodes handle session death, and watching the predecessor avoids a herd effect.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要任意健康实例处理请求，普通负载均衡比选主队列简单。
tradeoff: 有序接任 vs 协调复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是基于共识的协调服务，常用于小规模元数据、选主、锁和成员通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-backed coordination service for small metadata, leader election, locks, and membership notifications.

optionExplanations: 给每个候选者创建一个顺序临时节点，天然按创建顺序排出全局位置，每个候选者只监视排在自己前面的那一个，前驱挂掉才轮到自己，既公平又避免所有人同时被惊动。
所有进程同时写同一个普通文件既没有顺序保证，也没有跟会话生命周期绑定的自动清理机制。
每秒随机选一个 leader 完全没有公平排队和稳定接任的语义，跟这里的需求不匹配。
只比较本机启动时间无法处理某个候选者中途崩溃后该轮到谁接任的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Creating a sequential ephemeral node for each candidate naturally gives everyone a position by creation order, and each candidate only watches the one immediately ahead of it — when the predecessor dies, the next one takes over, both fair and avoiding a herd of everyone waking up at once.
All processes writing the same plain file gives neither an ordering guarantee nor automatic cleanup tied to session lifetime.
Randomly choosing a leader every second has none of the fair-queueing or stable-takeover semantics needed here.
Comparing only local start time can't handle who should take over when a candidate crashes partway through.

scenario: 团队要做选主和配置发布，但不想自己实现 Paxos/Raft。
scenario_en: A team needs leader election and config publication but does not want to implement Paxos or Raft.
q: 合理选择是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable choice?
options: 使用 ZooKeeper/etcd 这类成熟协调服务
自己用 UDP 心跳手写一套共识
直接把 leader 写死进每台机器的本地文件里
让客户端轮流指定谁是 leader
options_en: Use a mature coordination service such as ZooKeeper or etcd.
Hand-roll consensus on top of UDP heartbeats.
Hard-code the leader into each machine's local file.
Let clients take turns naming the leader.
why: 共识实现很容易在边界条件出错。把小而关键的协调交给成熟系统，通常比自研安全。
why_en: Consensus implementations fail easily at edge cases, so mature coordination services are safer for small critical metadata.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单机进程内协调，本地锁或数据库唯一约束就够。
tradeoff: 复用成熟共识 vs 额外依赖

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是基于共识的协调服务，常用于小规模元数据、选主、锁和成员通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-backed coordination service for small metadata, leader election, locks, and membership notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd 是基于 Raft 的分布式键值协调存储，常用于 Kubernetes 等系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a Raft-backed distributed key-value coordination store used by systems such as Kubernetes.

termDefinitions.meaning: Raft 是一种实际常用的崩溃容错共识算法，用 term、leader 和日志复制组织决策。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Raft is a practical crash-fault consensus algorithm organized around terms, leaders, and replicated logs.

optionExplanations: 共识实现细节很容易在各种边界条件上出错，把选主和配置发布这类小而关键的协调工作交给 ZooKeeper、etcd 这类已经被广泛验证过的成熟系统，通常比自己写更安全。
自己从 UDP 心跳手写共识，很容易在网络分区、节点崩溃这些边界场景踩坑，风险很高。
把 leader 写进每台机器本地文件没有任何跨机器的一致性保证，各台机器的文件很容易互相矛盾。
让客户端轮流指定 leader 缺乏一个统一、权威的仲裁机制，容易出现多个客户端各说各话的情况。
optionExplanations_en: Consensus implementation details are notoriously easy to get wrong at edge cases, so handing small but critical coordination work like leader election and config publishing to a battle-tested mature system like ZooKeeper or etcd is usually safer than rolling your own.
Hand-rolling consensus from UDP heartbeats is prone to breaking exactly at edge cases like network partitions and node crashes, a high-risk approach.
Writing the leader into each machine's local file gives no cross-machine consistency guarantee at all, and the files can easily contradict each other.
Letting clients rotate who designates the leader lacks a single, authoritative arbitration mechanism, prone to different clients disagreeing with each other.

scenario: 社交点赞计数允许短暂不一致，并能后台合并。
scenario_en: A social like counter can be temporarily inconsistent and merged later.
q: 是否需要全局共识？
q_en: Does it need global consensus?
options: 通常不需要；分片计数和异步合并更合适
必须给每个点赞都跑一次完整的 Raft
必须跨所有地区 2PC
只能单机运行
options_en: Usually no; sharded counters and async merge fit better
You must run a full Raft round per like.
Every region must join 2PC
It can only run on one machine
why: 共识适合不可分裂的决定，不适合每个高频弱一致事件。能合并的业务应避免全局协调。
why_en: Consensus fits indivisible decisions, not every high-volume event that can be merged later.
whenOtherWins: 如果点赞触发唯一奖励或资金结算，提交路径可能需要强一致。
tradeoff: 可合并吞吐 vs 全局决定正确性
optionExplanations: 点赞计数允许短暂不一致、还能后台合并，这种可以被合并、不要求绝对唯一决定的场景，用分片计数各自累加、再异步汇总合并会更轻量，用不着全局共识。
每个点赞都跑一次 Raft 的协调成本远超点赞本身的价值，对这种高频弱一致事件来说完全不必要。
跨所有地区做 2PC 会让点赞这种轻量操作背上极重的协调开销，跟场景描述的“允许短暂不一致”正相反。
点赞计数完全可以分布式部署、分片处理，不是只能局限在单机上运行。
optionExplanations_en: Since likes can tolerate brief inconsistency and get merged in the background, this kind of mergeable, non-unique-decision scenario fits sharded counters that each accumulate independently and merge asynchronously, lighter weight and not needing global consensus.
Running Raft for every single like costs far more in coordination overhead than the value of the like itself, unnecessary for this kind of high-volume, weakly-consistent event.
Requiring 2PC across every region would saddle a lightweight operation like liking with heavy coordination overhead, the opposite of the scenario's stated tolerance for brief inconsistency.
Like counting can absolutely be distributed and sharded; it isn't restricted to running on a single machine.

scenario: 事务隔离和副本一致性经常被混用。
scenario_en: Transaction isolation and replica consistency are often mixed up.
q: 哪句区分最准确？
q_en: Which distinction is most accurate?
options: 事务像串行；副本像单副本
可串行化保证跨洲低延迟
线性化只处理 SQL 死锁
二者都只描述缓存淘汰
options_en: Transactions look serial; replicas look single-copy
Serializability guarantees low cross-region latency
Linearizability only handles SQL deadlocks
Both describe cache eviction only
why: 这两个保证可以同时需要，也可以只需要其中一个。设计时要分别问隔离和读新鲜度。
why_en: You may need either or both, so ask separately about transaction isolation and read freshness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可串行化保证事务结果等价于某个串行执行顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializability guarantees that transactions produce a result equivalent to some serial order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

tradeoff: 事务隔离 vs 副本新鲜度

rows: 事务像串行；副本像单副本
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
事务像串行；副本像单副本成本
可串行化保证跨洲低延迟
必须保护最新读或不变量时
线性化只处理 SQL 死锁
必须保护最新读或不变量时
二者都只描述缓存淘汰
能接受短暂滞后、想降延迟时

optionExplanations: 事务隔离追求的是并发执行看起来像串行执行一样，副本一致性追求的是多副本看起来像只有一份数据一样，这两个比喻分别抓住了它们各自真正在保护的东西。
可串行化保护的是事务并发执行的正确性，不涉及跨洲物理距离的延迟，说它保证低延迟不成立。
线性化管的是读写新鲜度这种一般性保证，不是专门处理 SQL 死锁这种具体机制问题。
这两个概念分别描述的是事务隔离和副本一致性的不同侧面，不只是缓存淘汰这种狭窄的话题。
optionExplanations_en: Transaction isolation is about concurrent execution looking as if it ran serially, while replica consistency is about multiple copies looking as if there were just one — these two analogies each capture what they're actually protecting.
Serializability protects the correctness of concurrent transaction execution and has nothing to do with cross-continent physical-distance latency, so claiming it guarantees low latency doesn't hold.
Linearizability is a general recency guarantee about reads and writes, not a mechanism specifically for handling SQL deadlocks.
These two concepts describe distinct sides of transaction isolation and replica consistency respectively, not the narrow topic of cache eviction alone.

q: 一句话区分 serializability 和 linearizability？
q_en: How can you distinguish serializability and linearizability in one sentence?
text: {{Serializability}} 约束事务结果像某个串行顺序；{{linearizability}} 约束读写对象在真实时间上像单副本。
text_en: {{Serializability}} constrains transaction results to some serial order; {{linearizability}} constrains object reads and writes to look like one real-time copy.
why: 前者主要防并发事务异常，后者主要防读到旧副本。二者不互相替代。
why_en: The former prevents transaction anomalies; the latter prevents stale replica reads, and they do not replace each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可串行化保证事务结果等价于某个串行执行顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serializability guarantees that transactions produce a result equivalent to some serial order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

scenario: 评审中有人说“CAP 只能三选二，所以我们选 AP”。
scenario_en: In a review, someone says, “CAP says pick two, so we choose AP.”
q: 更好的追问是什么？
q_en: What is the better follow-up?
options: 分区时哪些操作可用，哪些必须线性化？
少数派分区里是否可以继续接受写入？
读请求是否允许返回旧的缓存值？
是否能靠重试直接消除网络分区？
options_en: During a partition, which operations stay available and which must stay linearizable?
Can the minority side keep accepting writes?
Are reads allowed to return a stale cached value?
Can retries make the network partition go away?
why: CAP 口号太粗。面试里要落到具体操作：哪些可以弱一致，哪些必须拒绝请求来保护正确性。
why_en: A useful CAP discussion names the exact operations that stay available and the ones that must reject requests to preserve correctness.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 在严格形式下讨论网络分区时线性化和可用性的取舍，但常被口号化误用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP, in its strict form, discusses the tradeoff between linearizability and availability during a network partition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

tradeoff: CAP 口号 vs 操作级取舍

必须保护最新读或不变量时
你选的两个字母颜色是什么？

为什么不把网络关掉？成本
是否能把 P 永久删除？
前提换成它擅长的问题形状时才合适
是否能把 P 永久删除？成本

optionExplanations: CAP 口号太粗，评审真正该追问的是具体到操作层面：分区发生时，哪些操作应该继续可用（哪怕数据旧一点），哪些操作必须坚持线性化、宁可拒绝也不能给出错误结果。
少数派要不要继续接受写入只是这个大问题下的一个具体子问题，不足以覆盖“哪些操作”这个更完整的追问范围。
读请求能不能返回旧缓存值同样只是众多操作里的一种，不能代表对整体设计该怎么权衡的完整追问。
重试解决的是网络暂时不可达的问题，不能消除真正的网络分区本身，这个追问方向偏了。
optionExplanations_en: CAP as a slogan is too blunt; the review should push down to the operation level: during a partition, which operations should stay available even with slightly stale data, and which must insist on staying linearizable, refusing rather than returning a wrong result.
