Whether the minority may keep accepting writes is just one specific sub-question under this bigger issue, not broad enough to cover the fuller which operations framing.
Whether reads may return stale cached values is likewise just one operation among many, not representative of the full tradeoff question for the overall design.
Retries address temporary network unreachability; they can't eliminate an actual network partition, so this line of questioning is off track.

scenario: 全球个人资料页可以展示几秒旧头像；用户保存后本地页面先乐观展示新头像。
scenario_en: A global profile page may show an avatar that is a few seconds stale; after saving, the local page shows the new avatar optimistically.
q: 哪种一致性通常够用？
q_en: Which consistency model is usually enough?
options: 最终一致加读己之写体验处理
所有地区线性化读
每次头像更新跑 2PC
禁止缓存
options_en: Eventual consistency plus read-your-writes UX handling
Linearizable reads in every region
2PC for every avatar update
No caching
why: 头像展示不是强不变量，短暂旧读可接受。用会话读己之写改善体验即可。
why_en: Avatar display is not a strong invariant, so eventual consistency with read-your-writes UX is usually enough.
whenOtherWins: 如果头像变更是身份认证或权限凭据，读路径保证要更强。
tradeoff: 全球低延迟 vs 读新鲜度
optionExplanations: 头像展示不是需要严格保护的不变量，几秒旧完全可以接受，用最终一致就够，再配合会话内读己之写让用户至少能看到自己刚保存的新头像，体验就不会有明显问题。
每个地区都要求线性化读，会把跨洲往返延迟带进头像这种轻量展示场景，代价远超实际需要。
每次头像更新都跑 2PC 会给一个不需要强一致的操作背上沉重的协调成本，完全不成比例。
禁止缓存会让每次查看资料页都要打到源数据，白白牺牲性能，跟头像这种低风险数据的需求不匹配。
optionExplanations_en: Avatar display isn't an invariant that needs strict protection — a few seconds of staleness is fine, so eventual consistency is enough, and session-level read-your-writes ensures the user at least sees their own freshly saved avatar, keeping the experience smooth.
Requiring linearizable reads in every region drags cross-continent round-trip latency into what's just a lightweight display feature, far more cost than necessary.
Running 2PC for every avatar update saddles a low-stakes operation with heavy coordination overhead, wildly disproportionate.
Disabling caching entirely forces every profile-page view to hit the source, needlessly sacrificing performance for data this low-risk.

scenario: etcd 客户端刚写入配置，然后另一个客户端必须马上读到。
scenario_en: One etcd client writes config, and another client must read it immediately.
q: 读请求应选择什么模式？
q_en: What read mode should it choose?
options: 线性化读或 quorum read
任意 follower 的 stale read
浏览器缓存
离线快照文件
options_en: A linearizable read or quorum read
A stale read from any follower
Browser cache
An offline snapshot file
why: 很多协调系统为了速度提供可能陈旧的读模式。需要读最新配置时要显式请求线性化读。
why_en: Many coordination systems offer possibly stale reads for speed; request a linearizable read when freshness matters.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是监控面板展示，stale read 能减轻 leader 压力。
tradeoff: 读新鲜度 vs leader/quorum 负载

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd 是基于 Raft 的分布式键值协调存储，常用于 Kubernetes 等系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a Raft-backed distributed key-value coordination store used by systems such as Kubernetes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

optionExplanations: 另一个客户端必须马上读到刚写入的配置，这正是需要新鲜度保证的场景，应该显式请求线性化读或 quorum read，而不是走可能陈旧的默认读路径。
任意 follower 的 stale read 恰恰可能读不到刚写入的这条配置，跟“必须马上读到”的要求直接冲突。
浏览器缓存是客户端本地的缓存机制，跟服务端配置系统的读新鲜度保证不是一回事。
离线快照文件是某个历史时间点的静态副本，不会包含刚刚才写入的最新配置。
optionExplanations_en: Another client needing to see the just-written config immediately is exactly a recency-critical scenario, calling for an explicit linearizable read or quorum read instead of the default, potentially stale read path.
A stale read from any follower might well miss this just-written config entirely, directly conflicting with the must-read-it-immediately requirement.
Browser cache is a client-local caching mechanism, unrelated to the server-side configuration system's read-recency guarantee.
An offline snapshot file is a static copy from some past point in time and wouldn't contain the config that was just written.

scenario: 服务从协调系统 follower 读到旧 leader 地址并继续写。
scenario_en: A service reads an old leader address from a coordination follower and keeps writing.
q: 风险是什么？
q_en: What is the risk?
options: 可能写旧 leader
读旧地址一定更安全
旧 leader 会自动转发所有写
这只影响 UI
options_en: It may write to an old leader
A stale address is always safer
The old leader automatically forwards all writes
This only affects the UI
why: 协调元数据如果参与正确性，读新鲜度也参与正确性。必要时用 sync 或线性化读确认。
why_en: If coordination metadata drives correctness, read freshness is part of correctness; use sync or linearizable reads when needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

optionExplanations: 读到的是一个已经过时的 leader 地址，服务照着这个地址继续写下去，很可能实际写到的是一个已经不再是 leader 的旧节点，这个写可能被拒绝、丢失或产生歧义。
读到旧地址不但不更安全，反而是风险的来源，这个说法说反了。
旧 leader 不会自动帮你转发所有写请求到真正的新 leader，这不是它的默认行为。
如果协调元数据参与决定写到哪里，读新鲜度就直接影响正确性，不只是 UI 层面的展示问题。
optionExplanations_en: Reading an already-stale leader address and having the service keep writing to it likely means writing to a node that's no longer actually the leader, and that write could get rejected, lost, or produce ambiguous results.
Reading a stale address isn't safer at all — it's actually the source of the risk, so this claim has it backwards.
An old leader doesn't automatically forward every write to the real new leader on your behalf; that's not its default behavior.
If coordination metadata drives where writes go, read freshness directly affects correctness, not just a cosmetic UI concern.

scenario: 两个客户端同时尝试把 /leader 从空改成自己的 ID。
scenario_en: Two clients simultaneously try to change /leader from empty to their own ID.
q: CAS 要正确选主，需要什么保证？
q_en: What guarantee does CAS need for correct leader election?
options: 线性化 compare-and-set
最终一致的读缓存加上客户端反复重试
按客户端本地时钟决定先后
把两次请求排进异步批处理
options_en: A linearizable compare-and-set.
An eventually-consistent read cache plus client retries.
Ordering by each client's local clock.
Batching both requests asynchronously.
why: CAS 只有在所有客户端看到同一个原子顺序时才能选出唯一赢家。弱一致 CAS 可能让两边都以为成功。
why_en: CAS elects one winner only if all clients share one atomic order; weakly consistent CAS can admit two winners.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是抢占本地线程任务，进程内 CAS 就够。
tradeoff: 唯一赢家 vs 协调延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS 只有在当前值仍等于预期值时才写入新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set writes a new value only if the current value still equals the expected value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

codeSample:
CAS(key="leader", expect=old_epoch, update=new_epoch)
# compare-and-set 必须线性化。
# 否则两个候选者可能都以为自己成功。
optionExplanations: 两个客户端同时想把空值改成自己的 ID，只有当所有客户端都基于同一个原子顺序看待这次 compare-and-set 时，才能保证唯一一个真正成功、另一个被拒绝，这正是线性化 CAS 提供的保证。
最终一致的读缓存可能让两个客户端都看到值还是空的，从而各自都以为自己能成功写入，选不出唯一赢家。
客户端本地时钟排序容易受时钟偏差影响，不同客户端各自的判断可能互相矛盾。
异步批处理会让选举结果延迟很久才能确定，也没有原子比较交换这种即时唯一性保证。
optionExplanations_en: With two clients simultaneously trying to change an empty value to their own ID, only when every client shares one atomic view of this compare-and-set can exactly one succeed and the other get rejected — that's what linearizable CAS provides.
An eventually consistent read cache could let both clients see the value as still empty, letting each believe it will succeed, failing to pick a unique winner.
Client-local clock ordering is prone to clock skew, so different clients' judgments could contradict each other.
Asynchronous batch processing would delay the election outcome significantly and lacks the immediate uniqueness guarantee an atomic compare-and-swap provides.

scenario: 三个副本要执行相同的状态机命令。
scenario_en: Three replicas need to execute the same state-machine commands.
q: 应该先保证什么？
q_en: What should be guaranteed first?
options: 所有副本得到同一命令顺序
每个副本按本地网络到达顺序执行
只保证最终收到部分命令
让客户端决定每个副本顺序
options_en: All replicas receive the same command order
Each replica executes in local network arrival order
Only guarantee eventually receiving some commands
Let clients decide each replica order
why: 复制状态机的前提是同输入同顺序。全序广播或共识日志提供这个输入流。
why_en: State-machine replication needs the same inputs in the same order, which total order broadcast or a consensus log provides.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作可交换，例如 G-Counter 增量，严格全序可能不是必需。
tradeoff: 确定性复制 vs 协调成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 全序广播保证所有节点以同一顺序投递同一批消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Total order broadcast makes all nodes deliver the same messages in the same order.

optionExplanations: 要让三个副本执行相同的状态机命令、得到一致的结果，前提是所有副本都拿到完全一样的命令顺序，这才是复制状态机的基础保证，之后才谈得上确定性执行。
每个副本按本地网络到达顺序执行，不同副本网络到达顺序本来就可能不一样，会让各自状态跑偏。
只保证最终收到部分命令达不到复制状态机要求的完整性，会让某些副本落下关键的状态变化。
让客户端各自决定每个副本的执行顺序会让不同副本按不同顺序处理命令，状态机很快就会分叉。
optionExplanations_en: For three replicas executing the same state-machine commands and reaching the same result, the precondition is that all replicas get exactly the same command order — that's the basic guarantee state-machine replication needs before deterministic execution even matters.
Each replica executing in its own local network arrival order fails because different replicas can naturally receive messages in different orders, letting their states drift apart.
Only guaranteeing eventually receiving some commands falls short of the completeness state-machine replication needs, letting some replicas miss critical state changes.
Letting clients each decide each replica's execution order would have different replicas processing commands in different sequences, quickly diverging the state machines.

scenario: 一个 key-value 存储使用共识日志复制命令。
scenario_en: A key-value store replicates commands through a consensus log.
q: 把复制状态机路径排好序。
q_en: Order the replicated state-machine path.
steps: 副本按日志顺序执行命令
leader 把客户端命令追加到日志槽位
多数派确认该槽位
所有副本最终得到同一有序日志
why: 多数派先决定日志槽位，副本再按同一顺序执行。只要状态机确定性，副本状态就会收敛。
why_en: A majority decides log slots, then replicas execute the same ordered log; deterministic state machines converge.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

scenario: 系统要识别哪些设计问题本质上需要节点达成一致。
scenario_en: A system needs to identify which design problems fundamentally require node agreement.
q: 哪些问题常可归约到共识？
q_en: Which problems are commonly reducible to consensus?
options: 选主
原子提交
全序广播
生成 UI 主题色
options_en: Leader election
Atomic commit
Total order broadcast
Generating a UI theme color
why: 选主、原子提交和全序广播都需要节点对某个决定达成一致。UI 主题色不是分布式正确性问题。
why_en: Leader election, atomic commit, and total order broadcast all require nodes to agree on a decision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全序广播保证所有节点以同一顺序投递同一批消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Total order broadcast makes all nodes deliver the same messages in the same order.

optionExplanations: 选主要求所有节点就唯一的一个 leader 达成一致，本质上就是共识问题。
原子提交要求所有参与者对同一个提交或放弃的结果达成一致，同样是共识问题的一种形式。
全序广播要求所有正确节点按同一顺序看到同一批消息，也需要节点间就顺序达成共识。
生成 UI 主题色是纯粹的产品或前端设计决定，跟节点之间要不要就某个值达成一致毫无关系。
optionExplanations_en: Leader election requires all nodes to agree on exactly one leader, fundamentally a consensus problem.
Atomic commit requires all participants to agree on the same commit-or-abort outcome, also a form of the consensus problem.
Total order broadcast requires all correct nodes to see the same batch of messages in the same order, which also needs nodes to reach consensus on ordering.
Generating a UI theme color is a purely product or frontend design decision, unrelated to whether nodes need to agree on some value.

scenario: 你在给面试官解释一致性模型选择。
scenario_en: You are explaining consistency-model choices in an interview.
q: 哪种模型最适合“读必须看到刚成功的写”？
q_en: Which model fits “reads must see a just-completed write”?
options: 线性化
最终一致
因果一致但允许旧读
读未提交
options_en: Linearizability
Eventual consistency
Causal consistency while allowing stale reads
Read uncommitted
why: “刚成功的写后续必须可见”是线性化的新鲜度定义。其他模型可能更快，但要接受旧读。
why_en: A completed write being visible to later reads is the recency guarantee of linearizability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

tradeoff: 读最新值 vs 低延迟旧读
optionExplanations: “刚成功的写必须能被后续读看到”正是线性化对新鲜度的定义，是这几个选项里唯一能满足这个要求的模型。
最终一致明确不保证这一点，它只承诺迟早收敛，不承诺立刻可见。
因果一致但允许旧读，顾名思义就是允许读到旧值，达不到“必须看到”这个强度。
读未提交连已提交的数据都不一定保证看到，比这里的要求弱得多。
optionExplanations_en: A completed write must be visible to later reads is precisely linearizability's recency definition, the only option here that actually satisfies that requirement.
Eventual consistency explicitly doesn't guarantee this — it only promises eventual convergence, not immediate visibility.
Causal consistency while allowing stale reads, as the name says, allows stale reads, falling short of the must be visible strength required.
Read uncommitted doesn't even reliably guarantee seeing committed data, far weaker than what's needed here.

scenario: 多个调度器用 etcd 抢占 /leader，只有空值时才能写入自己。
scenario_en: Several schedulers use etcd to claim /leader, writing their ID only if the key is empty.
q: 这段事务体现什么机制？
q_en: What mechanism does this transaction show?
options: 线性化 CAS 选出单一 leader
异步批量去重
依赖 2PC 协议的 prepare 阶段
物理时钟排序
options_en: Linearizable CAS to elect one leader
Asynchronous batch deduplication
Rely on the prepare phase of 2PC.
Physical-clock ordering
why: etcd 事务把比较和写入放在同一个 Raft 顺序里，因此只有一个客户端能从空值变成 leader。
why_en: The etcd transaction puts compare and write in one Raft order, so only one client can claim the empty leader key.
whenOtherWins: 如果只在单进程内选一个 worker，本地互斥锁更简单。
tradeoff: 分布式唯一性 vs 协调服务依赖

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd 是基于 Raft 的分布式键值协调存储，常用于 Kubernetes 等系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a Raft-backed distributed key-value coordination store used by systems such as Kubernetes.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS 只有在当前值仍等于预期值时才写入新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set writes a new value only if the current value still equals the expected value.

termDefinitions.meaning: Raft 是一种实际常用的崩溃容错共识算法，用 term、leader 和日志复制组织决策。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Raft is a practical crash-fault consensus algorithm organized around terms, leaders, and replicated logs.

codeSample:
etcdctl txn <<EOF
cmp version /leader = 0
then put /leader node-a
else get /leader
EOF
optionExplanations: etcd 把比较（这个 key 是不是空值）和写入（写自己的 ID）放进同一个 Raft 顺序里原子执行，多个调度器同时抢占时，只有恰好在空值状态下执行比较的那一个能成功写入，这正是线性化 CAS 选主的机制。
这不是先攒一批再统一处理的批量操作，而是每次请求都立即原子生效的操作，不是异步批量去重。
这里没有涉及分阶段的准备投票再提交，是一次性的原子比较写入，不是 2PC 的 prepare 阶段。
排序靠的是 Raft 内部的日志顺序，不是靠物理时钟来决定谁先谁后。
optionExplanations_en: etcd fuses the comparison (is this key still empty) and the write (write my own ID) into one atomic step within the same Raft order, so when multiple schedulers race, only the one that happens to execute its comparison while the key is still empty succeeds — exactly linearizable CAS electing one leader.
This isn't a batch-then-process-together operation; each request takes effect atomically and immediately, not asynchronous batch deduplication.
There's no separate prepare-then-vote-then-commit phasing here, it's a one-shot atomic compare-and-write, not 2PC's prepare phase.
The ordering comes from Raft's internal log order, not from physical clocks deciding who came first.

scenario: 2PC 参与者重启后发现本地有 prepared 事务。
scenario_en: A 2PC participant restarts and finds a prepared transaction in its local log.
q: 把恢复链排好序。
q_en: Order the recovery chain.
steps: 参与者联系协调者查询最终决定
参与者读取本地 prepared 记录
按 commit/abort 决定完成并释放资源
如果协调者不可达，继续保持 in-doubt 状态
why: prepared 记录说明它不能单方面做决定。协调者不可达时只能等待或人工恢复。
why_en: A prepared record means the participant cannot decide alone; if the coordinator is unreachable, it remains in doubt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

scenario: 协调服务有大量只读服务发现查询，偶尔旧列表可接受。
scenario_en: A coordination service receives many read-only service-discovery queries, and a slightly stale list is acceptable.
q: 怎样减轻共识组压力？
q_en: How can it reduce load on the consensus group?
options: 使用只读缓存副本或普通 DNS 风格发现
每次查询都强制 quorum read
把所有业务数据塞进共识日志
禁用本地缓存
options_en: Use read-only cache replicas or DNS-style discovery
Force a quorum read for every query
Put all business data in the consensus log
Disable local caches
why: 服务发现和选主的正确性要求不同。允许旧列表时，用缓存读能减少 leader/quorum 压力。
why_en: Service discovery has weaker correctness needs than leader election, so cached reads can reduce leader or quorum load.
whenOtherWins: 如果读的是当前 leader 或锁持有者，就要用线性化读或版本校验。
tradeoff: 读扩展 vs 元数据新鲜度
optionExplanations: 服务发现的查询大多是只读的，偶尔旧列表能接受，用只读缓存副本或者类似 DNS 的发现机制来分担读压力，就不用每次都打到共识组本身。
每次查询都强制走 quorum read，会让共识组承担远超它承受能力的读流量，跟“大量只读查询”这个前提矛盾。
把所有业务数据塞进共识日志会让本该轻量的共识组背上不该有的存储和吞吐压力，违背它适合小而关键数据的定位。
禁用本地缓存恰恰会让所有查询都必须打到源头，加重共识组的压力，跟减轻压力的目标相反。
optionExplanations_en: Since most service-discovery queries are read-only and an occasional stale list is tolerable, using read-only cache replicas or DNS-style discovery to absorb the read load means not every query has to hit the consensus group itself.
Forcing a quorum read on every query would burden the consensus group with far more read traffic than it can bear, contradicting the premise of a large volume of read-only queries.

Stuffing all business data into the consensus log would saddle an otherwise lightweight consensus group with storage and throughput it was never meant to carry, against its fit for small, critical data.
Disabling local caches would force every query to hit the source directly, increasing pressure on the consensus group, the opposite of the goal of relieving it.

scenario: Raft 集群里一个节点被攻击后故意给不同 peer 发不同日志。
scenario_en: In a Raft cluster, a compromised node intentionally sends different logs to different peers.
q: 普通 Raft 假设覆盖吗？
q_en: Does ordinary Raft cover this assumption?
options: 不覆盖 Byzantine 行为
完全覆盖任意恶意节点
只要加 NTP 就覆盖
只要把节点数加到 2 就能覆盖
options_en: It does not cover Byzantine behavior
Yes; it fully handles arbitrary malicious nodes
Adding NTP covers it
Just raise the node count to 2 to cover it.
why: 普通共识算法通常假设节点不会撒谎。恶意环境需要 BFT 协议和签名等额外机制。
why_en: Ordinary consensus usually assumes nodes do not lie; malicious environments need BFT protocols and signatures.

termDefinitions.meaning: Raft 是一种实际常用的崩溃容错共识算法，用 term、leader 和日志复制组织决策。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Raft is a practical crash-fault consensus algorithm organized around terms, leaders, and replicated logs.

optionExplanations: 普通 Raft 通常假设节点最多是崩溃停止，不会主动撒谎或篡改消息，一旦有节点被攻击后故意给不同 peer 发不同内容，这已经超出了它的故障模型，普通 Raft 覆盖不了。
普通共识算法明确不覆盖任意恶意行为，说它完全覆盖是不成立的，恶意场景需要额外的 BFT 机制。
NTP 解决的是时钟同步问题，跟节点会不会故意撒谎、发送矛盾消息毫不相关。
节点数量增加不会改变算法本身的故障模型假设，两个节点同样防不住一个恶意撒谎的节点。
optionExplanations_en: Ordinary Raft typically assumes a node at worst crashes and stops, never actively lying or tampering with messages, so once a compromised node deliberately sends different peers different content, that's outside its fault model — plain Raft doesn't cover it.
Ordinary consensus algorithms explicitly don't cover arbitrary malicious behavior, so claiming it fully covers it doesn't hold; malicious scenarios need additional BFT mechanisms.
NTP addresses clock synchronization, entirely unrelated to whether a node deliberately lies or sends contradictory messages.
Adding more nodes doesn't change the algorithm's own fault-model assumptions; two nodes are equally unable to defend against one maliciously lying node.

scenario: 你需要实现一个容错的线性化寄存器。
scenario_en: You need to implement a fault-tolerant linearizable register.
q: 实践中通常会走向什么？
q_en: Where does this usually lead in practice?
options: 共识或等价的多数派复制协议
只用客户端缓存
只按各节点本地时间排序
每日批处理修正
options_en: Consensus or an equivalent majority-replication protocol
Only client-side caching
Order only by each node's local time.
Daily batch repair
why: 容错线性化需要节点对值的顺序达成一致，和共识问题非常接近。不要轻易手写。
why_en: Fault-tolerant linearizability needs nodes to agree on value order, which is very close to consensus.
whenOtherWins: 如果单机故障不可接受程度低，单主加人工恢复可能够用但会牺牲自动终止。
tradeoff: 自动容错新鲜度 vs 协议复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum 是做决定所需的节点集合；多数派 quorum 通过交集避免冲突决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the node set required for a decision; majority quorums overlap to prevent conflicting decisions.

optionExplanations: 要在有节点可能故障的情况下让一个寄存器仍然表现出线性化的行为，本质上要求所有节点就每次读写的顺序达成一致，这已经非常接近共识问题，通常就会走向共识或等价的多数派复制协议。
只靠客户端缓存解决不了多个节点之间要不要就顺序达成一致这个根本问题，缓存只是本地的加速手段。
只按本地时间排序会受时钟偏差影响，给不出容错场景下可靠的线性化保证。
每日批处理修正是事后补救，跟“容错的线性化寄存器”这种要求实时正确顺序的场景完全不匹配。
optionExplanations_en: Getting a register to still behave linearizably despite possible node failures fundamentally requires all nodes to agree on the order of every read and write — that's already very close to the consensus problem, and in practice leads to consensus or an equivalent majority-replication protocol.
Client-side caching alone doesn't address the underlying question of whether multiple nodes agree on ordering; caching is just a local speedup, not a coordination mechanism.
Ordering only by local time is subject to clock skew and can't provide a reliable linearizable guarantee in a fault-tolerant setting.
Daily batch repair is an after-the-fact fix, a poor match for a fault-tolerant linearizable register that needs correct real-time ordering.

scenario: 一个系统只在“谁是 leader”上用 ZooKeeper，业务写入仍走各分区数据库。
scenario_en: A system uses ZooKeeper only for “who is leader,” while business writes go to partition databases.
q: 这种边界为什么常见？
q_en: Why is this boundary common?
options: 把少量协调决策交给共识，避免每条业务写都付共识成本
ZooKeeper 更适合直接存放所有订单明细
业务写入不需要任何正确性
分区数据库不能做持久化
options_en: It sends small coordination decisions to consensus without charging every business write
ZooKeeper is better for storing all order line-items.
Business writes need no correctness
Partition databases cannot persist data
why: 共识很贵但强，适合小而关键的控制面。数据面可以用分区、事务和复制各自扩展。
why_en: Consensus is strong but costly, so it often belongs in the small control plane while the data plane scales separately.
whenOtherWins: 如果每条业务写本身就是全局唯一决定，例如证券撮合，数据面也可能需要强顺序。
tradeoff: 控制面强一致 vs 数据面吞吐

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper 是基于共识的协调服务，常用于小规模元数据、选主、锁和成员通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a consensus-backed coordination service for small metadata, leader election, locks, and membership notifications.

optionExplanations: 把谁是 leader 这种小而关键的决策交给共识去管，业务写入照样走各自分区的数据库，这样既拿到了共识的强保证，又不用让每一条业务写都背上共识的协调成本。
ZooKeeper 适合小而关键的协调元数据，不适合存放所有订单明细这种大体量、高吞吐的业务数据。
业务写入同样需要正确性保证，只是它可以靠分区数据库自己的事务和复制机制来满足，不代表不需要任何正确性。
分区数据库完全具备持久化能力，这不是它被排除在共识职责之外的原因。
optionExplanations_en: Handing a small but critical decision like who is leader to consensus while letting business writes keep going through their own partitioned databases gets the strong guarantee of consensus without saddling every business write with its coordination cost.
ZooKeeper suits small, critical coordination metadata, not storing high-volume, high-throughput business data like every order row.

Business writes still need correctness guarantees too, they just get satisfied through the partitioned database's own transaction and replication mechanisms — it doesn't mean no correctness is needed.
Partitioned databases are fully capable of persisting data; that's not why they're excluded from consensus's responsibility.

q: 第 9 章的主线是什么？
q_en: What is Chapter 9’s main storyline?
text: 强一致从{{线性化}}讲到{{因果和全序}}，再走到{{原子提交和共识}}；共同问题是让节点在故障中对顺序或决定达成一致。
text_en: Strong consistency moves from {{linearizability}} to {{causality and total order}}, then to {{atomic commit and consensus}}; the common problem is agreement on order or decisions despite faults.
why: 面试里要先问哪条路径真的需要强协调；不是所有读写都该付共识成本。
why_en: In interviews, first ask which path truly needs strong coordination; not every read or write should pay consensus cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性化让多副本对象看起来像单副本，并保证成功写入后后续读能看到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes replicated data look like one copy and ensures later reads see a completed write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全序广播保证所有节点以同一顺序投递同一批消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Total order broadcast makes all nodes deliver the same messages in the same order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交先让参与者 prepare，再由协调者决定 commit 或 abort。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit first asks participants to prepare, then the coordinator decides commit or abort.

scenario: 你要每天重算一次推荐候选集，输入是昨天冻结的点击日志和用户快照，结果允许几小时后上线。
scenario_en: You need to recompute recommendation candidates once a day from frozen click logs and a user snapshot, and results may arrive hours later.
q: 这个任务更像哪类系统？
q_en: What kind of system does this task fit?
options: 在线请求服务
批处理作业
低延迟流处理
同步 RPC 聚合
options_en: Online request service
Batch processing job
Low-latency stream processing
Synchronous RPC aggregation
why: 输入有固定边界，输出也不需要立刻返回给用户，所以我会把它当成批处理作业。代价是新数据要等下一轮或增量管线才能体现。
why_en: Because the input is bounded and the output is not user-blocking, this is a batch job, with freshness limited by the run schedule.
whenOtherWins: 如果推荐必须在用户点击后几秒内改变，就该把核心更新放进流处理或在线特征服务。
tradeoff: 吞吐与可重跑性 vs 低延迟新鲜度

termDefinitions.meaning: 远程过程调用：像调用本地函数一样请求另一个服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Remote Procedure Call means invoking another service as if it were a local function.

optionExplanations: 在线请求服务要求实时响应用户请求，跟这里“输入昨天冻结的日志、结果几小时后上线”完全不匹配。
输入边界固定、结果几小时后才上线也可以接受，这正是批处理作业的典型形状。
低延迟流处理是为了尽快处理持续到来的事件，跟这里“每天重算一次”的节奏不符。
同步 RPC 聚合要求调用方等待结果立刻返回，跟这里允许几小时后才上线的宽松时限不匹配。
optionExplanations_en: An online request service must respond to users in real time, which doesn't match input frozen from yesterday's logs with results going live hours later.
With a fixed time boundary on the input and no requirement to return results to a user immediately, this is a textbook shape for a batch job.
Low-latency stream processing exists to handle continuously arriving events as fast as possible, mismatched with the once-a-day recompute cadence here.
Synchronous RPC aggregation requires the caller to wait for an immediate result, mismatched with the generous hours-later deadline allowed here.

scenario: 你临时分析 20GB Nginx 日志，只想找访问最多的 URL，结果今天交付，不准备长期维护一套服务。
scenario_en: You need a one-off analysis over 20 GB of Nginx logs to find the most visited URLs today, with no long-lived service to maintain.
q: 先用哪种实现更合适？
q_en: Which implementation should you try first?
options: Unix 管道串 awk/sort
直接去写后台任务和数据库的服务
把日志逐行发进消息队列
先做跨团队平台 API
options_en: A Unix pipeline with awk and sort
Just write a background job and a database service directly.
Send log lines into a message queue
Design a cross-team platform API first
why: 一次性日志分析更看重快速组合和可检查中间结果，Unix 管道能把每一步用文本流接起来。代价是它主要适合单机或少量机器上的临时处理。
why_en: For one-off log analysis, a Unix pipeline gives fast composition and inspectable intermediate output, but it is mainly a single-machine tool.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个分析要每天稳定运行、被多人依赖，应该迁到受调度和监控的批处理工作流。
tradeoff: 临时组合速度 vs 长期运维能力

termDefinitions.meaning: Unix 管道：把一个进程的标准输出连接到下一个进程的标准输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Unix pipe connects one process's standard output to another process's standard input.

diagram:
flowchart LR
  Log["log file"] --> Awk["extract URL"]
  Awk --> Sort["sort"]
  Sort --> Uniq["count"]
  Uniq --> Head["top N"]
optionExplanations: 一次性分析、当天交付、不打算长期维护服务，Unix 管道把 awk、sort 这些小工具串起来能很快拼出结果，还能随时看中间输出对不对。
写后台任务和数据库服务需要搭建和维护一整套长期运行的系统，跟“今天交付、不长期维护”这个前提不成比例。
把日志逐行发进消息队列引入了额外的基础设施和排队开销，对一次性的临时分析来说是不必要的复杂度。
先做跨团队平台 API 是为长期复用设计的重量级工程，跟眼前这个一次性任务的规模完全不匹配。
optionExplanations_en: For a one-off analysis delivered today with no intent to maintain a long-running service, a Unix pipeline chaining small tools like awk and sort gets results fast and lets you inspect intermediate output along the way.
Building a service with workers and a database means standing up and maintaining a long-running system, disproportionate to a deliver-today, no-long-term-maintenance task.
Sending log lines into a message queue introduces extra infrastructure and queueing overhead, unnecessary complexity for a one-off ad hoc analysis.
Designing a cross-team platform API first is heavyweight engineering meant for long-term reuse, completely mismatched with the scale of this one-off task.

scenario: 日志里可能有上亿条记录，URL 种类数未知，单机内存只有 16GB。你要按 URL 计数。
scenario_en: The log may contain hundreds of millions of rows, the number of distinct URLs is unknown, and the machine has 16 GB of RAM.
q: 为什么外部排序比内存哈希更稳？
q_en: Why is external sorting safer than an in-memory hash table here?
options: 排序可以分块落盘并归并，工作集超过内存也能跑
排序让所有 URL 计数都变成 O(1) 随机写
内存哈希天然把热门 URL 分散到多台机器
内存哈希能自动从崩溃点恢复
options_en: Sorting can spill chunks to disk and merge them, so it can handle a working set larger than memory
Sorting turns all URL counts into O(1) random writes
An in-memory hash table automatically spreads hot URLs across machines
An in-memory hash table automatically resumes after a crash
why: 种类数未知时，内存哈希可能被不同 key 数打爆；外部排序用磁盘换内存上限。代价是排序要读写临时文件，内存放得下时哈希通常更快。
why_en: External sorting is safer when distinct keys may exceed memory because it spills and merges on disk, trading I/O for bounded RAM use.
tradeoff: 内存速度 vs 磁盘兜底

termDefinitions.meaning: 外部排序：数据大于内存时，先排序小块再在磁盘上归并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: External sort sorts chunks that fit in memory and then merges them from disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希聚合：用哈希表按 key 累加计数或指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash aggregation uses a hash table to accumulate values by key.

optionExplanations: URL 种类数未知时，外部排序能把数据分块写到磁盘再归并，工作集超过内存也能正常跑完，不会被数据规模突然打垮。
排序本身要做大量比较和归并操作，不会把计数变成 O(1) 随机写，这个说法夸大了排序的效果。
内存哈希表运行在单机内存里，不会自动把热门 URL 分散到多台机器，这需要额外的分布式机制。
内存哈希表的数据都在进程内存里，一旦进程崩溃数据就没了，不具备自动从崩溃点恢复的能力。
optionExplanations_en: When the number of distinct URLs is unknown, external sorting can spill chunks to disk and merge them, so it keeps running correctly even when the working set exceeds memory, instead of suddenly blowing up.
Sorting itself does a lot of comparison and merging work; it doesn't turn counting into O(1) random writes, this claim overstates what sorting does.
An in-memory hash table runs within one machine's memory and doesn't automatically spread hot URLs across multiple machines — that needs a separate distributed mechanism.
An in-memory hash table's data lives in process memory, so a crash loses it entirely; it has no built-in ability to resume from a crash point.

scenario: 你在评审一个内部数据工具，目标是让别的团队把它接进自己的脚本和工作流。
scenario_en: You are reviewing an internal data tool that other teams should be able to compose into their scripts and workflows.
q: 哪些设计更符合 Unix 式可组合性？
q_en: Which designs improve Unix-style composability?
options: 从 stdin 读、向 stdout 写
只提供需要人工点击的图形界面
输出稳定的文本或记录格式
把业务逻辑和文件路径硬编码在一起
options_en: Read from stdin and write to stdout
Expose only a manually clicked GUI
Emit a stable text or record format
Hard-code business logic together with file paths
why: 可组合工具把数据接口做窄，把输入输出交给外部连线。这样脚本、管道和调度器都能复用同一个程序。
why_en: Composable tools keep the data interface narrow and let external wiring decide where input and output go.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标准输入：进程默认读取输入数据的文件描述符。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Standard input is the default file descriptor a process reads from.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标准输出：进程默认写出结果的文件描述符。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Standard output is the default file descriptor a process writes to.

optionExplanations: 从 stdin 读、向 stdout 写，让工具能被任意脚本、管道或调度器直接接进去，不用关心它内部是怎么实现的。
只提供需要人工点击的图形界面完全没法被脚本自动调用，跟“接进自己的脚本和工作流”这个目标正相反。
输出稳定的文本或记录格式，让下游工具能可靠地解析这份输出，不用担心格式随时变化。
把业务逻辑和文件路径硬编码在一起，会让工具没法在不同团队、不同环境下复用，违背了可组合性的初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Reading from stdin and writing to stdout lets the tool be plugged directly into any script, pipeline, or scheduler without anyone needing to know how it's implemented internally.
Exposing only a manually clicked GUI can't be invoked programmatically by scripts at all, the opposite of the goal of integrating it into other teams' scripts and workflows.
Emitting a stable text or record format lets downstream tools reliably parse the output without worrying about the format shifting unpredictably.
Hard-coding business logic together with file paths keeps the tool from being reused across different teams and environments, defeating the point of composability.

scenario: 多个小工具要串起来处理日志，但它们由不同团队用不同语言写。
scenario_en: Several small tools written by different teams in different languages must be chained together to process logs.
q: 统一字节流接口带来的主要好处是什么？
q_en: What is the main benefit of a uniform byte-stream interface?
options: 工具不用共享同一种运行时也能连接
每个工具都能理解所有业务字段语义
它自动保证 JSON schema 向后兼容
它消除了所有解析错误
options_en: Tools can connect without sharing the same runtime
Every tool understands the business meaning of all fields
It automatically guarantees JSON schema backward compatibility
It eliminates all parsing errors
why: 统一接口让工具只约定输入输出形状，不约定内部语言和库。代价是文本解析弱，字段变更仍需要约定和测试。
why_en: A uniform byte-stream interface decouples tool internals from wiring, though parsing and schema discipline are still your job.

termDefinitions.meaning: JSON：常用的文本数据交换格式，用对象和数组表示结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: JavaScript Object Notation is a text format for structured data made of objects and arrays.

optionExplanations: 字节流是最低共同分母，不同语言、不同运行时写的工具只要都读写这种统一的字节流接口，就能直接串起来，不用共享同一套运行时环境。
统一的字节流接口本身不携带业务语义，每个工具依然只理解自己需要的那部分字段，不会自动理解所有业务字段的含义。
统一字节流只是传输接口，不涉及 JSON schema 的版本管理，字段的向后兼容还是要靠约定和测试自己保证。
字节流本身不做任何语义校验，格式错乱、字段缺失这些解析错误依然可能发生，不会被这个接口自动消除。
optionExplanations_en: A byte stream is the lowest common denominator; tools written in different languages and runtimes only need to read and write this uniform interface to connect directly, without sharing the same runtime.
A uniform byte-stream interface carries no business semantics on its own; each tool still only understands the fields it needs, not automatically the meaning of every business field.
A uniform byte stream is just the transport interface; it doesn't manage JSON schema versioning — backward compatibility for fields still needs to be handled by convention and testing.
A byte stream performs no semantic validation on its own; parsing errors like malformed data or missing fields can still happen, not automatically eliminated by this interface.

scenario: 一个清洗程序既可读本地文件，也可接管道，也可由调度器读取 HDFS 路径。你希望它的核心逻辑不用改。
scenario_en: A cleaning program may read local files, a pipe, or an HDFS path via a scheduler, and you want the core logic unchanged.
q: 应该怎样组织程序边界？
q_en: How should you structure the program boundary?
options: 核心逻辑处理输入流，外部配置负责来源和去向
直接在代码里写死生产环境的绝对文件路径
每种输入来源复制一份清洗逻辑
让程序自己启动所有下游任务
options_en: Let core logic process an input stream while external config wires sources and sinks
Hard-code absolute production file paths directly in the code.
Copy the cleaning logic for every input source
Have the program launch all downstream tasks itself
why: 把逻辑和连线分开后，同一段处理逻辑能被命令行、调度器和测试复用。代价是你需要把配置、契约和错误处理做清楚。
why_en: Separating logic from wiring lets the same processor run under a shell, scheduler, or test harness with different inputs and outputs.
whenOtherWins: 如果是一次性脚本且路径不会复用，硬编码能更快交付，但很快会变成维护负担。
tradeoff: 复用测试性 vs 一次性速度

termDefinitions.meaning: HDFS：Hadoop 的分布式文件系统，把大文件切块并复制到多台机器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hadoop Distributed FileSystem stores large files as replicated blocks across machines.

optionExplanations: 核心逻辑只处理一条输入流，具体这条流是本地文件、管道还是 HDFS 路径，交给外部配置去决定，这样核心逻辑本身完全不用改动就能适应不同来源。
在代码里写死生产文件路径，会让这段逻辑只能用于那一个特定环境，没法直接用于管道或测试场景。
每种输入来源复制一份清洗逻辑，会让同一段业务规则散落在多份代码里，改一处容易漏改另一处。
让程序自己启动所有下游任务，把编排职责也塞进了这段本该只管清洗的逻辑里，违背了逻辑和连线分离的原则。
optionExplanations_en: With the core logic only processing an input stream, whether that stream comes from a local file, a pipe, or an HDFS path is decided by external configuration, so the core logic itself never needs to change across sources.
Hard-coding production file paths in the code locks that logic into one specific environment, unusable directly in a pipeline or a test.
Copying the cleaning logic for every input source scatters the same business rule across multiple copies of code, making it easy to update one and forget another.
Having the program launch all downstream tasks itself stuffs orchestration responsibility into logic that should only be doing cleaning, violating the separation of logic from wiring.

scenario: 数据清洗结果异常，你需要快速定位是哪一步把字段弄坏了。工作流由多个小步骤组成。
scenario_en: A data cleaning output looks wrong, and the workflow is made of several small steps; you need to find where a field was corrupted.
q: 哪种组织方式最利于排查？
q_en: Which organization makes debugging easiest?
options: 每步输出可单独查看的中间结果
把所有步骤合成一个不可中断二进制
只保留最终聚合数字
让错误重试直到成功但不记录输入
options_en: Make each step's intermediate output inspectable
Merge all steps into one opaque binary
Keep only the final aggregate number
Retry errors until success without recording inputs
why: 能查看中间结果，就可以二分定位坏数据从哪一步开始出现。代价是中间结果可能暴露敏感数据，需要访问控制和清理策略。
why_en: Inspectable intermediate output lets you localize bad data step by step, with access control needed for sensitive records.
optionExplanations: 每一步的输出都能单独查看，出问题时就能一步步比对，二分定位到底是哪一步把字段弄坏了，而不用从头猜。
把所有步骤合成一个不可中断的二进制，出问题时完全看不到中间发生了什么，排查只能靠猜。
只保留最终聚合数字，中间过程完全不可见，一旦最终结果不对，根本无从定位问题出在哪一步。
让错误重试直到成功但不记录输入，会让排查者既看不到中间结果，也不知道当初到底喂了什么数据进去。
optionExplanations_en: With each step's output individually inspectable, you can compare step by step when something breaks and binary-search which stage corrupted the field, instead of guessing from scratch.
Merging all steps into one opaque binary hides everything that happened in between, leaving debugging to pure guesswork.
Keeping only the final aggregate number leaves the intermediate process entirely invisible, so if the final result is wrong there's no way to trace which step is at fault.
Retrying errors until success without recording inputs leaves an investigator with neither the intermediate output nor a record of what data actually went in.

scenario: 你要在普通服务器集群上存 PB 级日志，机器和磁盘会坏，批处理会全量扫描这些文件。
scenario_en: You need to store petabytes of logs on commodity servers, tolerate disk and machine failures, and run batch scans over those files.
q: 为什么选 HDFS 这类共享无关文件系统？
q_en: Why choose an HDFS-style shared-nothing filesystem?
options: 它把文件块复制到多台普通机器，计算可贴近数据
它让所有的节点都同时写入同一整块本地磁盘
它把每个查询都变成单机 SQL 扫描
它保证每条记录都有跨表事务语义
options_en: It replicates file blocks across commodity machines so computation can run next to the data.
It has all nodes write the same local disk at once.
It turns every query into a single-machine SQL scan.
It gives every record cross-table transaction semantics.
why: 批处理扫描大文件时，移动计算通常比移动 PB 级数据便宜。HDFS 用复制换故障容忍，但不提供 OLTP 事务语义。
why_en: For large scans, moving compute to replicated file blocks is cheaper than moving petabytes of data, but HDFS is not an OLTP transaction store.
whenOtherWins: 如果主要需求是低延迟随机更新和事务，关系数据库或专用 KV 存储更合适。
tradeoff: 顺序扫描吞吐 vs 随机事务能力

termDefinitions.meaning: HDFS：面向大文件顺序读写的分布式文件系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hadoop Distributed FileSystem is a distributed filesystem optimized for large sequential files.

termDefinitions.meaning: OLTP：面向用户请求的在线事务处理，强调低延迟读写和并发控制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Online Transaction Processing handles user-facing transactional reads and writes with concurrency control.

optionExplanations: HDFS 把文件块复制到多台普通机器上，机器或磁盘坏了也不会丢数据，批处理还能把计算调度到数据所在的那台机器附近跑，省掉搬运 PB 级数据的开销。
HDFS 不是让所有节点同时写同一个本地磁盘，每个文件块是被复制到不同机器，不是共享同一块盘。
HDFS 是一个分布式文件系统，不会把查询变成单机 SQL，查询能力是上层计算框架的事，跟 HDFS 本身无关。
HDFS 提供的是文件级的存储和复制，不提供跨表事务这种数据库层面的语义保证。
optionExplanations_en: HDFS replicates file blocks across commodity machines, so a broken machine or disk doesn't lose data, and batch computation can be scheduled near wherever a block already lives, avoiding the cost of shuffling petabytes around.
HDFS doesn't let every node write the same local disk simultaneously; each file block is replicated across different machines, not shared on one disk.
HDFS is a distributed filesystem and doesn't turn a query into single-node SQL; query capability belongs to the compute framework layered on top, not to HDFS itself.
HDFS provides file-level storage and replication; it doesn't provide database-level guarantees like cross-table transactions.

scenario: 一个 MapReduce 作业要扫描 500TB 日志。集群网络容易成为瓶颈，但每台机器本地有一部分 HDFS block。
scenario_en: A MapReduce job scans 500 TB of logs. The cluster network is a bottleneck, and each machine stores some HDFS blocks locally.
q: 调度器为什么尽量把 mapper 放到数据所在机器？
q_en: Why does the scheduler try to place mappers where the data lives?
options: 减少跨网络读取大块输入数据
让 reducer 永远不需要 shuffle
保证所有任务在同一秒结束
让 mapper 共享同一个内存堆
options_en: To reduce cross-network reads of large input blocks
To make reducers never need a shuffle
To guarantee all tasks finish in the same second
To make mappers share one memory heap
why: 输入块很大时，本地读能省掉最重的网络流量。shuffle 仍然可能发生，因为 mapper 输出通常要按 key 重新分区。
why_en: Local mapper placement saves heavy input network traffic, while the shuffle may still move mapper output by key.

termDefinitions.meaning: mapper：MapReduce 中处理输入分片并输出 key-value 记录的任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mapper processes an input split and emits key-value records.

termDefinitions.meaning: shuffle：按 key 重新分区、排序并把 mapper 输出送到 reducer 的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shuffle repartitions, sorts, and transfers mapper output to reducers by key.

optionExplanations: 扫描的输入块本身就很大，把 mapper 调度到数据所在的机器上运行，能省掉这部分数据跨网络传输的最重开销，这是数据局部性优化的核心目的。
reducer 通常仍然需要按 key 重新分区收集 mapper 的输出，数据局部性优化的是输入读取，不会让 shuffle 消失。
任务放到数据所在机器只影响读取效率，不能保证所有任务同一秒结束，不同任务的处理量和速度本来就可能不一样。
每个 mapper 运行在自己的进程或容器里，各自有独立的内存空间，不会共享同一个内存堆。
optionExplanations_en: With the input blocks themselves being huge, scheduling a mapper to run on the machine that already holds the data saves the heaviest part of the cost — moving that data across the network — which is the whole point of data locality.
Reducers typically still need to collect mapper output repartitioned by key, so data locality optimizes input reads but doesn't make the shuffle disappear.
Placing tasks near the data only improves read efficiency; it doesn't guarantee every task finishes in the same second, since different tasks can naturally have different workloads and speeds.
Each mapper runs in its own process or container with its own separate memory space; they don't share one memory heap.

scenario: 你要向候选人解释一次 MapReduce 从输入文件到最终结果的主路径。
scenario_en: You need to explain the main path of a MapReduce job from input files to final output.
q: MapReduce 作业的执行顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the execution order of a MapReduce job?
steps: reducer 按 key 拉取并归并 mapper 输出
mapper 读取输入分片并产生 key-value
框架按 key 分区、排序 mapper 输出
成功任务的输出被提交到最终目录
why: MapReduce 的核心是先并行提取 key-value，再用 shuffle 把同 key 数据带到同一个 reducer。最终提交通常只暴露成功任务的输出。
why_en: MapReduce first emits key-value pairs in parallel, then shuffles equal keys to reducers before committing successful output.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  In["input blocks"] --> Map["map"]
  Map --> Shuffle["partition + sort"]
  Shuffle --> Reduce["reduce"]
  Reduce --> Out["committed output"]

termDefinitions.meaning: key-value：用 key 决定分组或分区，用 value 承载记录内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A key-value record uses the key for grouping or partitioning and the value for payload.

scenario: 一个 reducer 需要一次处理某个 user_id 的全部活动事件。输入来自很多 mapper。
scenario_en: A reducer must process all activity events for a given user_id, and the input comes from many mappers.
q: MapReduce 隐式排序的关键作用是什么？
q_en: What is the key role of MapReduce's implicit sort?
options: 让同一个 key 的记录连续到达 reducer
让每个 mapper 都输出一个全局唯一的 ID
让 reducer 可以随机访问远端数据库
让所有 key 按业务重要性排序
options_en: Make records with the same key arrive contiguously at the reducer
Make each mapper emit a globally unique ID.
Let reducers randomly query a remote database
Sort all keys by business importance
why: 连续的同 key 记录让 reducer 可以用一个迭代器流式处理一组数据，不必把所有 key 都放内存。排序成本很高，所以新执行引擎会尽量只在需要时排序。
why_en: The implicit sort groups equal keys contiguously so reducers can stream one group at a time, at the cost of expensive sorting.

termDefinitions.meaning: reducer：接收某个 key 的一组 value 并输出聚合或连接结果的任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reducer receives all values for a key and emits aggregate or joined output.

optionExplanations: 隐式排序让同一个 user_id 的记录在到达 reducer 时是连续排列的，reducer 就能用一个迭代器顺序流过这组数据，不用把这个用户的所有事件都塞进内存。
每个 mapper 输出的 key 本身来自输入数据，排序不会给每条记录生成全局唯一 ID，这跟排序的作用无关。
reducer 处理的是已经到达的、经过 shuffle 和排序的数据，不涉及去随机访问一个远端数据库。
排序是按 key 的字节或值来比较排列的，不会按业务重要性这种语义信息去排序。
optionExplanations_en: The implicit sort places all records for the same user_id contiguously by the time they reach the reducer, letting it stream through that group with one iterator instead of loading every event for that user into memory.
The key each mapper outputs comes from the input data itself; sorting doesn't generate a globally unique ID for each record, that's unrelated to what sorting does.
A reducer processes data that has already arrived through shuffle and sort; it doesn't randomly query a remote database.
Sorting compares and arranges by the key's bytes or values, not by semantic business importance.

scenario: 你的 MapReduce 作业 reducer 数量太少，少数任务运行很久；太多时，每个任务开销和小文件数量又变高。
scenario_en: Your MapReduce job has too few reducers and some run forever; too many reducers increase task overhead and create many small files.
q: reducer 数量主要在权衡什么？
q_en: What tradeoff does the reducer count control?
options: 并行度与任务/文件开销
SQL 语法与对象存储价格
压缩率与 JSON 字段名长度
用户请求延迟与浏览器缓存
options_en: Parallelism versus task and file overhead
SQL syntax versus object storage price
Compression ratio versus JSON field-name length
User request latency versus browser cache
why: 更多 reducer 能把 key 空间切得更细，提高并行度；但调度、网络连接和输出文件也会变多。这个数字通常要按数据量、key 分布和下游读取方式调。
why_en: More reducers increase key-space parallelism, but they also add scheduling, network, and output-file overhead.
optionExplanations: reducer 越多，key 空间被切得越细，并行度越高；但每个任务本身都有调度开销，产出的小文件数量也会跟着变多，这正是这个数字要权衡的两头。
这里讨论的是并行度和任务开销的取舍，跟 SQL 语法或对象存储定价没有关系。
reducer 数量的取舍跟压缩率、JSON 字段名长度这些编码细节完全不是一个维度的问题。
这里讨论的是批处理内部 reducer 的调度问题，跟用户面对的请求延迟或浏览器缓存无关。
optionExplanations_en: More reducers slice the key space finer, raising parallelism, but each task also carries its own scheduling overhead and produces more output files — that's exactly the tension being weighed here.
This is a tradeoff between parallelism and task overhead, unrelated to SQL syntax or object storage pricing.
The reducer-count tradeoff has nothing to do with encoding details like compression ratio or JSON field-name length.
This is about internal reducer scheduling within batch processing, unrelated to user-facing request latency or browser caching.

scenario: 推荐系统由 60 个批处理步骤组成，后一步必须等前一步产出完整数据集后才能开始。
scenario_en: A recommender workflow has 60 batch steps, and each later step waits for the prior step's complete dataset.
q: 为什么需要工作流调度器？
q_en: Why do you need a workflow scheduler?
options: 管理依赖、重试、可见产物和运行历史
把所有步骤自动改写成单个 SQL
保证每个步骤都不需要输入数据
替代所有监控和容量规划
options_en: To manage dependencies, retries, visible outputs, and run history
To automatically rewrite all steps into one SQL query
To guarantee each step needs no input data
To replace all monitoring and capacity planning
why: MapReduce 本身只知道单个作业，复杂链路需要外部系统决定何时启动、失败后重跑哪一段、产物在哪里。调度器不消除数据依赖，只把依赖显式化。
why_en: MapReduce understands one job at a time, so complex pipelines need a scheduler for dependencies, retries, artifacts, and history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 产物：作业完成后可被下游或用户引用的数据输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An artifact is a durable output dataset that downstream jobs or users can reference.

optionExplanations: 60 个步骤之间有严格的先后依赖，需要有系统知道该按什么顺序启动、哪一步失败了该重跑哪一段、每一步产出的数据放在哪，这正是工作流调度器要管的事。
60 个步骤各自有自己的处理逻辑和依赖关系，不可能被自动改写成一个单一的 SQL 查询。
每个步骤恰恰需要依赖前一步产出的数据才能开始，说保证每步都不需要输入数据跟场景描述矛盾。
调度器管理的是依赖和运行历史这类编排问题，不能替代监控告警和容量规划这些独立的运维职责。
optionExplanations_en: With strict dependencies between 60 steps, something needs to know what order to run them in, which segment to rerun after a failure, and where each step's output lives — exactly what a workflow scheduler manages.
Each of the 60 steps has its own processing logic and dependencies; it can't be automatically rewritten into a single SQL query.
Each step specifically depends on the data the previous one produced before it can start, contradicting the claim that it guarantees each step needs no input data.
A scheduler manages orchestration concerns like dependencies and run history; it can't substitute for separate operational responsibilities like monitoring and capacity planning.

scenario: 批作业失败到一半时，在线服务不应该读到半新半旧的推荐结果。
scenario_en: If a batch job fails halfway, the online service must not read a half-new, half-old recommendation dataset.
q: 批处理输出应如何发布？
q_en: How should batch output be published?
options: 写到新目录，全部成功后原子切换指针
边算边覆盖线上目录中的旧文件
每个 reducer 成功一个就立刻对用户可见
失败后让在线服务猜哪些分片可用
options_en: Write to a new directory and atomically switch the pointer after full success
Overwrite old files in the live directory while computing
Expose each reducer's output to users as soon as it succeeds
Let the online service guess which failed shards are usable
why: 先构建完整新版本再切换，可以让读路径只看到旧版本或新版本。代价是需要额外存储空间和清理旧版本。
why_en: Build a complete new version and then switch atomically so readers see either the old dataset or the new one, never a partial mix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子切换：一次元数据更新让读者从旧版本跳到新版本，中间状态不可见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic switch makes readers move from the old version to the new version with no visible in-between state.

optionExplanations: 先在一个新目录里把完整的新结果构建出来，全部成功之后再原子地切换指针，这样读路径任何时候看到的都是完整的旧版本或完整的新版本，不会是半新半旧的中间状态。
边算边覆盖线上目录中的旧文件，会让在线服务在批作业运行期间随时可能读到一部分新数据混着一部分旧数据。
每个 reducer 成功一个就立刻对用户可见，会让用户在整个作业完成之前就看到不完整、不一致的结果。
失败后让在线服务自己猜哪些分片可用，把本该由批处理系统保证的一致性问题甩给了在线服务，风险很大。
optionExplanations_en: Building the complete new result in a fresh directory first, then atomically switching the pointer only after everything succeeds, means the read path always sees either the complete old version or the complete new one, never a half-new-half-old mix.
Overwriting old files in the live directory while computing risks the online service reading a mix of some new and some old data at any point during the batch run.
Exposing each reducer's output to users as soon as it succeeds lets users see incomplete, inconsistent results before the whole job finishes.
Letting the online service guess which failed shards are usable offloads a consistency problem that should be the batch system's responsibility onto the online service, a risky approach.

scenario: 你要把数 TB 的点击事件和数 TB 的用户画像按 user_id 连接；两边都太大，不能复制到每个 mapper。
scenario_en: You need to join terabytes of click events with terabytes of user profiles by user_id; both sides are too large to broadcast to every mapper.
q: 默认最稳的 join 策略是什么？
q_en: What is the safest default join strategy?
options: reduce-side sort-merge join
broadcast hash join 把小表广播出去
每条事件都远程查一次用户库
在浏览器里做这个 join
options_en: A reduce-side sort-merge join.
A broadcast hash join that broadcasts the small table.
One remote lookup into the user database per event.
Doing the join in the browser.
why: 两边都很大时，按 user_id 分区和排序能把同一用户的数据送到同一个 reducer。代价是 shuffle 和排序重，但不要求输入预先同分区或小到可广播。
why_en: When both inputs are large, a reduce-side sort-merge join is robust because partitioning and sorting bring equal keys to the same reducer.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户画像很小，broadcast hash join 可以省掉大规模 shuffle 和 reducer 排序。
tradeoff: 通用性 vs shuffle 成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序归并连接：先按连接 key 排序，再顺序归并同 key 记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sort-merge join sorts inputs by join key and then merges records with the same key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广播哈希连接：把小表复制到每个处理大表分片的任务中。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broadcast hash join copies the small input to every task scanning the large input.

optionExplanations: 两边数据都太大、都放不进单个 mapper 的内存，按 user_id 分区并排序能把同一个用户的点击和画像送到同一个 reducer 汇合，不要求任何一边预先分区好或小到能广播。
broadcast hash join 要求其中一边足够小、能被复制进每个 mapper 的内存，这里两边都是数 TB，完全不满足这个前提。
每条点击事件都远程查一次用户库，会产生海量的网络请求，对数 TB 规模的数据量来说完全不现实。
在浏览器里做 join 既没有处理数 TB 数据的能力，也不是批处理架构该考虑的执行位置。
optionExplanations_en: With both sides too large to fit in one mapper's memory, partitioning and sorting by user_id brings each user's clicks and profile together at the same reducer, without requiring either side to be pre-partitioned or small enough to broadcast.
A broadcast hash join requires one side to be small enough to be copied into every mapper's memory, but both sides here are terabytes, failing that premise entirely.
Doing a remote lookup on the profile database for every single click event would generate an enormous number of network requests, unrealistic at terabyte scale.
Joining in the browser has neither the capacity to handle terabytes of data nor is it a sensible place to run this within a batch architecture.

scenario: 你要解释 reduce-side sort-merge join 如何把事件和画像按 user_id 连接。
scenario_en: You need to explain how a reduce-side sort-merge join connects events and profiles by user_id.
q: sort-merge join 的步骤顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the order of a sort-merge join?
steps: reducer 收到同一 user_id 的两边记录并输出连接结果
mapper 从两份输入抽取 user_id 作为 key
框架按 user_id 分区并排序
记录带上来源标签，区分事件还是画像
why: 来源标签让 reducer 知道哪条是维表记录、哪条是事实事件；排序和分区保证同 key 在一起。这个模式牺牲 I/O 来换通用 join 能力。
why_en: Source tags tell the reducer which side each record came from, while partitioning and sorting bring matching keys together.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  E["events"] --> M["map key=user_id + tag"]
  P["profiles"] --> M
  M --> S["shuffle by user_id"]
  S --> R["reduce join"]
  R --> O["enriched events"]

scenario: 你要为每个用户计算一天内的全部行为序列，事件来自多台 Web 服务器。
scenario_en: You need to compute each user's daily behavior sequence, and events come from many web servers.
q: MapReduce grouping 解决了什么问题？
q_en: What problem does MapReduce grouping solve?
options: 把同一用户的分散事件聚到同一个 reducer
把整份用户画像复制进每一台 Web 服务器
让所有事件按写入机器分组
跳过网络直接在客户端聚合
options_en: Collect events for the same user at one reducer
Copy the full user profile into every web server.
Group events by the machine that wrote them
Skip the network and aggregate on clients
why: 分组的目标是把同 key 的记录带到同一个地方，让 reducer 能看到完整上下文。代价是热点 key 会让某个 reducer 变慢。
why_en: Grouping brings records with the same key to one place so the reducer can see the full context, with hot keys causing skew.

termDefinitions.meaning: 热点 key：拥有远多于其他 key 的记录，容易压垮单个分区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key has far more records than other keys and can overload one partition.

optionExplanations: grouping 的作用正是把散落在不同 Web 服务器上、属于同一个用户的事件都收集到同一个 reducer，这样这个 reducer 才能看到这个用户一整天的完整行为序列。
用户画像复制进每台 Web 服务器解决的是别的问题（比如本地查询画像），跟把散落事件聚合到一起完全不是一回事。
如果按写入机器分组，同一个用户的事件很可能分散在不同机器写入，反而拼不出完整的用户行为序列。
跳过网络在客户端聚合，会让不同客户端各自只看到自己产生的那部分事件，拼不出这个用户在所有服务器上的完整行为。
optionExplanations_en: Grouping's whole purpose is to gather events scattered across different web servers but belonging to the same user into one reducer, so that reducer can see the user's complete day of behavior.
Copying user profiles into every web server solves a different problem, like local profile lookups, completely unrelated to gathering scattered events together.
Grouping by the machine that wrote the event would likely scatter one user's events across different machines, failing to assemble the complete behavior sequence.
Skipping the network and aggregating on the client would leave each client only seeing the events it produced itself, unable to piece together the user's full behavior across all servers.

scenario: 某个明星用户的事件量占全站 8%，按 user_id 分区后一个 reducer 长时间拖尾。
scenario_en: One celebrity user accounts for 8% of all events, so a user_id partition leaves one reducer as a long straggler.
q: 处理 skew join 的常见做法是什么？
q_en: What is a common way to handle a skewed join?
options: 把热点 key 再加随机盐拆成多个子分区
把 reducer 数量降到 1
让所有 mapper 顺序等待热点 reducer
删除热点用户的数据
options_en: Add a salt to split the hot key into multiple subpartitions
Reduce the reducer count to one
Make all mappers wait sequentially for the hot reducer
Delete the hot user's data
why: 给热点 key 分片能把单点压力分散到多个 reducer，再用后续步骤合并。代价是 join 逻辑更复杂，小表或另一侧数据可能要复制到多个盐值。
why_en: Salting a hot key spreads its work across reducers and then merges later, trading simplicity for better skew handling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据倾斜：少数 key 或分区的数据量远大于其他部分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Skew means a few keys or partitions carry much more data than the rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加盐分片：给 key 附加额外随机或分桶字段，把热点拆散。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Salting adds an extra bucket field to split a hot key across partitions.

optionExplanations: 给热点 key 加上随机盐拆成多个子分区，能把原本压在一个 reducer 上的 8% 流量分散到多个 reducer 并行处理，之后再把子分区的结果合并起来。
把 reducer 数量降到 1，会让所有数据都挤到一个任务里处理，比现在的情况还要糟糕，跟解决 skew 的方向正相反。
让所有 mapper 顺序等待热点 reducer，不但没解决拖尾问题，反而让本可以并行完成的其它 mapper 也被迫串行等待。
删除热点用户的数据是丢失真实业务数据的做法，不是处理数据倾斜该有的技术手段。
optionExplanations_en: Adding a random salt to split the hot key into multiple subpartitions spreads what used to be 8% of traffic on one reducer across several reducers running in parallel, with results merged afterward.
Reducing the reducer count to one would cram all the data into a single task, worse than the current situation and the opposite direction from solving skew.
Making all mappers wait sequentially for the hot reducer doesn't fix the tail-latency problem at all — it forces otherwise-parallel mappers into unnecessary serial waiting.
Deleting the hot user's data means losing real business data, not a legitimate technical approach to handling data skew.

scenario: 点击事件有 80TB，国家代码维表只有 5MB，维表每天更新一次。你要给事件补国家名称。
scenario_en: Click events are 80 TB, the country-code dimension table is 5 MB and updates once per day, and you need to enrich events with country names.
q: 哪种 join 最省 shuffle？
q_en: Which join minimizes shuffle?
options: broadcast hash join
reduce-side sort-merge join
table-table stream join
每条事件查远程 SQL
options_en: Broadcast hash join
Reduce-side sort-merge join
Table-table stream join
Remote SQL lookup per event
why: 小维表能装进每个 mapper 的本地哈希表，大事件流只需顺序扫描。代价是小表必须真的小，并且每个任务都要能拿到同一版本。
why_en: A tiny dimension table can be loaded into each mapper's local hash table, so the huge event input is scanned without a large shuffle.
whenOtherWins: 如果维表也很大或频繁变化，reduce-side join 或同分区 map-side join 更稳。
tradeoff: 复制小表 vs 打散大表

termDefinitions.meaning: 维表：用于补充事实记录属性的小型参考数据表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dimension table is reference data used to enrich fact records.

termDefinitions.meaning: 哈希表：通过 key 快速查找 value 的内存索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash table is an in-memory index for fast key-to-value lookup.

optionExplanations: 5MB 的国家维表可以整份复制到每个任务内存里，80TB 事件流顺序扫一遍边扫边查，不用 shuffle。
reduce-side sort-merge join 是给两边都很大时用的稳健方案，这里小表只有 5MB，用它反而浪费了排序和 shuffle 的开销。
table-table stream join 是给两个持续更新的流之间做 join 的场景准备的，跟这里一张静态小维表配一个批量事件流不匹配。
每条事件都查一次远程 SQL，在 80TB 规模下会产生天文数字的查询请求，完全不现实。
optionExplanations_en: A 5MB country-code table is small enough to be fully copied into each mapper's local hash table, so the 80TB event stream just needs one sequential scan, looking up the country name locally without any large shuffle for this join.
A reduce-side sort-merge join is the robust choice when both sides are large; using it here for a 5MB table wastes sorting and shuffle overhead unnecessarily.
A table-table stream join is meant for joining two continuously updating streams, which doesn't match a static small dimension table against a batch event stream.
Querying remote SQL for every single event would generate an astronomical number of requests at 80TB scale, completely unrealistic.

scenario: 订单表和支付表都已按 order_id 用同一哈希函数切成 256 个桶，每个同编号桶只包含可匹配记录。
scenario_en: Orders and payments are both bucketed into 256 partitions by order_id using the same hash function; matching records are in the same bucket number.
q: 哪种 map-side join 最合适？
q_en: Which map-side join fits best?
options: partitioned hash join
broadcast hash join
reduce-side sort-merge join
笛卡尔积后过滤
options_en: Partitioned hash join
Broadcast hash join
Reduce-side sort-merge join
Cartesian product then filter
why: 两边同分区时，每个 mapper 只连接对应桶，不需要全局 shuffle。前提很硬：分区数、key 和哈希函数都要一致。
why_en: With matching partitioning, each mapper joins corresponding buckets locally and avoids a global shuffle.
whenOtherWins: 如果分区元数据不可信或两边桶数不同，reduce-side join 更安全。
tradeoff: 预布局约束 vs 运行时 shuffle

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区哈希连接：两边数据按同一 key 和规则预分区后，在对应分区内本地连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partitioned hash join locally joins matching partitions that were bucketed by the same key and rule.

optionExplanations: 两边都已经用同一个哈希函数、按 order_id 切成对应编号的 256 个桶，每个编号相同的桶里的数据一定能互相匹配，每个 mapper 只需要本地连接对应编号的两个桶，不用做全局 shuffle。
broadcast hash join 是给一边足够小、能整体装进内存时用的，这里描述的是两边已经按相同方式分好区，不需要广播整张表。
reduce-side sort-merge join 是在没有现成分区布局时的通用稳健方案，这里两边已经按同一函数预先分好桶，直接利用这个布局更省事。
笛卡尔积后过滤会先产生两表所有记录两两组合的巨大中间结果，再从里面挑出匹配的，代价极高，完全没利用已有的分区信息。
optionExplanations_en: With both sides already split into 256 matching buckets by the same hash function on order_id, matching data is guaranteed to land in the same-numbered bucket, so each mapper can just join the corresponding local buckets without any global shuffle.
A broadcast hash join is for when one side is small enough to fit entirely in memory; here both sides are already partitioned the same way, so broadcasting the whole table isn't needed.

A reduce-side sort-merge join is the general, robust fallback when there's no existing partition layout; here both sides are already bucketed by the same function, so using that layout directly is far cheaper.

A Cartesian product followed by filtering first produces a huge intermediate result of every possible pairing before picking out matches, extremely expensive and ignoring the existing partition information entirely.

scenario: 两份大输入已经按 customer_id 同分区且各分区内部有序；上游保证这个布局，当前作业只负责连接。
scenario_en: Two large inputs are already co-partitioned by customer_id and sorted within each partition; upstream guarantees this layout.
q: 如何利用已有排序？
q_en: How should you exploit the existing ordering?
options: 做 map-side merge join，顺序归并两个有序分区
重新做一遍完整的 reduce-side sort-merge
把其中一边全部广播到所有 mapper
对每条记录远程调用画像服务
options_en: Run a map-side merge join by sequentially merging the two sorted partitions
Redo a full reduce-side sort-merge again.
Broadcast one full input to every mapper
Call a remote profile service for each record
why: 已有同分区和有序性时，本地顺序归并能省掉重新分区和排序。代价是工作流必须保留并校验这些布局元数据。
why_en: If inputs are already co-partitioned and sorted, a map-side merge join reuses that layout and avoids another shuffle and sort.
whenOtherWins: 如果上游排序可能失效，重新走 reduce-side join 虽慢但更不容易产出错结果。
tradeoff: 复用布局元数据 vs 自包含稳健性

termDefinitions.meaning: map-side merge join：mapper 在本地顺序归并两个已同分区且有序的输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A map-side merge join merges two co-partitioned, sorted inputs locally inside mappers.

optionExplanations: 两份输入已经按同一个 key 分好区、每个分区内部又是有序的，map-side merge join 只需要在本地像归并两个有序列表一样顺序走一遍，就能完成连接，完全不用再重新分区排序。
重新做一遍 reduce-side sort-merge，等于扔掉了上游已经保证好的分区和排序布局，白白多付一次 shuffle 和排序的代价。
把其中一边全部广播到所有 mapper，是给一边足够小时才划算的做法，这里两份都是大输入，广播不合适，也没必要，因为已经有现成的排序布局可以利用。
对每条记录远程调用画像服务，会产生大量额外的网络请求，完全没有利用已有的本地有序数据这个优势。
optionExplanations_en: With both inputs already partitioned by the same key and sorted within each partition, a map-side merge join just needs to walk through them locally like merging two sorted lists, no need to repartition or resort.
Running another round of reduce-side sort-merge would throw away the partitioning and sorting layout the upstream already guaranteed, needlessly paying for another shuffle and sort.

Broadcasting one full input to every mapper only pays off when one side is small; both inputs here are large, so broadcasting is inappropriate and unnecessary given the existing sorted layout to exploit.
Calling a remote profile service for each record would generate a huge number of extra network requests, failing to leverage the already-local sorted data at all.

scenario: 你想把 reduce-side join 改成 map-side join 来减少 shuffle。
scenario_en: You want to replace a reduce-side join with a map-side join to reduce shuffle.
q: 哪些前提通常必须先确认？
q_en: Which assumptions should you confirm first?
options: 小表是否能放进每个任务的内存或本地索引
两边是否已经按同一 key 同分区
输入是否已经按 join key 有序
reducer 是否能自动修复任意错误分区
options_en: Whether the small side fits in each task's memory or local index
Whether both sides are already partitioned by the same key
Whether inputs are already sorted by the join key
Whether reducers can automatically repair arbitrary mispartitioning
why: map-side join 用输入布局换运行时 shuffle，所以要先确认大小、分区和排序这些事实。布局错了不会变慢而已，可能直接产出漏 join 的结果。
why_en: Map-side joins trade runtime shuffle for stronger input-layout assumptions around size, partitioning, and ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本地索引：任务所在机器可直接读取的查找结构，避免每条记录远程查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A local index is a lookup structure available to the task without a remote query.

optionExplanations: 要省掉 shuffle，先得确认小表真塞得进每个任务的内存或本地索引，塞不下这条路就走不通。
它依赖两边已经按同一个 key 分好区，否则同一 key 的记录不会落到同一个任务上处理。
利用有序性做归并连接，同样需要先确认输入是不是真的已经按 join key 排好序，不然归并逻辑本身就是错的。
reducer 不会自动修复分错的分区；分区不对时会静默产出漏掉记录的结果，这不是它的能力。
optionExplanations_en: To save a shuffle with a map-side join, you first need to confirm the small side actually fits in each task's memory or local index — without that, this path simply doesn't work.
A map-side join depends on both sides already being partitioned by the same key; without that, there's no guarantee records with the same key land in the same task.
Exploiting existing order for a merge join likewise requires confirming the input is genuinely sorted by the join key already, otherwise the merge logic itself is simply wrong.
Reducers can't automatically fix mispartitioned data — bad partitioning silently produces missed or incorrect joins in a map-side join, not a capability it has.

scenario: 一个 join 作业的输出马上会被下游按同一个 key 再次聚合。
scenario_en: The output of a join job will immediately be grouped downstream by the same key.
q: 为什么输出布局要一起设计？
q_en: Why should the output layout be designed with downstream jobs?
options: 保留分区/排序可让下游少一次 shuffle
输出布局只影响文件名，不影响性能
下游一定会从浏览器读取这些文件
保留输出布局会让所有 key 分布完全均匀
options_en: Preserving partitioning or ordering can save a downstream shuffle
Output layout affects only file names, not performance
Downstream jobs will always read these files from browsers
Keeping the layout makes all keys perfectly even.
why: 批处理链路的成本常在阶段之间的数据搬运；如果下游需要同 key 聚合，复用现有布局能省 I/O。代价是生产者和消费者之间多了布局契约。
why_en: Batch workflow cost often sits between stages, so preserving useful partitioning or ordering can remove a downstream shuffle.
optionExplanations: 这次 join 的输出接下来就要按同一个 key 再聚合一次，如果输出继续保留同样的分区或排序，下游就能直接复用这个布局，省掉自己再做一次 shuffle 的成本。
输出布局直接决定下游要不要额外付 shuffle 的代价，这是实实在在的性能问题，不只是文件命名这种表面细节。
下游作业通常是别的批处理任务，不是从浏览器读取这些数据文件，这个说法混淆了批处理和前端展示。
保留分区或排序只是复用已有布局，不会改变数据本身各个 key 的实际分布，说它会让所有 key 完全均匀不成立。
optionExplanations_en: With this join's output about to be aggregated again by the same key downstream, keeping the same partitioning or sort in the output lets the next job reuse that layout directly, saving it from doing another shuffle itself.
Output layout directly determines whether downstream jobs have to pay for an extra shuffle, a real performance concern, not merely a cosmetic filename detail.
Downstream jobs are typically other batch tasks, not something reading these data files from a browser — this option conflates batch processing with frontend display.
Preserving partitioning or sorting just reuses an existing layout; it doesn't change the actual underlying distribution of keys, so claiming it makes all keys perfectly uniform doesn't hold.

scenario: 你有一批静态文档，每晚重建全文搜索索引，在线查询只读索引文件。
scenario_en: You have a static-ish document corpus, rebuild the full-text search index nightly, and online queries only read index files.
q: 批处理适合产出什么？
q_en: What should the batch job produce?
options: 一套完整的新搜索索引文件
每个查询到来时临时扫描原文
只写一串未排序日志给搜索服务
让用户请求直接运行 MapReduce
options_en: A complete new set of search-index files
Scan all source documents at query time
Write only an unsorted log to the search service
Run MapReduce directly from user requests
why: 搜索索引是典型派生数据：离线把读路径需要的结构预先建好。代价是索引新鲜度取决于批处理周期或增量索引补充。
why_en: A search index is derived data: batch work prebuilds the structure that makes online reads fast.
whenOtherWins: 如果文档更新必须秒级可搜，就要加流式或增量索引路径。
tradeoff: 离线预计算吞吐 vs 在线新鲜度

termDefinitions.meaning: 派生数据：可由源数据重新计算出来、用于加速读取或分析的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Derived data is data that can be recomputed from source data and is often built to speed reads or analysis.

optionExplanations: 批处理正好适合离线把在线读路径需要的结构预先建好，每晚重建一套完整的搜索索引文件，白天在线查询只管读这些现成的索引文件，速度很快。
每个查询到来时临时扫描原文，等于把批处理省下来的工作又原封不动地还给了在线路径，完全违背了预建索引的意义。
只写一串未排序日志给搜索服务，等于没有真正构建索引结构，搜索服务还是得自己现场处理这些原始数据。
让用户请求直接运行 MapReduce，会让每次查询都背上批处理的高延迟，跟在线查询该有的响应速度完全不匹配。
optionExplanations_en: Batch processing is exactly suited to prebuilding offline the structure the online read path needs, rebuilding a complete set of search-index files each night so daytime online queries just read those ready-made files quickly.
Scanning all source documents at query time hands right back to the online path exactly the work batch processing was meant to save, defeating the whole point of prebuilding an index.
Writing only an unsorted log to the search service means no real index structure was actually built, leaving the search service to process the raw data on the fly itself.
Running MapReduce directly from user requests would saddle every query with batch-processing latency, completely mismatched with what an online query needs.

scenario: 批作业每天生成 2TB 推荐结果，线上 KV 服务只需要按 user_id 查询，不能在构建中暴露半成品。
scenario_en: A daily batch job generates 2 TB of recommendation results; the online key-value service only reads by user_id and must not expose partial builds.
q: 更好的发布方式是什么？
q_en: What is the better publishing approach?
options: 批作业生成新 KV 数据文件，拷贝完成后原子切换
让 reducer 直接逐条写入线上 KV 服务
先清空线上库再慢慢回填
让线上请求缺失时同步调用批作业
options_en: Have the batch job build new KV data files and atomically switch after copying
Have the reducer write to the live KV store row by row.
Clear the live store first and slowly refill it
Have online requests synchronously call the batch job on misses
why: 批量构建不可变数据文件能避免大量随机写和半成品可见。代价是需要版本切换、容量预留和回滚策略。
why_en: Bulk-building immutable serving files avoids many random live writes and keeps partial output hidden until an atomic switch.
whenOtherWins: 如果每条结果必须实时生效，在线写入或流式更新会比整库切换更合适。
tradeoff: 整批一致发布 vs 单条实时更新

termDefinitions.meaning: KV：按 key 查找 value 的存储模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key-Value storage retrieves a value by key.

optionExplanations: 批作业先把新一批 KV 数据文件构建完整，拷贝到位之后再原子切换指针，线上查询要么看到完整的旧数据，要么看到完整的新数据，从不会暴露构建过程中的半成品。
reducer 直接逐条写线上 KV 服务，会在构建过程中不断产生大量随机写，还会让还没写完的半成品数据被在线查询读到。
先清空线上库再慢慢回填，会有一段时间线上数据是不完整甚至是空的，直接违反了不能暴露半成品的要求。
让线上请求缺失时同步调用批作业，会把批处理这种高延迟的操作直接接到用户请求路径上，响应会变得极慢。
optionExplanations_en: The batch job builds a full new set of KV data files, and only after the copy is done does it atomically switch the pointer, so live queries always see either the complete old data or the complete new data, never a half-built intermediate state.
Having reducers write each row directly to the live KV service generates a huge number of random writes during the build and exposes incomplete, half-finished data to online queries in the meantime.
Clearing the live store first and slowly refilling it leaves a window where live data is incomplete or even empty, directly violating the requirement not to expose partial results.
Having online requests synchronously call the batch job on a miss would splice a high-latency batch operation straight into the user request path, making response times crawl.

scenario: 某团队让每个 reducer 直接写线上数据库。任务失败重试后，部分用户推荐出现重复或旧值覆盖新值。
scenario_en: A team lets reducers write directly to the live database; after task retries, some recommendations are duplicated or overwritten by older values.
q: 为什么批任务应避免外部副作用？
q_en: Why should batch tasks avoid external side effects?
options: 失败任务会重跑，外部写入不一定能被框架丢弃
数据库写入一定总是比写文件更加便宜更快
reducer 无法打开网络连接
外部数据库不能存储批处理结果
options_en: Failed tasks may rerun, and the framework cannot always discard external writes
Database writes are always cheaper and faster than files.
Reducers cannot open network connections
External databases cannot store batch results
why: 框架能丢弃失败任务的指定输出文件，却管不住已经提交到外部系统的副作用。想直接写外部库，就要自己处理幂等、事务或版本切换。
why_en: The framework can discard failed task output files, but it cannot automatically undo side effects already committed to an external system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一操作执行多次与执行一次的可见效果相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation has the same visible effect whether it runs once or multiple times.

optionExplanations: 框架能丢弃失败任务写到自己指定输出文件里的内容，但一个 reducer 已经直接写进外部数据库的那些行，框架管不到，任务失败重跑后这些外部写入可能重复或互相覆盖。
写数据库不见得比写文件便宜，这里的问题不在写入成本，而在失败重试后外部写入没法被框架统一撤销。
reducer 完全能打开网络连接去写外部数据库，问题恰恰出在这个能力被滥用之后带来的副作用管理难题。
外部数据库当然能存储批处理结果，问题不在能不能存，而在直接写会让失败重试变得不安全。
optionExplanations_en: The framework can discard whatever a failed task wrote to its own designated output files, but rows a reducer already wrote directly to an external database are outside its reach — a rerun after failure can leave duplicates or overwrite newer values with older ones.
Database writes aren't necessarily cheaper than file writes; the issue here isn't write cost, it's that external writes can't be uniformly rolled back by the framework after a retry.
Reducers absolutely can open network connections to write an external database; the problem is precisely the side-effect management difficulty that capability creates when misused.
External databases can certainly store batch results; the issue isn't whether they can store it, it's that writing directly makes failed-task retries unsafe.

scenario: 多个团队会在不同时间读取同一份清洗后的用户行为数据，并把它作为自己作业的输入。
scenario_en: Several teams read the same cleaned user-activity dataset at different times and use it as input to their own jobs.
q: 为什么把批输出当不可变数据集发布？
q_en: Why publish batch output as an immutable dataset?
options: 读者按版本复现，生产者无需知道消费者
它让所有下游消费者自动获得强事务
它允许下游直接修改上游文件
它保证数据永远不需要被删除
options_en: Readers can reproduce results by version, and the producer need not know its consumers.
It gives all downstream consumers strong transactions automatically.
It lets downstream jobs edit the upstream files.
It guarantees data never has to be deleted.
why: 不可变数据集像稳定接口，消费者可以按路径或版本引用。代价是存储会增长，必须有保留、压缩和删除策略。
why_en: An immutable dataset acts like a stable interface that consumers can reference by path or version, with storage retention to manage.
optionExplanations: 不可变数据集像一个稳定的接口，任何读者都能按具体的路径或版本号复现出当时的结果，生产者发布出去之后也不需要知道到底有哪些团队正在消费它。
不可变数据集本身不会自动给消费者带来强事务保证，事务是另一套独立的机制。
不可变恰恰意味着下游不能直接修改上游文件，这个说法把不可变性的含义说反了。
数据总会累积增长，不可变数据集同样需要保留、压缩和删除策略，不是说永远不需要删除。
optionExplanations_en: An immutable dataset acts like a stable interface — any reader can reproduce that point-in-time result by referencing a specific path or version, and the producer doesn't need to know who all the consumers even are.
An immutable dataset doesn't automatically grant consumers strong transactions on its own; transactions are a separate mechanism.
Immutability specifically means downstream jobs cannot modify upstream files directly — this option has the meaning of immutability backwards.
Data always accumulates over time, so an immutable dataset still needs retention, compaction, and deletion policies — it doesn't mean deletion is never needed.

scenario: 团队要做大规模分析：一边是结构化报表 SQL，另一边是大量原始日志、图片元数据和自定义解析代码。
scenario_en: The team needs large-scale analysis: structured reporting SQL on one side, and raw logs, image metadata, and custom parsers on the other.
q: Hadoop/MapReduce 相比 MPP 数据库的优势在哪里？
q_en: Where does Hadoop/MapReduce have an advantage over an MPP database?
options: 更容易接收原始多格式数据并运行任意代码
总是比 MPP SQL 查询延迟更低
自动提供完整 OLTP 事务
不需要任何数据治理
options_en: It more easily accepts raw multi-format data and runs arbitrary code
It always has lower latency than MPP SQL queries
It automatically provides full OLTP transactions
It needs no data governance
why: MapReduce 血统的系统牺牲了一些查询优化体验，换来对存储格式和自定义代码的宽容。报表型 SQL 工作负载往往仍是 MPP 数据库更顺手。
why_en: MapReduce-style systems trade some query polish for flexibility in raw formats and arbitrary code, while MPP databases shine on structured SQL analytics.
tradeoff: 格式/代码灵活性 vs 集成 SQL 优化

termDefinitions.meaning: MPP：多节点并行执行查询的数据库架构，常用于数据仓库分析。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Massively Parallel Processing databases execute analytic queries in parallel across many nodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: ETL：抽取、转换、加载数据到目标系统的管线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Extract, Transform, Load is a pipeline that moves and transforms data into a target system.

optionExplanations: 它能直接吃进原始日志、图片元数据这些非结构化数据，还能跑任意自定义代码。
结构化报表这类 SQL 工作负载通常还是 MPP 数据库跑得更顺、延迟更低，说 MapReduce 总是延迟更低正好说反了。
MapReduce 系统本身不是为 OLTP 场景设计的，不会自动提供完整的事务语义，这跟它的定位不符。
数据治理该做的事一点没少，格式、血缘、权限这些问题在灵活的原始数据场景里反而更需要认真管理。
optionExplanations_en: MapReduce-style systems can ingest raw logs, image metadata, and other unstructured data directly, and run arbitrary custom code — that flexibility is precisely its edge over a structured MPP database.
Structured reporting SQL workloads usually still run more smoothly and with lower latency on an MPP database, so claiming MapReduce always has lower latency has it backwards.
MapReduce-style systems weren't designed for OLTP scenarios and don't automatically provide full transaction semantics, inconsistent with their actual role.
Data governance concerns don't disappear — format, lineage, and access control actually need more careful management in a flexible raw-data setting, not less.

scenario: 数据湖先接入半结构化日志，未来多个团队会用不同方式解释同一份原始事件。
scenario_en: A data lake ingests semi-structured logs first, and future teams will interpret the same raw events in different ways.
q: schema-on-read 的设计含义是什么？
q_en: What is the design implication of schema-on-read?
options: 先保留原始数据，读取或加工时再施加解释
写入时必须拒绝所有未知字段
它让数据质量问题自动消失
它只适合处理单机上的 CSV 文件
options_en: Keep raw data first and apply interpretation when reading or processing
Reject every unknown field at write time
It automatically removes data-quality problems
It only suits single-machine CSV files.
why: schema-on-read 给探索和多视图留空间，但解释负担会转移到每个读取作业。生产化后仍要把关键字段契约、测试和血缘补上。
why_en: Schema-on-read preserves flexibility for exploration, but each reader must carry the interpretation and quality checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读时模式：写入时少约束，读取或处理时再解释字段结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Schema-on-read stores data with minimal upfront structure and applies interpretation when reading.

optionExplanations: 先老老实实把原始事件存下来，等真要读取加工时，每个团队按自己的理解去解释它。
写入时就拒绝未知字段是 schema-on-write 的做法，跟先接受原始数据的思路正相反。
数据质量问题不会自动消失，只是把解释和校验的负担挪到了每个读取作业身上。
它广泛用于分布式数据湖这种多机场景，不是只适合单机 CSV 文件的小规模用法。
optionExplanations_en: Schema-on-read honestly keeps the raw data first, and only when it's actually being read or processed does each team apply its own interpretation to the same raw events, leaving room for multiple views.
Rejecting every unknown field at write time is exactly what schema-on-write does, the opposite of schema-on-read's approach of accepting raw data first.
Data-quality problems don't automatically disappear with schema-on-read — the burden of interpretation and validation just shifts onto every reading job instead.
Schema-on-read is widely used in large-scale distributed data lakes, not something limited to small-scale single-machine CSV file use.

scenario: 同一份 HDFS 数据既要跑 SQL 报表，也要跑 Python 自然语言处理和机器学习特征生成。
scenario_en: The same HDFS data must support SQL reporting, Python NLP, and machine-learning feature generation.
q: 共享文件系统带来的架构价值是什么？
q_en: What architectural value does a shared filesystem provide?
options: 多种处理模型可以复用同一份持久数据
所有作业必须使用同一种查询语言
它把 Python 代码自动优化成 SQL
它让在线请求直接访问 HDFS 最快
options_en: Multiple processing models can reuse the same durable data
All jobs must use one query language
It automatically optimizes Python code into SQL
It makes online requests fastest when reading HDFS directly
why: 共享持久数据层让 SQL、批代码和专用算法各取所需。代价是权限、格式、元数据和资源隔离要认真治理。
why_en: A shared durable data layer lets SQL, custom batch code, and specialized algorithms reuse the same source data.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有标准 BI 报表，单一 MPP 数据仓库通常更简单。
tradeoff: 生态多样性 vs 治理复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: BI：面向报表、指标和商业分析的查询与展示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Business Intelligence covers reporting, metrics, and business analytics.

optionExplanations: 同一份数据存在共享的持久文件系统里，SQL 报表引擎、Python NLP 库和机器学习特征生成各自按自己的方式去读同一份数据，谁也不用为了兼容别人重新导一份。
