共享文件系统本身不强制所有作业用同一种查询语言，恰恰是它的灵活之处在于容纳多种处理模型。
共享文件系统不会自动把 Python 代码优化成 SQL，这两者是完全不同的执行方式，互不转换。
HDFS 是为批处理这种大规模扫描设计的，不是给在线请求做低延迟点查用的，这个说法说反了它的定位。
optionExplanations_en: With the same data sitting in a shared durable filesystem, the SQL reporting engine, the Python NLP library, and the ML feature pipeline can each read it their own way, with nobody needing to re-import a separate copy just to be compatible with the others.
A shared filesystem doesn't force every job to use one query language; its flexibility comes precisely from accommodating multiple processing models.
A shared filesystem doesn't automatically optimize Python code into SQL — those are entirely different execution paths that don't convert into each other.
HDFS is designed for large-scale scans like batch processing, not for low-latency point queries on the online request path — this option misstates its role.

scenario: 一个 mapper 运行 40 分钟后机器被抢占，输入文件仍在 HDFS，mapper 没有外部副作用。
scenario_en: A mapper runs for 40 minutes and then its machine is preempted; the input file remains in HDFS and the mapper has no external side effects.
q: MapReduce 如何恢复？
q_en: How does MapReduce recover?
options: 在别的机器重跑该任务，并丢弃失败尝试的输出
让所有已经完成的任务都手动去回滚数据库
从失败机器内存继续执行
把失败分片标记为已处理
options_en: Rerun that task elsewhere and discard the failed attempt's output
Manually roll back the database for every finished task.
Resume from the failed machine's memory
Mark the failed split as processed
why: 输入不可变、输出按任务隔离时，重跑能得到等价结果。前提是 mapper/reducer 逻辑确定性强，且没有不可撤销外部写入。
why_en: With immutable input and isolated task output, MapReduce can rerun a failed task and ignore the failed attempt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抢占：调度器为了更高优先级任务而终止正在运行的低优先级任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Preemption means the scheduler kills a running low-priority task to free resources for higher-priority work.

optionExplanations: 输入文件还完整存在 HDFS 上，这个 mapper 也没有产生任何外部副作用，只要在另一台机器上重跑这个任务、丢弃这次失败尝试留下的任何输出，就能得到跟正常完成一样的结果。
重跑失败任务不需要牵连到已经正常完成的其它任务，让所有已完成任务都手动回滚数据库是不必要也不合理的过度反应。
失败的机器已经被抢占了，没法从它已经丢失的内存状态继续执行，只能在别的机器上重新开始。
把失败分片标记为已处理会让这部分数据的处理结果永久缺失，跟保证每份输入都被正确处理的要求相反。
optionExplanations_en: With the input file still intact in HDFS and this mapper having produced no external side effects, simply rerunning the task on another machine and discarding whatever the failed attempt output gives an equivalent result to a normal completion.
Rerunning a failed task doesn't need to touch tasks that already completed normally; requiring all completed tasks to manually roll back their databases is an unnecessary, disproportionate reaction.
The failed machine has already been preempted, so there's no in-memory state left to resume from — it can only start over on another machine.
Marking the failed split as processed would permanently leave that portion of data unprocessed, the opposite of guaranteeing every input actually gets handled correctly.

scenario: 一个多租户集群希望白天把资源让给高优先级线上分析，夜间低优先级批任务可以被随时杀掉重跑。
scenario_en: A multi-tenant cluster wants daytime resources for high-priority analytics, while low-priority batch tasks may be killed and retried at any time.
q: 为什么 MapReduce 偏向频繁落盘和任务级重试？
q_en: Why does MapReduce favor frequent disk writes and task-level retry?
options: 这样低优先级任务被抢占时损失可控
这样每个任务都会更快完成
这样不需要调度器参与资源分配
这样能保证所有代码都是确定性的
options_en: So preempted low-priority tasks lose only bounded work
So every task always finishes faster
So no scheduler is needed for resource allocation
So all code is guaranteed deterministic
why: 频繁物化让失败或抢占后的恢复边界清楚，集群可以更大胆地回收资源。代价是无故障路径也要付出更多磁盘 I/O。
why_en: Frequent materialization gives clear recovery boundaries for preemption, trading failure-free speed for robust cluster scheduling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 物化：把中间计算结果提前写成可读取的数据，而不是按需重新计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Materialization means eagerly writing an intermediate result instead of recomputing it on demand.

optionExplanations: 频繁把中间结果落盘、以任务为单位重跑，让一个低优先级任务被抢占时最多只丢掉这一小段还没落盘的工作，损失被限制在一个可控的范围内，集群才敢放心地随时回收资源。
频繁落盘本身会带来额外的磁盘 I/O 开销，反而不是让每个任务都跑得更快的做法，这个说法把代价说成了收益。
调度器仍然要参与资源分配和抢占决策，频繁落盘只是让抢占之后的恢复更简单，不代表调度器可以不参与。
频繁落盘和任务级重试解决的是恢复边界的问题，不能保证所有代码本身都是确定性的，这是两个不同的话题。
optionExplanations_en: Frequently materializing to disk and retrying at the task granularity means a preempted low-priority task loses at most the small unfinished chunk of work — bounded, predictable loss that lets the cluster reclaim resources aggressively without worry.
Frequent materialization itself adds extra disk I/O overhead; it isn't what makes every task finish faster — this option turns the cost into a claimed benefit.
The scheduler still has to participate in resource allocation and preemption decisions; frequent materialization only makes recovery after preemption simpler, it doesn't remove the scheduler's role.
Frequent materialization and task-level retry address the recovery-boundary problem; they don't guarantee the code itself is deterministic, a separate topic.

scenario: 一个 80 步推荐工作流的大多数中间结果只被下一步使用，并不对外发布。
scenario_en: An 80-step recommender workflow has many intermediate results that are consumed only by the next step and are never published.
q: 为什么 Spark/Flink/Tez 这类 dataflow engine 可能更快？
q_en: Why might a Spark/Flink/Tez-style dataflow engine be faster?
options: operator 图少写 HDFS 中间态
每步都写三副本 HDFS 中间态
禁用本地内存和本地磁盘
让每个 operator 都先做一次全局排序
options_en: An operator graph with fewer HDFS intermediates
Every step writes replicated HDFS intermediates
Disable local memory and local disk
Make each operator do a global sort first.
why: 中间结果只给下一步用时，管道化和本地中间状态能省大量复制 I/O。代价是失败后可能需要按血缘重算。
why_en: When intermediates are private to the next stage, pipelining and local state save replicated I/O, with lineage-based recomputation on failure.
tradeoff: 少物化提速 vs 失败重算成本

termDefinitions.meaning: operator：数据流引擎中的处理节点，如 filter、join、groupBy。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An operator is a processing node in a dataflow engine, such as filter, join, or groupBy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 血缘：记录某份数据由哪些输入和算子计算而来，用于重算和追踪。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lineage records which inputs and operators produced a piece of data, enabling recomputation and tracing.

optionExplanations: 大多数中间结果只被紧接着的下一步消费、不对外发布时，operator 图能少写很多份三副本的 HDFS 中间态，直接把结果管道化传给下一步，省下大量复制 I/O。
每步都写三副本 HDFS 中间态正是传统 MapReduce 的做法，也正是 dataflow engine 想要避免的开销，不是它更快的原因。
dataflow engine 恰恰会利用本地内存和本地磁盘来加速执行，禁用它们只会更慢，这个说法说反了。
每个 operator 先全局排序会引入不必要的排序开销，dataflow engine 更倾向只在真正需要排序时才排序，不是每步都先排序。
optionExplanations_en: When most intermediate results are only consumed by the very next step and never published elsewhere, the operator graph can skip writing many replicated HDFS intermediates and pipe results straight to the next stage, saving a lot of replicated I/O.
Writing replicated HDFS intermediates at every step is exactly what traditional MapReduce does and exactly the overhead dataflow engines are trying to avoid — not the reason they're faster.
Dataflow engines specifically exploit local memory and local disk to speed things up; disabling them would only slow things down, so this option has it backwards.
Globally sorting before every operator introduces unnecessary sorting overhead; dataflow engines prefer to sort only where actually needed, not as a default before every step.

scenario: 某个清洗后的用户数据集会被十几个团队复用，并且需要稳定路径、权限和版本。
scenario_en: A cleaned user dataset will be reused by a dozen teams and needs a stable path, permissions, and versions.
q: 此时中间结果应不应该物化到 HDFS？
q_en: Should this intermediate result be materialized to HDFS?
options: 应该，因为它其实是对外发布的数据产品
不应该，任何中间状态都必须只放内存
不应该，HDFS 不能被多个团队读取
应该，但只能覆盖旧目录
options_en: Yes, because it is effectively a published data product
No, all intermediate state must stay only in memory
No, HDFS cannot be read by multiple teams
Yes, but only by overwriting the old directory
why: 一旦结果有多个未知消费者，稳定物化就是解耦接口，不只是性能开销。代价是要维护版本、文档和生命周期。
why_en: Once many consumers depend on the output, materializing it as a stable dataset is a decoupling interface, not just overhead.
whenOtherWins: 如果它只被同一工作流下一步消费，dataflow 管道化通常更划算。
tradeoff: 组织解耦 vs 执行 I/O

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据产品：有契约、版本和消费者的数据集，而不是临时文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data product is a dataset with contracts, versions, and consumers, not just a temporary file.

optionExplanations: 一旦这份清洗后的数据被十几个团队复用、还需要稳定的路径、权限和版本管理，它实际上就是一份对外发布的数据产品，理应物化到 HDFS 作为解耦接口，而不只是内部的中间状态。
数据只放内存对这种要被多个团队长期依赖、需要稳定引用的场景完全不现实，进程一重启数据就没了。
HDFS 本来就是设计给多团队共享读取的分布式文件系统，说它不能被多个团队读取不成立。
每次都覆盖旧目录会让下游没法按版本引用某个具体的历史结果，也没法安全地回滚，不满足需要版本管理的要求。
optionExplanations_en: Once this cleaned dataset is reused by a dozen teams and needs a stable path, permissions, and versioning, it's effectively a published data product and should be materialized to HDFS as a decoupling interface, not just treated as internal intermediate state.
Keeping data only in memory is completely unrealistic for something many teams depend on long-term and need to reference reliably — the data vanishes the moment the process restarts.
HDFS is precisely designed as a distributed filesystem for multi-team shared reads, so claiming it can't be read by multiple teams doesn't hold.
Overwriting the old directory every time leaves downstream unable to reference a specific historical version or safely roll back, failing the requirement for version management.

scenario: 你把原来的 map/reduce 串改成 dataflow DAG，某些阶段只需要重分区不需要排序，某些阶段需要广播小表。
scenario_en: You convert a map/reduce chain into a dataflow DAG; some stages need repartitioning without sorting, and others need broadcasting a small table.
q: dataflow operator 图提供了什么灵活性？
q_en: What flexibility does a dataflow operator graph provide?
options: 每条边可选择 shuffle、同分区、广播或管道化连接
所有边都必须走 map 后接 reduce
所有 operator 都必须写进同一个输出目录里
每个函数都能随意修改上游输入文件
options_en: Each edge can choose shuffle, co-partitioning, broadcast, or pipelined transfer
Every edge must be map followed by reduce
All operators must write to the same output directory.
Every function may mutate upstream input files
why: dataflow 引擎把数据依赖显式成图，执行器就能只在需要处插入排序、广播或网络传输。这个自由度来自更复杂的调度器和运行时。
why_en: A dataflow engine exposes dependencies as a graph, so the runtime can insert sorting, broadcast, or network transfer only where needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: DAG：有方向且无环的图，常用来表示批处理阶段依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Directed Acyclic Graph is a directed graph with no cycles, often used for batch-stage dependencies.

optionExplanations: dataflow 图把数据依赖显式表达成边，每条边可以按需选择走 shuffle、同分区连接、广播还是直接管道化传输，执行器只在真正需要的地方才插入排序或网络传输。
dataflow DAG 并不要求所有边都必须是 map 后接 reduce 这一种固定形状，它比传统 MapReduce 灵活得多。
不同 operator 可以有各自独立的输出目的地，不必须都写同一个输出目录，这个说法限制得过死。
允许函数随意修改上游输入文件会破坏批处理依赖的不可变输入假设，dataflow 系统不会允许这种做法。
optionExplanations_en: A dataflow graph expresses data dependencies explicitly as edges, and each edge can choose shuffle, co-partitioning, broadcast, or direct pipelined transfer as needed, letting the runtime insert sorting or network transfer only where it's actually required.
A dataflow DAG doesn't require every edge to be a fixed map-then-reduce shape — it's far more flexible than traditional MapReduce.
Different operators can have their own independent output destinations; they aren't required to all write the same output directory, an overly restrictive claim.
Allowing a function to freely mutate upstream input files would break the immutable-input assumption batch processing relies on — dataflow systems don't permit that.

scenario: 你在解释为什么同一个 Hive 查询从 MapReduce backend 换到 Tez backend 后明显更快。
scenario_en: You are explaining why the same Hive query gets much faster after switching from a MapReduce backend to a Tez backend.
q: 哪些是 dataflow engine 的常见收益？
q_en: Which are common benefits of dataflow engines?
options: 避免不必要的排序
让下游 operator 更早开始
把中间状态保存在内存或本地磁盘
保证所有用户函数都自动变成 SQL
options_en: Avoid unnecessary sorting
Let downstream operators start earlier
Keep intermediate state in memory or local disk
Automatically turn every user function into SQL
why: dataflow 引擎的收益主要来自少物化、少排序和更早流水线执行。它不会魔法般理解任意用户代码的语义。
why_en: Dataflow engines are faster mainly by reducing materialization and sorting and by pipelining stages earlier.
optionExplanations: 避免不必要的排序是 dataflow engine 常见的加速来源，只在真正需要的地方才付排序的代价。
让下游 operator 更早开始，靠的是管道化执行，不用等上一步全部写完中间态才能开始下一步。
把中间状态保存在内存或本地磁盘，省掉了写多副本 HDFS 的开销，这也是常见的速度提升来源。
它不会自动理解任意用户函数在做什么，更不会把它们变成 SQL，这个说法过度神化了。
optionExplanations_en: Avoiding unnecessary sorting is a common source of speedup in a dataflow engine, only paying the sorting cost where it's genuinely required.
Letting downstream operators start earlier comes from pipelined execution, not waiting for the previous stage to fully materialize before starting the next one.
Keeping intermediate state in memory or local disk saves the cost of writing replicated HDFS copies, another common source of speed gains.
A dataflow engine doesn't automatically understand what arbitrary user functions do, let alone turn them into SQL on its own — this option overstates its capability.

scenario: Spark 作业中某台机器丢失了一个中间分区；原始输入还在 HDFS，operator 链也可重放。
scenario_en: A Spark job loses an intermediate partition on one machine; the original input is still in HDFS and the operator chain can be replayed.
q: dataflow 引擎通常如何恢复这块数据？
q_en: How does a dataflow engine usually recover that data?
options: 根据血缘从可用输入重新计算丢失分区
要求所有用户手工上传备份
直接把丢失的分区当成空数据继续跑
让下游猜测缺失记录
options_en: Recompute the lost partition from available inputs using lineage
Require users to manually upload a backup
Treat the lost partition as empty data and continue.
Let downstream stages guess missing records
why: 少写 HDFS 的代价是失败时靠血缘重算。若重算太贵或中间结果很小，主动物化检查点可能更划算。
why_en: Avoiding HDFS writes shifts recovery to lineage-based recomputation, unless checkpointing is cheaper for expensive stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查点：把当前状态或中间结果写到可靠存储，作为恢复起点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint writes current state or intermediate data to reliable storage as a recovery point.

optionExplanations: 原始输入还完好地留在 HDFS 里，operator 链条本身也能重新跑一遍，丢失的分区完全可以从可用的输入按照血缘关系重新计算出来，不需要额外的备份。
要求用户手工上传备份，把本该由系统自动完成的恢复工作转嫁给了人，跟血缘重算这种自动化方式相比是不必要的负担。
把丢失的分区直接当空数据继续，会让结果悄悄变得不完整，属于产出错误结果而不是正确的恢复方式。
让下游猜测缺失记录同样会产出不可靠、不确定的结果，不是可靠的恢复手段。
optionExplanations_en: With the original input still intact in HDFS and the operator chain itself replayable, the lost partition can be recomputed from available input following the lineage graph, no extra backup needed.
Requiring users to manually upload a backup shifts recovery work that should be automatic onto a human, an unnecessary burden compared to lineage-based recomputation.
Treating the lost partition as empty data and continuing quietly makes the result incomplete — that's producing a wrong result, not a proper recovery.
Letting downstream stages guess missing records likewise produces unreliable, nondeterministic output, not a dependable recovery method.

scenario: 一个 operator 用系统当前时间和无固定种子的随机数生成输出；失败重算后，下游已经收到的旧输出与新输出不一致。
scenario_en: An operator uses the system clock and unseeded randomness; after recomputation, new output conflicts with old output already sent downstream.
q: 为什么批处理 operator 应尽量确定性？
q_en: Why should batch operators be deterministic?
options: 同输入重算应得到同输出，恢复才简单
确定性会自动减少所有网络流量
确定性让数据不需要分区
确定性要求所有代码只能写 SQL
options_en: The same input should recompute to the same output, making recovery simple
Determinism automatically reduces all network traffic
Determinism removes the need for partitioning
Determinism requires all code to be SQL
why: 恢复依赖重算时，同输入不同输出会把矛盾传播到下游。随机数、时钟和外部服务调用要固定、记录或隔离。
why_en: When recovery uses recomputation, nondeterministic output can conflict with downstream data, so clocks, randomness, and external calls need control.

termDefinitions.meaning: 确定性：相同输入和状态总是产生相同输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Deterministic means the same inputs and state always produce the same outputs.

optionExplanations: 如果恢复要靠重新计算，同样的输入就必须重算出同样的输出，不然新算出来的结果会跟下游已经收到的旧输出对不上，把矛盾一路传播下去。
确定性解决的是重算结果一不一致的问题，不会自动减少网络流量，这是两个不相关的话题。
确定性跟数据要不要分区完全没有关系，分区是另一套独立的设计决定。
确定性要求的是同输入同输出这个性质，不要求代码只能用 SQL 写，用回调函数写也完全可以做到确定性。
optionExplanations_en: If recovery relies on recomputation, the same input must produce the same output every time, otherwise the freshly recomputed result won't match what downstream already received earlier, propagating the contradiction further down.
Determinism addresses whether recomputed results are consistent; it doesn't automatically reduce network traffic, an unrelated topic.
Determinism has nothing to do with whether data needs partitioning — that's a separate, independent design decision.
Determinism just requires the same-input-same-output property; it doesn't require code to be written only in SQL — callback-based code can be just as deterministic.

scenario: 某阶段把 100TB 原始数据压缩成 20GB 特征表，但计算要跑 8 小时 CPU。下游会反复试验。
scenario_en: One stage compresses 100 TB of raw data into a 20 GB feature table, but it takes 8 CPU-hours to compute and downstream experiments reuse it.
q: 这个中间结果应如何处理？
q_en: How should this intermediate result be handled?
options: 物化或 checkpoint，避免反复昂贵重算
永远只保存在单个 executor 的内存里
每次下游试验都从 100TB 重算
直接删除，因为它不是最终输出
options_en: Materialize or checkpoint it to avoid repeated expensive recomputation
Keep it only in a single executor's memory forever.
Recompute from 100 TB for every downstream experiment
Delete it because it is not final output
why: 当中间结果远小于输入且计算昂贵，物化能用少量存储换大量 CPU 和扫描成本。代价是多一个数据版本需要管理。
why_en: If an intermediate is much smaller than the source and expensive to compute, materializing it trades small storage for large recomputation savings.
whenOtherWins: 如果中间结果巨大且只被下一步消费一次，管道化不落盘通常更快。
tradeoff: 存储版本成本 vs 重算成本
optionExplanations: 这份中间结果远小于原始输入、又要花 8 小时 CPU 才能算出来，把它物化或做检查点保存下来，能用一点存储空间换掉后续每次试验都要重新烧 8 小时 CPU 的成本。
只留在单个 executor 的内存里，进程一旦重启或崩溃就全没了，跟“下游会反复试验”这个需要多次复用的场景不匹配。
每次下游试验都从 100TB 重算，等于把已经算好的 20GB 结果白白扔掉，每次都要重新付出 8 小时的代价。
直接删除会让下游每次试验都得从头再算一遍，虽然它不是最终输出，但它是极其昂贵的中间产物，值得保留。
optionExplanations_en: With this intermediate far smaller than the source and costing 8 hours of CPU to produce, materializing or checkpointing it trades a bit of storage for skipping that 8-hour recompute on every subsequent experiment.
Keeping it only in one executor's memory forever means it's gone the moment the process restarts or crashes, mismatched with a scenario where downstream repeatedly reuses it.
Recomputing from 100TB for every downstream experiment throws away the already-computed 20GB result and pays the 8-hour cost again and again for no reason.
Deleting it outright would force every downstream experiment to recompute from scratch — it may not be the final output, but it's an expensive intermediate worth keeping.

scenario: 一个 dataflow 工作流大多可以边产生边消费，但其中一步要按全局 key 排序后输出。
scenario_en: Most of a dataflow workflow can consume records as they are produced, but one stage must globally sort by key before emitting output.
q: 排序为什么会打断流水线？
q_en: Why does sorting break pipelining?
options: 可能要看到最后一条才能输出第一条
它只能在单台浏览器里执行
它不需要任何内存或磁盘状态
它会让所有 key 自动变均匀
options_en: It may need the last input record before it can emit the first output.
It can only run inside a single browser.
It needs no memory or disk state at all.
It automatically evens out every key.
why: 全局排序是典型 pipeline breaker，必须积累足够输入才能输出正确顺序。能不用排序的 join 或聚合，就不要把排序当默认步骤。
why_en: A global sort is a pipeline breaker because it must accumulate input before emitting records in the correct order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流水线阻断算子：必须先收集大量或全部输入，不能边收边稳定输出的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pipeline breaker must collect much or all input before it can emit stable output.

optionExplanations: 要按全局 key 排出正确顺序，第一条要输出的记录到底是什么，很可能要等到看过最后一条输入才能确定，这就迫使这一步必须先攒够所有输入才能开始产出。
排序是数据处理里的一个逻辑步骤，跟能不能在浏览器里执行完全不相关。
全局排序恰恰需要额外的内存或磁盘空间去缓存和归并数据，不是不需要任何状态的操作。
排序只是把已有的 key 重新排列成有序，不会改变各个 key 原本的实际分布，不会让它们自动变得均匀。
optionExplanations_en: To emit records in the correct global order, what the very first output record should be often can't be known until the last input record has been seen, forcing this step to accumulate everything before it can start producing output.
Sorting is a logical processing step, entirely unrelated to whether it can only run in a browser.
A global sort specifically needs extra memory or disk space to buffer and merge data, not an operation that needs no state at all.
Sorting only rearranges existing keys into order; it doesn't change their actual underlying distribution or automatically make them balanced.

scenario: 候选人把 Spark DAG 和 PageRank 图处理混为一谈。你要纠正概念。
scenario_en: A candidate confuses a Spark DAG with graph processing such as PageRank; you need to clarify the concepts.
q: dataflow DAG 和 graph processing 的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between a dataflow DAG and graph processing?
options: DAG 是执行依赖，graph 是点边数据
DAG 要求输入必须是网页链接
graph processing 只表示 SQL 计划
两者都不能在集群上执行
options_en: A DAG is execution dependency; graph data is vertices and edges
A DAG requires web-link input data
Graph processing only represents SQL plans
Neither can run on a cluster
why: 一个是计算计划的形状，一个是输入数据模型的形状。名字都叫 graph，但面试里要先问清楚是在说执行图还是业务图。
why_en: A dataflow DAG is the shape of the computation plan, while graph processing is about data whose records are vertices and edges.
tradeoff: 执行依赖图 vs 数据关系图

termDefinitions.meaning: PageRank：根据链接关系迭代估计网页重要性的图算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PageRank is a graph algorithm that iteratively estimates page importance from links.

optionExplanations: DAG 描述的是计算步骤之间的执行依赖关系，是执行计划的形状；graph processing 里的图指的是业务数据本身长成点和边的样子，两者是完全不同层面的概念，只是碰巧都叫 graph。
DAG 只是执行依赖的形状，跟输入数据到底是不是网页链接毫无关系，任何批处理管线都可以用 DAG 表达。
graph processing 描述的是点边这种业务数据模型，不是用来表示 SQL 执行计划的概念，这个说法把两者搞混了。
Spark 的 DAG 执行计划和 PageRank 这类图算法都能在集群上正常运行，说两者都不能执行不成立。
optionExplanations_en: A DAG describes the execution dependencies between computation steps, the shape of an execution plan; graph in graph processing refers to business data whose records are vertices and edges — two completely different levels of concept that just happen to share the word graph.
A DAG is just the shape of execution dependencies and has nothing to do with whether the input data happens to be web links; any batch pipeline can be expressed as a DAG.
Graph processing describes a vertex-and-edge business data model, not a concept for representing SQL execution plans — this option conflates the two.
Both Spark's DAG execution plan and graph algorithms like PageRank run perfectly well on a cluster, so claiming neither can execute doesn't hold.

scenario: 你用普通 MapReduce 跑 PageRank，每轮只有少量 rank 变化，但每轮都读完整图并写完整新图。
scenario_en: You run PageRank with plain MapReduce; only a small amount changes per round, but each round reads and writes the whole graph.
q: 这种实现的主要浪费是什么？
q_en: What is the main waste in this implementation?
options: 没有利用迭代局部变化，每轮全量扫描和重写
没有把网页内容存在浏览器缓存
没有让每个 reducer 直接修改 HDFS 输入
没有把所有顶点放进一个 SQL 行
options_en: It ignores local iterative change and scans and rewrites everything each round
It does not cache web pages in the browser
It does not let every reducer mutate HDFS input directly
It does not put all vertices into one SQL row
why: 迭代图算法常只传播新增消息或变化值，普通 MapReduce 却按一轮一全量批处理。图专用模型能把顶点状态跨轮保留下来。
why_en: Iterative graph algorithms often only propagate changes, while plain MapReduce tends to rescan and rewrite the whole graph each round.
optionExplanations: 每一轮明明只有少量 rank 发生了变化，但普通 MapReduce 还是把整张图读一遍、把新版本整张图重新写一遍，完全没有利用迭代算法本该只传播局部变化这个特性。
这里讨论的是每轮全量扫描重写图数据的浪费，跟网页内容有没有存进浏览器缓存毫无关系。
允许 reducer 直接修改 HDFS 输入会破坏批处理依赖的不可变输入假设，跟这里描述的迭代浪费问题不是一回事。
把所有顶点塞进一个 SQL 行不是这里讨论的问题所在，浪费的根源是每轮全量重算，不是数据存储的行列结构。
optionExplanations_en: Each round only a small number of ranks actually change, but plain MapReduce still reads the entire graph and writes out a whole new version of it every time, never exploiting the fact that an iterative algorithm should only propagate local changes.
This is about the waste of full-scan-and-rewrite every round, unrelated to whether web page content is cached in the browser.
Letting reducers mutate HDFS input directly would break the immutable-input assumption batch processing relies on, a different problem from the iterative waste described here.
Cramming all vertices into one SQL row isn't the issue here — the root of the waste is recomputing everything every round, not the row-versus-column storage structure.

scenario: 你要在超大社交图上迭代传播分数；每个顶点只需要接收邻居消息、更新本地状态、再发消息。
scenario_en: You need to iteratively propagate scores over a huge social graph; each vertex receives neighbor messages, updates local state, and sends messages onward.
q: 哪种模型更贴合？
q_en: Which model fits this workload?
options: Pregel/BSP 式顶点消息模型
每轮手写完整 reduce-side join
在线 OLTP 点查询循环
单个全局锁保护的共享哈希表
options_en: Pregel/BSP-style vertex messaging
A hand-written full reduce-side join each round
A loop of online OLTP point queries
One shared hash table protected by a global lock
why: Pregel 让顶点保留跨轮状态，只处理收到的消息，适合迭代图算法。代价是轮与轮之间有同步屏障，跨机器消息仍可能很重。
why_en: Pregel keeps per-vertex state across rounds and processes incoming messages, which matches iterative graph algorithms.
whenOtherWins: 如果图能装进单机内存，简单单机算法可能因为没有网络开销而更快。
tradeoff: 分布式容量 vs 网络/同步开销

termDefinitions.meaning: Pregel：一种按顶点计算、按超级步传递消息的分布式图处理模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pregel is a distributed graph model where vertices compute and exchange messages in supersteps.

termDefinitions.meaning: BSP：批量同步并行模型，计算分成多轮，每轮结束有同步屏障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bulk Synchronous Parallel computation proceeds in rounds separated by global synchronization barriers.

optionExplanations: 每个顶点只需要接收邻居发来的消息、更新自己的本地状态、再往外发消息，这正是 Pregel/BSP 式顶点消息模型的核心设计，天然贴合这种迭代传播场景。
每轮手写完整 reduce-side join 会把每一轮都当成一次全新的批处理任务，没有利用顶点状态能跨轮保留的这个优势。
在线 OLTP 点查询循环是给低延迟单点查询设计的，跟这里超大规模图的批量迭代传播完全不是一回事。
单个全局锁保护的共享哈希表在超大社交图规模下会变成严重的并发瓶颈，完全不适合这种大规模并行迭代场景。
optionExplanations_en: Each vertex only needs to receive messages from neighbors, update its own local state, and send out messages — exactly the core design of the Pregel/BSP vertex-messaging model, naturally suited to this iterative propagation pattern.
Hand-writing a full reduce-side join every round treats each round as a brand-new batch job, failing to exploit the fact that vertex state can persist across rounds.
A loop of online OLTP point queries is designed for low-latency single lookups, a completely different thing from bulk iterative propagation over a massive graph.
A single shared hash table protected by one global lock would become a severe concurrency bottleneck at massive social-graph scale, entirely unsuited to this large-scale parallel iterative scenario.

scenario: 你要说明 Pregel 风格图计算中一个超级步如何推进。
scenario_en: You need to explain how one Pregel-style superstep progresses.
q: Pregel 超级步的顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the order of a Pregel superstep?
steps: 框架把上一轮消息交给目标顶点
顶点函数读取本地状态和消息
顶点更新状态并向邻居发送下一轮消息
所有分区到达屏障后进入下一超级步
why: Pregel 的确定边界是超级步：上一轮消息在本轮处理，本轮发送的消息到下一轮才可见。这个屏障简化推理，也带来等待慢分区的成本。
why_en: Pregel uses supersteps: messages sent in one round become visible in the next, simplifying reasoning at the cost of barriers.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  M["messages from round N-1"] --> V["vertex compute"]
  V --> S["send messages"]
  S --> B["barrier"]
  B --> N["round N+1"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 超级步：Pregel/BSP 中一轮并行顶点计算加同步屏障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A superstep is one round of parallel vertex computation followed by a synchronization barrier.

scenario: Pregel 作业运行到第 30 个超级步时一台机器丢失内存中的顶点状态。
scenario_en: A Pregel job reaches superstep 30 and one machine loses its in-memory vertex state.
q: 常见恢复方式是什么？
q_en: What is a common recovery strategy?
options: 回滚最近 checkpoint 并重放
把丢失的顶点状态直接清空之后继续跑
让邻居远程查询丢失机器
让用户手工重新输入消息
options_en: Roll back to the latest checkpoint and replay
Clear the lost vertex state and just continue.
Have neighbors query the lost machine remotely
Ask users to manually re-enter messages
why: 顶点状态在内存中跨轮存在，所以要周期性 checkpoint 到可靠存储。checkpoint 越频繁恢复越快，但正常执行 I/O 越多。
why_en: Because vertex state lives across rounds in memory, Pregel systems periodically checkpoint it to durable storage for recovery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查点：把顶点状态和必要元数据写到可靠存储，故障后从这里恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint writes vertex state and metadata to durable storage so computation can recover after failure.

optionExplanations: 顶点状态本来就活在内存里、跨越多个超级步，一旦某台机器丢失内存中的状态，只能回滚到最近一次持久化的 checkpoint，再从那里重放到当前进度。
直接把丢失的顶点状态清空继续跑，会让这些顶点的历史累积状态凭空消失，破坏算法的正确性。
让邻居远程查询丢失机器毫无意义，那台机器已经丢失了内存中的状态，没有东西可查。
让用户手工重新输入消息完全不现实，超级步之间的消息是算法自动产生和传递的，不是用户手动输入的。
optionExplanations_en: Vertex state lives in memory across many supersteps, so once a machine loses that in-memory state, the only option is to roll back to the most recent durable checkpoint and replay forward from there to the current progress.
Simply clearing the lost vertex state and continuing would wipe out those vertices' accumulated history for nothing, breaking the algorithm's correctness.
Having neighbors remotely query the lost machine makes no sense — that machine has already lost its in-memory state, there's nothing left to query.
Asking users to manually re-enter messages is completely unrealistic — messages between supersteps are generated and passed automatically by the algorithm, not entered by hand.

scenario: 社交图按 vertex_id 哈希分区后，很多边跨机器，消息量甚至大于原始图大小。
scenario_en: A social graph is hash-partitioned by vertex_id; many edges cross machines, and message traffic exceeds the original graph size.
q: 图分区差会造成什么后果？
q_en: What happens when graph partitioning is poor?
options: 跨机器消息开销高，慢分区拖住同步屏障
所有顶点都会自动变成热点 key
每条边都能本地处理所以更快
checkpoint 不再需要可靠存储
options_en: Cross-machine messaging is high, and slow partitions hold up barriers
Every vertex automatically becomes a hot key
Every edge becomes local and faster
Checkpoints no longer need durable storage
why: 图算法的成本常在边上的通信；分区没把强相关顶点放近，就会把计算变成网络等待。优化分区很难，哈希只是简单但不聪明的默认值。
why_en: Graph algorithms often pay on edge communication, so poor partitioning turns computation into network waiting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顶点：图中的实体节点，如用户、网页或地点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A vertex is an entity node in a graph, such as a user, page, or location.

termDefinitions.meaning: 边：图中连接两个顶点的关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge is a relationship connecting two vertices in a graph.

optionExplanations: 很多边跨机器意味着大量消息要走网络，某个分区处理得慢，整个同步屏障就要等它，其它已经算完的分区只能干等着，通信开销直接拖慢了整体进度。
按 vertex_id 哈希分区打散的是负载，不会让所有顶点都变成热点，热点通常指个别度数极高的顶点，是另一个问题。
这里描述的正好相反，很多边跨机器意味着大量边需要走网络传输，不是变成本地处理。
checkpoint 需要可靠存储来保证故障后能恢复，这跟图分区好坏是两个独立的问题，分区差不会让 checkpoint 不再需要可靠存储。
optionExplanations_en: With many edges crossing machines, a large volume of messages travels over the network, and one slow partition holds up the entire synchronization barrier while other partitions that already finished just sit waiting — communication overhead directly drags down overall progress.
Hashing by vertex_id spreads load out; it doesn't turn every vertex into a hotspot — a hotspot usually refers to a few individual high-degree vertices, a different problem.
This is the opposite of what's described — many edges crossing machines means a lot of edge traffic goes over the network, not that it becomes local.

Checkpointing still needs durable storage to enable recovery after a failure; that's an independent concern from partition quality — bad partitioning doesn't remove the need for durable checkpoint storage.

scenario: 你的图有 30GB，单机 256GB 内存能放下；分布式版本每轮都产生大量跨机器消息。
scenario_en: Your graph is 30 GB and fits in a 256 GB RAM machine; the distributed version creates heavy cross-machine messages every round.
q: 面试中应先考虑什么？
q_en: What should you consider first in an interview?
options: 先评估单机或单机多线程算法是否足够
默认上 Pregel，因为分布式一定更快
把图拆到更多机器直到消息消失
把所有边改成远程数据库查询
options_en: First evaluate whether a single-machine or multithreaded algorithm is enough
Default to Pregel because distributed is always faster
Add machines until messages disappear
Turn all edges into remote database queries
why: 图处理很容易被网络和同步拖慢；能放进单机内存时，少网络的朴素方案常赢。代价是单机容量和容错边界更有限。
why_en: Graph processing can be dominated by network and barriers, so a single-machine solution may win when the graph fits in memory.
whenOtherWins: 如果图超过单机内存或磁盘，分布式图处理才变成容量上的必要选择。
tradeoff: 无网络低开销 vs 单机容量上限
optionExplanations: 30GB 的图完全能装进 256GB 内存的单机，先评估单机或单机多线程算法能不能满足需求，很可能比引入分布式带来的网络和同步开销更划算。
默认认为分布式一定更快是个常见误区，这里描述的分布式版本恰恰产生了大量跨机器消息，反而可能比单机方案更慢。
把图拆到更多机器只会增加更多跨机器边，消息量往往不会因此消失，反而可能更多。
把所有边改成远程数据库查询会引入大量网络往返，跟“图能放进单机内存”这个前提相比是不必要的复杂化。
optionExplanations_en: With a 30GB graph fitting comfortably into 256GB of memory on one machine, first checking whether a single-machine or multithreaded algorithm is enough is likely more worthwhile than the network and synchronization overhead a distributed setup brings.

Assuming distributed is always faster is a common misconception — the distributed version described here specifically generates a lot of cross-machine messages and could actually be slower than a single-machine approach.
Splitting the graph across more machines just adds more cross-machine edges; the message volume typically doesn't disappear and could even grow.
Turning every edge into a remote database query introduces a huge number of network round trips, unnecessary complexity given that the graph already fits in one machine's memory.

scenario: 数据科学家在探索新特征，每天要多次改过滤条件、join 和 groupBy。手写 MapReduce 迭代很慢。
scenario_en: Data scientists are exploring features and repeatedly changing filters, joins, and groupBy operations; hand-written MapReduce slows iteration.
q: 高层 dataflow API 的主要价值是什么？
q_en: What is the main value of a high-level dataflow API?
options: 用关系式算子表达常见处理，让人和优化器都更容易工作
强迫所有逻辑写成底层 mapper/reducer
禁止交互式探索
自动证明业务指标正确
options_en: Express common processing with relational operators, helping both humans and optimizers
Force all logic into low-level mapper/reducer code
Disable interactive exploration
Automatically prove business metrics correct
why: filter、join、groupBy 这些算子比手写回调更短，也给优化器留下选择执行计划的空间。它提升开发效率，但仍需要理解数据语义。
why_en: High-level operators are shorter than hand-written callbacks and give the optimizer room to choose an execution plan.

termDefinitions.meaning: groupBy：按 key 分组后对每组做聚合或处理的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: groupBy groups records by key so each group can be aggregated or processed.

optionExplanations: 用关系式算子表达常见处理逻辑，比手写底层回调短得多，优化器也有空间挑执行计划。
强迫所有逻辑写成底层 mapper/reducer 回调正是高层 API 想要摆脱的负担，跟“提升效率”这个目标相反。
高层 API 恰恰是为了支持更快的交互式探索而设计的，不是要禁止它。
高层 API 提升的是开发和优化效率，不会替你自动证明业务指标本身对不对，这仍然需要人去判断。
optionExplanations_en: Expressing common processing with relational operators like filter, join, and groupBy is far shorter than writing low-level callbacks, and it gives the optimizer room to pick a better execution plan, letting a data scientist iterate faster.
Forcing all logic into low-level mapper/reducer callbacks is exactly the burden a high-level API is meant to remove, the opposite of the efficiency goal.
A high-level API is specifically designed to support faster interactive exploration, not to disable it.
A high-level API improves development and optimization efficiency; it doesn't automatically prove whether a business metric is correct — that judgment still needs a human.

scenario: 一个批查询有三个 join，其中一张表很小，两张表很大且已按 key 分桶。你不想手写 join 算法。
scenario_en: A batch query has three joins: one small table and two large tables already bucketed by key; you do not want to hand-code join algorithms.
q: 为什么声明式 join 有优势？
q_en: Why are declarative joins useful?
options: 让优化器按大小和布局选 join 算法
声明式 join 忽略输入数据规模
它保证所有 UDF 都没有开销
它只能生成固定 MapReduce 模板
options_en: Let the optimizer choose a join algorithm from size and layout
Declarative joins ignore input size
It guarantees every UDF has no cost
It can only emit a fixed MapReduce template
why: 声明式写出想要的关系，优化器才能利用统计信息和布局减少中间状态。代价是复杂 UDF 可能让优化器看不懂。
why_en: Declarative joins state the desired relation, letting the optimizer use statistics and layout to reduce intermediate data.
whenOtherWins: 如果处理逻辑是复杂自定义算法，手写代码或 UDF 可能比纯声明式表达更现实。
tradeoff: 优化器自由度 vs 自定义代码透明度

termDefinitions.meaning: UDF：用户自定义函数，嵌入查询或数据流中执行自定义逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User-Defined Function embeds custom logic inside a query or dataflow.

optionExplanations: 声明式地写出想要连接的三张表，优化器就能根据表的大小和已有的分桶布局，自动挑选广播、分区哈希还是排序归并这类合适的 join 算法，不用自己手写判断逻辑。
声明式 join 恰恰要利用输入数据的大小信息才能选出更好的执行计划，说它忽略输入规模正好说反了它的优势所在。
声明式方式本身不能保证所有 UDF 都没有开销，复杂的用户自定义函数依然会有执行成本，优化器甚至可能因此看不透它。
声明式查询会根据具体情况生成不同的执行计划，不是只能套用固定的 MapReduce 模板，这个说法低估了优化器的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Declaring the desired join across the three tables lets the optimizer automatically pick an appropriate algorithm — broadcast, partitioned hash, or sort-merge — based on table sizes and the existing bucketing layout, without hand-coding that decision logic.
A declarative join specifically relies on knowing the input size to choose a better execution plan, so claiming it ignores input size has its actual advantage backwards.
Being declarative doesn't by itself guarantee every UDF is free — a complex user-defined function still carries execution cost and can even make the plan opaque to the optimizer.
A declarative query generates different execution plans depending on the situation; it isn't limited to one fixed MapReduce template, an option that undersells the optimizer's capability.

scenario: 你要在批处理中解析图片、跑 NLP 库，并调用团队已有 Java 包；同时也有简单 SQL 报表。
scenario_en: Your batch pipeline must parse images, run NLP libraries, and call existing Java packages, while also supporting simple SQL reports.
q: 自定义代码模型相对纯 SQL 的优势是什么？
q_en: What is the advantage of a custom-code model over pure SQL?
options: 能复用通用编程语言生态处理非关系逻辑
它一定能比 SQL 优化器跑得更快
自动生成列式存储布局
让依赖管理不再需要
options_en: It can reuse general programming ecosystems for non-relational logic
It must run faster than a SQL optimizer.
It automatically generates columnar storage layouts
It removes the need for dependency management
why: MapReduce/dataflow 的回调模型适合调用库和表达复杂算法；SQL 更适合优化关系式过滤、投影和 join。现代系统往往把两者混合。
why_en: Callback-based dataflow code can reuse libraries for complex algorithms, while SQL is better for optimizable relational work.
tradeoff: 通用语言生态 vs 查询优化可见性

termDefinitions.meaning: NLP：处理文本语言的算法和工程技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Natural Language Processing covers algorithms and systems for working with human language text.

optionExplanations: 处理图片解析、调用 NLP 库和团队已有的 Java 包，正好能借助通用编程语言现成的生态和库，这是自定义代码模型相对纯 SQL 的核心优势。
自定义代码不见得总能比 SQL 优化器更快，SQL 在关系式过滤、投影这类场景反而往往能被优化得更好。
自定义代码模型不会自动生成列式存储布局，这属于存储引擎层面的能力，跟回调式编程模型是两回事。
用自定义代码调用 Java 包和 NLP 库，依赖管理该做的一点没少，这个说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Parsing images, calling NLP libraries, and invoking the team's existing Java packages is exactly where reusing a general programming language's ecosystem of libraries shines — the core advantage of custom code over pure SQL.
Custom code isn't always faster than a SQL optimizer; SQL often gets optimized better precisely for relational filtering and projection work.
A custom-code model doesn't automatically generate columnar storage layouts on its own — that's a storage-engine-level capability, a different thing from the callback programming model.
Using custom code to call Java packages and NLP libraries still requires just as much dependency management as ever, so this claim doesn't hold.

scenario: 一个过滤步骤只读取 200 列宽表中的 5 列，但旧实现每行调用一次用户函数并反序列化整行。
scenario_en: A filter reads only 5 columns out of a 200-column table, but the old implementation calls a user function per row and deserializes entire rows.
q: 声明式表达能带来什么执行优化？
q_en: What execution optimization can declarative expression unlock?
options: 只读需要的列，并用向量化内循环批量处理
把所有列都复制到 reducer 内存
让磁盘寻道变成零成本
让随机数生成变确定性
options_en: Read only required columns and process batches with vectorized inner loops
Copy every column into reducer memory
Make disk seeks free
Make random-number generation deterministic
why: 过滤和投影如果对优化器可见，就能利用列式存储和 CPU cache 友好的批处理循环。任意 per-row 回调通常会挡住这些优化。
why_en: When filters and projections are visible, the engine can use column pruning and vectorized CPU-friendly loops.

termDefinitions.meaning: 列裁剪：查询只读取实际需要的列，跳过无关列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Column pruning reads only the columns a query needs and skips the rest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 向量化执行：一次处理一批值，减少函数调用并提升 CPU cache 利用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vectorized execution processes batches of values to reduce calls and improve CPU cache use.

optionExplanations: 声明式过滤和投影对优化器是可见的，它就能只读需要的那 5 列而跳过其余 195 列，还能用向量化的批量内循环处理数据，比逐行调用用户函数快得多。
把所有列都复制到 reducer 内存正是旧实现每行反序列化整行的低效做法，声明式表达恰恰是要避免这种浪费。
磁盘寻道的物理成本不会因为声明式表达就变成零，这个说法夸大了它的效果。
随机数生成的确定性跟这里讨论的列裁剪和向量化执行完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: With declarative filters and projections visible to the optimizer, it can read only the 5 needed columns while skipping the other 195, and process data with vectorized batch inner loops, far faster than calling a user function row by row.
Copying every column into reducer memory is exactly the inefficient old approach of deserializing the whole row per call — declarative expression is precisely what avoids that waste.
The physical cost of disk seeks doesn't become zero just because expression is declarative — this claim overstates the effect.
Whether random-number generation is deterministic has nothing to do with the column pruning and vectorized execution being discussed here.

scenario: 批处理平台已经解决了调度和分布式执行，团队开始沉淀可复用算法库。
scenario_en: The batch platform has solved scheduling and distributed execution, so teams are building reusable algorithm libraries.
q: 哪些领域常会形成专用批处理组件？
q_en: Which domains often grow reusable batch-processing components?
options: 机器学习特征和训练算法
空间近邻或相似度搜索
基因序列近似匹配
每次用户登录的同步鉴权
options_en: Machine-learning features and training algorithms
Spatial nearest-neighbor or similarity search
Approximate matching for genomic sequences
Synchronous authentication on every login
why: 当通用执行层稳定后，重复出现的算法会被做成库或声明式算子。同步登录鉴权是在线请求路径，不是典型离线批处理组件。
why_en: Once the execution layer is stable, repeated offline algorithms become reusable libraries or declarative operators.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近邻搜索：在向量或空间中寻找距离某个对象最近的对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Nearest-neighbor search finds objects closest to a target in a vector or spatial space.

optionExplanations: 机器学习特征工程和训练算法在批处理平台稳定之后，经常被沉淀成可以反复复用的专用组件或算子。
空间近邻或相似度搜索这类计算模式也经常出现在多个业务场景里，值得抽出来做成专用库。
基因序列近似匹配是生物信息学里反复出现的计算模式，同样适合沉淀成专用的批处理组件。
每次用户登录的同步鉴权是在线请求路径上的实时校验，不是离线批处理该处理的任务，跟这里讨论的批处理专用组件不是一类。
optionExplanations_en: Machine-learning feature engineering and training algorithms often get distilled into reusable, specialized components or operators once the batch platform stabilizes.
Spatial nearest-neighbor or similarity search is another computation pattern that recurs across many business scenarios, worth extracting into a dedicated library.
Approximate matching for genomic sequences is a recurring computation pattern in bioinformatics, equally suited to becoming a dedicated batch component.

Synchronous authentication on every login is a real-time check on the online request path, not something offline batch processing handles — a different category from the batch-specific components discussed here.

q: 批处理的核心输入边界是什么？
q_en: What input boundary defines batch processing?
text: 批处理作业读取的是{{有边界的输入}}：例如某个时间点的日志文件集合或数据库快照，所以它能判断自己何时读完并完成。
text_en: A batch job reads a {{bounded input}}, such as log files or a database snapshot at a point in time, so it can know when it is done.
why: 这个边界让批处理可以全量重跑、比较版本、在成功后一次性发布输出。流处理的输入没有这个自然完成点。
why_en: Bounded input lets batch jobs rerun, compare versions, and publish output once complete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 有边界输入：大小和范围已知、最终会读完的数据集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Bounded input is a dataset with a known scope that can eventually be fully read.

q: 分布式批处理为什么总在按 key 搬数据？
q_en: Why does distributed batch processing move data by key?
text: MapReduce shuffle 的核心目的，是把{{同一个 key 的相关记录}}带到同一个处理位置。
text_en: The core purpose of a MapReduce shuffle is to bring {{records with the same key}} to the same processing location.
why: join、groupBy 和去重都需要某个任务看到同 key 的完整上下文。这个模式简单，但会被热点 key 和大 shuffle 成本限制。
why_en: Joins, groupBy, and deduplication need one task to see the full context for a key, but hot keys and shuffle cost can dominate.

termDefinitions.meaning: shuffle：把上游输出按 key 重新分区并传输给下游任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shuffle repartitions upstream output by key and transfers it to downstream tasks.

scenario: 你在面试中设计离线推荐重算：输入是昨日事件和用户快照，输出给在线 KV 服务查询。
scenario_en: In an interview, you design offline recommendation recomputation from yesterday's events and user snapshots, with output served by an online key-value store.
q: 合理的批处理设计链路是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable batch-processing design chain?
steps: 用批处理读取冻结输入，保证可重跑
按 user_id shuffle，把事件和画像 join 到一起
生成新版本推荐 KV 文件，而不是直接覆盖线上库
全部成功后原子切换在线服务的读取版本
why: 这条链路把批处理的强项用在可重跑、全量 join 和整批发布上。它不追求秒级新鲜度，必要时再加流式增量补偿。
why_en: This design uses batch strengths for rerunability, full joins, and atomic publication, with streaming added only if freshness requires it.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要求点击后几秒内改变推荐排序，纯每日批处理就不够，需要流式特征或在线更新。
tradeoff: 可重跑整批正确性 vs 秒级新鲜度
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Snapshot["frozen logs + profile snapshot"] --> Batch["batch join + features"]
  Batch --> Files["new KV files"]
  Files --> Switch["atomic version switch"]
  Switch --> Online["online reads"]

scenario: 订单事件不断到达，风控希望几秒内更新风险分数，而不是等 nightly job。
scenario_en: Order events keep arriving, and risk scoring should update within seconds rather than waiting for a nightly job.
q: 这个需求为什么偏向流处理？
q_en: Why does this requirement lean toward stream processing?
options: 输入无边界且结果要持续更新
输入是固定文件且只需一次输出
所有事件都必须同步 RPC 返回
结果永远不需要状态
options_en: The input is unbounded and results must update continuously
The input is a fixed file and needs one output
Every event must return through synchronous RPC
The result never needs state
why: 流处理面对的是持续到达的数据，系统长期运行并逐步更新派生结果。代价是时间、乱序和故障恢复都比固定批输入更难。
why_en: Stream processing fits unbounded input and continuous derived output, with harder time and recovery semantics than batch.
tradeoff: 持续新鲜度 vs 有界重跑简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: RPC：一个服务同步或异步调用另一个服务的接口方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Remote Procedure Call is a service-to-service invocation style.

optionExplanations: 订单事件源源不断地进来、没有一个固定的结束点，风险分数还要跟着每条新事件持续更新，这正是流处理面对的形状：无边界输入配合持续更新的结果。
输入是固定文件、只需要跑一次出结果，是批处理的形状，跟这里持续到达的订单事件正相反。
是否用同步 RPC 是接口设计的选择，不是决定该用流处理还是批处理的依据。
风险分数需要跟着历史事件累积计算，这里恰恰需要维护状态，不是不需要状态。
optionExplanations_en: Order events keep arriving with no fixed endpoint, and the risk score has to keep updating with each new event — exactly the shape stream processing handles: unbounded input paired with continuously updated results.
A fixed file processed once for one output is the shape of batch processing, the opposite of the continuously arriving order events here.
Whether to use synchronous RPC is an interface design choice, not what determines whether stream or batch processing is the right fit.
The risk score needs to accumulate from historical events, which specifically requires maintaining state, not the absence of it.

scenario: 支付服务把“订单已支付”发送给邮件、风控和记账系统。
scenario_en: A payment service emits an order-paid record to email, risk, and accounting systems.
q: 在事件流里 producer 和 consumer 分别是什么？
q_en: In an event stream, what are producer and consumer?
options: producer 生成事件，consumer 订阅并处理事件
producer 只保存数据库索引，consumer 只做压缩
producer 是 broker 的磁盘，consumer 是 TCP 包
producer 必须等待所有 consumer 同步完成
options_en: A producer creates events, and consumers subscribe to and process them
A producer only stores database indexes, and a consumer only compresses
A producer is broker disk, and a consumer is a TCP packet
A producer must wait synchronously for every consumer to finish
why: 事件是已经发生的事实记录，生产者发布它，消费者用它更新下游状态或触发动作。是否同步等待取决于消息系统和业务语义。
why_en: An event is a fact that happened; producers publish it and consumers use it to update downstream state or trigger work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产者：生成并发布事件的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A producer is the component that creates and publishes events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者：订阅、读取并处理事件的组件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer subscribes to, reads, and processes events.

optionExplanations: 支付服务是产生已支付事件的一方，是 producer；邮件、风控、记账系统各自订阅这个事件并据此做自己的处理，是 consumer。
producer 生成的是事件本身，不只是数据库索引；consumer 处理的是事件带来的业务逻辑，不只是压缩这一个动作。
producer 和 consumer 都是应用层面的角色，不是把 broker 磁盘或 TCP 包这类底层实现细节直接等同于它们。
producer 要不要等所有 consumer 同步完成取决于具体的消息系统设计，不是这个概念定义本身要求的。
optionExplanations_en: The payment service is the one producing the order-paid event, making it the producer; email, fraud, and ledger systems each subscribe to and act on it, making them consumers.
A producer generates the event itself, not just a database index; a consumer handles whatever business logic the event drives, not just a single action like compression.
Producer and consumer are application-level roles, not to be equated directly with low-level implementation details like broker disk or a TCP packet.
Whether a producer waits synchronously for every consumer depends on the specific messaging system's design, not something required by the concept's definition itself.

scenario: 库存数据库每秒可能有几千次变更，搜索索引用轮询每分钟扫表一次，延迟高且数据库压力大。
scenario_en: An inventory database changes thousands of times per second; the search index polls the table once a minute, causing lag and database load.
q: 为什么推送式事件通知更合适？
q_en: Why is push-based event notification a better fit?
options: 变更发生时才通知，减少空轮询
它让消费者不需要处理任何失败
它能保证搜索索引永远强一致
它把所有变更都变成浏览器缓存
options_en: Consumers are notified when a change happens, which cuts empty polls and lag.
It frees consumers from handling failures.
It keeps the search index strongly consistent forever.
It turns every change into a browser cache entry.
why: 频繁轮询会把“有没有新数据”的问题变成数据库负载。推送事件能降低无效读，但仍要处理积压、重复和失败恢复。
why_en: Polling turns change detection into database load, while push events reduce empty reads but still require backlog and retry handling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轮询：消费者定期主动检查是否有新数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polling means consumers periodically check for new data.

optionExplanations: 每分钟扫一次表大部分时候都是白跑，真正有变化才应该通知；变更一发生就推给消费者，能把这些无意义的空轮询和检测延迟一起省掉。
推送通知不代表消费者不用处理失败，失败恢复、重试这些问题依然存在，只是投递方式变了。
推送式通知不会自动保证搜索索引强一致，它通常还是异步的，索引可能短暂落后于数据库。
推送通知跟浏览器缓存是完全不相关的两个概念，这个说法答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Scanning the table every minute is mostly wasted work when nothing changed; notifying consumers the moment a change actually happens removes that pointless empty polling along with the detection delay.
Push notification doesn't mean consumers no longer handle failure — retry and recovery concerns still exist, only the delivery mechanism changed.
Push-style notification doesn't automatically guarantee the search index is strongly consistent; it's typically still asynchronous, so the index can lag briefly behind the database.
Push notification and browser caching are unrelated concepts, so this option doesn't address the question.

scenario: 一个监控 agent 每秒发送 CPU 指标；偶尔丢一个点可接受，但 agent 不应被中央存储拖慢。
scenario_en: A monitoring agent sends CPU metrics every second; losing an occasional point is acceptable, and the agent should not be slowed by central storage.
q: 哪种消息方式可能足够？
q_en: Which messaging style may be enough?
options: 直接发送或轻量 pub-sub，允许少量丢失
必须使用事务性队列保存每条指标
把指标写进用户主数据库事务
每个 agent 同步等待所有 dashboard 确认
options_en: Direct send or lightweight pub-sub with some loss allowed
A transactional queue that stores every metric
Write metrics inside the user primary database transaction
Have every agent wait for all dashboards to acknowledge
why: 监控指标通常看趋势，少数点丢失不影响判断，低开销更重要。代价是不能用它承载账务、订单这类不可丢事件。
why_en: For trend metrics, low overhead may matter more than perfect delivery, as long as occasional loss is acceptable.
whenOtherWins: 如果事件代表付款、库存或审计事实，就要用持久 broker 或日志来保留可恢复记录。
tradeoff: 低开销低耦合 vs 可恢复交付

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布订阅：生产者发布到主题，消费者订阅主题接收消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Publish-subscribe lets producers publish to topics and consumers subscribe to those topics.

optionExplanations: CPU 指标看的是整体趋势，偶尔丢一个数据点不影响判断，直接发送或轻量 pub-sub 换来的是 agent 本身不被阻塞、开销更低。
要求每条指标都进事务性队列可靠保存，会给这种可以容忍少量丢失的场景背上不必要的重量级开销。
把监控指标写进用户主数据库事务，会让业务核心事务背上额外的负担，跟指标数据的重要性不成比例。
要求每个 agent 同步等所有 dashboard 确认，会让 agent 被下游拖慢，跟“不应被中央存储拖慢”这个要求正相反。
optionExplanations_en: CPU metrics are about overall trend, and losing an occasional data point doesn't hurt the picture, so direct send or lightweight pub-sub buys lower overhead without blocking the agent.
Requiring every metric to go through a reliable transactional queue saddles a scenario that can tolerate some loss with unnecessary heavyweight overhead.
Writing monitoring metrics inside the user's primary database transaction burdens the core business transaction, disproportionate to how critical metrics data actually is.
Requiring every agent to synchronously wait for all dashboards to acknowledge lets downstream slow the agent down, the opposite of the requirement that it not be slowed by central storage.

scenario: 订单创建后要异步发邮件、扣优惠券和通知仓库；消费者可能宕机几分钟，订单事件不能丢。
scenario_en: After order creation, email, coupon, and warehouse work run asynchronously; consumers may be down for minutes, and order events must not be lost.
q: 为什么需要 message broker？
q_en: Why use a message broker?
options: broker 持久保存消息并在消费者恢复后继续投递
broker 会让所有消费者都同步阻塞订单接口
broker 自动知道业务补偿逻辑
broker 让消息无需序列化
options_en: A broker stores messages durably and continues delivery when consumers recover
The broker makes all consumers synchronously block the order API.
A broker automatically knows business compensation logic
A broker removes the need to serialize messages
why: broker 把生产者和消费者解耦，并能在消费者离线时缓冲消息。代价是端到端延迟、积压监控和重复投递处理都要设计。
why_en: A broker decouples producers from consumers and buffers messages while consumers are offline, at the cost of lag and duplicate handling.
whenOtherWins: 如果消费者必须在请求内给出结果，直接 RPC 或同步事务更符合语义。
tradeoff: 异步可恢复性 vs 同步确定结果

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息代理：位于生产者和消费者之间，负责存储、路由和投递消息的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message broker stores, routes, and delivers messages between producers and consumers.

optionExplanations: 消费者可能会宕机几分钟、订单事件又不能丢，broker 能把消息持久保存下来，等消费者恢复之后继续投递，正好补上这段离线窗口。
broker 的意义正是让生产者和消费者解耦，不是让所有消费者反过来同步阻塞订单接口，那样会让下单变慢甚至卡住。
broker 只负责消息的存储和投递，不理解具体的业务补偿逻辑，这些还是要由消费方自己实现。
消息要经过序列化才能在系统间传输和存储，broker 不会让这一步凭空消失。
optionExplanations_en: With consumers potentially down for minutes and order events not allowed to be lost, a broker persists messages durably and keeps delivering once consumers recover, exactly covering that offline window.
The whole point of a broker is to decouple producers from consumers, not to make every consumer synchronously block the order API — that would slow down or even stall checkout.
A broker only handles storing and delivering messages; it has no understanding of business compensation logic, which the consumer still has to implement itself.
Messages still need to be serialized to be transported and stored across systems; a broker doesn't make that step disappear.

scenario: 你在选订单事件传输方式：一个方案让生产者直接推给消费者，另一个让生产者先写 broker。
scenario_en: You are choosing how to deliver order events: producers push directly to consumers, or producers first write to a broker.
q: direct messaging 和 broker 最大差异是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest difference between direct messaging and a broker?
options: broker 集中缓冲重投递，direct 更轻
direct 一定会持久保存所有历史消息
broker 禁止多个消费者同时订阅
direct 自动提供分区日志的 offset
options_en: A broker buffers and redelivers centrally; direct messaging is lighter but riskier when a consumer is offline.
Direct messaging always keeps every historical message durably.
A broker forbids multiple consumers from subscribing.
Direct messaging gives you partitioned-log offsets for free.
why: 直接通信少一跳，适合可丢或强同步场景；broker 用中心化队列换离线容忍和重试。选择时先问消息丢失是否可接受。
why_en: Direct messaging is lightweight, while a broker buys offline tolerance and redelivery through centralized buffering.
tradeoff: 低延迟少组件 vs 离线缓冲和重试
optionExplanations: broker 把消息集中缓冲起来、还能重投递，适合消费者可能离线的场景；direct messaging 少一跳、更轻量，但消费者掉线时消息就直接没人接住了。
点对点直发恰恰不天然持久保存历史，消息发出去接不住就没了。
broker 完全可以支持多个消费者订阅同一份消息，这个说法把它的能力说反了。
它是点对点的即时传递，不天然带有分区日志这种带 offset 的持久结构。
optionExplanations_en: A broker centrally buffers messages and can redeliver them, fitting a scenario where consumers might go offline; direct messaging skips a hop and stays lighter, but the message has nowhere to land if the consumer is down.
Direct messaging specifically doesn't durably store history by nature — it's closer to immediate delivery, and a message is gone if nobody catches it.
A broker can absolutely support multiple consumers subscribing to the same messages, so this option has its capability backwards.
Direct messaging is point-to-point immediate delivery and doesn't naturally come with a durable, offset-based partitioned log structure.

scenario: 你设计股票交易系统的成交事件流，每条成交都影响资产和审计。
scenario_en: You are designing a trade-execution event stream; every trade affects assets and audit records.
q: 消息丢失策略应是什么？
q_en: What should the loss policy be?
options: 不可静默丢失，要持久记录、确认和补偿路径
允许随机丢弃部分消息，靠图表平滑就行
只在消费者在线时发送，离线就跳过
把失败消息写到开发者本地文件
options_en: Do not silently lose messages; use durable records, acknowledgements, and repair paths
Drop some messages randomly and smooth it over in charts.
Send only while consumers are online and skip offline ones
Write failed messages to a developer's local file
why: 成交是业务事实，丢一条就是资产错误。可以接受延迟或重试，但不能接受无痕丢失。
why_en: A trade is a business fact, so loss creates incorrect assets; delay or retry is acceptable, silent loss is not.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是高频性能指标，少量采样点丢失通常可以接受。
tradeoff: 业务正确性 vs 传输开销

termDefinitions.meaning: 确认：消费者处理成功后告知 broker 可以推进或删除消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An acknowledgement tells the broker that a consumer successfully processed a message.

optionExplanations: 每一笔成交都是会影响资产和审计的业务事实，必须持久记录下来、要有确认机制，出问题还要有能补救的路径，绝不能悄无声息地丢掉。
随机丢弃再靠图表平滑，对趋势展示或许能接受，但对每一笔都要精确对账的成交事件来说，会直接造成资产记录错误。
只在消费者在线时发送、离线就跳过，等于主动放弃了这段时间的成交记录，跟“每条成交都影响资产”这个要求直接冲突。
把失败消息写到开发者本地文件既不可靠也不可审计，一旦这台开发机出问题，这些成交记录就彻底找不回来了。
optionExplanations_en: Every trade is a business fact affecting assets and audit trails, so it must be durably recorded with an acknowledgement mechanism and a repair path when things go wrong — it can never quietly disappear.
Randomly dropping messages and smoothing the chart might be acceptable for a trend display, but for trade events that must reconcile exactly, it directly corrupts asset records.
Sending only while consumers are online and skipping the rest effectively abandons trades during that window, directly conflicting with the requirement that every trade affects assets.
Writing failed messages to a developer's local file is neither reliable nor auditable, and if that machine has a problem, those trade records are gone for good.

scenario: 团队想把任务队列当数据库使用，希望任意查询旧任务、按字段过滤、长期保存所有历史。
scenario_en: A team wants to use a task queue as a database: arbitrary queries over old tasks, field filters, and permanent history.
q: 传统 message broker 与数据库的边界在哪里？
q_en: Where is the boundary between a traditional broker and a database?
options: broker 重投递确认，数据库重查询与状态
broker 天然就支持任意的二级索引查询
数据库不能长期保存历史记录
broker 的事务一定比数据库更强
options_en: A broker optimizes delivery and acknowledgement; a database optimizes querying and long-lived state.
A broker natively supports arbitrary secondary-index queries.
Databases cannot keep historical records for long.
Broker transactions are always stronger than database ones.
why: 传统队列通常在消息确认后删除或隐藏消息，不是为任意历史查询设计。若要保留和回放历史，分区日志或数据库模型更贴近。
why_en: Traditional queues focus on delivery and ack, not arbitrary historical queries; logs or databases fit history and replay better.
tradeoff: 投递语义 vs 查询/历史语义

termDefinitions.meaning: JMS：Java 生态中的消息服务标准接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Java Message Service is a standard messaging API in the Java ecosystem.

termDefinitions.meaning: AMQP：面向消息队列互操作的协议规范。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol is a messaging protocol for interoperable queues.

rows: broker 优先投递和确认，数据…
broker 天然支持任意二级索引
数据库不能保存历史记录
数据库不能保存历史…场景
数据库不能保存历史记录成本
broker 一定比数据库事务更强

optionExplanations: 传统 broker 关心的是把消息可靠投递出去并确认，投递完通常就删除或隐藏；数据库关心的是长期保存状态、支持任意条件查询，两者的设计重心本来就不一样。
传统 broker 不天然支持任意字段的二级索引，它的核心是投递语义而不是通用查询能力。
数据库当然可以保存历史记录，说数据库不能保存历史是不成立的。
broker 和数据库的事务能力设计目标不同，不能笼统地说 broker 一定比数据库事务更强。
optionExplanations_en: A traditional broker cares about reliably delivering and acknowledging messages, typically deleting or hiding them once delivered; a database cares about long-term state and supporting arbitrary queries — their design priorities are fundamentally different.
A traditional broker doesn't naturally support arbitrary secondary indexes on fields; its core strength is delivery semantics, not general-purpose querying.
A database can absolutely store history — claiming it can't doesn't hold.
Brokers and databases target different transactional goals, so it isn't accurate to broadly claim a broker's transactions are always stronger than a database's.

scenario: 一个 topic 同时被邮件服务、风控服务和多个邮件 worker 读取。
scenario_en: One topic is read by an email service, a risk service, and multiple email workers.
q: 消息系统常见的多消费者模式有哪些？
q_en: What are common multi-consumer patterns in messaging systems?
options: 同组消费者负载均衡处理一份工作
不同消费者组各自收到全量事件
每个消息只能被全世界一个消费者看见
消费者组内分片可提升并行度
options_en: Consumers in one group load-balance one copy of the work
Different consumer groups each receive the full event stream
Each message can be seen by only one consumer globally
Partitioning within a group can increase parallelism
why: 队列语义解决“多个 worker 分担任务”，发布订阅语义解决“多个系统各自派生状态”。很多系统把两者组合成消费者组。
why_en: Queue semantics split work within a group, while publish-subscribe semantics fan out the stream to different groups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者组：共同消费一个流的一组实例，组内通常分担分区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of instances that share consumption of a stream, often by partition.

optionExplanations: 同一个消费者组里的多个消费者会分摊同一份工作，比如多个邮件 worker 一起处理这个 topic，每条消息只被组内一个成员处理。
不同的消费者组（比如邮件组和风控组）各自独立收到完整的事件流，互不影响，这正是发布订阅式的 fan-out。
每条消息在全局意义上只能被一个消费者看见，这个说法忽略了不同消费者组各自都能收到全量事件这个事实。
在一个消费者组内部，把 topic 分片给多个成员各自处理不同分片，正是提升并行度的常见方式。
optionExplanations_en: Multiple consumers within the same group split the same work — several email workers together handling this topic, with each message going to only one member of the group.
Different consumer groups, like the email group and the fraud group, each independently receive the full event stream without affecting each other — that's exactly publish-subscribe fan-out.
Claiming each message can only ever be seen by one consumer globally ignores the fact that different consumer groups each still get the full stream.
Sharding a topic across multiple members within one consumer group, each handling its own shard, is exactly the common way to increase parallelism.

scenario: 邮件发送服务有 20 个 worker，每封邮件只应被一个 worker 发送，但吞吐要横向扩展。
scenario_en: An email sending service has 20 workers; each email should be sent by one worker, while throughput scales horizontally.
q: 应该用哪种消费模式？
q_en: Which consumption pattern should you use?
options: 同一消费者组内负载均衡
每个 worker 都订阅全量事件
让生产者轮询每个 worker 的内存队列
把所有邮件写进一个共享文本文件
options_en: Load-balance within one consumer group
Have every worker subscribe to the full stream
Have producers poll each worker's in-memory queue
Write all emails to one shared text file
why: 同组消费把每条任务交给一个实例，能横向扩展 worker 数量。代价是组内通常不再让每个实例看到全量历史。
why_en: A consumer group gives each task to one instance, scaling workers while avoiding duplicate sends.
whenOtherWins: 如果风控和数据仓库也要各自看到所有邮件事件，它们应使用独立消费者组。
tradeoff: 任务分摊 vs 全量广播
optionExplanations: 20 个 worker 放进同一个消费者组，broker 会把每一封邮件分给组里的某一个 worker 处理，横向加 worker 就能扩展吞吐，还不会让同一封邮件被重复发送。
让每个 worker 都订阅全量事件，会导致同一封邮件被 20 个 worker 各自发送一遍，跟“每封邮件只应被一个 worker 发送”直接冲突。
让生产者主动去轮询每个 worker 的内存队列，既低效又难以扩展，也不是消息系统该有的分工方式。
把所有邮件写进一个共享文本文件会带来严重的并发写入冲突，完全没有横向扩展能力。
optionExplanations_en: Putting the 20 workers into the same consumer group lets the broker hand each email to exactly one worker, so adding more workers scales throughput without any email being sent twice.
Having every worker subscribe to the full stream would send the same email through all 20 workers, directly conflicting with the requirement that each email be sent by only one worker.
Having the producer actively poll each worker's in-memory queue is both inefficient and hard to scale, not how a messaging system should divide labor.
Writing all emails to one shared text file would create severe concurrent-write conflicts and has no horizontal scalability at all.

scenario: 订单事件要同时驱动邮件、风控、发票和数据仓库，每个系统都需要完整事件流。
scenario_en: Order events drive email, risk, invoicing, and the data warehouse; each system needs the full stream.
q: 应该用哪种消费模式？
q_en: Which consumption pattern should you use?
options: 为每个系统建独立消费者组，实现 fan-out
把所有的下游系统都放进同一个组里去平分事件
让邮件服务处理后转发给其它系统
只保留最快消费者的 offset
options_en: Use independent consumer groups for fan-out to each system
Put all downstream systems in one group to split events.
Have email process and forward to every other system
Keep only the fastest consumer's offset
why: 不同派生系统都需要完整输入时，fan-out 让每个组独立推进自己的进度。代价是 broker 要承受更多读取和保留压力。
why_en: Fan-out with separate consumer groups lets each derived system read the full stream and track its own progress.
whenOtherWins: 如果多个实例只是同一个服务的 worker 池，它们应在同一组内分摊。
tradeoff: 独立派生视图 vs broker 读取/保留成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 扇出：同一事件被多个独立消费者或消费者组接收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out means the same event is delivered to multiple independent consumers or consumer groups.

optionExplanations: 邮件、风控、发票、数据仓库各自都要看到完整的订单事件流，给每个系统建一个独立的消费者组，各组互不干扰地各自追赶自己的进度，正是 fan-out 的做法。
把所有系统放进同一组会让它们互相分摊事件、谁都看不到完整的事件流，跟“每个系统都需要完整事件流”这个要求正相反。
让邮件服务处理完再转发给其它系统，会把邮件服务变成一个不必要的单点瓶颈和额外的耦合环节。
只保留最快消费者的 offset 会让处理慢的系统丢掉还没消费的事件，达不到每个系统都要完整历史的要求。
optionExplanations_en: With email, fraud, invoicing, and the warehouse each needing the complete order event stream, giving each system its own independent consumer group lets them each track their own progress without interfering — exactly fan-out.
Putting all systems in one group would have them split the events among themselves, so none sees the complete stream — the opposite of every system needing the full event stream.
Having the email service process events and then forward them to other systems turns it into an unnecessary single point of failure and adds needless coupling.
Keeping only the fastest consumer's offset would let slower systems lose events they haven't consumed yet, failing the requirement that every system gets the complete history.

scenario: 队列按顺序投递任务 1、2、3；worker 处理 2 时崩溃，broker 后来把 2 重新投给另一个 worker。
scenario_en: A queue delivers tasks 1, 2, 3 in order; the worker crashes on task 2, and the broker later redelivers task 2 to another worker.
q: 确认与重投递会带来什么风险？
q_en: What risk do acknowledgement and redelivery introduce?
options: 重投递可能导致重复处理或处理顺序变化
消息一定永久丢失
broker 一定停止所有其它分区
消费者不再需要幂等
options_en: Redelivery may cause duplicate processing or changed processing order
The message is always permanently lost
The broker always stops all other partitions
Consumers no longer need idempotence
why: 未确认消息要重投递才能避免丢失，但失败前的副作用可能已经发生。消费者要用幂等键、去重表或事务来兜住重复。
why_en: Redelivery avoids loss but can repeat side effects, so consumers need idempotence, dedupe keys, or transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 重投递：broker 在未收到确认后再次发送同一消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redelivery means the broker sends the same message again after no acknowledgement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等性：同一消息处理多次与处理一次的可见效果相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotence means processing the same message multiple times has the same visible effect as once.

optionExplanations: worker 处理任务 2 时崩溃、消息又被重新投给了另一个 worker，原来那次处理可能已经产生了部分副作用，重投递之后既可能重复处理，也可能打乱原本 1、2、3 的处理顺序。
消息没有丢失，恰恰是因为 broker 主动重投递才保住了它，这个说法跟场景描述矛盾。
这里描述的只是一条消息的重投递，不代表 broker 会因此停掉其它所有分区。
重投递恰恰是消费者更需要幂等处理的原因，不是不再需要幂等的理由，这个说法说反了。
optionExplanations_en: With the worker crashing while handling task 2 and the message being redelivered to another worker, the original attempt may already have produced partial side effects, so redelivery can both duplicate the processing and shuffle the intended 1-2-3 order.
The message wasn't lost precisely because the broker proactively redelivered it, which contradicts this claim.
This describes the redelivery of one message; it doesn't mean the broker stops every other partition because of it.
Redelivery is exactly why consumers need idempotent handling more, not a reason they no longer need it — this option has it backwards.

scenario: 你要构建搜索索引、推荐特征和审计仓库；新消费者上线时希望从历史订单事件开始追赶。
scenario_en: You need to build a search index, recommendation features, and audit warehouse; new consumers should start from historical order events and catch up.
q: 为什么 partitioned log 比传统队列更合适？
q_en: Why is a partitioned log a better fit than a traditional queue?
options: 日志保留消息，可按 offset 回放
日志会在确认之后立刻删除掉所有消息
日志禁止多个消费者组同时读取
日志只能保存单个分区的数据
options_en: The log keeps messages, so a consumer can replay from any offset.
The log deletes all messages right after acknowledgement.
The log forbids several consumer groups from reading it.
The log can only hold one partition's data.
why: 派生系统需要重建和回放，分区日志把消息当持久历史而不只是一次性任务。代价是保留策略、磁盘和慢消费者积压要监控。
why_en: Derived systems need rebuild and replay, so a partitioned log treats events as durable history rather than one-shot tasks.
whenOtherWins: 如果消息只是一次性后台任务，传统工作队列更简单。
tradeoff: 可回放历史 vs 队列式删除简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区日志：按分区追加记录，每个分区内有稳定顺序和 offset。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partitioned log appends records to partitions, each with a stable order and offsets.

termDefinitions.meaning: offset：消息在日志分区中的位置编号，消费者用它记录进度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is a message position in a log partition used by consumers to track progress.

optionExplanations: 新消费者上线时要从历史订单事件开始追赶，分区日志把已经处理过的消息也继续保留在日志里，消费者按自己的 offset 从头读起就能回放整段历史。
如果确认后立刻删除消息，新上线的消费者就没有历史可以追赶了，这跟场景需求正相反。
分区日志完全支持多个消费者组各自独立读取，这个说法把它的能力说反了。
分区日志本身可以拆成多个分区并行存储和读取，不是只能保存单一分区。
optionExplanations_en: With a new consumer needing to catch up from historical order events, a partitioned log keeps already-processed messages around, letting the consumer replay the whole history by reading forward from its own offset.
If messages were deleted right after acknowledgement, a newly onboarded consumer would have no history to catch up on, the opposite of what the scenario needs.
A partitioned log fully supports multiple consumer groups reading independently, so this option has its capability backwards.
A partitioned log can itself be split into multiple partitions stored and read in parallel, not limited to storing just one partition.

scenario: 你要解释 Kafka 风格分区日志里消费者如何读取和恢复进度。
scenario_en: You need to explain how consumers read and recover progress in a Kafka-style partitioned log.
q: 分区日志消费的主路径是什么？
q_en: What is the main path of consuming a partitioned log?
steps: producer 把事件追加到某个分区
broker 给分区内事件分配递增 offset
consumer 顺序读取分配给自己的分区
consumer 处理后提交已完成 offset
why: 分区内顺序和 offset 让消费者用一个位置表示进度。故障后新实例从上次提交的位置继续读，因此仍要处理可能重复的最后一段。
why_en: Partition order and offsets let a consumer track progress with one position and resume from the last committed offset.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  P["producer"] --> L["append to partition"]
  L --> O["offset assigned"]
  O --> C["consumer reads"]
  C --> K["commit offset"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：常见的分布式分区日志和事件流平台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a common distributed partitioned log and event streaming platform.

scenario: 你比较传统队列和分区日志的消费进度管理。
scenario_en: You are comparing progress tracking in a traditional queue and a partitioned log.
q: offset 相比逐条 ack 的简化点是什么？
q_en: How does an offset simplify progress tracking compared with per-message ack?
options: 顺序消费时，一个 offset 可代表此前所有消息已处理
offset 让所有消息都不需要持久化
offset 允许同一分区被同组多个消费者乱序并行处理
offset 自动处理外部数据库副作用
options_en: With sequential consumption, one offset represents all earlier messages as processed
Offsets remove the need to persist messages
An offset lets many consumers in a group process one partition out of order.
Offsets automatically handle external database side effects
why: 日志分区按顺序读，提交位置就能压缩进度状态。代价是单分区并行度受限，跳过慢消息不像任务队列那么自然。
why_en: Sequential log consumption compresses progress into one committed offset, but limits per-partition parallelism.
tradeoff: 进度状态简单 vs 单分区并行限制

rows: 顺序消费时，一个 offset 可…
顺序消费时，一个 of…成本
offset 让所有消息都不需要持…
offset 允许一个分区被同组多…
offset 自动处理外部数据库副…

optionExplanations: 日志内的消息是按顺序处理的，只要记住处理到了哪个 offset，就等于确认了它之前的所有消息都已经处理完，不用像逐条 ack 那样每条都单独标记。
消息本身仍然要被持久化存储在日志里，offset 只是记录消费进度，不会让消息本身不需要持久化。
同一个分区在同一个消费者组内通常按顺序交给一个消费者处理，不是允许被多个消费者乱序抢着处理。
offset 只是记录消费到了哪里，它不理解外部数据库副作用到底有没有真正生效，这仍然需要消费者自己处理。
optionExplanations_en: Messages within a log partition are processed in order, so remembering the offset already implies everything before it has been processed, no need to mark each message individually like per-message acknowledgement.
Messages still need to be durably stored in the log; the offset only tracks consumption progress, it doesn't remove the need to persist messages.
A partition is typically handed to one consumer within a group to process in order, not opened up for multiple consumers to process it out of order.
An offset just records how far consumption has gotten; it has no understanding of whether an external database side effect actually took hold — the consumer still has to handle that itself.

scenario: 日志保留 7 天，但某个数据仓库消费者停了 10 天后才恢复。
scenario_en: The log retains data for 7 days, but a warehouse consumer is down for 10 days before restarting.
q: 最大的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk?
options: 旧 offset 已过期，要用快照恢复
broker 为慢消费者永久留磁盘
其它消费者都必须回退 10 天
新事件会自动等它追上
options_en: The old offset expired, so recover from a snapshot
The broker keeps disk forever for the slow consumer
All other consumers must rewind ten days
New events automatically wait for it to catch up
why: 日志是大缓冲，不是无限归档；慢消费者落后超过保留窗口就会断档。要监控 consumer lag，并准备快照重建路径。
why_en: A log is a large buffer, not infinite archive, so a consumer behind retention needs a snapshot or rebuild path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费延迟：消费者已处理 offset 与日志最新 offset 的距离。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consumer lag is the distance between a consumer's processed offset and the log head.

optionExplanations: 日志只保留 7 天，一个消费者停了 10 天，它上次记住的 offset 早就被清理掉了，只能靠某种快照来恢复到一个相对新的起点，再重新开始跟着日志追赶。
broker 不会为了照顾某一个慢消费者就无限期保留磁盘空间，保留策略是统一设置的，跟哪个消费者慢没有关系。
其它正常追赶的消费者不受这一个慢消费者的影响，不需要跟着一起回退 10 天。
新事件不会因为一个消费者落后就自动停下来等它，日志会继续正常写入新数据。
optionExplanations_en: With retention set to 7 days and one consumer offline for 10, its old remembered offset has already expired out of the log, so it can only recover via some kind of snapshot to a reasonably fresh starting point and then resume tracking the log.
The broker doesn't hold disk indefinitely just to accommodate one slow consumer — retention policy is a uniform setting unrelated to how slow any particular consumer is.
Other consumers keeping up normally are unaffected by this one slow consumer and don't need to rewind ten days along with it.
New events don't automatically pause just because one consumer fell behind — the log keeps being written to normally.

scenario: 搜索索引代码有 bug，过去三天的索引字段算错了；订单事件仍在日志保留期内。
scenario_en: A search indexing bug computed a field incorrectly for the last three days; order events are still within log retention.
q: 分区日志如何降低修复成本？
q_en: How does a partitioned log reduce repair cost?
options: 修好代码后从旧 offset 回放重建索引
只能手工逐条修改每条索引记录
必须让订单服务从头重新产生所有历史事件
只能放弃这三天的历史错误
options_en: Fix the code, then replay from the old offset to rebuild the index.
Hand-edit every affected index record.
You must make the order service re-emit all history events.
Just write off the three days of bad data.
why: 日志把输入历史留住，派生状态错了可以删掉重建或从某个 offset 追赶。代价是重放会消耗计算资源，也要求处理逻辑对重复输入安全。
why_en: Because the log retains input history, a bad derived index can be rebuilt by replaying from an earlier offset.
optionExplanations: 订单事件仍在日志保留期内，只要修好索引代码，就可以从一个更早的 offset 重新把事件回放一遍，重建出正确的索引，不用去动已经产生的历史数据本身。
日志保留了完整的输入历史，可以整批重建索引，不需要逐条手工去改每条已经算错的索引记录。
订单事件本身没有丢，就在日志里，不需要让订单服务重新产生一遍这些历史事件。
日志把历史留住了，正好是为了让这类错误可以被修复，不是只能放弃了事。
optionExplanations_en: With order events still within the log's retention window, fixing the indexing code and replaying events from an earlier offset rebuilds a correct index without touching the historical data that was already produced.
The log retains the full input history, so the index can be rebuilt in bulk, no need to manually edit every miscalculated index record one by one.
The order events themselves were never lost — they're sitting right there in the log — so there's no need to make the order service regenerate them.
The log keeping history around is exactly what makes an error like this fixable, not something that has to be abandoned.

scenario: 用户更新邮箱时，服务先写主数据库，再写搜索索引；两个请求并发更新同一用户。
scenario_en: When a user updates email, the service writes the primary database and then the search index; two requests update the same user concurrently.
q: dual writes 的核心问题是什么？
q_en: What is the core problem with dual writes?
options: 两个系统可能看到不同顺序或只有一边成功
只要重试就一定没有重复
它自动提供全局事务顺序
搜索索引写入失败就会阻止数据库提交
options_en: The two systems may observe different orders, or only one write may succeed
Retries always avoid duplicates
It automatically provides a global transaction order
A failed search-index write blocks the database commit.
why: 双写没有单一顺序来源，竞态和部分失败都会让派生系统偏离主库。重试能提高成功率，但也可能放大乱序和重复。
why_en: Dual writes lack one ordering source, so races and partial failures can make derived systems diverge from the primary database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双写：一个请求路径同时写两个独立系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dual writes means one request path writes two independent systems.

optionExplanations: 主数据库和搜索索引是两次独立的写，没有单一顺序来源来保证它们按同样的顺序生效，并发更新时可能出现两边看到不同顺序，甚至只有一边写成功另一边失败的情况。
重试只是提高了成功的概率，如果没有幂等保护，重试反而可能引入重复写入，不能说重试就一定不会重复。
两次独立的写入本身不构成任何自动的全局事务顺序保证，这个说法把双写想得比它实际能做到的更强。
搜索索引是被动接收数据库写入结果的一方，它不会反过来阻止数据库自己的提交。
optionExplanations_en: The primary database write and the search index write are two independent writes with no single source of ordering guaranteeing they take effect in the same order, so concurrent updates can leave the two systems seeing different orders, or even have only one of them succeed.
Retrying only improves the odds of success — without idempotency protection, a retry can actually introduce a duplicate write, so it isn't accurate to say retries always avoid duplicates.
Two independent writes provide no automatic global transaction ordering on their own; this option credits dual writes with more than they actually achieve.
The search index passively receives the effects of the database write; it doesn't turn around and block the database's own commit.

scenario: 主数据库仍是用户资料的真相源，但搜索索引、缓存和数据仓库都要持续跟随它。你想避免业务请求双写。
scenario_en: The primary database remains the source of truth for user profiles, while search, cache, and warehouse must follow it continuously; you want to avoid dual writes.
q: 应该用什么机制同步派生系统？
q_en: What mechanism should sync the derived systems?
options: CDC 读取数据库变更日志
每个请求同时写所有下游系统
每晚全量 dump，白天不更新
让搜索索引直接成真相源
options_en: CDC reads the database change log
Every request writes all downstream systems
Run nightly full dumps and no daytime updates
Make the search index the source of truth
why: CDC 让主库的提交顺序成为同步顺序，下游只消费变更流。它通常是异步的，所以读索引可能短暂落后主库。
why_en: CDC uses the primary database's commit order as the synchronization order, while downstream systems consume changes asynchronously.
whenOtherWins: 如果下游必须和主库同事务强一致，异步 CDC 不够，需要同步事务或把读写收敛到同一存储。
tradeoff: 单一提交顺序 vs 派生系统短暂滞后

termDefinitions.meaning: 变更数据捕获：从数据库提交日志或等价机制提取数据变更事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Change Data Capture extracts data-change events from a database commit log or equivalent mechanism.

optionExplanations: CDC 直接读取主数据库自己的变更日志，把提交顺序当作同步顺序，下游各系统只管消费这条变更流，不用让业务请求自己去写多份。
每个请求同时写所有下游系统正是想要避免的双写模式，跟这里“避免业务请求双写”的目标直接矛盾。
每晚全量 dump、白天不更新，会让下游系统白天完全看不到主库的实时变化，跟“持续跟随”这个要求不符。
让搜索索引直接成为真相源会打乱原本的架构，主库仍然是用户资料的真相源，这个说法说反了角色。
optionExplanations_en: CDC reads the primary database's own change log directly, treating its commit order as the sync order, so downstream systems just consume that change stream instead of business requests writing multiple copies themselves.
Having every request write all downstream systems is exactly the dual-write pattern being avoided, directly conflicting with the goal of avoiding dual writes from business requests.
Nightly full dumps with no daytime updates would leave downstream systems completely blind to the primary's changes all day, failing the requirement to continuously follow it.
Making the search index the source of truth would upend the architecture — the primary database remains the source of truth for user profiles, so this option has the roles backwards.

scenario: 你要给现有 5TB 用户表新建搜索索引，同时之后的更新不能漏。
scenario_en: You need to build a new search index for an existing 5 TB users table while not missing later updates.
q: CDC 初始快照的安全顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the safe order for a CDC initial snapshot?
